Dr. Pudhiavan

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT SHOULDER JOINT AND SCREENING OF

CERVICAL SPINE

Clinical profile: Right shoulder mild joint tenderness, painful abduction. No h/o recent injury.

Technique: PDfs in all planes, T1 sag, T2/IR coronal, GRE axial and CT correlation.

Cervical spine screening: T2 sagittal and axial

Bones and joints:

Right shoulder joint appears grossly normal. Trace of joint fluid is seen.

No bony Bankart/ Hill-Sachs lesion is seen. Rest of the articulating bones is normal in outline and marrow signal intensities.

Rotator cuff:

Mild supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendinosis is seen. Small chronic intrasubstance tear is seen at insertion foot print region of anterior part of supraspinatus tendon (AP dimension of 7.5 mm and about 50% thickness).

Two small intramuscular cysts are seen at MTJ of supraspinatus, largest measuring 8.9 x 3 x 2.7 mm.

No full thickness tears or retracted tendon fibres seen. Rest of the rotator cuff muscles and tendons appear normal.

Long head of biceps appears intact. The deltoid muscle is also normal.

Labroligamentous structures:

Mild degenerative changes are seen in superior labrum. Rest of the glenoid labrum is well demonstrated and is normal in signal intensity. No acute tear or displaced fragment is seen. 

Biceps pulley appears intact. No definite capsular or ligamentous disruption seen.

AC joint:

Mild AC joint arthropathy is seen. The acromion is of type II morphology and is laterally sloping.

The subacromial space is mildly reduced (4.6 mm). Subacromial bursitis is seen with mild fluid.  Rest of the soft tissue appears normal.

Cervical spine screening:

Chronic post-operative changes are seen at C5-6 level.

Disc desiccation is seen at multiple levels. No significant mass effect over spinal cord or nerve roots seen. Spinal cord appears normal.

No other significant abnormality seen in screening cervical spine.

IMPRESSION:

Rotator cuff tendinosis with partial thickness tear and small intramuscular cysts as detailed.

Mild AC joint arthropathy with reduced subacromial space and mild subacromial bursitis, suggestive of sub acromial impingement.

Mild cervical spondylosis and post-operative changes as detailed.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF LUMBOSACRAL SPINE

Clinical profile: Low back pain, for evaluation.

Technique: Sagittal, T1, T2, IR, Axial T2, IR/ T1 Coronal for SI joints

Screening of rest of the spine: T2 sagittal

Considering left discrete vertebra as L5, 5

Chronic bilateral spondylolysis is seen at L5 level with grade I anterolisthesis of L5 over S1 vertebra.

Rest of the lumbosacral spine displays a normal lordotic curvature and vertebral column alignment.

Rest of the individual vertebrae are normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities.

Disc desiccation is seen at almost all levels with mild endplate changes and facetal arthropathy at few levels. The intervertebral discs are normal in heights. Rest of the vertebral end-plates are grossly normal.

D12-L1 and L1-2: Normal for age.

L2-3: Mild disc bulge with small right paracentral disc protrusion are seen causing anterior thecal sac indentation. No significant mass effect or nerve roots seen.

L3-4: Mild diffuse disc bulge with small left subarticular disc protrusion and facetal arthropathy are seen causing effacement of left lateral recess and mild indentation of left traversing L4 nerve root.

L4-5: Diffuse asymmetric annular disc bulge with posterior annular fissure and facetal arthropathy are seen causing effacement of lateral recess (R>L) and mild indentation of right traversing L5 nerve root.

L5-S1: Uncovered disc with mild posterior bulge and facetal arthropathy are seen causing mild indentation of right exiting L5 nerve root.

Thin fibrolipoma of the filum terminale is seen. The conus medullaris ends at D12-L1 level and the cauda equine is normal in appearance.

The prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues are grossly normal.

Both SI joints are grossly normal in joint space and signal intensities for age.

IMPRESSION:

Diffuse degenerative changes of lumbar spine with L5 spondylolysis and L5-S1 anterolisthesis as detailed.

Disc bulge with protrusion and facetal arthropathy causing mass effect over left L4 and right L5 nerve roots from L3-4 to L5-S1 levels as detailed.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr. Arul raj

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT KNEE JOINT

Clinical profile: Known marathon runner. C/o acute onset of right knee pain since few days. No h/o recent injury.

Technique: PDfs, T1, T2, IR and GRE in all planes.

Bones and joints:

Patellofemoral joint predominant osteoarthrosis is seen with partial thickness articular cartilage loss, chondral fissure and small osteophytes. Mild stress related marrow edema is seen in medial tibial plateau region without a definite fracture line or focal osteochondral defect.

Mild joint effusion is seen with reactive synovitis and suprapatellar plica. No full thickness cartilage loss or osteochondral fragment is seen.

Rest of the articulating bones are normal in outline and bone marrow signal intensity characteristics.

Meniscus:

Degenerative changes are seen in menisci.

Complex tear with predominant oblique component is seen involving posterior body and adjacent posterior horn regions of medial meniscus. Mild extrusion of inferior flap fragment is seen causing stress/ inflammatory changes along posteromedial soft tissue and MCL/ pes anserinus bursae.

Small flipped fragment is seen anterior to posterior horn of medial meniscus.

An incomplete discoid morphology of the lateral meniscus is noted. Small chronic oblique tear is seen in anterior body and anterior horn of lateral meniscus.

Rest of the medial and lateral menisci appear grossly normal for age.

Ligaments:

The medial and lateral collateral ligaments and patellar retinaculum appear grossly intact with mild degenerative changes.

Mild degenerative changes are seen in ACL. No significant tear or waviness of fibres seen. The posterior cruciate ligament appears grossly intact.

Posterolateral and posteromedial corner ligament complexes appear grossly intact.

Rest of soft tissues:

Mild grade I/ II strain of distal part of vastus lateralis muscle is seen. Patchy edema is seen in lateral part of prefemoral fat pad and anterior suprapatellar fat pad regions.

No fluid collection is seen.

The extensor mechanism appears grossly normal for age. Rest of the surrounding muscles, tendons and neurovascular structures are grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Mild right knee osteoarthrosis with joint effusion as detailed.

Medial meniscal tear with flipped fragments and mild extrusion causing mild stress/ inflammatory soft tissue/ bone changes as detailed.

Incomplete discoid lateral meniscus with small chronic tear.

Mild grade I/ II strain of distal part of vastus lateralis muscle with edema in prefemoral and anterior suprapatellar fat pad regions.

Mild degenerative changes are seen in ACL.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
MRI OF LEFT FEMUR

Clinical profile: C/o swelling in left distal thigh for past 2 months? Osteogenic sarcoma.

Technique: T1, IR, T2, DWI, Pre and post contrast T1 in all planes. CT correlation.

Left distal thigh and knee regions:

Primary tumor:

Abnormal large ill-defined mass lesion with diffuse and patchy sclerosis is seen in the distal femur with epicentre in medullary cavity of distal metadiaphyseal region. Ill-defined permeative destruction of cortex, patchy areas of sclerosis, sun burst and Codman’s triangle type of periosteal reaction and a large soft tissue component, all around the bone is seen.

The entire mass lesion including the medullary component and surrounding enhancing soft tissue component measures approximately 25.5 x 8.7 x 7.9 cm (CC x AP x TR). The lesion appears predominantly isointense to muscle in T1 and heterointense in T2/ IR images.

The enhancing soft tissue component shows patchy areas of tumor matrix ossification and areas of enhancing soft tissue component showing significant diffusion restriction (ADC values of 0.73 to 0.85 × 10−3 mm2/s). The soft tissue component is crossing the periosteum all around the involved region in distal metaphyseal region. Patchy areas of necrosis are seen in this lesion. No significant cystic component/ hemorrhage or fluid levels are seen in lesion.

Proximally, the intramedullary component with contrast enhancement and restricted diffusion is seen extending upto the midshaft level, about 25.6 cm from femoral condyle region.

Distally, the lesion is seen extending upto the subarticular regions of femoral condyles (lateral > medial) across the physis and is limited by articular cortex.

No significant enhancing skip lesions are seen in femur or other visualized bones in the present study.

Rest of the visualized bones show no alteration in signal intensity.

Rest of the soft tissue: 

The enhancing soft tissue component causes indentation, loss of fat planes and mass effect over prefemoral fat pad and adjacent distal part of vastus medialis, intermedius and lateralis muscles with soft tissue and fascial edema. The possibility of involvement has to be ruled out.

Mild smooth indentation over adjacent part of short head of biceps femoris is seen without significant loss of fat plane.  Edema is seen in the adjacent fascial planes and soft tissue.

Rest of the visualized muscles and soft tissue appear grossly normal.

Few small insignificant discrete lymph nodes are seen in bilateral inguinal regions. No significant sized lymphadenopathy is seen.

Neurovascular structures:

Small enhancing soft tissue component is seen indenting anterior aspect of popliteal vessels and sciatic nerve without significant encasement.

Sciatic, tibial and common peroneal nerves appear grossly normal in thickness and signal intensity.

Visualized Joints:

Minimal left knee joint effusion is seen with diffuse synovitis. To rule out early involvement.

Left hip joint appears normal.

IMPRESSION:

Large ill-defined sclerotic mass lesion in distal diametaepiphyseal region of left femur with extensive marrow involvement and soft tissue component as detailed.

Mass effect and loss of fat plane between enhancing soft tissue component and surrounding muslces and neurovascular structures in distal thigh as detailed.

Minimal effusion with synovitis in left knee joint as detailed.

No obvious skip lesion or significant sized regional lymphadenopathy.

Imaging features suggest the possibility of malignant etiology; Osteosarcoma is more likely than other tumors. Suggested clinical and HPE correlation.

MRI SCAN OF BILATERAL LOWER LIMBS WITH SCREENING OF LUMBAR SPINE (PLAIN + CONTRAST)

Clinical profile: K/c/o rheumatoid arthritis with inflammatory myositis on treatment, c/o pain bilateral pain for the past 6 months, persistent bilateral thigh and leg pain. For follow up.

Technique: T2, T1, IR, DWI, GRE and PC T1 in all planes for lower limbs, Screening of lumbar spine: T2 sagittal and axial.

Compared with previous MRI dated 06/ April/ 2026, present study shows,

Bones and joints:

Bilateral hip joints are maintained with no significant joint effusion or synovial thickening.

No imaging evidence of acute osteomyelitis or septic arthritis.

The visualized pelvic and lower limb bones demonstrate preserved marrow signal without focal marrow-replacing lesion or acute osseous abnormality.

Muscles and Soft Tissues:

Significant interval progression in the severity and extent of diffuse muscle signal abnormality involving bilateral lower limbs compared with the previous study.

On the previous study, the abnormal muscle signal was predominantly confined to the posterior and lateral compartments of the left leg.

On the present study, diffuse and extensive IR/ STIR hyper intensity is seen involving:

All muscles of the posterior compartment of the left leg.

Bilateral gluteus maximus muscles.

Anterior and posterior compartment muscles of both thighs, more pronounced on the left side.

Muscles of all three compartments of both legs, with left-sided predominance.

Mild muscle volume loss/ atrophy of left biceps femoris and gastrocnemius.

Subtle patchy post-contrast enhancement is seen within some of the involved muscles of the left lower limb.

No significant restricted diffusion, intramuscular necrosis, focal intramuscular collection or abscess is identified.

No abnormal fascial thickening or enhancement is seen.

The overlying skin, subcutaneous fat and fascial planes are preserved without significant inflammatory change or fluid collection.

Visualized neurovascular structures are grossly unremarkable.

Knees:

Mild bilateral knee joint osteoarthrosis with associated joint effusions is seen.

No acute osseous abnormality.

Screening of lumbar spine:

Disc desiccation and facetal arthropathy are seen at all levels and flaval thickening at multiple levels.

Small vertebral body haemangiomas are seen at few levels.

Disc bulge, facetal arthropathy and flaval thickening causing secondary spinal canal stenosis and compression of bilateral traversing nerve roots is seen from L2-3 to L5-S1 levels. Mild indentation of cauda equina is also seen at few levels.

No other significant abnormality seen in lumbar spine.

IMPRESSION:

Significant interval progression and marked increase in severity and extent of diffuse bilateral lower-limb myositis, compared with 06/ April/ 2026.

Abnormal muscle signal has progressed from predominantly involving left leg to extensive bilateral involvement of gluteal, thigh and leg musculature (L>R).

Associated mild atrophy of left biceps femoris and gastrocnemius muscles with subtle patchy enhancement in some of involved muscles, consistent with active inflammatory myositis on the background of chronic muscle involvement.

No restricted diffusion, intramuscular necrosis, abscess or significant fascial/ subcutaneous inflammatory changes.

Mild bilateral knee osteoarthrosis with joint effusion.

Multilevel lumbar spondylosis with canal stenosis and mass effect over nerve roots from L2-3 to L5-S1 levels as mentioned.

Overall, the muscular findings demonstrate significant interval radiological progression of the known inflammatory myositis. Suggested clinical correlation/ further evaluation and review as advised.

reports.fullText:
Dr Akila

MRI SCAN OFLEFT KNEE JOINT (P+C)

Clinical profile: H/o fever with c/o acute onset of left knee pain and swelling with restricted movements since 15.08.2026. To rule out acute osteomyelitis and septic arthritis.

Technique: PD fs in all planes, T1 , T2 sag, DWI axial , GRE and 3D PD. Pre and post contrast T1fs in all planes.

Bones and Marrow:

Abnormal ill-defined patchy marrow signal intensity is noted involving distal femoral metaphyseal region, appearing hypo intense on T1-weighted images and hyperintense on fluid-sensitive sequences with diffuse post-contrast enhancement.

Few tiny scattered intramedullary fluid collections are seen within the involved metaphysis demonstrating restricted diffusion and peripheral enhancement, consistent with intraosseous abscesses. Few branching/ arborizing intramedullary abscess tracts are seen within the distal femoral metaphysis demonstrating restricted diffusion and central non-enhancement.

Patchy marrow changes are also seen in the physis in anterolateral aspect of the distal femoral epiphysis. However, no obvious physeal involvement/ widening or transphsyeal infected fluid collection seen.

Associated focal periosteal elevation is present along the anterolateral aspect with sub periosteal abscess at metaphyseal and physeal level, measuring approximately 2.2 x 1.5 x 0.7 cm (CC × AP × TR) with restricted diffusion and peripheral enhancement.

No evidence of cortical devascularisation, marrow infarction, sequestrum formation, or significant periosteal stripping is identified.

The remaining visualized osseous structures demonstrate normal marrow signal intensity.

Knee Joint:

Mild knee joint effusion is present with smooth synovitis. The joint fluid does not demonstrate restricted diffusion but with mild altered diffusivity in the present study.

Mild adjacent inflammatory edema is noted within suprapatellar and Hoffa's fat pads.

Meniscus and Ligaments:

The medial and lateral menisci are normal in configuration and signal intensities. No acute tear or displaced fragment seen.

The medial and lateral collateral ligaments and patellar retinaculum appear intact.

The anterior cruciate and posterior cruciate ligaments appear intact. The intermeniscal and meniscofemoral ligaments are also normal.

Posterolateral and posteromedial corner ligament complexes appear normal.

Soft Tissues:

Extensive inflammatory edema and enhancement are seen within the soft tissues and muscles surrounding the distal femur, most pronounced along the anterolateral aspect of the distal thigh region. No deep intramuscular abscess is identified.

IMPRESSION:

Acute osteomyelitis involving distal femoral metaphysis with extension into part of distal femoral epiphysis as detailed.

Few tiny intraosseous abscesses within distal femoral metaphysis, including branching/ arborizing intramedullary abscess tracts.

Associated periosteal elevation with sub periosteal abscess along anterolateral aspect of distal femoral metaphysis as detailed.

Extensive surrounding soft-tissue inflammation/ cellulitis around distal femur, more severe along the anterolateral aspect of distal thigh region.

Mild knee joint effusion with synovitis, likely early septic arthritis. Suggested fluid evaluation.

Overall findings are consistent with acute distal femoral osteomyelitis with tiny intraosseous and sub periosteal abscess formation and early infective arthritis as detailed.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr Akila

MRI SCAN OF LEFT UPPER LIMB

Clinical profile: C/o  painless asymmetrical enlargement of left upper limb extending from the axilla to the fingers since birth.

Technique: IR, T1, T2, DWI and PDfs in all planes. CT correlation.

Findings:

Diffuse, relatively uniform hypertrophy of the muscles of the left upper limb is seen, involving the muscles of the arm, forearm and hand, with corresponding increase in muscle bulk compared with the contralateral right side.

There is also diffuse hypertrophy of the subcutaneous adipose tissue throughout the visualized left upper limb, contributing to the overall asymmetrical enlargement. Focal prominent axillary fat pad is also seen.

Mild diffuse asymmetrical prominence/ hypertrophy of the visualized bones of the left upper limb are noted compared with the contralateral side.

A small slow-flow venous malformation is seen within the proximal aspect of the flexor digitorum superficialis muscle demonstrating a small phlebolith and measuring about 2.6 x 1.1 x 1.4 cm. Another small similar looking lesion is seen along posterior aspect of distal arm region in subcutaneous plane and without phlebolith, measuring about 1.2 x 0.9 x 0.7 cm.

No other definite venous malformation is identified in the visualized left upper limb.

Mild asymmetrical prominence of the superficial/ deep draining veins of the left upper limb is noted compared with the right side.

Mild subcutaneous edema is seen predominantly in hand and posterior aspect of elbow.

No prominent feeding artery/ arterialized vascular channels or other imaging features to suggest a high-flow arteriovenous malformation are identified.

No other significant focal soft-tissue mass, significant joint abnormality or other significant abnormality is seen in the visualized left upper limb.

IMPRESSION:

Diffuse congenital unilateral overgrowth of left upper limb, involving muscles, subcutaneous adipose tissues and bones, resulting in generalized enlargement of entire left upper limb.

Associated small slow-flow venous malformations involving proximal flexor digitorum superficialis muscle and subcutaneous fat plane as mentioned.

Mild asymmetrical prominence of draining veins with mild subcutaneous edema, predominantly involving hand and posterior elbow regions.

No imaging evidence of a high-flow vascular malformation or significant arteriovenous shunting.

Overall findings are suggestive of a congenital segmental overgrowth syndrome with associated small venous malformations, within the PIK3CA-related overgrowth/ vascular malformation spectrum. Suggested clinical correlation/ further evaluation and review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
MRI SCAN OF LEFT KNEE JOINT

Clinical profile: H/o trivial trauma to leg approximately 10 days ago, associated with a small abrasion in knee. Subsequently developed pain, swelling and purulent discharge from the wound on 31.05.2026, followed by persistent fever and difficulty walking since 01.06.2026. The patient received treatment with intravenous antibiotics at an outside hospital, due to persistent high-grade fever and ongoing symptoms, came here for further evaluation and management.

Technique: PD fs, IR, T1, GRE, DWI and PC T1 in all planes.

Screening of left leg: IR, T1, DWI, Post contrast T1

Bones and Marrow:

Extensive abnormal marrow signal intensity is noted involving the proximal tibial metaphysis with extension into the proximal metadiaphyseal region, appearing hypointense on T1-weighted images and hyperintense on fluid-sensitive sequences with diffuse post-contrast enhancement.

Multiple tiny scattered intramedullary fluid collections are seen within the involved metaphysis demonstrating restricted diffusion and peripheral enhancement, consistent with intraosseous abscesses. Few branching/ arborizing intramedullary abscess tracts are seen within the proximal tibial metaphysis demonstrating restricted diffusion and central non-enhancement.

Infective marrow changes extend across the physis into the anterior aspect of the proximal tibial epiphysis.

Associated periosteal reaction is present, predominantly along the anteromedial aspect of the proximal tibia.

Thin elongated subperiosteal abscess is seen along anteromedial aspect of the proximal tibial metaphysis measuring approximately 2.3 x 2.0 x 0.5 cm (CC × TR × AP) with restricted diffusion and peripheral enhancement.

No evidence of cortical devascularisation, marrow infarction, sequestrum formation, or significant periosteal stripping is identified.

The remaining visualized osseous structures demonstrate normal marrow signal intensity.

Knee Joint:

Minimal knee joint effusion is present with mild reactive synovitis.

The joint fluid does not demonstrate restricted diffusion and no convincing MRI evidence of septic arthritis are identified.

Mild adjacent inflammatory edema is noted within the inferior Hoffa's fat pad.

Meniscus and Ligaments:

The medial and lateral menisci are normal in configuration and signal intensities. No acute tear or displaced fragment seen.

The medial and lateral collateral ligaments and patellar retinaculum appear intact.

The anterior cruciate and posterior cruciate ligaments appear intact. The intermeniscal and meniscofemoral ligaments are also normal.

Posterolateral and posteromedial corner ligament complex appear normal.

Soft Tissues:

Extensive inflammatory edema and enhancement are seen within the soft tissues and muscles surrounding the proximal tibia, most pronounced along the anteromedial aspect of the proximal leg. No deep intramuscular abscess is identified.

Popliteal Fossa:

Small Baker's cyst measuring approximately 5.0 x 2.3 x 0.8 cm is noted.

IMPRESSION:

Acute osteomyelitis involving proximal tibial metaphysis with extension into proximal metadiaphysis and transphyseal spread into proximal tibial epiphysis.

Multiple intraosseous abscesses within the proximal tibial metaphysis, including branching/ arborizing intramedullary abscess tracts.

Associated periosteal reaction with thin subperiosteal abscess along anteromedial proximal tibial metaphysis as detailed.

Extensive surrounding soft-tissue inflammation/ cellulitis around proximal tibia, more severe along the anteromedial aspect of proximal leg.

Minimal knee joint effusion with mild reactive synovitis. Suggested fluid evaluation to rule out early infection.

Overall findings are consistent with aggressive acute proximal tibial osteomyelitis with intraosseous and subperiosteal abscess formation.

reports.fullText:
CT SCAN OF LUNGS

Clinical Profile: Known case of Autoimmune Myasthenia gravis on immunosuppressive therapy. Patient c/o of persistent mild symptoms. Study compared with previous CT scan dated 5th May 2026: 

High resolution C.T.Scan of lungs shows: 

Persistent fatty thymic tissue is noted within the anterior mediastinum. Compared with the previous examination, there is a significant interval increase in multiple tiny soft-tissue density nodules/ foci within the residual thymic fat, in keeping with interval progression of thymic lymphoid (follicular) hyperplasia. LIMITED MRI SCAN OF LUMBOSACRAL SPINE

Clinical profile: K/c/o L5-S1 infective spondylodiscitis. Post stabilisation status. Now with c/o low back ache -10 days.

Study compared to previous MRI dated on 18.04.2026.

Technique: Sagittal, T1, T2, IR, Axial T2, IR, DWI, sag IR/ T1 Coronal for SI joints.

Postoperative changes of L5-S1 posterior instrumented fusion are noted, with bilateral pedicle screws and connecting rods in situ and an interbody disc spacer at L5–S1. Hardware alignment and position appear satisfactory on the provided images, without obvious periprosthetic lucency or hardware-related complication.

Small sub-acute Schmorl’s node with mild marrow edema is seen along superior endplate of L2 vertebra.

L5-S1 level:

There is mild interval reduction in the previously noted T2/ IR hyperintense marrow signal abnormality involving the L5 and S1 vertebral bodies, suggesting interval improvement of the previously described inflammatory marrow changes.

Persistent irregularity/ erosion of the opposing L5–S1 vertebral endplates are noted, with mild patchy sclerosis, consistent with the known treated spondylodiscitis.

There is minimal-to-mild interval reduction in the inflammatory soft-tissue changes centered around L5–S1 disc/ interbody spacer and the adjacent prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues.

Mild interval reduction in posterior paravertebral soft-tissue edema is also noted, with near-complete resolution of the previously described subcutaneous fat edema.

Persistent anterior epidural inflammatory soft tissue is seen at L5–S1, resulting in secondary narrowing of the spinal canal with bilateral lateral recess/neural root compression, greater on the left, involving the traversing L5/S1 nerve roots.

Residual thecal sac measures approximately 8.7 × 7.4 mm (transverse × AP) at this level.

No new or enlarging drainable epidural, prevertebral or paravertebral fluid collection is identified.

Other lumbar levels:

No significant interval change in the remaining lumbar levels.

A small sub-acute Schmorl's node along the superior endplate of L2 vertebra is noted with mild surrounding marrow edema.

Mild multilevel disc desiccation and facet arthropathy are present. The remaining intervertebral disc heights are maintained, with no significant additional disc pathology.

The remaining vertebral endplates are preserved.

The conus medullaris terminates at approximately the D12–L1 level. The visualized cauda equina is grossly unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

Study compared to previous MRI dated on 18.04.2026,

Postoperative L5–S1 posterior instrumented fusion with interbody spacer in situ.

Mild interval reduction in marrow edema, L5-S1 disc space and adjacent pre/ paravertebral and posterior soft-tissue inflammatory changes.

Persistent anterior epidural inflammatory soft tissue at L5–S1 causing spinal canal narrowing and mass effect over bilateral nerve roots (L>R).

No new drainable epidural, prevertebral or paravertebral collection.

Small sub-acute Schmorl's node at superior endplate of L2 vertebra with mild reactive marrow edema.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Clinical History: 35-year-old female with bilateral pes planus (flat feet) and pain along the medial aspects of both ankles and feet. Evaluation of the posterior tibial tendons.

Technique: Multiplanar, multisequence MRI of both ankles and hind feet was performed without intravenous contrast.

Bones and Joints:

Bilateral Type II accessory navicular bones are present, forming pseudo articulations with the navicular tuberosities.

Mild subchondral marrow edema is noted across the pseudo articulations bilaterally, with mild adjacent medial soft tissue edema, in keeping with symptomatic accessory navicular syndrome.

A small osteochondral lesion of talar dome is present on the right, associated with a tiny sub articular cyst. No unstable osteochondral fragment is identified.

Minimal joint fluid is present within both tibiotalar and posterior subtalar joints.

Mild edema is seen within the sinus tarsi bilaterally.

The remaining visualized osseous structures demonstrate normal marrow signal without acute fracture or osteonecrosis.

Tendons:

The posterior tibial tendons are intact bilaterally with maintained calibre and normal signal intensity. Mild tenosynovitis of the left posterior tibial tendon is present.

No significant tendinosis, partial-thickness or full-thickness tear is identified on either side.

The remaining flexor, extensor, peroneal, and Achilles tendons are intact without significant abnormality.

Ligaments:

The spring (plantar calcaneonavicular) ligaments are intact bilaterally.

The medial and lateral ligament complexes are otherwise grossly intact.

Plantar Fascia:

Mild thickening and increased signal intensity of the proximal plantar fascia on the right, consistent with mild plantar fasciitis.

The left plantar fascia is unremarkable.

Soft Tissues:

Mild soft tissue edema is present along the medial aspects of PTT tendon insertion on both sides. No focal fluid collection or soft tissue mass is seen.

IMPRESSION:

Bilateral Type II accessory navicular bones with features of mild symptomatic accessory navicular syndrome as detailed.

Mild left posterior tibial tendon tenosynovitis.

Small stable osteochondral lesion of talar dome on the right as detailed.

Mild bilateral sinus tarsi edema.

Mild right plantar fasciitis.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: C/o right shoulder pain since 2 years. No h/o of recent injury or shoulder dislocation.

Technique: PDfs, T1, T2, IR and GRE in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Mild cortical irregularity/ remodeling of the anteroinferior glenoid rim are seen without significant osseous glenoid bone loss. Mild subchondral sclerosis is seen along the anterior and posterior aspects of the bony glenoid.

No Hill-Sachs impaction deformity or other convincing evidence of prior anterior glenohumeral dislocation is seen.

Articular cartilage of the glenohumeral joint is maintained without focal full-thickness chondral defect. No significant joint effusion is seen.

The shoulder joint is grossly normal with respect to joint space and alignment. Rest of the articulating bones is normal in outline and marrow signal intensities.

Rotator cuff:

Mild supraspinatus and subscapularis tendinosis is seen. No significant tear is seen.

Rest of the rotator cuff muscles and tendons appear normal.

Mild LHBT tendinosis is seen. The deltoid muscle is also normal.

Labroligamentous structures:

Mild irregularity and chronic undisplaced tears are seen involving anteroinferior, anterosuperior, posteroinferior and posterior quadrants of the glenoid labrum, with relative sparing of superior/ posterosuperior labrum. No significant paralabral cyst formation is seen.

No acute tear or displaced fragment is seen.

Associated thickening and scarring of anteroinferior capsuloligamentous complex, including the anterior band of the inferior glenohumeral ligament.

Biceps pulley appears intact. No definite capsular or ligamentous disruption noted.

AC joint:

IMPRESSION:

Chronic multiquadrant glenoid labral tears with associated chronic scarring/ thickening of anteroinferior capsuloligamentous complex.

Mild chronic cortical irregularity and subchondral sclerosis along anterior and posterior aspects of bony glenoid as detailed.

Significant AC joint osteoarthropathy.

Mild rotator cuff tendinosis as detailed.

The above constellation of findings may represent chronic repetitive mechanical stress/ micro instability-related changes. Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Rest of the articulating bones appear grossly normal for age.

Rest of the visualised ligaments appears grossly normal.

No imaging features of acute osteomyelitis or septic arthritis.

Advanced ankle and midfoot osteoarthrosis as detailed.

Clinical profile: H/o RTA 2 days ago, during which the patient sustained a right shoulder dislocation that spontaneously reduced with self-manipulation. C/o right shoulder pain and painful restriction of movements since then.

Screening of cervical spine: T2 sagittal and axial.

Bones and Glenohumeral Joint:

Acute unicortical undisplaced fracture involving anterior aspect of greater tuberosity of proximal humerus is seen with adjacent trabecular injury and extensive marrow edema.

No acute Hill-Sachs impaction defect or osseous Bankart lesion identified.

Mild glenohumeral joint effusion is seen. No intra-articular osteochondral loose body.

Glenohumeral alignment is maintained.

Rest of the visualized osseous structures demonstrate normal marrow signal intensity.

Rotator Cuff:

Acute strain/ tendinous edema involving supraspinatus, infraspinatus and subscapularis tendons are seen.

Small partial-thickness intrasubstance tear involving supraspinatus tendon at its footprint, measuring approximately 5.7 mm in AP dimension. Small partial-thickness articular surface tear involving the posterior fibres of infraspinatus tendon.

No full-thickness rotator cuff tear or tendon retraction.

Mild Grade I-II myofascial strain is seen involving the rotator cuff musculature, deltoid and remaining visualized shoulder girdle muscles.

Long head of the biceps tendon is intact and normally positioned.

Labroligamentous Structures:

Soft tissue Bankart lesion with tear of anteroinferior glenoid labrum and adjacent periosteal injury is seen. Remaining glenoid labrum is intact. No displaced labral fragment.

Sprain of inferior glenohumeral ligament (IGHL) and inferior capsule with partial tear of anterior band of IGHL at its humeral attachment (partial HAGL lesion).

Mild sprain of the biceps pulley is seen. No complete capsular or ligamentous disruption.

Acromioclavicular Joint:

Mild AC joint sprain changes are seen. Type I acromion is seen. Acromiohumeral interval is maintained. Mild subacromial-bursal fluid is seen.

Soft tissue and fascial edema is seen along anteroinferior aspect of joint.  No focal soft tissue collection or hematoma is seen. Remaining visualized muscles and soft tissues are unremarkable.

Screening of cervical spine:

Loss of cervical lordosis is seen with multilevel disc desiccation.

Disc bulge and uncovertebral arthropathy are seen at few levels and small disc protrusion at C5-6 level. Mild indentation of cord is seen at few levels and nerve roots at C3-4 level.

No spinal cord signal changes are seen. No other significant abnormality seen.

IMPRESSION:

Acute post-traumatic anterior shoulder dislocation (currently reduced) with soft tissue Bankart lesion and capsuloligamentous injury as detailed.

No Hill-Sachs impaction defect or osseous Bankart lesion.

Acute undisplaced unicortical fracture in greater tuberosity with adjacent trabecular injury and extensive marrow edema.

Rotator cuff strain with small partial-thickness intrasubstance/ articular surface tears in supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendons as detailed.

Mild Grade I/ II myofascial strain in rotator cuff and shoulder girdle muscles.

Mild AC joint sprain with mild subacromial bursal and joint fluid.

Mild cervical spondylosis as mentioned.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI OF LEFT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: Known case of RA. C/o pain and restricted movements in left shoulder region for past 2 months. For detailed evaluation.

Technique: PD fs, T1, GRE, T2 fs in all planes and CT correlation.

Bones and Glenohumeral Joint:

Focal cortical erosion with marrow edema is seen along anterior aspect of humeral head region. Patchy subarticular marrow edema is also seen in central part of glenoid bone. No significant fracture or features of dislocation is seen.

Glenohumeral alignment is maintained. No Hill-Sachs impaction defect or osseous Bankart lesion identified.

Mild glenohumeral joint effusion is seen. No intra-articular osteochondral loose body.

Rest of the visualized osseous structures demonstrate normal marrow signal intensity.

Rotator Cuff:

Severe supraspinatus tendinosis is seen with fraying of fibres. Mild to moderate infraspinatus and subscapularis tendinosis is seen.

Focal full thickness tear is seen involving posterior part of supraspinatus tendon just proximal to insertion foot print region (AP dimension of 5.1 mm and with retraction of fibres of about 8.5 mm).

Partial thickness articular surface/ intrasubstance tears are seen in supraspinatus tendon. Small partial thickness tear is also seen in cranial part of subscapularis tendon.

Long head of the biceps tendon is intact and normally positioned. Deltoid muscle appears grossly normal.

Labroligamentous Structures:

Degenerative changes are seen in glenoid labrum. Small chronic tear is seen in superior and posterosuperior quadrants. Remaining glenoid labrum is intact. No displaced labral fragment is seen.

Diffuse synovial/ capsular thickening are seen in the joint, more severe in rotator interval and axillar recess regions. Thickening and increased signal intensity is seen involving biceps pulley and IGHL, suggestive of adhesive capsulitis.

No complete capsular or ligamentous disruption.

Acromioclavicular Joint:

Mild AC joint arthropathy changes are seen. Type IV acromion is seen. Acromiohumeral interval measures 5.2 mm.

Subacromial bursitis is seen with fluid collection. Few prominent axillary nodes are seen, likely benign reactive. Remaining visualized muscles and soft tissues are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

Imaging features of active inflammatory arthritis involving left shoulder with focal cortical erosion, subcortical marrow edema, diffuse synovitis and joint effusion.

Severe supraspinatus tendinosis with focal full-thickness tear and additional partial-thickness articular surface and intrasubstance tears.

Other Rotator cuff tendinosis with partial-thickness tear as detailed.

MRI features consistent with adhesive capsulitis and small labral tear as detailed.

Mild AC joint arthropathy and subacromial bursitis.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT ANKLE JOINT

Clinical profile: C/o pain along medial aspect of ankle for past 20 days? OLT. H/o recent surgical excision (before 15 days) of corn over plantar aspect of forefoot region.

Technique: PD fs, T1, T2, GRE, IR and DWI in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and Joints:

A large osteochondral lesion is seen involving the medial aspect of the talar dome, measuring approximately 3.0 × 1.5 × 1.4 cm. The lesion demonstrates multiple subcortical cystic changes with adjacent subchondral sclerosis and mild flattening of overlying articular cortex. No fluid-filled undermining of the osteochondral fragment, unstable fragment, or displaced intra-articular fragment is identified.

Imaging features are consistent with a stable chronic osteochondral lesion of the talus (Hepple stage V) due to the presence of subchondral cyst formation.

Minimal joint effusion is present within the ankle and posterior subtalar joints.

No acute fracture or dislocation is identified.

Ligaments:

Medial and lateral ligament complex appears intact. No significant tear is seen.

Rest of the visualised ligaments appear grossly intact.

Tendons:

The Achilles tendon, plantar fascia, peroneal tendons, flexor tendons, and anterior extensor tendons are intact.

No evidence of tenosynovitis, tendon tear, or tendon subluxation.

Postoperative Changes:

Postsurgical changes are noted along the plantar aspect of first MTP joint.

Tiny hypointense foci with susceptibility artefacts are present in the operative bed, likely related to postsurgical material or metallic debris.

No focal fluid collection, abscess, or sinus tract is identified.

Muscles and Soft Tissues:

Diffuse edema-like signal changes and mild atrophy involving the intrinsic muscles of the foot and distal leg regions are noted, consistent with diabetic myoneuropathy changes.

Mild diffuse subcutaneous edema is seen involving the distal leg, ankle, and foot.

No focal soft tissue collection or hematoma is identified.

IMPRESSION:

Large chronic osteochondral lesion of medial talar dome as detailed, compatible with Hepple stage V osteochondral lesion.

Minimal ankle and posterior subtalar joint effusions.

Postsurgical changes along plantar aspect of 1st MTP joint with tiny hypointense focus and artefacts as detailed.

Diffuse myoneuropathy changes involving intrinsic foot musculature.

Mild diffuse subcutaneous edema involving distal leg, ankle, and foot region.

No other significant abnormality seen.

LEFT SHOULDER

Clinical Profile: C/o neck pain, shoulder pain and bilateral lower limb pain for 1 week.

Technique: Sagittal T1, T2, IR, Axial T2.

Screening of rest of the spine: T2 sagittal

The cervical spine shows normal lordotic curvature and vertebral column alignment.

The individual vertebrae are normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities.

Disc desiccation is seen at almost all levels with mild uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy at multiple levels. The vertebral end-plates are normal. The intervertebral discs are normal in heights.

C2-3: No significant abnormality seen.

C3-4 and C4-5: Mild disc bulge and uncovertebral arthropathy are seen. No significant mass effect over nerve roots seen.  

C5-6: Disc bulge with bilateral uncovertebral arthropathy (R>L) are seen causing mild indentation of right exiting C6 nerve root.   

C6-7: Mild disc bulge and uncovertebral arthropathy are seen. No significant mass effect over nerve roots seen.  

C7-D1: Normal.  

Spinal cord shows normal signal intensity.

The prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues are normal.

The cranio vertebral junction and atlanto axial joint are normal.

Screening of dorsal spine:

Mild disc desiccation and flaval thickening are seen at few levels. Small vertebral body hemangiomas are seen at D8 and D9 levels. Spinal cord appears normal.

Screening of lumbar spine:

The conus medullaris ends at D12 level and the cauda equine is normal in appearance.

Mild disc desiccation, disc bulge and facetal arthropathy are seen at few levels. No significant mass effect over nerve roots seen.

Mild AC joint arthropathy is seen. The acromion is of type II morphology. Reduced subacromial space is seen (3.5 mm) with minimal subacromial bursitis.

No other significant abnormality seen.

IMPRESSION:

Mild diffuse degenerative changes of spine as detailed.

Disc bulge and uncovertebral arthropathy causing mild indentation of right C6 nerve root at C5-6 level as detailed.

Rotator cuff tendinosis, AC joint arthropathy and features of mild subacromial impingement as detailed.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF LEFT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: C/o left shoulder pain and upper arm, restricted abduction / internal rotation? Rotator cuff tear.

Technique: PDfs, T1, T2, IR and GRE in all planes.

Bones and joints:

Left shoulder joint appears grossly normal. No significant joint effusion is seen.

Subchondral cyst measuring 8 x 8 mm is seen head of humerus.

No bony Bankart/ Hill-Sachs lesion is seen. Rest of the articulating bones is normal in outline and marrow signal intensities.

Rotator cuff:

Supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendinosis is seen with intrasubstance tear at insertion foot print region of conjoined tendon (AP dimension of 1.2 cm and about 25-50% thickness).

Subscapularis tendinosis is seen with small chronic partial thickness articular surface tears. Intramuscular cyst measuring 3.9 x 0.4 x 0.3 cm is seen in subscapularis muscle.

No full thickness tears or retracted tendon fibres seen. Rest of the rotator cuff muscles and tendons appear normal.

Long head of biceps appears intact. The deltoid muscle is also normal.

Labroligamentous structures:

Degenerative changes are seen in labrum with small chronic labral tears in superior and anteroinferior quadrants. Rest of the glenoid labrum is well demonstrated and is normal in signal intensity. No acute tear or displaced fragment is seen. 

Mild synovial/ capsular thickening is seen in rotator interval region. Thickening with increased signal intensity of biceps pulley is seen. No definite capsular or ligamentous disruption seen.

AC joint:

Moderate AC joint arthropathy is seen. The acromion is of type II morphology and is laterally sloping with prominent acromial spur.

The subacromial space is mildly reduced (4.9 mm). Mild subacromial bursitis is seen with trace of fluid.  Rest of the soft tissue appears normal.

IMPRESSION:

Rotator cuff tendinosis with partial thickness tears and small intramuscular cyst as detailed.

Degenerative changes with labral tears and mild capsulitis as detailed.

AC joint arthropathy with reduced subacromial space and mild subacromial bursitis, suggestive of sub acromial impingement.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI OF THIGHS WITH SCREENING OF EXTREMITIES

Clinical Profile: Presented with small tiny papules in skin followed by muscle pain for the past one and half months? Connective tissue disease? Dermatomyositis.

Technique: IR/ T2/ T1 and DWI Coronal/ Axial for Whole Body covering chest, upper and lower extremities, Post contrast T1 images. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Visualized vertebra, shoulder girdle, pelvis and lower limb bones are grossly normal.

Minimal joint fluid is seen in bilateral knee and elbow joints.

Rest of the visualised joints appear normal.

Muscles and soft tissue:

Bilateral abnormal, symmetrical IR hyperintensities with altered diffusivity and post contrast enhancement are seen involving multiple groups of muscles in bilateral upper and lower limbs and thoracoabdominal regions as detailed below.

Mild perifascial edema/ inflammation and post contrast enhancement is seen along the involved muscles.

Multifocal patchy areas of inflammation and post contrast enhancement are seen involving the subcutaneous fat planes and overlying skin, more significant in bilateral arm/ elbow regions and left gluteal region.

No fatty changes are seen in the involved muscles. No calcification is seen in muscles or skin.

Rest of the visualised soft tissue appears normal. No abnormal fluid collection is seen.

Shoulder girdle and upper limbs:  Significant signal abnormality is seen in bilateral triceps and most of bilateral shoulder girdle region muscles. Mild involvement of anterior compartment muscles of arms and extensor group of forearm region is also seen. Relative sparing of forearm muscles is seen.

Thoracoabdominal regions: Significant signal abnormality is seen in bilateral paraspinal and posterior thoracic muscles. Relative sparing of anterior thoracic, intercostal and abdominal wall muscles is seen.

Pelvis and lower limbs: Significant signal abnormality is seen involving muscles in bilateral pelvic, anterior and medial compartments of thigh regions. Mild involvement of posterior compartment muscles of thighs is seen. Relative sparing of leg muscles is seen.

Rest of the visualised muscles and tendons appear normal.

No other significant abnormality seen in head, neck, thorax and abdomen regions.

IMPRESSION:

Bilateral symmetrical signal changes with contrast enhancement in multiple groups of muscles in bilateral upper and lower limb muscles, shoulder girdle and thoracoabdominal regions as detailed.

Multifocal inflammation in subcutaneous fat planes and overlying skin as detailed.

No other significant abnormality seen.

Imaging features are suggestive of inflammatory myopathy. In view of multifocal involvement of subcutaneous fat planes/ skin, the possibility of Dermatomyositis may be considered. Suggested clinical and muscle biopsy correlation/ follow up study as indicated.

Dr.U.Shobana

MRI OF WHOLE BODY

Clinical profile:  K/c/o dermatomyositis x 10 years, for assessment of disease progression. Previous details are not available.

Technique: T1 and IR coronal, T1, T2 and IR axial, DWI axial.

Brain:  

A well-defined extra axial simple cystic lesion measuring 2.4 x 1.6 cm is seen in left occipital region causing mass effect over underlying brain, may represent arachnoid cyst.

Rest of the visualized brain appears grossly normal.  

No significant focal lesion/ signal abnormality seen.  

Neck:  

No significant abnormality is seen in the visualized structures of neck.  

No significant sized focal lesion or lymphadenopathy is seen.  

Thorax:

Visualized lung fields appear unremarkable.

Bilateral mild sternoclavicular joint arthropathy changes are seen (R>L).

Bilateral acromioclavicular joints, clavicle and ribs show normal signal intensity.  

No other significant abnormality seen in thorax and mediastinum.  

Abdomen:

A simple cyst measuring 1.9 x 1.4 cm is seen in interpolar region of right kidney.

Rest of the visualized abdominal organs are unremarkable. 

No significant focal lesion/ signal abnormality or collection seen in the abdomen.  

Visualized bilateral upper limbs:  

The humerus on both sides reveals normal IR marrow signal intensity. No focal lesion or signal abnormality seen. 

Spine and pelvis:

The visualized pelvic bones appear normal. The visualized vertebrae appear normal. No other obvious IR signal changes are seen.

Bilateral sacroiliac joints, hip joints and iliac bones appear normal. No evidence of any hip joint effusion/ synovial hypertrophy is seen.  

Bilateral lower limbs and foot:

Bilateral tibia, fibula and foot region appear normal.

Muscles:

Muscle atrophy with varying degree of fatty infiltration is seen on both sides involving trunk, gluteal, and thigh and leg muscles in near symmetrical fashion as detailed below.

Fatty changes grading: Mild - minimal fatty changes. Moderate <50% fat. Severe >50% fat.  End stage appearance – entire muscle replaced with fat.

Diffuse IR hyperintensities with mild atrophy is seen involving left trapezius, bilateral medial & lateral head of gastrocnemius, and bilateral posterior deep compartment muscles of leg (L>R).

Mild IR hyperintensities with end stage atrophy and severe fat infiltration is seen involving bilateral soleus muscles.

Moderate to severe atrophy with fatty changes and without IR hyperintensities are seen in bilateral external and internal oblique, transverse abdominis and rectus abdominis.

End stage atrophy and severe fat infiltration and without IR hyperintensities are seen involving the right trapezius, bilateral serratus anterior, latissimus dorsi, bilateral paraspinal muscles in thorax and abdomen, bilateral psoas, iliacus, tensor fascia lata, bilateral hamstroing muscles with relative sparing of left semitendinosus and biceps femoris.

Subcutaneous and fascial edema changes are seen in left anterior abdominal wall, left pelvic region and bilateral lower limbs.

No evidence of focal collection, abscess, or myonecrosis seen. Rest of the visualized soft tissue appears grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

K/c/o dermatomyositis,

Extensive chronic myopathic changes with severe diffuse muscle atrophy and fatty replacement involving multiple muscle groups, consistent with advanced/ chronic sequelae of dermatomyositis.

Superimposed patchy muscle edema-like signal hyperintensities in few muscles, suggestive of mild ongoing active inflammatory myositis.

Mild associated fascial and subcutaneous soft tissue edema, in keeping with active inflammatory changes.

No evidence of focal collection, abscess, or myonecrosis.

Suggested clinical correlation/ further evaluation and review as indicated.

Dr. Saravanan.

MRI SCAN OF LEFT FOOT

Clinical profile: K/c/o Actinomycosis left foot (HPE proven) on medical treatment, now scan done to assess treatment response.

Technique: T1, IR, T2, DWI and Dynamic contrast, PC T1 in all planes. CT correlation.

On comparing with the previous MRI dated 07/ July/ 2026,

Bones and joints: 

Ankle joint alignment is normal. Minimal joint effusion is seen.

Rest of the bones and joints appear normal for age.

No imaging features of osteomyelitis or septic arthritis is seen.

Ligament complex:

Medial and lateral ligament complex appears intact. No significant tear is seen.

Rest of the visualised ligaments appears grossly normal. 

Tendons and rest of soft tissue:

Redemonstration of large ill-defined enhancing soft tissue lesion measuring about 7.9 x 7.5 x 3.9 cm (TRA x AP x CC)  involving the skin and subcutaneous fat plane in plantar aspect of foot, predominantly in midfoot region is redemonstrated without significant interval change in the extent.

Mild interval decrease in surrounding edema is seen.

Redemonstration of multiple subcentimetric sized focal lesions appearing mild hyperintense with central hypointense dot and peripheral hypointense rim on T2-weighted images is seen within the above mentioned lesion. Multiple small focal skin lesions are seen over the above mentioned soft tissue lesion.

Along the deeper aspect, the lesion is seen involving flexor digitorum brevis muscle and adjacent fascia. The lesion is encasing the lateral plantar neurovascular bundle for a short segment in midfoot region.

No other significant infected fluid collection or restricted diffusion seen in the present study. No adjacent soft tissue fluid collection is seen.

No new lesion is seen.

No prominent arteries or draining veins seen in the present study.

No significant sinus tarsi inflammation is seen. 

The anterior, medial and posterior tendons appear normal. No features of tenosynovitis are seen. Peroneal and flexor retinaculum is intact.

Rest of the soft tissue appears normal. There is no evidence of fluid collection seen.

IMPRESSION:

Persistent large ill-defined infiltrative enhancing soft-tissue lesion involving skin and subcutaneous tissues along plantar aspect of left midfoot as detailed. No significant interval changes in size or extent of lesion.

Multiple small intralesional T2-hyperintense foci with central hypo intense dots and peripheral hypo intense rims, along with overlying cutaneous lesions, compatible with known Actinomycosis involvement.

Mild interval reduction in surrounding soft-tissue edema, suggesting mild interval response.

No new lesion, drainable abscess, significant restricted-diffusion focus, or other significant fluid collection.

No evidence of osteomyelitis or septic arthritis.

Suggested clinical correlation and review as indicated.

Dr M Arun

MRI OF WHOLE BODY

Clinical profile:  H/o treatment for GBS with IVIG in August 2026, then improved, now c/o difficulty in walking, standing and inability to raise bilateral upper limbs. Rasied CPK-743. ?Idiopathic inflammatory myopathy.

Technique: T1 and IR coronal, T1, T2 and IR axial, DWI axial. PC T1 fs axial.

Findings:

Brain:

Visualized brain parenchyma appears grossly unremarkable. No focal signal abnormality identified.

Neck / Thorax / Abdomen:

Sub segmental atelectasis/ consolidations are noted in right lung segments.

No significant abnormality identified in the visualized neck, mediastinum, or abdominal viscera. No significant lymphadenopathy or focal collection seen.

Bones and joints:

Visualized vertebrae, pelvic bones, bilateral upper and lower limb bones demonstrate preserved marrow signal without focal lesion.

Bilateral sacroiliac and hip joints appear unremarkable without significant effusion or synovial thickening.

No imaging features of acute osteomyelitis or septic arthritis seen. No aggressive focal lesion seen.

Muscles:

There is diffuse, bilateral and relatively symmetrical T2/IR-STIR hyperintense signal involving the majority of the visualized skeletal muscles, including muscles of the neck, shoulder girdles, trunk, pelvic girdles and bilateral upper and lower limbs.

The distribution is predominantly diffuse and symmetric, without a discrete focal muscular mass or focal asymmetric lesion.

Diffuse and patchy post-contrast enhancement is seen corresponding to the involved muscles, consistent with active muscular edema/inflammation.

No significant muscular volume loss, fatty infiltration or established muscle atrophy is identified on the present examination.

No focal intramuscular fluid collection, abscess, organized hematoma or significant myonecrosis is seen.

Fascia and subcutaneous tissues:

Mild diffuse subcutaneous and fascial edema is seen involving the neck, thorax, abdomen and bilateral upper and lower limbs. No significant abnormal fascial enhancement or focal fascial fluid collection is identified.

No abnormal skin or subcutaneous enhancement to suggest cellulitis is seen.

Rest of soft tissues:

The remaining visualized soft tissues are grossly unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

Diffuse, bilateral and relatively symmetrical IR hyper intensity with corresponding patchy enhancement involving majority of visualized skeletal muscles of neck, shoulder girdles, trunk, pelvic girdles and bilateral upper and lower limbs, consistent with widespread active myopathic edema/ inflammation.

No significant muscle atrophy or fatty replacement in present study.

No focal intramuscular collection, abscess or significant myonecrosis.

Mild diffuse subcutaneous/ fascial edema without abnormal enhancement.

Sub segmental atelectasis-consolidative changes in visualized right lung.

In view of clinical features, the imaging findings are suggestive of active generalized myopathic process (inflammatory/ immune-mediated myopathy). Suggested clinical correlation/ further evaluation and review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr.Saravanan.

MRI OF BONY PELVIS

Clinical profile: Pain over the anterior aspect of the right hip, particularly on flexion, for 3 years, increasing over the past few months. History of slip and fall 3 years ago. Suspected right femoroacetabular impingement.

Technique: IR, T1, T2, PDfs, DWI and GRE in all planes. CT correlation. 

Right hip joint:

Prominent ossification of the antero superolateral acetabular labrum is seen, measuring approximately 2.7 × 2.5 × 0.6 cm (CC × AP × TR). The ossified labral component is contiguous with the adjacent antero superolateral acetabular rim, with associated subcortical sclerosis/ remodeling of the adjacent acetabular bone. No discrete or separately corticated acetabular rim fragment is identified.

The ossified labral component projects into the pericapsular soft tissues and causes focal indentation of the adjacent joint capsule and iliofemoral ligament.

Femoral morphology / CAM assessment:

The femoral head demonstrates preserved spherical contour. Alpha angle: 51°. Femoral head–neck offset: 10.8 mm (preserved). No focal osseous bump or abnormal contour deformity of femoral head-neck junction is identified.

No significant cam-type morphology is evident.

Acetabular morphology / Pincer assessment:

Acetabular version angle: 17°.

Lateral center-edge angle (LCEA) measured to the native acetabular rim: 47°.

LCEA including the ossified labral component: 64°.

Anterior center-edge angle (ACEA) measured to the native acetabular rim: 53°.

ACEA including the ossified labral component: 81°.

The above measurements demonstrate acetabular over coverage, particularly along the antero superolateral aspect, which is markedly accentuated by the extensive labral ossification.

The findings are compatible with acetabular-sided/ pincer-type femoroacetabular impingement morphology, predominantly related to the prominent antero superolateral labral ossification and associated increased focal acetabular coverage.

No definite imaging evidence of acetabular retroversion is identified.

Articular cartilage:

No significant focal chondral delamination or full-thickness cartilage loss is identified.

No significant subchondral marrow edema or cystic degenerative change is seen involving the femoral head or acetabulum.

Joint:

Trace right hip joint effusion. No intra-articular loose body identified.

Left Hip Joint:

Left femoral head demonstrates preserved contour and femoral head-neck morphology.

No significant labral or acetabular rim abnormality identified.

No significant joint effusion or cartilage abnormality.

Bony Pelvis:

The visualized pelvic bones, sacroiliac joints and pubic symphysis demonstrate preserved marrow signal.

No acute fracture, osteonecrosis, focal marrow edema or aggressive osseous lesion identified.

Soft Tissues:

The visualized periarticular muscles, tendons and soft tissues are grossly preserved.

No significant bursitis, muscle tear or focal soft-tissue collection identified.

IMPRESSION:

Prominent right acetabular labral ossification/ subcortical sclerosis as detailed.

Significant acetabular over coverage, predominantly in antero superolateral aspect by extensive labral ossification as detailed.

No significant cam morphology at present.

No significant cartilage loss or subchondral marrow changes.

Trace right hip joint effusion.

Findings are consistent with acetabular-sided/ pincer-type femoroacetabular impingement morphology, predominantly related to prominent antero superolateral labral/ rim ossification.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr Abhirami

MRI SCAN OF LEFT KNEE JOINT

Clinical profile: Alleged H/o RTA (Pedestrian hit by four wheeler), mediolateral instability of knee.

Technique: PD fs, T2, T1, IR and GRE in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Few chip like avulsion fractures of proximal tibiofibular ligament are seen involving posteromedial aspect of head of fibula.

Bone contusions with trabecular injuries and marrow edema are seen involving anterior aspect of medial femoral condyle, posterior aspects of medial and lateral tibial plateau and proximal fibula.

Mild joint effusion is seen. No full thickness cartilage loss or osteochondral loose body is seen.

Posterior translation of tibia is seen. Abnormal widening of medial tibiofemoral joint is seen. Rest of knee joint and articulating bones appear grossly normal for age.

Meniscus:

Contusion and strain changes are seen in both menisci.

Small horizontal and oblique tears are seen involving the body and anterior horn/ root of lateral meniscus and anterior and posterior roots of medial meniscus.

Rest of the medial and lateral menisci appears grossly normal.

Medial and lateral meniscocapsular sprain changes are seen, with likely disruption of medial meniscofemoral ligament.

Ligaments:

Full thickness tear of ACL is seen involving proximal third region with edematous, wavy fibres and altered contour.

Acute full thickness tear of PCL is seen involving femoral third with edematous, wavy fibres and altered contour.

Acute full thickness tear is seen involving the femoral part of medial collateral ligament and medial patellar retinaculum.

Grade II sprain changes of lateral collateral ligament and lateral patellar retinaculum are seen. No full thickness tear is seen.

Disruption of posterolateral and posteromedial corner ligament complexes and posterior complex is seen.

Rest of soft tissues:

Partial thickness tears with myofascial sprain changes are seen involving soleus, medial and lateral gastrocnemius muscles. Focal disruption of deep fascia is seen with herniation of part of muscle in lateral aspect.

Myofascial sprain changes are also seen involving the popliteus, and plantaris muscles, vastus lateralis and medialis muscles.

Extensive subcutaneous and fascial edema is seen around the knee joint with soft tissue hematoma on the lateral aspect of knee joint.

Diffuse hemolymphatic fluid collection is seen around the knee joint region superficial to the deep fascia.

Rest of the extensor mechanism appears grossly intact. Rest of the surrounding muscles, tendons and neurovascular structures are grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Few chip like avulsion fractures in head of fibula.

Acute bone contusions with trabecular injuries in medial femoral condyle, proximal tibia and fibula with joint effusion and capsular injury.

Full thickness tears of ACL, PCL, MCL and medial patellar retinaculum with sprain changes in multiple other ligaments as detailed.

Meniscal and meniscocapsular injuries with small meniscal tears as detailed.

Myofascial injuries with tears, fascial tear with focal herniation of muscle, other soft tissue injuries, fluid collection and edema as detailed.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Dr.Aathithya

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT KNEE JOINT

Clinical profile: H/o slip and fall with right knee joint dislocation and reduced outside. c/o right knee tenderness, swelling and difficulty in walking. Proximal fibula fracture, to r/o ligament injury

Technique: PD fs, IR, T1, T2, GRE in all planes, CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Minimally displaced avulsion fracture is seen involving superolateral aspect of proximal fibula at attachment of LCL/ biceps tendon. (Arcuate sign).

Bone contusions and osteochondral injuries are seen involving anterior aspect of medial femoral condyle and proximal tibia/ fibula.

Focal cartilage injury is seen in femoral trochlea region towards medial aspect with displaced chondral fragment measuring 9 x 9 x 2 mm.

Moderate hemarthrosis is seen with few clots. Full thickness capsular injury is seen along the posterior aspect.

Posterior translation of tibia is seen. Rest of knee joint and articulating bones appear grossly normal for age.

Meniscus:

Mild contusion and strain changes are seen in both menisci.

Small horizontal tears are seen in body regions of medial and lateral menisci. Small tears are also seen in roots of menisci. No displaced fragment is seen.

Rest of the medial and lateral menisci appears grossly normal.

Medial and lateral meniscocapsular sprain changes are seen.

Ligaments:

Acute full thickness tear of ACL is seen involving femoral third region with edematous, distally retraced wavy fibres and with altered contour.

Acute high grade partial tear of PCL is seen involving femoral attachment with mild wavy fibres and altered contour.

Avulsion fracture of fibular attachment of LCL is seen. Grade II sprain with partial tear is also seen at femoral attachment of LCL.

Grade II sprain with partial tear is seen involving femoral third of MCL. Near full thickness tear of femoral attachment of medial patellar retinaculum is seen with wavy and edematous fibres.

Grade II sprain of lateral patellar retinaculum is seen at femoral attachment region.

Disruption of posterolateral corner ligament complex is seen with full thickness tear.  Grade I/ II sprain of posteromedial corner complex is seen.

Rest of soft tissues:

Partial thickness tears with myofascial strain changes are seen involving lateral gastrocnemius, popliteus and plantaris muscles.

Mild myofascial strain changes and edema are also seen in adjacent parts of posterior and lateral compartment muscles and adjacent fascia.

Mild myofascial sprain changes are also seen involving distal parts of vastus lateralis and medialis muscles.

Extensive subcutaneous and fascial edema is seen around the knee joint, predominantly along the lateral and posterior aspects of knee joint.

Diffuse hemolymphatic fluid collection is seen around the knee joint region superficial to the deep fascia, along lateral and posterior aspects.

Rest of the extensor mechanism appears grossly intact. Rest of the surrounding muscles, tendons and neurovascular structures are grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Severe multiligamentous knee injury following traumatic knee dislocation.

Acute complete proximal ACL tear as detailed.

Acute high-grade partial femoral attachment tear of PCL.

Complete posterolateral corner disruption with fibular head (arcuate sign) avulsion fracture involving LCL/ biceps tendon insertion.

Near-complete tear of femoral attachment of medial patellar retinaculum and grade II proximal MCL tear and lateral patellar retinacula injury.

Small medial and lateral meniscal tears with associated meniscocapsular sprain.

Osteochondral injury involving medial femoral condyle and proximal tibia/ fibula with displaced trochlear chondral fragment measuring 9 × 9 × 2 mm.

Moderate hemarthrosis with posterior capsular disruption.

Mild posterior tibial subluxation, grade I-II myofascial injuries and extensive periarticular soft tissue edema and hemolymphatic fluid collection.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr M Arun

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT ANKLE

Clinical profile: Known h/o inflammatory arthropathy on treatment for past 4 years. Stopped treatment for past 1year. Right ankle pain and swelling for past few months. No h/o recent injury. 

Technique: PD fs in all 3 planes, T1 and IR sag, T1, T2,IR, DWI, GRE axial, PC T1 in all planes and CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Acute trabecular insufficiency fractures are seen in anterior aspect of talus, navicular bone, medial cuneiform and cuboid with extensive marrow edema.

A subchondral cyst measuring about 10 x 7 x 4 mm (AP x CC x TRA) is seen in posteromedial aspect of talar dome with mild marrow edema. Increased signal intensity of overlying articular cartilage is seen. No separation/ displacement of bony fragment are seen. Features are suggestive of osteochondral lesion of talus (OLT) stage IIA.

Diffuse osteopenia with osteoarthrosis changes are seen in midtarsal bones and articulations.

Minimal joint fluid with synovitis is seen in ankle and subtalar joints. Diffuse synovitis is also seen in almost all midfoot articulations.

Rest of the bones and joints appear grossly normal for age.  

Ligament complex:

Medial and lateral ligament complexes appear intact. No significant tear is seen.

Rest of the visualised ligaments appear grossly normal. 

Tendons and rest of soft tissue:

Mild tenosynovitis of tibialis posterior, flexor digitorum and flexor hallucis tendons is seen.

The anterior and medial tendons appear normal. Peroneal and flexor retinaculum is intact.

Sinus tarsi inflammation is seen. Mild periarticular soft tissue inflammation is seen in midfoot region, predominantly along the dorsal aspect.

Diffuse subcutaneous edema is seen in dorsum of foot, medial and lateral aspects of ankle joint region, more in medial aspect. No abnormal fluid collection is seen.

IMPRESSION:

Acute trabecular insufficiency fractures in talus, navicular bone, medial cuneiform and cuboid with extensive marrow edema as detailed.

Osteochondral lesion of talus (IIA) as detailed.

Diffuse osteopenia of bones, osteoarthrosis and diffuse synovitis in midfoot region with mild periarticular soft tissue changes as detailed.

Mild flexor tenosynovitis and sinus tarsi inflammation as detailed.

Diffuse subcutaneous edema in foot and ankle regions as detailed.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
MRI SCAN OF RIGHT THIGH AND SCREENING OF HIP AND KNEE JOINTS

Clinical profile: C/o acute onset of right thigh pain for 5 days.  H/o fever with chills and rigor for 1 day? Right thigh cellulitis.

Technique: IR, TI, T2, DWI, GRE and PC T1 in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

The visualized right femur demonstrates normal marrow signal intensity without focal marrow edema, cortical destruction or periosteal reaction.

No focal osseous lesion or stress-related injury is identified.

Right hip joint is grossly unremarkable without significant joint effusion or synovitis.

Minimal right knee joint effusion is seen with mild smooth reactive synovitis. No abnormal marrow changes, periarticular collection or other MRI features to suggest septic arthritis.

No evidence of acute osteomyelitis or septic arthritis.

Soft tissue:

Right thigh region:

Diffuse extensive inflammatory edema and enhancement involving skin and subcutaneous tissues is seen along the medial aspect of mid and distal right thigh, consistent with acute cellulitis.

There is associated extensive inflammatory edema and enhancement tracking along the posteromedial and posterolateral intermuscular fascial planes of the distal thigh and extending into the popliteal fossa.

Within the posteromedial distal thigh, there is an ill-defined thin rim-enhancing fluid collection with restricted diffusion, extending in a sheet-like fashion along intermuscular fascial plane, measuring approximately 10.0 × 3.2 × 0.5 cm (CC × TR × AP). It is located between the posterior aspect of vastus medialis anteriorly, medial aspects of sartorius and gracilis, and anterior aspects of semimembranosus and semitendinosus muscles.

The collection is consistent with an infected intermuscular fluid collection / abscess.

There is associated edema and post-contrast enhancement involving the adjacent portions of the vastus medialis, vastus lateralis, sartorius, adductor magnus, biceps femoris and adjacent thigh musculature, consistent with acute infective myositis/ pyomyositis.

No significant intramuscular abscess or definite myonecrosis is identified.

No soft-tissue gas/air pockets are seen. No sinus tract or extension to the underlying bone or hip/knee joints is identified.

The remaining visualized muscles, tendons and fascial structures are grossly preserved.

Neurovascular structures:

The visualized superficial femoral and popliteal arteries and veins are grossly patent on the limited Doppler correlation.

No significant abnormality of the adjacent neurovascular structures is identified.

IMPRESSION:

Features of acute infective fasciitis involving medial aspect of distal right thigh, with associated thin rim-enhancing infected fluid collection and extensive inflammatory edema tracking along adjacent intermuscular fascial planes, as detailed above.

Acute cellulitis involving medial aspect of right mid/ distal thigh regions as detailed.

Associated acute infective myositis involving adjacent thigh muscles as detailed. No significant myonecrosis or intramuscular abscess.

No imaging features of acute osteomyelitis / septic arthritis.

Minimal right knee joint effusion with mild smooth reactive synovitis.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Lungs and pleura:

Chronic post-surgical changes consistent with right lower lobectomy are seen with mild reduction in right hemi thoracic lung volume.

No focal consolidation, nodule or mass lesion seen.

No pleural effusion or pneumothorax seen.

Mediastinum;

Mediastinal structures appear grossly normal. No significant abnormality seen.

Asymmetrical atrophy involving inferior fibers of right latissimus dorsi, serratus anterior and intercostal muscles are seen at and below the thoracotomy site as compared to left side.

Small focal defect is seen in latissimus dorsi muscle at incision site with proximal retracted fibers. No other significant focal lesion or abnormality seen.

No imaging features of acute or chronic muscle denervation seen.

Rest of the soft tissue appears normal. No inflammation or collection is seen.

Chronic post-operative remodeling of right thoracic cage and ribs is seen.

Status post right lower lobectomy changes in right hemithorax as detailed.

Localized mild atrophy of right latissimus dorsi, serratus anterior and intercostal muscles with small muscle defect at and below thoracotomy level as detailed, likely represent chronic post thoracotomy muscular injury and disuse.

Dr M Arun

CT OF RIGHT ANKLE

Clinical profile: A/h/o RTA

Acute undisplaced oblique fracture of distal fibula is seen in the trans syndesmotic region. Small undisplaced avulsion fracture is seen in anterolateral aspect of distal tibia at insertion of AITFL. Avulsion fracture of medial malleolus is seen with mild displacement (Weber B stage 4).

Small undisplaced chip avulsion fracture is seen in posterolateral aspect of talus.

Mild comminuted fracture is seen in medial cuneiform bone.

No lytic areas or lesion is seen. No intra articular fragments or abnormal widening of ankle joint or distal syndesmosis is seen in the present study.

Mild adjacent soft tissue contusion/ edema are seen. No soft tissue loss is seen.

Mild osteoarthrosis changes are seen in ankle and few joints in visualized foot region.

Rest of the visualized bones and joints appear grossly normal for age.

IMPRESSION:

Acute fractures in distal tibia and fibula as detailed.

Small acute fractures in talus and medial cuneiform bones as detailed.

Mild adjacent soft tissue contusion/ edema as mentioned.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

CT OF RIGHT WRIST

Clinical profile: H/o RTA.

Acute comminuted fracture of the distal radius is seen, predominantly involving the metaphyseal/ epimetaphyseal region, with extension into radiocarpal and distal radioulnar articular surfaces.

Mild volar displacement of distal fracture fragment is noted. No significant gross articular incongruity is identified.

A linear undisplaced fracture is suspected involving the distal ulna, without significant cortical step-off, angulation or displacement.

The distal radioulnar joint alignment is maintained.

Radiocarpal alignment is maintained. No perilunate dislocation or other carpal dislocation is identified.

Mild widening of the scapholunate interval is noted. The lunotriquetral interval is maintained.

The remaining visualized carpal and metacarpal bones demonstrate preserved cortical integrity and trabecular architecture without definite acute fracture.

Mild periarticular soft-tissue swelling, edema and contusion are seen around the wrist, predominantly adjacent to the fracture site. No significant soft-tissue defect is identified.

IMPRESSION:

Acute comminuted mildly displaced intra-articular fracture of distal radius with extensions as detailed.

Suspected linear undisplaced fracture of distal ulna as detailed.

Mild widening of scapholunate interval, suspicious for ligament injury.

Soft tissue contusion and edema as mentioned.
