reports.fullText:
Dr. Varuna.

CT OF RIGHT WRIST

Clinical Profile: Alleged H/o trauma, right distal radius and right distal femur fractures.

Acute extensively comminuted displaced intra-articular fracture involving distal radius, with multiple fracture lines extending into radiocarpal and distal radioulnar articular surfaces. Associated impaction and metaphyseal comminution are present.

Mildly displaced avulsion fracture of the ulnar styloid process is seen.

Small well-corticated ossific fragment along the dorsal aspect of the Scaphoid, favouring an accessory ossicle or remote healed avulsion fragment. No adjacent donor site or acute fracture line is identified.

Carpal bones are otherwise intact with maintained overall carpal alignment. No additional acute fracture or dislocation is identified.

Distal radioulnar joint alignment is maintained.

Diffuse soft tissue swelling and contusion involving the wrist and distal forearm.

No soft tissue emphysema, radiopaque foreign body or significant soft tissue loss.

IMPRESSION:

Acute extensively comminuted displaced intra-articular fracture of distal radius with extension to radiocarpal and distal radioulnar articular surfaces.

Mildly displaced avulsion fracture of ulnar styloid process.

Small well-corticated ossific fragment dorsal to scaphoid, likely accessory ossicle or chronic healed avulsion fragment. No CT evidence of an acute scaphoid fracture.

Diffuse periarticular soft tissue swelling about the wrist and distal forearm.

reports.fullText:
Dr. Thamaraikkannan

MRI OF LUMBOSACRAL SPINE AND SCREENING OF REST OF SPINE

Clinical Profile: C/o right lower limb pain? Sciatica.

Technique: Sagittal T1, T2, IR, Axial T2, IR/ T1 Coronal for SI joints

Screening of rest of spine: T2 sagittal.

The lumbosacral spine displays a normal lordotic curvature and vertebral column alignment.

The individual vertebrae are grossly normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities.

Disc desiccation is seen at all levels with reduced disc height and Modic type II endplate changes at L5-S1 level. Facetal arthropathy is seen at few levels. Rest of the intervertebral discs appear normal in heights. Rest of the vertebral end-plates are normal.

D12-L1 and L1-2: No significant abnormality seen.

L2-3: Disc bulge with right paracentral protrusion are seen causing anterior thecal sac indentation and partial effacement of lateral recess. No significant mass effect over nerve roots.

L3-4: Diffuse disc bulge, flaval thickening and facetal arthropathy are seen causing partial effacement of lateral recess. No significant mass effect over nerve roots.

L4-5: Diffuse disc bulge, right paracentral disc extrusion with inferior migration, facetal and flaval hypertrophy are seen causing spinal canal stenosis and compression of bilateral traversing L5 nerve roots (R>L). Residual thecal sac measures 5 mm in midsagittal dimension. The extruded disc measures 10 x 6 x 4 mm and is seen in sub membranous position.

L5-S1: Diffuse disc bulge, flaval thickening and facetal arthropathy are seen causing effacement of lateral recess and indentation of bilateral traversing S1 nerve roots.

The conus medullaris ends at L1 level and the cauda equine is normal in appearance.

The prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues are normal.

Both SI joints appear grossly normal in joint space and signal intensities for age.

Screening of cervical spine:

Mild loss of cervical lordosis is seen with disc desiccation at all levels, uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy and reduced disc heights at few levels.

Disc bulge and uncovertebral arthropathy causing mild indentation of cord and exiting nerve roots is seen from C4-5 to C6-7 levels. No abnormal cord signal intensity is seen.

No other significant abnormalities are seen.

Screening of dorsal spine:

Disc desiccation is seen at all levels and ligamentum flavum thickening and small disc protrusions at few levels. Spinal cord appears normal.

No other significant abnormalities are seen.

IMPRESSION:

Diffuse degenerative changes of spine as detailed.

Disc bulge with extrusion, facetal arthropathy and flaval thickening causing canal stenosis and compression of L5 nerve roots (R>L) at L4-5 level as detailed.

Disc bulge, flaval thickening and facetal arthropathy causing indentation of bilateral S1 nerve roots at L5-S1 level as detailed.

Cervical spondylosis as mentioned.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF LEFT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: H/o injury in left shoulder region few months back. For detailed evaluation:

Technique: PD f, T1, IR, T2 and GRE in all planes.

Bones and joints:

Hill-Sachs defect without edema is seen, measuring about 11 x 10 x 3.8 mm (CC x TRA x Depth). No bony Bankart is seen. No edema or acute fracture is seen.

No joint effusion is seen. No intra articular osteochondral fragment is seen.

Rotator cuff:

Mild tendinosis/ resolving strain changes are seen involving supraspinatus tendon with small partial thickness articular surface tear in anterior part. Small intra substance tear is seen in subscapularis tendon. No other significant acute tear or retraction of fibres is seen.

Rest of the muscles and tendons of the rotator cuff appears normal. No atrophy or fatty infiltration is seen.

LHBT is intact. The deltoid muscle is also normal.

Labroligamentous structures:

Soft tissue Bankart lesion is seen with anteroinferior labral tear and adjacent periosteal injury. Extension of tear to anterosuperior, superior, posterosuperior and posteroinferior quadrants is seen. Rest of the glenoid labrum appear grossly intact.

Mild sprain of anterior band of IGHL and adjacent capsule is seen. No complete disruption is seen.

AC joint:

IMPRESSION:

reports.fullText:
MRI SCAN OF RIGHT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: H/o RTA with right anterior shoulder dislocation on 27.03.2026, on conservative treatment. For detailed evaluation.

Technique: PD fs, T1, T2, IR, T2 and GRE in all planes.

Bones and Glenohumeral Joint:

Chronic Hill-Sachs impaction defect is seen involving the posterolateral humeral head measuring approximately 18 × 13 × 9 mm (CC × TR × depth) without significant residual marrow edema, consistent with a chronic lesion.

No osseous Bankart lesion or glenoid rim fracture. No acute fracture or marrow edema.

Mild glenohumeral joint effusion is seen. No intra-articular osteochondral loose body.

Glenohumeral articular cartilage is preserved.

Rotator Cuff:

Resolving strain/ tendinosis of supraspinatus tendon is seen with extensive articular surface partial-thickness tear involving nearly entire tendon width and up to 50% tendon thickness.

Small focal full-thickness perforation of supraspinatus tendon is seen located approximately 7 mm proximal to its footprint, measuring 3.5 mm in AP dimension.

Mild subscapularis tendinosis with small chronic articular surface and intrasubstance partial-thickness tears is seen. Mild infraspinatus tendinosis without tear is seen.

Teres minor tendon is intact. No rotator cuff muscle atrophy or fatty infiltration.

Long head of the biceps tendon is intact and normally located within the bicipital groove.

Deltoid muscle is unremarkable.

Labroligamentous Complex:

Soft tissue Bankart lesion involving the anteroinferior labrum with adjacent periosteal stripping is seen. Labral tear extends from anteroinferior labrum into anterosuperior, superior and inferior quadrants.

Mild sprain of the biceps pulley, anterior band of inferior glenohumeral ligament (IGHL), and adjacent anterior capsule is seen without complete disruption.

Mild synovial/ capsular thickening involving rotator interval and axillary recess is seen, suggestive of mild post-traumatic adhesive capsulitis/ capsulitis.

Acromioclavicular Joint and Outlet:

Mild AC joint arthropathy is seen. The acromion is of type II morphology and is laterally sloping. Reduced subacromial space is seen (4 mm). Mild subacromial bursitis is seen.

Remaining visualized muscles and neurovascular structures are unremarkable.

Rest of the soft tissue appear grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Sequelae of previous anterior shoulder dislocation with chronic Hill-Sachs lesion and soft tissue Bankart lesion. No associated osseous Bankart lesion.

Supraspinatus tendinosis with articular surface partial-thickness tear and small focal full-thickness perforation as detailed.

Mild subscapularis and infraspinatus tendinosis with small chronic tears.

Mild joint effusion with capsulitis, labral tear and capsuloligamentous changes as detailed.

Mild AC joint arthropathy with features of subacromial impingement.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF  RIGHT KNEE JOINT

Clinical profile: K/c/o bilateral osteochondritis dissecans of the knee joints (L > R) with intra-articular loose bodies in the left knee. H/o arthroscopic chondroplasty of the left knee joint. C/o right knee pain and locking for the past few months.

Technique: PDfs, T1, T2, IR and GRE in all planes.

Bones and joints:

An osteochondral lesion is seen along the lateral aspect of the medial femoral condyle, measuring approximately 1.8 × 1.2 × 0.5 cm (AP × TRA x thickness). The lesion demonstrates irregularity of the overlying articular cartilage with underlying subchondral marrow signal alteration and mild adjacent marrow edema. Few tiny subchondral cystic changes are seen at the lesion/ donor bed.

No definite fluid-filled cleft, displacement or separation of the osteochondral fragment is identified. No definite intra-articular osteochondral loose body is seen.

Based on MRI features, the lesion is compatible with an osteochondritis dissecans lesion, currently appearing stable.

Minimal knee joint effusion is seen.

Rest of the articular surfaces are maintained. Alignment is preserved. No other focal osteochondral lesion is identified.

Rest of the visualized osseous structures demonstrate preserved marrow signal.

Meniscus:

The medial and lateral menisci are normal in configuration and signal intensities.

No acute tear or displaced fragment seen.

Ligaments:

The medial and lateral collateral ligaments and patellar retinaculum appear intact.

The anterior cruciate and posterior cruciate ligaments appear intact. The intermeniscal and meniscofemoral ligaments are also normal.

Posterolateral and posteromedial corner ligament complex appear normal.

Rest of soft tissues:

No fluid collection is seen. The extensor mechanism appears normal. The surrounding muscles, tendons and neurovascular structures are normal.

IMPRESSION:

Osteochondritis dissecans lesion involving lateral aspect of medial femoral condyle as detailed. No MRI evidence of displaced fragment / intra-articular loose body.

Minimal knee joint effusion.

No other significant abnormality seen.

Suggested clinical correlation and review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr Akila

MRI SCAN OF LEFT KNEE JOINT AND PROXIMAL LEG REGION

Clinical profile: C/o pain in left knee region and swelling in anterior aspect of proximal leg region for past few months. No h/o injury/ fever.

Technique: PD fs, IR, T2, T1, GRE and DWI in all planes for knee and proximal leg regions.

Bones and joints:

Mild genu varum deformity is seen.

Medial and patellofemoral joint predominant severe osteoarthrosis is seen with partial to full thickness articular cartilage loss, subchondral edema and prominent large osteophytes. Full thickness cartilage loss is seen in medial joint and in patella.

Mild joint effusion is seen with reactive synovitis and suprapatellar plica.

Mild stress related marrow changes are seen in proximal tibia. Rest of the articulating bones appear grossly normal for age.

Meniscus:

Chronic tears with grossly attenuated medial meniscus are seen. Degenerative changes with chronic oblique tear are seen in anterior root/ horn of lateral meniscus.

Ligaments:

ACL is not normally seen, likely chronic tear with attenuated fibres. Degenerative changes of posterior cruciate ligament are seen. No significant tear or waviness is seen.

The medial and lateral collateral ligaments and patellar retinaculum appear grossly intact with significant degenerative changes.

Posterolateral and posteromedial corner ligament complexes appear grossly intact.

Rest of soft tissues:

Significant degenerative arthrosis of proximal tibiofibular joint is seen with few small proximal tibiofibular joint ganglion cysts, largest measuring about 1.5 x 1.2 cm.

Large multilobulated ganglion cyst measuring about 15 x 4.2 x 1.6 cm (CC x TRA x AP) is seen arising from posterolateral aspect of knee joint region at joint level and extending along the posterior aspect of proximal tibia, and then wrapping around the medial and then to anterior aspects of proximal tibia. The cystic lesion is closely abutting the cortex along the medial and anterior aspects. No adjacent bone changes are seen. No restricted diffusion is seen in the cystic lesion. Features are consistent with ganglion cyst.

No fluid collection is seen. The extensor mechanism appears grossly intact. Rest of the surrounding muscles, tendons and neurovascular structures are grossly normal.

IMPRESSION

Severe left knee osteoarthrosis with joint effusion and genu varum as detailed.

Chronic ACL tear and degenerative changes of PCL as mentioned.

Degenerative meniscal tears and grossly attenuated medial meniscus as detailed.

Osteoarthrosis of proximal tibiofibular joint with few ganglion cysts as detailed.

Large multiloculated ganglion cyst from posterior aspect of knee joint extending to medial and anterior aspects of proximal tibia as detailed.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

CT OF RIGHT KNEE

Clinical details: S/p right TKR (2 months back) with recurrent patellar dislocation, to assess alignment of implants

Technique: Non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) of the right knee was performed with multiplanar reconstructions.

(Suboptimal evaluation due to metallic artifacts).

Total knee prosthesis is seen insitu with normal alignment of tibial and femoral component. No periprosthetic loosening of tibial or femoral component is seen.

The angle between surgical transepicondylar axis (sTEA) and posterior condylar line of the implant was measured. The angle between these 2 lines (Femoral component rotation) measures about 3 degrees of external rotation (optimal range is 2° to 5° of external rotation).

The angle between tibial tubercle axis and implant axis was measured. The tibial component rotation measures 17 degrees of internal rotation relative to the tip of the tibial tuberosity. (Normally around 18 degrees of internal rotation).

Avulsion fracture of medial margin of patella is seen. Patella lies laterally with lateral tilt and loss of contact with the prosthetic trochlear surface.

Rest of the visualised bones appears normal for age.

Rest of the visualised soft tissue appears grossly normal for age.

IMPRESSION:

Features of lateral patellar dislocation with avulsion fracture of medial margin.

TKR prosthesis insitu with grossly normal alignment.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr. Aathithya

MRI SCAN OF BILATERAL LOWER LIMBS

Clinical profile: Walking difficulty for 2 years? Myopathy? Myositis? Dystrophy.  CPK levels are raised. NCS- bilateral peroneal axonopathy.

Technique: IR coronal/ axial, T2, T1, IR axial for lower limbs, DWI, 3D IR coronal for lumbar plexus,

Bilateral lower limbs:

Soft tissue:

Diffuse symmetric muscle atrophy with fatty replacement is seen involving both thigh and leg regions. Posterior compartment and adductor group of muscles show the most severe involvement. Anterior thigh muscles show mild to moderate fatty changes.

Mild to moderate involvement of calf muscles and peroneal muscles is seen. Relative sparing of anterior compartment muscles is seen in leg regions.

Pelvic and gluteal muscles appear grossly preserved.

Mild T2/ IR hyperintensity is seen in the involved muscles, suggestive of acute denervation/ ongoing myopathy changes.

Mild subcutaneous edema is seen in distal leg and ankle regions. Rest of the subcutaneous fat, fascia and skin appear normal.

No intramuscular fluid collection or mass seen.

Visualised peripheral nerves appear normal in signal and caliber.

Vascular structures appear grossly normal.

Bones and joints:

The visualised bones and appear grossly normal for age.

No other significant abnormality seen in the visualised structures.

Lumbosacral plexus:

The visualised lumbosacral plexus appear grossly normal on both sides.

No other significant abnormality or mass lesion is seen.

Bilateral sciatic, tibial and peroneal nerves appear grossly normal in thickness, signal intensity and course. No other significant compression or mass effect over the nerve roots seen in the present study.

IMPRESSION:

Bilateral symmetric muscle atrophy with fatty changes and mild active denervation changes in bilateral lower limbs, predominantly affecting hamstrings, and adductor and calf muscles and with relative sparing of pelvic and gluteal muscles.

No other significant abnormality seen.

In view of clinical and imaging features, the possibility of chronic neurogenic myopathy pattern, like lower motor neuron disease (MND/ SMA spectrum) is more likely than other inflammatory myopathy/ muscular dystrophy.

Suggested clinical and EMG correlation/ review as indicated.

Dr Sathishmani

MRI OF LUMBOSACRAL SPINE AND SCREENING OF REST OF THE SPINE

Clinical Profile: H/o arthritis, Difficulty in walking, stiffness of upper and lower limb during waking up for 20 days, Pain in left side of the body, Hypermobility of joints, ?spondyloarthritis, H/o pain in lumbosacral area (left lumbar area).

Technique: Sagittal, T1, T2, IR, Axial T2, T1 and IR Coronal for SI joints, Screening of rest of the spine – T2 sagittal, IR sagittal, CT whole spine correlation.

The lumbosacral spine displays a normal lordotic curvature and vertebral column alignment.

Anterior vertebral corner signal changes with focal fat deposition and IR hyper intensities are seen at multiple dorsolumbar vertebrae and few cervical vertebral levels, suggestive of acute on chronic inflammation. Acute inflammation is also seen involving bilateral costo transverse and costovertebral articulation at few levels. No significant endplate changes are seen. No significant facet joint fusion is seen.

reports.fullText:
Dr Pragadesh

MRI SCAN OF LEFT WRIST JOINT

Clinical profile: H/o injury to left wrist region about 4 months back followed by swelling and pain. H/o of watery discharge since 07.09.2026 from the ulnar aspect of distal forearm.

Technique: T1, PDfs, IR, T2, DWI, GRE and PC T1 in all planes. CT correlation.

Osseous structures:

Irregular destruction of lunate is seen with extensive cortical irregularity and near complete loss of its normal osseous architecture. The lunate demonstrates abnormal marrow signal intensity with corresponding post-contrast enhancement.

Similar abnormal marrow signal intensity and enhancement with partial osseous destruction and articular cortical erosions are seen involving the adjacent scaphoid, triquetrum, trapezoid, capitate and hamate.

Features are consistent with active infective osteomyelitis involving multiple carpal bones, with predominant involvement and destruction of the lunate.

There are also articular surface erosions and abnormal marrow signal intensity with post-contrast enhancement involving the distal articular portion of the radius, consistent with secondary osteomyelitis involvement.

No definite pathological fracture is identified on the provided sequences.

Subtle edema is seen in distal ulna. Rest of the visualised bones and joints appear grossly intact.

Joints and synovium:

Diffuse synovial thickening and synovial enhancement is seen involving radiocarpal and ulnocarpal joints. Mild associated joint effusion is seen within wrist joint. Multiple articular erosions involving the carpal bones and distal radius are noted.

Features are consistent with infective/ septic arthritis of wrist region. There is associated inflammatory involvement of the surrounding joint capsule and capsuloligamentous structures.

Sinus tract / soft tissues:

A small enhancing sinus tract is seen arising from the region of the infected radiocarpal joint and the destroyed lunate.

The tract extends along the volar aspect of the wrist into the distal forearm, coursing between the pronator quadratus muscle deep to it and the flexor digitorum superficialis and flexor digitorum profundus tendons superficially.

It subsequently courses toward the ulnar aspect of the distal forearm, where it reaches and communicates with the skin/ subcutaneous tissues, corresponding to the clinically described site of discharge.

There is significant surrounding inflammatory soft-tissue signal and enhancement along the course of this sinus tract.

A second smaller blind-ending enhancing tract extends from the previous described tract in the distal forearm toward the radial aspect. This tract does not demonstrate definite communication with the skin surface.

There is associated diffuse inflammatory edema and enhancement of the adjacent subcutaneous soft tissues and fascial planes, compatible with surrounding cellulitis/ inflammatory phlegmon change.

No definite well-defined drainable soft-tissue abscess is identified.

Tendons:

The flexor digitorum superficialis and profundus tendons are displaced/closely related to the sinus tract along the volar distal forearm.

There is surrounding inflammatory change along the adjacent tendon sheaths. No definite tendon discontinuity is identified.

The extensor tendons are grossly maintained.

Ligaments/ capsule:

Diffuse inflammatory changes and enhancement involve the wrist capsule and surrounding intrinsic/ extrinsic ligamentous structures, in keeping with the adjacent infective inflammatory process.

Neurovascular structures:

The visualized major neurovascular structures are maintained. No definite vascular thrombosis is identified on the MRI sequences.

IMPRESSION:

Extensive destructive osteomyelitis involving multiple carpal bones, predominantly involving lunate bone as detailed.

Infective/ septic arthritis of wrist joint with synovitis, joint effusion and associated articular erosions.

Mild secondary osteomyelitis of distal radius, involving articular portion.

Enhancing draining sinus tract arising from wrist joint, extending along volar distal forearm and communicating with skin at ulnar aspect of distal forearm.

Extensive surrounding capsuloligamentous and soft tissue inflammation and along adjacent fascial planes and flexor tendon sheaths.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
MRI SCAN OF LEFT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: C/o recurrent left anterior shoulder dislocation. Two episodes of dislocation following surgery, the latest approximately one month ago. Status post mini-open Latarjet procedure in March 2023. Previous history of bilateral recurrent shoulder dislocations associated with seizures.

Technique: PDfs, T1, T2, GRE, T2fs in all planes and CT correlation.

Limitations:

Suboptimal evaluation of the anteroinferior glenoid, Latarjet graft and adjacent capsulolabral structures due to susceptibility/ metallic artifacts from fixation screws.

Glenohumeral alignment and osseous structures:

Glenohumeral alignment is currently maintained. No current subluxation or dislocation.

No acute fracture or marrow-replacing lesion.

Large Hill-Sachs impaction defect is seen involving the posterolateral humeral head, measuring approximately 34 × 32.8 × 15 mm (TRA x CC x Depth). Associated marrow edema is present, suggestive of recent/ recurrent impaction injury.

No significant glenohumeral joint effusion or definite intra-articular loose body.

Post-Latarjet changes:

Chronic postsurgical changes of prior Latarjet coracoid bone-block reconstruction of the anteroinferior glenoid are seen.

The transferred coracoid bone graft is seen incorporated along anteroinferior glenoid rim. The graft measures approximately 6.3 mm in AP thickness and 17.3 mm in craniocaudal extent. There is complete osseous union of the graft with the native glenoid, without significant graft osteolysis or resorption.

The graft is positioned flush with the native glenoid articular surface and appropriately extends along the anteroinferior glenoid rim. No graft fracture, migration or significant malposition is evident.

Two fixation screws traverse the graft. No definite periscrew lucency, hardware loosening, breakage or migration. No definite intra-articular screw penetration.

Glenoid and glenoid track assessment:

The reconstructed glenoid, including the coracoid bone graft, measures approximately 32 mm in AP diameter. No significant residual glenoid osseous deficiency is identified.

Despite satisfactory incorporation and positioning of Latarjet bone graft with no significant residual anterior glenoid bone loss, the large posterolateral Hill-Sachs defect extends beyond the reconstructed glenoid track suggestive of off track lesion.

Labrum and capsuloligamentous structures:

Chronic tearing is seen involving anterosuperior, superior and posterosuperior labral quadrants, with diffuse labral attenuation.

The anteroinferior labrum is sub optimally visualized because of metallic susceptibility artifact; however, no definite displaced labral fragment is identified on the available sequences.

Chronic postoperative scarring/ sprain and attenuation of anterior capsuloligamentous structures are seen. No definite HAGL lesion identified on the available images.

Rotator cuff:

Mild supraspinatus, infraspinatus, subscapularis tendinosis is seen. No significant tear is seen.  Teres minor tendons are intact without significant tendinosis or tear.

The subscapularis shows postoperative scarring. No significant tear is seen. No significant rotator cuff muscle atrophy or fatty infiltration is seen.

LHBT appears intact. Deltoid muscle appears normal.

AC joint:

AC joint appears grossly normal. The acromion is of type II morphology. The subacromial space is normal. Rest of the soft tissue appears normal.

IMPRESSION:

Status post Latarjet procedure and complete osseous union of graft with native anteroinferior glenoid as detailed. No significant glenoid bone loss.

Large Hill-Sachs impaction defect with marrow edema indicating recent/ recurrent impaction.

Off-track Hill-Sachs lesion relative to reconstructed glenoid track as detailed.

Chronic sprain/ scarring of anterior capsuloligamentous structures with chronic labral tears as detailed.

Mild rotator cuff tendinosis without significant rotator cuff tear.

MRI SCAN OF LUMBOSACRAL SPINE AND SCREENING OF REST OF SPINE

Clinical profile: C/o lower back pain for 3 years, aggravated after lifting weight for past few days, tenderness at lumbar spine--L4-L5 spondylo listhesis.

Technique: Sagittal, T1, T2, IR, Axial T2, IR/ T1 Coronal for SI joints

Screening of rest of the spine: T2 sagittal

Bilateral chronic L5 spondylolysis is seen with grade I/ II anterolisthesis of L5 over S1 vertebra.

Advanced degenerative endplate changes are seen at L5-S1 level, with mixed Modic type I and type III changes, associated with prominent endplate sclerosis and marrow edema involving opposing L5 and S1 vertebral endplates.

There is marked reduction of L5-S1 disc height, with disc desiccation, annular fissuring and small intradiscal vacuum foci.

Mild adjacent prevertebral and paravertebral soft-tissue edema is present. No paravertebral or epidural collection, cortical/ endplate destructive change or abnormal diffusion restriction is identified. The overall appearance favours advanced degenerative disc/ endplate disease rather than infective spondylodiscitis.

Rest of the individual vertebrae is normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities. Small vertebral body hemangioma is seen at L2 level.

Disc dedication and facetal arthropathy are seen at few levels. Rest of the intervertebral discs is normal in heights and hydration. Rest of the vertebral end-plates is normal.

D12-L1 to L3-4: No significant disc bulge or mass effect over nerve roots seen.

L4-5: Mild disc bulge and facetal arthropathy are seen. No significant mass effect over nerve roots seen.

L5-S1: L5-S1 anterolisthesis, uncovered disc and facetal/ flaval hypertrophy are seen causing severe foraminal stenosis, impingement of bilateral exiting L5 nerve roots and mild indentation of bilateral traversing S1 nerve roots. Residual thecal sac measures 10 mm in midsagittal dimension.

The conus medullaris ends at L1-2 level and the cauda equine is normal in appearance.

Rest of the prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues is normal.

Both SI joints show mild degenerative changes.

Screening of cervical spine:

Straightening of cervical spine is seen with disc desiccation at all levels. Disc bulge and uncovertebral arthropathy are seen at multiple levels.

Disc bulge with endplate changes and uncovertebral arthropathy are seen at C6-7 level causing anterior thecal sac indentation with mass effect on right exiting C7 nerve root. No significant mass effect on spinal cord is seen.

Spinal cord appears normal. No other significant abnormality seen.

Screening of dorsal spine:

Small vertebral body haemangiomas is seen at D10 level.

Disc desiccation is seen at few levels and endplate changes at D9-10 level.

Spinal cord appears normal. No other significant abnormalities are seen.

IMPRESSION:

Chronic bilateral L5 spondylolysis with grade I/ II L5-S1 anterolisthesis.

Advanced L5-S1 degenerative disc disease with marked disc-space narrowing, adjacent vertebral marrow changes and mild soft tissue edema as detailed.

Uncovered disc and facetal/ flaval hypertrophy causing impingement of bilateral L5 nerve roots and indentation of S1 nerve roots at L5-S1 level as detailed.

Mild cervical spondylosis as mentioned.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI OF LUMBOSACRAL SPINE AND SCREENING OF REST OF THE SPINE

Clinical Profile: ALK + NSCLC, on crizotinib since May 2021. Now with c/o low back pain for past few years, more significant for past few months. No h/o fever.

Technique: Sagittal, T1, T2, IR, Axial T2, T1 and IR Coronal for SI joints

Screening of rest of the spine: T2 sagittal.

L3-4 level:

There is bilateral chronic L3 pars interarticularis spondylolysis with associated Grade II anterolisthesis of L3 over L4.

There are advanced degenerative disco vertebral/ endplate changes at L3–4, characterized by marked disc-space narrowing, disc desiccation, annular fissuring and mixed Modic type I and type III endplate changes. Prominent subchondral sclerosis, subarticular cystic changes and extensive opposing vertebral endplate marrow edema are noted involving the L3 and L4 vertebral bodies.

Small intradiscal vacuum foci with minimal fluid signal are noted within the markedly degenerated L3–4 disc. Mild chronic periosteal/ reactive osseous changes are also seen.

There is no convincing cortical/ endplate destruction, aggressive osseous lesion or abnormal marrow replacement at this level. No abnormal paravertebral or epidural collection is identified.

Minimal fluid signal is seen within the anterior epidural space and interspinous soft tissues at L3–4, without associated restricted diffusion. Mild adjacent prevertebral and paravertebral soft-tissue edema is present.

The overall appearance favours advanced degenerative disc/ endplate disease rather than infective spondylodiscitis.

Rest of lumbar spine:

Bilateral chronic spondylosis of L5 vertebra is seen without significant anterolisthesis.

Rest of the individual vertebrae are normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities.

Disc desiccation and facetal arthropathy are seen at few levels with grossly reduced disc height and endplate changes at L3-4 level. Rest of the intervertebral discs are normal in heights. Rest of the vertebral end-plates are grossly normal.

D12-L1 to L2-3: No significant abnormality is seen.

L3-4:

Grade II anterolisthesis of L3 over L4 with an uncovered and markedly degenerated disc. Associated severe bilateral facet arthropathy and ligamentum flavum hypertrophy is seen.

A small well-defined cystic fluid-signal focus measuring approximately 9 × 8 × 6 mm is seen in the right anterior epidural space, immediately adjacent to the L3–4 disc, without restricted diffusion. This may represent a small degenerative/ discal cystic focus; no definite associated epidural abscess is identified.

The above changes result in severe secondary central spinal canal stenosis, with marked crowding/ indentation of the cauda equina nerve roots. The residual thecal sac measures approximately 8.4 × 8.4 mm (AP × transverse).

There is bilateral lateral recess narrowing with impingement of the traversing L4 nerve roots and bilateral neural foraminal narrowing with impingement of the exiting L3 nerve roots.

L4-5 and L5-S1: Mild diffuse disc bulge and facetal arthropathy are seen causing effacement of lateral recess. No significant mass effect over nerve roots seen.

The conus medullaris ends at L1 level and the cauda equina is normal in appearance.

Rest of the prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues are grossly normal.

Both SI joints show mild degenerative changes.

Small uterine fibroids are seen, largest measuring 1 x 1 cm in posterior sub mucosal position.

Subcutaneous edema is seen in the posterior aspect of lumbar region. No fluid collection is seen.

Screening of cervical spine:

Mild disc desiccation and uncovertebral arthropathy are seen at few levels.

Spinal cord appears normal. No other significant abnormality seen.

Screening of dorsal spine:

Mild disc desiccation is seen at few levels. Spinal cord appears normal.

No other significant abnormality seen.

IMPRESSION:

Chronic bilateral L3 and L5 spondylolysis with grade II anterolisthesis at L3-4 level as detailed.

Advanced L3-4 degenerative disc disease with marked disc-space narrowing, adjacent vertebral marrow changes and mild soft tissue edema as detailed.

Severe spinal canal stenosis at L3–4 level causing impingement of bilateral L3 and L4 nerve roots as detailed.

Small right anterior epidural cystic focus at L3–4 level, likely represents a degenerative/ discal cystic focus. No definite epidural abscess.

Degenerative changes in rest of the spine as detailed.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Complete distal syndesmotic disruption with ligament avulsion injuries as detailed.

reports.fullText:
MRI SCAN OF RIGHT ANKLE

Clinical profile: A/h/o slip and fall  on 17.08.2026 and sustained injury to right ankle. Now with c/o pain and swelling. For detailed evaluation of ligaments. 

Technique: PDfs, T T2, GRE and IR in all planes. CT correlation. 

Bones and joints: 

Acute displaced oblique fracture of the distal fibula is seen at the suprasyndesmotic level, with associated surrounding marrow edema.

Widening of the medial joint space is seen with associated disruption of deltoid ligament complex, indicating medial ankle instability.

Distal tibiofibular syndesmotic widening with disruption of the syndesmotic ligament complex is seen, consistent with distal tibiofibular syndesmotic injury.

Small bone contusion is seen in distal tibia. No complete tibiotalar dislocation identified.

Ankle mortise is mildly incongruent secondary to the above injuries.

No focal osteochondral defect of the talar dome is seen.

Subtalar and visualized midfoot joints are maintained.

Ligament complex:

Complete disruption of deltoid ligament complex is seen involving the deep and superficial components, with surrounding soft-tissue edema.

Complete disruption of anterior inferior tibiofibular ligament is seen with near complete disruption of posterior inferior tibiofibular ligament, with associated syndesmotic widening.

Grade I/ II sprain of the anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL) with ligamentous thickening and increased signal, without complete discontinuity.

Mild sprain of the remaining lateral collateral ligament complex, including the Calcaneofibular ligament is seen, without complete disruption.

Posterior talofibular ligament is grossly intact.

Tendons and rest of soft tissue:

Soft tissue contusion and edema is seen in distal leg and ankle regions. Injury of deep fascia is seen in the region of fracture in anterolateral aspect of distal leg region with minimal adjacent hemolymphatic fluid collection.

Strain of extensor and flexor retinacula is seen.

Visualized tendons are intact without significant tear or tenosynovitis. Achilles tendon is intact.

Diffuse subcutaneous and myofascial soft tissue edema is seen in distal leg, ankle and dorsum of foot regions.

Rest of the visualised soft tissue appear grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Acute displaced suprasyndesmotic fracture of distal fibula.

Complete deltoid ligament complex disruption and distal tibiofibular syndesmotic ligament disruption with syndesmotic and medial joint widening.

Mild Grade I/ II sprain of ATFL and remaining lateral ligament complex, without complete disruption.

Soft tissue injuries and diffuse soft tissue edema as detailed.

Overall imaging features are consistent with an unstable suprasyndesmotic ankle fracture pattern (Weber C), with associated syndesmotic and deltoid ligament disruption. Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Dr M Arun

MRI SCAN OF CERVICAL SPINE AND SCREENING OF REST OF THE SPINE

Clinical Profile: H/o C3, C4 & C5 cervical decompressive laminectomy for OPLL done on 01.4.24. C/o right hand on and off numbness x 3 months.

Technique: Sagittal T1, T2, IR, Axial T2.

Screening of rest of the spine: T2 sagittal

As compared with previous MRI done on 28/ Mar/2024,

Chronic postoperative changes are seen in cervical spine region with post laminectomy changes from C3 to C5 vertebral levels. No abnormal fluid collection is seen. Adequate posterior decompression is seen.

Redemonstration of OPLL is seen in cervical spine region. Redemonstration of inflammatory spondyloarthropathy changes are seen in the spine with ALL and ligamentum flavum ossification.

Loss of cervical lordosis is seen with normal vertebral column alignment.

Rest of the individual vertebrae are normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities. Vertebral body hemangioma is seen at C7 level.

Disc desiccation is seen at all levels and facetal arthropathy at few levels. The intervertebral discs are normal in heights. The vertebral end-plates are normal.

C2-3: OPLL is seen causing mild indentation of cord. No mass effect over exiting nerve roots.

C3-4: Posterior decompression changes are seen. OPLL with facetal arthropathy are seen causing indentation of cord and bilateral ventral C4 nerve roots. Residual thecal sac measures 6 mm in midsagittal dimension.

C4-5: Posterior decompression changes are seen. OPLL with facetal arthropathy are seen causing indentation of cord and bilateral C5 nerve roots. Residual thecal sac measures 7.1 mm in midsagittal dimension.

C5-6: OPLL with right uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy are seen causing indentation of cord and right exiting C6 nerve root. Residual thecal sac measures 7.4 mm in midsagittal dimension.

C6-7 and C7-D1: Mild disc bulge is seen. No significant mass effect over exiting nerve roots seen.

Spinal cord: Significant interval reduction of mass effect over cord and nerve roots is seen. Subtle T2/ IR hyperintensity is seen in the cord at C3-4 level. No abnormal thinning or cystic areas are seen.

Rest of the spinal cord shows normal signal intensity.

Rest of the prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues are grossly normal.

The cranio vertebral junction and atlanto axial joint are normal.

Screening of dorsal spine:

Disc desiccation is seen at almost all levels and ligamentum flavum thickening at multiple levels. Vertebral haemangiomas are seen at few levels, more prominent at D2 and D6 levels. Spinal cord appears normal. 

No other significant abnormalities are seen in dorsal spine.

Screening of lumbar spine:

The conus medullaris ends at L1 level and the cauda equine is normal in appearance.

Disc desiccation, disc bulge and facetal/ flaval hypertrophy are seen at multiple levels and disc protrusion at L5-S1 level. Spinal canal stenosis and compression of bilateral nerve roots is seen from L3-4 to L5-S1 levels.

No other significant abnormality seen in lumbar spine.

IMPRESSION:

Postoperative changes in cervical spine region with interval reduction in mass effect over spinal cord and neve roots as detailed.

OPLL and arthropathy causing mass effect over cord and nerve roots at few levels as detailed.

Mild compressive myelopathy changes at C3-4 level as detailed.

No other significant interval changes in spine.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr. Mithun

MRI SCAN OF LUMBOSACRAL SPINE AND SCREENING OF REST OF THE SPINE (P+C)

Clinical Profile: K/c/o L5-S1 TB spondylodiscitis with infected fluid collections, on ATT.  Follow up study to assess response. No new complaints.

As compared to previous MRI dated 27/ May/ 2026, present study shows,

Technique: Sagittal, T1, T2, IR, Axial T2, DWI, T1 and IR Coronal for SI joints, post contrast T1 axial. Screening of rest of the spine: T2/ IR sagittal, T1 PC.

Mild loss of lumbar lordosis with normal vertebral column alignment is noted.

Lumbarisation of S1 vertebra is seen.

Persistent abnormal marrow signal intensity and enhancement involving the L5 and S1 vertebral bodies with involvement of the intervening L5-S1 disc is seen, consistent with known spondylodiscitis.

There is mild interval reduction in the size of the infected discovertebral fluid collection at L5-S1, demonstrating central diffusion restriction and a smooth thin enhancing rim. It currently measures approximately 2.9 × 1.9 × 1.5 cm (CC × TR × AP), compared with 4.4 × 2.5 × 1.9 cm previously. There is associated mild interval reduction in the surrounding vertebral marrow edema and enhancement.

Mild interval reduction in the anterior epidural inflammatory tissue and inflammatory changes extending along the bilateral nerve root sheaths. No significant drainable anterior epidural collection is seen on the present study.

Mild interval reduction in the left paravertebral collection along the psoas muscle at L5-S1, currently measuring approximately 2.2 × 0.5 × 0.5 cm (CC × AP × TR), compared with 3.0 × 1.1 × 0.8 cm previously.

There is also mild interval reduction in the small collection anterior to the left psoas muscle.

Significant interval reduction in the prevertebral and anterior paravertebral inflammatory soft-tissue component is noted.

Mild interval reduction in inflammatory changes involving the left iliopsoas muscle, paraspinal muscular fascia and adjacent soft tissues is seen. No new significant fluid collection is identified.

Rest of the vertebrae is normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities.

Rest of the intervertebral discs is normal in heights and hydration. Rest of the vertebral end-plates is normal. Mild facetal arthropathy is seen at few levels.

L1-2 to L3-4 and L5-S1: Mild disc bulge is noted.

The conus medullaris ends at L2 level and the cauda equina is grossly normal in appearance. No abnormal enhancement of cord or cauda equina nerve roots seen.

Both SI joints appear grossly normal in joint space and signal intensities.

Screening of cervical spine:

Mild loss of cervical lordosis is seen with disc desiccation at few levels. Mild chronic posterior wedging few cervical vertebrae is seen.

Disc bulge with right paracentral protrusion and right uncovertebral arthropathy are seen causing indentation of cord and right exiting nerve root at C5-6 level.

Spinal cord appears normal. No other significant abnormality seen.

Screening of dorsal spine:

Spinal cord appears normal. No significant abnormality seen.

IMPRESSION:

Compared with previous MRI dated 27/ May/ 2026, present study shows,

Known L5-S1 tuberculous spondylodiscitis with reduction in size of collections, surrounding marrow inflammatory changes and pre/ paravertebral inflammatory soft-tissue component as detailed.

Interval reduction in L5-S1 discovertebral abscess, left paravertebral and anterior psoas collections, with no new significant collection.

Interval reduction in anterior epidural and bilateral nerve-root sheath inflammatory changes. No significant residual drainable epidural collection.

Residual inflammatory changes involving left iliopsoas, paraspinal fascia and adjacent soft tissues as detailed.

No other significant interval changes in spine.

Overall findings indicate favorable interval response to ATT.  Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF LEFT KNEE JOINT

Clinical profile: C/o left knee pain since 2 months. No h/o recent in injury.

Technique: PDfs, T1, T2, IR and GRE in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Patellofemoral joint predominant severe osteoarthrosis is seen with partial to full thickness articular cartilage loss, chondral fissures, subchondral cysts/ edema and prominent marginal osteophytes. Full thickness cartilage loss is seen in patella.

Mild joint effusion is seen with chronic reactive synovitis, suprapatellar plica and lipoma arborescens. Tiny loose body is seen along the posterior aspect.

Rest of the articulating bones are normal in outline and bone marrow signal intensity characteristics.

Multilolobulated T2/ IR hyperintense ganglion cyst measuring 3.1 x 2 x 0.9 cm is seen arising from femoral attachment site of medial gastrocnemius muscle.

Meniscus:

Degenerative changes seen in medial and lateral menisci.

Chronic oblique tear is seen involving posterior body and posterior horn of medial meniscus. No displaced fragment or extrusion is seen.

Chronic complex tear is seen involving anterior horn/ root and anterior body regions of lateral meniscus. Mild extrusion of lateral meniscus is seen with flipped superior flap fragment into meniscofemoral recess. Mild stress/ inflammatory changes are seen along anterolateral soft tissue.

Rest of the medial and lateral menisci appear grossly normal for age.

Ligaments:

The medial and lateral collateral ligaments and patellar retinaculum appear intact with mild degenerative changes.

Mild degenerative changes are seen in ACL. No significant tear or waviness of fibres seen. The posterior cruciate ligament appears grossly intact.

Posterolateral and posteromedial corner ligament complexes appear grossly intact.

Rest of soft tissues:

Impingement of lateral aspect of Hoffa fad pad is seen with edema.  No fluid collection is seen.

The extensor mechanism appears grossly normal for age. The surrounding muscles, tendons and neurovascular structures are grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Severe left knee osteoarthrosis with joint effusion as detailed.

Degenerative medial and lateral meniscal tears as detailed.

Complex lateral meniscal tear, mild lateral meniscal extrusion and flipped fragment causing mild stress/ inflammatory changes as detailed.

Lateral infrapatellar (Hoffa's) fat-pad impingement with focal edema.

Multiloculated ganglion cyst at femoral attachment of medial gastrocnemius.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Dr Akila

MRI SCAN OF CERVICAL SPINE AND SCREENING OF REST OF SPINE

Clinical profile? Ankylosing spondylitis. C/o neck and back pain x 10 years.

Technique: Sagittal T1, IR and T2, Axial T2. Coronal IR/ T1 for SI joints.

Screening of rest of the spine: T2/ IR sagittal. CT correlation.

Features of extensive chronic inflammatory spondyloarthropathy (ankylosing spondylitis) changes are seen with smooth ligament ossification involving ALL, interspinous and supraspinous ligaments at multiple levels, bony fusion of facet joints, costotransverse and costovertebral articulations at almost all levels and anterior vertebral corners (Romanus) lesions at multiple levels.

No acute fracture or dislocation is seen.

Both SI joints show bony ankylosis with subarticular fat deposition, suggestive of chronic sacroiliitis. No imaging features of acute inflammation seen.

Mild acute inflammation is seen in few facet joints, costo transverse and costovertebral articulations in dorsal and lumbar spine regions. Features are consistent with mild acute on severe chronic inflammatory spondyloarthropathy (Ankylosing spondylitis).

Rest of cervical spine:

Loss of cervical lordosis is seen with normal vertebral column alignment.

Rest of the individual vertebrae are grossly normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities.

Disc desiccation is seen at few levels. The intervertebral discs are normal in heights. The vertebral end-plates are grossly normal.

C2-3: No significant abnormality seen.

C3-4: Mild disc bulge and uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy are seen. No significant mass effect over nerve roots.

C4-5 to C7-D1: No significant abnormality seen.

Spinal cord shows normal signal intensity.

The prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues are grossly normal for age.

Bony fusion of atlanto occipital articulations is seen. Rest of the craniovertebral junction and atlantoaxial joint are grossly normal.

Screening of rest of dorsal spine:

Ligamentum flavum hypertrophy is seen at D11-12 level. Disc desiccation is seen at multiple levels. Small hemangioma is seen in D12 and L1 vertebrae. Mild exaggerated thoracic kyphosis is seen. Spinal cord appears normal.

No other significant abnormalities are seen.

Screening of rest of lumbar spine:

The conus medullaris ends at L1 level and the cauda equine is normal in appearance.

Mild disc desiccation is seen at few levels.

L4-5: Post-operative changes are seen with adequate posterior decompression and peridural fibrosis. Suboptimal evaluation of nerve roots due to artefacts.

No other significant abnormalities are seen.

Screening of dorsal spine:

MRI SCAN OF HIP JOINTS

Clinical Profile: C/o left gluteal pain since 4 days? IT band syndrome? IVDP.

Technique: IR, T1, PDfs, in all planes, GRE, DWI. CT correlation.

Left hip joint:

Left hip joint appears grossly normal. No significant joint effusion or synovitis is seen.

No imaging features of avascular necrosis (AVN) are seen now.

No significant labral tear or cartilage loss is seen in anterosuperior or posteroinferior areas.

Right hip joint appears normal.

Rest of bony pelvis:

Rest of the visualised bones appear normal. No significant focal lesion or signal abnormality seen.

Bilateral SI joints and pubic symphysis appear normal.

Soft tissues:

Calcific tendinopathy of left gluteus medius tendon is seen, with calcific focus measuring about 1.0 x 1.5 x 1.8 cm (TRA x AP x CC). Adjacent inflammatory changes with mild greater trochanteric bursitis are seen - Possibility of acute calcific tendinopathy can be considered. No significant muscle tear or retracted fibres is seen.

Rest of the visualised muscles and tendons appear normal. Rest of the soft tissue appear normal.

Lumbar spine screening:

The conus medullaris ends at L1 level and the cauda equine is normal in appearance.

Bilateral chronic L5 spondylolysis is seen with grade I anterolisthesis of L5 over S1 vertebra. Mild facetal arthropathy is seen at this level.

Disc desiccation is seen at multiple levels with mild endplate changes at few levels. Mild disc bulge and facetal arthropathy are seen at few levels. No significant mass effect over nerve roots is seen at L4-5 level.

Vertebral body hemangiomas are seen at L1 level.

IMPRESSION:

Acute calcific tendinopathy of left gluteus medius tendon with acute inflammation and mild greater trochanteric bursitis as detailed.

Mild degenerative changes of lumbar spine with L5-S1 anterolisthesis, as detailed.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Right knee osteoarthrosis with effusion and Baker cyst as detailed.

Mild resolving bone contusions/ trabecular injuries with marrow edema are seen involving multiple other carpal bones and base of 5th metacarpal bone, more so in capitate and halite bones. No other significant fracture or dislocation seen.

Mild dorsal tilt of the lunate is seen. Mild capsular sprain changes with minimal effusion are seen.

Rest of the visualised bones and joints appear grossly normal. Ulnocarpal, rest of intercarpal and carpometacarpal joints appear grossly normal. No dissociation of intercarpal joints is seen.

Resolving carpal and 5th metacarpal base bone contusions/ trabecular injuries.

Dr M Arun

MRI SCAN OF LEFT WRIST JOINT

Clinical profile: H/o fall injury x 2 month back, C/o left wrist pain and swelling? Scaphoid fracture ? AVN.

Technique: T1, PDfs, IR, T2, DWI and GRE in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Sub-acute mildly displaced fracture involving the waist of the scaphoid is seen, with mild volar angulation of the distal fracture fragment.

Residual/ resolving marrow edema is seen involving both fracture fragments. Normal T1 marrow signal is maintained without focal marrow replacement, sclerosis or collapse. No significant MRI features of avascular necrosis are identified in the present non-contrast study.

No other acute fracture or dislocation is identified.

Mild degenerative osteoarthritic changes of the wrist with a few tiny subchondral cysts.

Mild capsular sprain-related changes with minimal wrist joint effusion.

The remaining visualized carpal bones and articulations are grossly preserved.

Ligaments:

Mild sprain/ partial-thickness injury of volar and dorsal radiocarpal ligamentous complex is seen, predominantly involving radial collateral, radiolunotriquetral and radioscaphocapitate ligaments. No complete ligamentous disruption or significant fiber retraction/waviness is identified.

Mild sprain/ partial-thickness injury of the intrinsic carpal ligaments adjacent to the scaphoid bone is seen.

Focal partial-thickness tear involving the central portion of the scapholunate ligament is seen without complete ligamentous disruption or scapholunate interval widening.

The remaining intrinsic and extrinsic carpal ligaments are grossly intact.

Mild sprain/ partial-thickness injury of the ulnar attachment of the TFCC, without definite full-thickness tear or significant ulnar-sided ligamentous disruption.

Tendons and rest of soft tissue:

The flexor and extensor tendons appear grossly normal. No acute tear or retraction seen. No features of tenosynovitis.

Mild soft tissue edematous changes are seen involving adjacent soft tissue and subcutaneous fat planes. No hematoma or fluid collection seen.

Rest of the soft tissue appears grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Sub-acute mildly displaced scaphoid waist fracture with mild volar angulation of the distal fragment and resolving marrow edema. No significant MRI features of avascular necrosis of the scaphoid at present.

Focal partial-thickness tear of central scapholunate ligament, without complete disruption or scapholunate interval widening.

Low-grade sprain/ partial-thickness injuries of volar and dorsal radiocarpal ligaments and intrinsic carpal ligaments, as detailed above.

Low-grade partial-thickness injury of ulnar attachment of TFCC as detailed.

Mild capsular changes with minimal effusion and soft-tissue edema.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Dr Swetha

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT LEG WITH ANKLE REGION

Clinical profile: Lower limb cellulitis.

Technique: IR and T1 axial and coronal, T2, DWI, GRE, T1 fs – axial. Post contrast T1 fs in all planes, CT correlation. Ankle: PDfs, GRE, T1 and IR sagittal

Bones and joints:

The visualized bones of the right leg, ankle and foot demonstrate preserved marrow signal without focal marrow edema, cortical destruction or other focal osseous abnormality.

The visualized knee and ankle joints are grossly preserved. No significant joint effusion, synovial thickening or abnormal periarticular enhancement is seen.

No MRI evidence of acute osteomyelitis or septic arthritis.

Soft tissue:

Diffuse and extensive inflammatory edema is seen involving the skin and subcutaneous fat planes of the right leg, extending across the ankle and dorsum of the foot, appearing hyperintense on fluid-sensitive sequences with associated diffuse/patchy post-contrast enhancement.

The inflammatory changes are more pronounced along the lateral aspect of the distal thigh/ knee region, medial aspect of the leg and dorsum of the foot, in keeping with acute cellulitis.

No organized or drainable fluid collection/abscess is identified. No sinus tract or soft-tissue gas is seen.

No significant deep fascial fluid collection or abnormal fascial enhancement to suggest a deep necrotizing soft-tissue infection is identified.

Few superficial varicose veins are noted along the medial aspect of the right leg.

Muscles and tendons:

Diffuse chronic diabetic myoneuropathy changes involving the intrinsic muscles of the foot.

No focal intramuscular collection, significant myonecrosis or acute infective myositis is identified.

The remaining visualized muscles and tendons are grossly preserved without focal tear or significant tenosynovitis.

Neurovascular structures:

The visualized neurovascular structures are grossly unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

Extensive acute cellulitis involving skin and subcutaneous tissues of right leg, ankle and dorsum of foot as detailed. No drainable abscess, sinus tract or soft-tissue gas. No significant deep fascial or intramuscular collection.

No MRI evidence of acute osteomyelitis or septic arthritis.

Few superficial varicose veins along medial aspect of right leg.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF LUMBOSACRAL SPINE AND SCREENING OF REST OF SPINE

Clinical profile: C/o back pain. S/p micro lumbar discectomy at L4-5 level. Done On 30.07.2026, Now post Op follow up.

Technique: Sagittal, T1, T2, IR, Axial T2, IR/ T1 Coronal for SI joints

Screening of rest of the spine: T2 sagittal and CT correlation.

Immediate post procedural changes with few air pockets are seen within the lumbar canal. Adjacent posterior paravertebral soft tissue changes with few air pockets are seen. No significant fluid collection or hematoma is seen.

The lumbosacral spine displays a normal lordotic curvature and vertebral column alignment.

Rest of the individual vertebrae are normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities.

Disc desiccation and facetal arthropathy are seen at multiple levels. The intervertebral discs are normal in heights. The vertebral end-plates are normal.

D12-L1 to L2-3: No significant abnormality seen.

L3-4: Mild disc bulge is seen. No significant mass effect over nerve roots.

L4-5: Post-operative changes are seen in disc and adjacent anterior epidural space. No hematoma or fluid collection seen. Residual thecal sac measures 8.9 mm in AP diameter.

Diffuse annular disc bulge with broad based central protrusion and facetal arthropathy are seen causing effacement of lateral recess and mild indentation of bilateral traversing L5 nerve roots.

Small right extra foraminal disc component causing indentation of right exiting L4 nerve roots is seen with mild edematous L4 nerve root.

L5-S1: Mild disc bulge is seen. No significant mass effect over nerve roots

The conus medullaris ends at L1 level and the cauda equine is grossly normal in appearance.

Rest of the prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues are grossly normal.

Both SI joints show mild degenerative changes.

Small renal cortical cysts are seen on both sides.

Screening of cervical spine:

Disc desiccation is seen at all levels with uncovertebral and facetal arthropathy at multiple levels.

Disc bulge, protrusion and uncovertebral arthropathy causing indentation of cord and nerve roots are seen from C3-4 to C6-7 levels, more severe at C5-6 level.

No abnormal cord signal changes are seen. No other significant abnormality seen.

Diffuse thyromegaly with few T2 hyperintense nodules are seen. Suggested clinical and USG correlation.

Screening of dorsal spine:

Disc desiccation is seen at all levels with mild flaval thickening at few levels. Vertebral body haemangiomas are seen at D6 and D7 levels.

Spinal cord appears normal. No other significant abnormalities are seen.

IMPRESSION:

Immediate postoperative changes status post L4–L5 micro lumbar discectomy, with expected postoperative air foci in spinal canal and posterior paravertebral soft tissues. No postoperative hematoma or fluid collection.

Persistent L4–5 diffuse disc bulge with central protrusion and facet arthropathy causing mild indentation of traversing L5 nerve roots.

Small right extraforaminal disc component causing indentation of right exiting L4 nerve root with mild nerve root edema.

Diffuse degenerative changes of spine as detailed.

Cervical spondylosis causing mass effect over cord and nerve roots from C3-4 to C6-7 levels as mentioned.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Clinical profile: C/o neck pain and right shoulder pain for 1 week, difficulty in lifting right shoulder? Rotator cuff tear/ motor neuropathy.

Technique: PD fs in all planes, T1 sag, GRE axial, T2 IR coronal and CT correlation.

Bones and joint:

Severe osteoarthrosis of shoulder joint is seen with partial to full thickness articular cartilage loss, prominent osteophytes and subarticular edema/ cysts. Multiple loose bodies of varying sizes are seen, largest measuring 1.6 x 1 x 0.6 cm.

Posterosuperior migration of humeral head is seen abutting under surface of acromion. Acetabularization of acromion is seen, likely suggestive of rotator cuff tear arthropathy.

Mild joint effusion is seen with extension of fluid to subscapularis recess and subacromial bursa.

Rest of shoulder joint and articulating bones appear grossly normal for age.

Rotator cuff:

Chronic full thickness tear is seen involving entire supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendons (AP dimension of 4.5 cm). Retracted torn end is attenuated and is seen at joint level, about 5 cm from insertion.

Extension of tears to MTJ of supraspinatus and infraspinatus muscles is seen.

Severe tendinosis with partial thickness articular surface/ intrasubstance tears are seen in subscapularis tendon.

Moderate to severe atrophy of supraspinatus and infraspinatus muscles is seen with stage II/ III fatty changes (Goutallier's classification). 

Severe atrophy with grade IV fatty changes is seen in teres minor muscle with grossly intact tendon.

Rest of the rotator cuff muscles and tendons appear grossly normal. Deltoid muscle appears grossly normal. 

Chronic full thickness tear of LHBT is seen with attenuated and retracted tendon.  

Labrum and ligamentous structures:

Degenerative changes are seen in glenoid labrum with chronic tears and diffuse attenuation of labrum. Labral ossification is also seen in inferior aspect.

Disruption of biceps pulley is seen. Mild synovial/ capsular thickening is seen in rotator interval and axillary recess regions. 

No other definite capsular or ligamentous disruption seen.

AC joint:

AC joint arthropathy with joint fluid is seen. Type II acromion is seen and is laterally sloping. Grossly reduced sub acromial space is seen (1 mm) with mild subacromial bursitis.  

Rest of the soft tissue appear grossly normal.

Dr. Sarenya

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: C/o right shoulder pain x 2 weeks/ gives h/o local injury to right shoulder 2 weeks back/ right rotator cuff tear.

Technique: PDfs, T2, T1, IR and GRE in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

The shoulder joint appear grossly normal with mild osteoarthrosis changes. 

Mild joint effusion is seen with fluid extension along LHBT and subscapularis recess. Mild sub acromial bursal fluid is also seen.

No bony Bankart/ Hill-Sachs lesion is seen. Rest of the articulating bones appears grossly normal in outline and marrow signal intensities.

No acute fracture or features of dislocation seen. 

Rotator cuff:

Full thickness tear is seen involving entire supraspinatus tendon and almost entire infraspinatus tendon (AP dimension in total measures 4 cm). Retracted torn end of infraspinatus tendon is edematous.

Varying levels of retraction of torn tendon fibers is seen and with maximum retraction of supraspinatus tendon of 2.4 cm at mid humeral head level.

Severe tendinosis with tears is seen in residual few intact fibers of infraspinatus tendons. Subscapularis tendinosis is seen with small chronic partial thickness articular surface tears (<50% thickness).

Few intrasubstance tears are seen in MTJ of infraspinatus muscle.

No significant atrophy is seen in rotator cuff muscles, but with stage I fatty changes in all rotator cuff muscles (Goutallier's classification). No other significant tear is seen.

Tendinosis of LHBT is seen. The deltoid muscle is also normal.

Labroligamentous structures:

Degenerative changes are seen in glenoid labrum with small chronic tears in superior quadrants. Rest of the glenoid labrum appears grossly normal. No displaced fragment is seen. 

Sprain of biceps pulley is seen. Mild synovial/ capsular thickening is seen in rotator interval and axillary recess regions.

No other definite capsular or ligamentous disruption seen.

AC joint:

AC joint arthropathy is seen. Type II acromion is seen and is laterally sloping. Sub acromial space measures 4 mm with subacromial bursitis.

Rest of the soft tissue appears normal.

Torn tendon | Supraspinatus | Infraspinatus
Tear width ( Anteroposterior) | 4 cm
Tendon retraction ( Mediolateral) | Variable with maximum of 2.4 cm
Tendon degeneration ( Grade 0-3 ) | 3 | 3
Muscle atrophy ( Grade 0-3 ) | 0 | 0
Muscle fatty infiltration ( Grade 0-4 ) | 1 | 1

IMPRESSION:

Full thickness tears of supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendons as detailed.

Rotator cuff tendinosis, partial thickness tears and muscle changes as detailed.

Labroligamentous changes and LHBT tendinosis as detailed.

Mild synovial/ capsular thickening as detailed, likely capsulitis.

AC joint arthropathy and subacromial bursitis as detailed.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Dr. Thamaraikkannan

MRI SCAN OF LUMBOSACRAL SPINE AND SCREENING OF REST OF SPINE

Clinical profile: C/o LBA since two years more on the left, radiating to left lower limb, left hip joint pain since two years.

Technique: Sagittal, T1, T2, IR, Axial T2, IR/ T1 Coronal for SI joints, DWI, PC T1 in all planes. Screening of rest of spine: T2/ PC T1 sagittal.

Well defined elongated soft tissue mass lesion is seen in intra dural extra medullary region of spinal canal extending from L1-2 to L2-3 disc levels. The lesion appears slightly hyperintense to muscle in both T1 and T2 and shows diffusion restriction and moderate, mostly homogenous post contrast enhancement. It measures 5.2 x 1.9 x 1.4 cm (CC x TR x AP). The lesion cause mass effect and displacement of cauda equina nerve roots. No significant cystic changes/ fat component/ calcification/ haemorrhage seen within the lesion. No prominent flow voids are seen.

The lumbosacral spine displays a normal lordotic curvature and vertebral column alignment.

The individual vertebrae are normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities.

Mild disc desiccation and facetal arthropathy are seen at few levels. The intervertebral discs are normal in heights. The vertebral end-plates are grossly normal.

D12-L1 to L2-3: Normal.

L3-4 and L4-5: Early disc bulge is seen. No mass effect over nerve roots.

L5-S1: No significant abnormality seen.

There is no evidence of any significant disc bulge or protrusion at other levels.

The conus medullaris ends at D12-L1 level.

The prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues are normal.

Both SI joints are normal in joint space and signal intensities.

Screening of cervical spine:

Disc desiccation is seen at few levels. Disc protrusion and left uncovertebral arthropathy causing indentation of left hemi cord is seen at C5-6 level. No spinal cord signal changes are seen.

No other significant abnormalities are seen.

Screening of dorsal spine:

Small vertebral body haemangioma is seen at D9 level. Spinal cord appears normal.

No significant abnormalities are seen.

IMPRESSION:

Well defined elongated enhancing intradural extra medullary lesion in lumbar canal region as detailed. Myxopapillary ependymoma is more likely than nerve sheath/ other tumours.

Mild degenerative changes of spine as detailed.

Suggested clinical and HPE correlation of the lesion/ review as indicated.

Dr. Anushuya.

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: H/o right shoulder dislocation.

Technique: PD fs, T1, IR, T2 and GRE in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Small Hill-Sachs defect with bone marrow edema is seen measuring approximately 11 x 8 x 2 mm (L x W x D).  No acute bony Bankart fracture is seen.

Moderate joint effusion is seen. Cartilage injury with small displaced chondral fragment is seen in anteroinferior aspect, measuring about 7 x 5 x 2 mm.

Rest of articulating bones are normal in outline and marrow signal.

Rotator cuff:

Mild strain changes are seen in subscapularis, supra and infraspinatus tendons. Small partial thickness intrasubstance tears are seen in subscapularis MTJ region. No full thickness tear or retraction of fibres is seen.

Myofascial strain changes are seen along the anterior aspect of right shoulder joint and around subscapularis muscle.

Rest of muscles and tendons of rotator cuff appear grossly normal. Long head of biceps appears intact. The deltoid musolcle is normal.

Labroligamentous structures:

Acute tear of anteroinferior labrum extending to anterosuperior, superior and posterosuperior quadrants is seen. Stripping of adjacent scapular periosteum is seen with tear. However, no significant medial displacement of labrum is seen.

Rest of the labrum appears grossly normal.

Sprain with partial tear of anterior band of IGHL, adjacent capsule and biceps pulley are seen. No complete disruption or waviness is seen.

AC joint:

Mild AC joint sprain changes are seen. Type II acromion is seen and is laterally sloping.

Sub acromial space measures 5.5 mm. No other significant abnormality seen.

IMPRESSION:

Features of acute anterior dislocation with soft tissue Bankart, Hill Sachs lesion, chondral fragment and joint effusion as detailed.

Mild rotator cuff strain changes with small tears and capsuloligamentous injuries as detailed.

Mild AC joint sprain and myofascial injuries as mentioned.

reports.fullText:
MRI SCAN OF RIGHT ELBOW

H/o slip and fall with right elbow traumatic posterior dislocation, reduced. To r/o ligamentous injury.

Technique: IR, T1, T2, PDfs and GRE in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joint:

Post reduction status of elbow joint. Mild static posterior subluxation of radial head and proximal ulna are seen with abnormal widening of radiocapitellar articulation. Narrowed joint space is seen along medial joint.

Thin avulsion fracture of common flexor tendon attachment from medial epicondyle is seen, measuring about 7.5 x 2.8 x 1.5 mm.

Small osteochondral injury/ bone contusions are seen in capitellum and trochlea.

Mild joint effusion is seen with capsular injury, predominantly along the posterolateral aspect. Few tiny osteochondral fragments are seen.

Rest of the bones shows appears grossly normal. Proximal radioulnar joint appears grossly intact.

Ligaments:

Complete disruption of humeral attachment of radial collateral ligament and LUCL is seen. Partial tear of annular ligament is seen.

Near complete to full thickness disruption of humeral attachment of medial collateral ligament complex is seen with thickened and edematous fibers.

Soft tissue:

Full thickness tear of pronator teres muslce is seen. High grade partial to near full thickness tears are seen involving proximal parts of flexor carpi radialis, palmaris longus and flexor digitorum superficialis and anconeus muscles are seen.

Contusions and grade I/ II myofacial strain changes are seen involving almost all the muscles and fascial around the elbow joint region involving common flexor, extensor muscles, distal triceps and brachialis muscles.

Diffuse and extensive subcutaneous and fascial edema is seen, more prominent in medial and posterior aspects.

Mild post traumatic changes are seen involving short segment of ulnar nerve with thickening and altered signal intensity.

No other significant abnormality seen in the present study.

IMPRESSION:

Features of acute traumatic injury of right elbow joint with avulsion fracture, osteochondral injury, joint effusion and capsular injury as detailed.

Medial and lateral ligament complex injuries as detailed.

Strain and partial tears of common flexor and extensor tendons as detailed.

Myofascial injuries with diffuse edema and ulnar nerve changes as detailed.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr. Sarenya

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT HAND

Clinical profile: C/o slowly enlarging painless soft tissue lesion in right palmar region since 1 year of age. For detailed evaluation.

Technique: T1, PDfs, IR, T2 and GRE in all planes, DWI, Post contrast T1, CT correlation.

Soft tissue:

Moderately defined, slightly lobulated lesion measuring 2.2 x 2.1 x 2.0 cm (CC x TR x AP) is seen in subcutaneous plane of palmar aspect of 2nd web space. The lesion appears T2/IR hyperintense, T1 hypointense and shows restricted diffusion. Post contrast images show heterogeneous predominant peripheral enhancement in early phases and progressive/delayed homogenous enhancement of the lesion in 1 hr delayed images. No e/o fluid level/ haemorrhage/ calcification or fat component seen within.

Posteriorly, the lesion is insinuating into and widening the 2nd web space displacing the 2nd palmar interossei tendon posteriorly at insertion site and is also abutting the 2nd flexor digitorum tendon. No obvious intra articular extension is seen into 2nd MCP joint space. No evident arterial feeder/ venous drainage seen.

Rest of the flexor and extensor tendons appears normal. No features of tendinosis/ tear or tenosynovitis seen. 

Visualized ligaments appear grossly normal. Rest of the soft tissue appears grossly normal.

Bones and joints:

Distal radioulnar, radiocarpal, ulnocarpal and other joints appear grossly normal for age.

No other significant joint effusion or synovitis is seen.

The carpal bones appear normal in position, alignment and articulation. No subluxation or dislocation seen.

IMPRESSION:

Well defined, irregular lesion showing progressive and delayed heterogeneous enhancement in subcutaneous plane of palmar aspect of 2nd web space with extension and mass effect as mentioned. No obvious intra articular extension. Possibility of slow flow vascular malformation is more likely.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Dr. Sarenya

MRI OF BRACHIAL PLEXUS

Clinical Profile: H/o RTA, c/o left upper limb weakness.

Technique: 3D IR, Sag and Axial T2, Cor T1.

Left brachial plexus:

Small pseudomeningocele is seen along left T1 nerve root, suggestive of preganglionic avulsion injury. Similar mild features are seen along left C8 nerve root.

Rest of the preganglionic segments of left brachial plexus appears grossly normal.

Post ganglionic roots of left C5 to C7 nerve roots could not be normally visualized with indistinct visualization at root/ trunk region, likely suggestive of traction injury with disruption. Rest of the left brachial plexus appears edematous and thickened with mild retraction.

Adjacent soft tissue contusion changes and edema are seen.

Right brachial plexus:

Right brachial plexus appears normal.

Rest of cervical spine:

Desiccation is seen at almost all levels with uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy at multiple levels. Mild scoliosis is seen in cervical spine with convexity towards left side. No significant mass effect over spinal cord or nerve roots.

Spinal cord appears normal in thickness and signal intensity.

No other significant abnormality seen in rest of cervical spine.

Visualized muscles:

Soft tissue contusion changes are seen in the left neck and shoulder regions with small collection. AC joint sprain changes are seen. Denervation changes are seen in the left shoulder muscles.

Rest of the visualized muscles and soft tissue appear normal.

IMPRESSION:

Features of traction injury of left brachial plexus involving preganglionic and post ganglionic segments as detailed.

Denervation changes in left shoulder muscles as mentioned.

Soft tissue contusion in left neck and shoulder regions with AC joint injury.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Dr. Raghul

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT FOOT

Clinical profile: H/o acute onset of right foot pain since last few days. For evaluation.  

Technique: T1, IR, PDFs, DWI and T2 in all planes.  

Bones and joints:

Small thin transverse T1/ T2 hypointensity is seen in the base of 2nd metatarsal bone along the plantar aspect, consistent with fracture. Mild edema is seen in involved bone and adjacent soft tissue. Features are suggestive of stress fracture (Arendt grade 4 bone stress injury). No significant callus formation is seen.

No fluid collection/ focal lytic lesion/ soft tissue mass lesion seen.

Osteoarthrosis features are seen in 1st MTP joint. Minimal fluid is seen in ankle, posterior subtalar and 1st MTP joints.

Rest of the visualised bones and joints appear normal for age.  

Tendons and rest of soft tissue:

Mild diffuse subcutaneous edema is seen in dorsum of foot region. No significant fluid collection/ diffusion restriction or sinus tracts are seen. 

The anterior, medial and posterior tendons appear normal. Peroneal and flexor retinaculum is intact. Sinus tarsi appear normal. 

Visualised muscles appear grossly normal. Rest of the soft tissue appears normal. 

IMPRESSION:

Acute stress fracture in base of 2nd metatarsal bone as detailed.

Mild subcutaneous edema in dorsum of foot region.

No other significant abnormality seen.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.
