reports.fullText:
MRI OF WHOLE BODY (P+C)

Clinical profile: H/o limping for past few weeks. H/o fever, reduced appetite and weight loss for last 1 week. Increased ESR and CRP? CRMO.

Technique: T1, IR - coronal and axial, T2, DWI – axial, PC T1 FS in all planes.

Brain:

Visualised brain appears grossly normal.

No significant focal lesion/ signal abnormality seen.

Neck:

No significant abnormality seen in the visualised structures of neck.

No significant sized focal lesion or lymphadenopathy is seen.

Thorax:

Visualised lung fields appear unremarkable.

Bilateral acromioclavicular joints, clavicle and ribs show normal signal intensity.

No other significant abnormality seen in thorax and mediastinum.

Abdomen:

Visualised abdominal organs are unremarkable.

Bilateral kidneys and adrenal glands appear normal.

No significant focal lesion/ signal abnormality or collection seen in the abdomen.

Bilateral upper limbs:

Bilateral humerus, radius and ulna reveal normal marrow signal intensity. No focal lesion or signal abnormality seen.

Bilateral shoulder, elbow and wrist joints show normal signal intensity.

Spine and Bilateral lower limbs:

Multifocal patchy marrow IR hyper intensities are seen involving proximal and distal parts of femur and tibia in metaphysis, epiphysis and apophysis regions. Similar patchy areas of IR hyper intensities are also seen in bony pelvis, tarsal and metatarsal bones on both sides. Diaphysis of the lower limb long bones is spared. Bilateral fibula appears normal.

Mild heterogeneous enhancement and altered diffusivity are seen in these abnormal marrow regions. No significant fluid collection/ periosteal reaction/ extra osseous soft tissue component seen in the present study.

No significant abnormality seen in the vertebrae in the present study.

Bilateral sacroiliac joints, hip, knee and ankle joints appear normal. No synovitis or joint effusion is seen in the present study.

Visualised muscles and soft tissues show normal signal intensity. No obvious collection/ lesion are seen.

IMPRESSION:

Multifocal IR hyperintense marrow lesions in bilateral lower limb bones and bony pelvis as detailed.

No abnormal fluid collection/ periosteal reaction or extra osseous soft tissue component seen in the present study.

No imaging features of synovitis or arthritis seen.

No other significant abnormality in visualised structures.

In view of clinical and imaging features, the possibility of CRMO (chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis) can be considered. However, suggested clinical/ HPE correlation/ further evaluation to rule out other infective and neoplastic possibilities.

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT FOREARM

Clinical profile: H/o swelling in right forearm region for past few years with occasional mild pain.

Technique: T, IR, T2, GRE, DWI, PC T1 in al planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Ulnohumeral, radiocapitellar and proximal radio ulnar joints appears normal in alignment. 

No joint effusion or synovial thickening is seen. The ligaments appear normal. 

The bones show no significant abnormality. No significant focal lesion or abnormality seen. 

Soft tissue:

Fairly defined lobulated T2/ IR hyperintense lesion measuring 3 x 1.2 x 1.2 cm is seen in the anterior aspect of right proximal forearm region involving superficial fibres of pronator teres muscle and is seen projecting in between pronator teres and flexor carpi radialis muscle.

The lesion appears isointense on T1 and heterogeneously hyperintense on T2 with peripheral blooming on GRE. Minimal surrounding IR hyperintensity is seen. No prominent arterial feeder/ draining vein is seen.

The lesion is seen posteromedial to radial neurovascular bundle. Altered diffusivity is seen within the lesion. With contrast, the lesions show progressive enhancement. Small non enhancing foci are seen within, may represent thrombotic foci.

No e/o phleboliths/ calcification seen (on limited CT correlation).

Rest of the visualised tendons, soft tissue and fascial planes appear grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Small lobulated enhancing T2/ IR hyperintense lesion in right forearm region with imaging characteristics as described. The possibility of slow flow vascular malformation is more likely than other neoplastic etiology.

Suggested clinical correlation/ further evaluation as indicated.

Dr.B.Pravitha

MRI SCAN OF LUMBOSACRAL SPINE AND SCREENING OF REST OF SPINE AND BRAIN

Clinical Profile: Closed spinal dysraphism, for evaluation.

Technique: Sagittal T1, T2, IR, Axial T2/ T1, IR and T1 Coronal for SI joints.

Screening of rest of the spine: T2 sagittal

Screening of brain: FLAIR and DWI axial.

Non visualization/ defect of posterior elements are seen at L5-S1 level, s/o spina bifida. Mild expansion of spinal canal is seen in lumbosacral region.

The neural placode/ dorsal lipoma complex is seen within the spinal canal. Large intradural lipomatous component measuring about 3.4 x 1.1 x 0.5 (CC x TRA x AP) is seen extending from L3 to S1 vertebral levels.

The intradural lipomatous component appears to be contiguous with subcutaneous fat through the dysraphic defect at L5-S1 level. Increased subcutaneous fat is seen at this level. However, no significant sinus tract is seen in the present study.

No focal herniation of meninges or neural contents beyond the spinal canal is seen.

Tethering of the spinal cord is seen with conus medullaris at L5-S1 level. Filar lipoma is also seen.

No significant cord signal changes/ syrinx seen now. No skin defect is seen at this level posteriorly.

The lumbosacral spine displays a normal lordotic curvature and vertebral column alignment.

The intervertebral discs are normal in heights and hydration. No significant disc protrusion or disc bugle is seen.

Well defined T2/ IR hyperintense lesion measuring 2.2 x 1.7 x 1.6 cm is seen in right suprarenal region. Suggested further evaluation.

Screening of cervical spine:

CV junction appears normal. Spinal cord appears grossly normal.

No significant abnormality is seen.

Screening of dorsal spine:

Spinal cord appears grossly normal. No significant abnormality is seen.

Screening of brain:

No significant abnormality is seen in neuroparenchyma.

No features of hydrocephalus are seen.

IMPRESSION:

Features are suggestive of closed spinal dysraphism with spinal bifida, lipomyelocele and low lying tethered spinal cord as detailed.

No other significant abnormality in spine.

No significant abnormality in brain in screening study.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Dr Lokesh

LIMITED MRI STUDY OF DORSAL SPINE

Clinical Profile: H/o D2-3 infective spondylodiscitis of dorsal spine, s/p D1-D5 stabilisation and D2-D3 laminectomy done on 17/08/2023; for follow up. No new complaints.

Technique: Sagittal T1, T2, IR, DWI and T2 SPACE axial.

Screening of rest of spine: T2 sagittal. Limited CT correlation.

In comparison with the previous MRI done on 10/09/2023,

Post-surgical changes with defects in posterior elements are seen at D2 and D3 levels.

Bilateral pedicle screws are seen in situ from D1 to D5 vertebral levels.

No abnormal IR hyperintensity, soft tissue collection seen near D2-3 vertebrae.

Partial interval reduction in size of the previously mentioned well-defined fluid collection is seen in cervicodorsal region in posterior aspect, now measuring about 10 x 6.7 x 4.7 cm (CC x TRA x AP) (previously measured 13.5 x 9.2 x 7.5 cm). The collection is seen extending from C6 to D5 levels and abutting posterior dura.

Mild interval reduction of edema is seen in the adjacent posterior paravertebral soft tissue.

No spinal cord signal changes are seen.

Rest of the dorsal spine displays a normal curvature and vertebral column alignment.

Rest of the individual vertebrae are normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities.

Disc desiccation is seen at all levels. The vertebral end-plates are normal.

Mild disc bulge is redemonstrated at D8-9 level.

Screening of cervical spine:

Disc desiccation is seen at all levels. Disc bulge, protrusion and uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy causing indentation of cord and nerve roots are seen from C4-5 to C6-7 levels. No spinal cord signal changes are seen.

No other significant abnormality seen in cervical spine.

Screening of lumbar spine:

The conus medullaris ends at D12-L1 level and the cauda equine is normal in appearance.

Disc desiccation is seen at all levels, facetal arthropathy at few levels and small chronic Schmorl's nodule at L1 level.

Disc bulge and facetal arthropathy causing mass effect over nerve roots is seen at L4-5 and L5-S1 levels.

IMPRESSION:

Resolving post-surgical changes in upper dorsal spine as detailed.

Partial interval reduction in size of fluid collection and edema in posterior cervicodorsal region as detailed.

Diffuse degenerative changes of spine as mentioned.

No other significant interval changes in spine.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT KNEE JOINT

Clinical profile: H/o twisting injury to right knee joint in June 2020. For detailed evaluation.

Technique: PD fs, IR, T1, T2 and GRE in all planes.

Bones and joints:

Minimal joint effusion is seen. No full thickness cartilage loss/ osteochondral fragment seen.

Anterior translation of tibia is seen (9 mm). Rest of knee joint and articulating bones appear normal for age.

Menisci:

Focal blunting of posteroinferior corner and small partial superior peripheral tear in posterior horn are seen in medial meniscus (likely ramp lesion). Chronic medial meniscocapsular sprain changes are also seen. No acute tear or displaced fragment is seen.

Rest of the medial and lateral menisci appear grossly normal.

Ligaments:

Medial and lateral collateral ligaments and patellar retinacula appear grossly intact. No significant tear or waviness is seen.

Chronic full thickness tear of ACL is seen with grossly attenuated fibres. Posterior cruciate ligament appears intact.

Posterolateral and posteromedial corner ligament complexes appear grossly intact.

Rest of soft tissue:

Extensor mechanism appears normal. Rest of surrounding muscles, tendons and neurovascular structures appear normal.

IMPRESSION:

Minimal right knee joint effusion.

Chronic full thickness tear of ACL as detailed.

Small medial meniscal tear and chronic meniscocapsular sprain as detailed.

No other significant abnormality seen.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF LEFT KNEE JOINT

Clinical profile: C/o bilateral knee pain with recurrent patellar subluxation. No h/o  trauma.

Technique: PD fs, T1, IR, T2, GRE in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Minimal joint effusion is seen. Superolateral position of patella is seen. No significant bone changes are seen. No cartilage loss or displaced osteochondral fragment is seen.

Rest of knee joint and articulating bones appear grossly normal.

Risk factor assessment:

Wiberg type 2 patella is seen.

The lateral trochlear inclination is 25 degrees (within normal limits >11).

The trochlear sulcus angle is 142 degrees (within normal limits < 154 degrees).

Features of patella Alta are seen. (Insall-Salvati Index is 1.36. Abnormal is >1.2)

Trochlear facet ratio is 53 % (Rules out patellar facetal asymmetry (N > 40%).

The trochlear depth is 3.9 mm (Within normal limits >3 mm).

Tibial tubercle to trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measures 23 mm (> 20 mm is abnormal), suggestive of lateralization of tibial tuberosity with respect to trochlea.

Menisci:

The medial and lateral menisci appear grossly normal. No tear or displaced fragment is seen.

Ligaments:

Attenuated medial patellar retinaculum and MPFL are seen. No complete tear or waviness is seen.

The anterior and posterior cruciate ligament appears intact and normal in signal intensity.

Medial and lateral collateral ligament and lateral patellar retinacula appear normal.

Posteromedial and posterolateral corner ligament complexes appear grossly intact.

Rest of soft tissue:

Mild semimembranosus bursal inflammation is seen. No significant fluid collection seen.

Rest of the extensor mechanism appears grossly intact. Rest of surrounding muscles, tendons and neurovascular structures are grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Minimal joint effusion and attenuated medial patellar retinaculum as detailed.

Features of patella Alta and lateralization of tibial tuberosity as detailed.

No other significant abnormality seen.

Clinical Profile: C/o neck stiffness and immobility, to r/o spondyloarthritis.

Technique: Sagittal T1, T2, IR, Axial T2, T1 and IR Coronal for SI joints

Screening of rest of spine: T2 sagittal, IR sagittal. CT correlation.

Chronic inflammatory spondyloarthropathy changes are seen in the spine with fusion of bilateral facet joints, costo transverse and costovertebral articulations at multiple levels.

Bony ankylosis of bilateral sacroiliac joints is seen with subarticular fat deposition. Anterior vertebral corner signal changes are also seen at multiple levels.

Acute inflammation with IR hyperintensity is seen involving facet, costo transverse and costo vertebral articulations at multiple cervical, dorsal and lumbar levels. Features are consistent with acute on chronic axial inflammatory spondyloarthropathy.

Rest of cervical spine:

Mild loss of cervical lordosis is seen with normal vertebral column alignment.

Rest of the individual vertebrae are normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities.

Disc desiccation is seen at multiple levels. The intervertebral discs are normal in heights. Rest of the vertebral end-plates are normal.

C2-3 to C7-D1: No significant abnormality seen. No mass effect over spinal cord or nerve roots is seen.

Spinal cord shows normal signal intensity.

The prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues are grossly normal.

Fusion of atlanto occipital joints is seen. Rest of the cranio vertebral junction and atlanto axial joint are grossly normal.

Screening of rest of dorsal spine:

Disc desiccation is seen at few levels. Spinal cord appears normal.

No other significant abnormality.

Screening of rest of lumbar spine:

Mild straightening of lumbar spine is seen. Disc desiccation is seen at L5-S1 level.

No other significant abnormality seen in lumbar spine.

IMPRESSION:

Imaging features are consistent with acute on chronic axial inflammatory spondyloarthropathy, likely Ankylosing spondylitis.

Mild degenerative changes of spine as detailed.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT KNEE JOINT

Bones and joints:

Small bone contusions and trabecular injury with edema are seen in posterior aspects of tibial plateau and lateral femoral condyle.

Mild to moderate joint effusion is seen. Small loose body measuring 7 x 4 x 2 mm is seen in popliteal tendon sheath. Small chondral flap is seen in medial patellar facet.

Anterior translation of tibia is seen (1.3 cm). Rest of the articulating bones and joints appear grossly normal.

Meniscus:

Vertical longitudinal tear is seen in posterior horn of lateral meniscus in outer third region (Wrisberg rip tear). Chronic oblique tear is seen in posterior body and postero horn regions of lateral meniscus.

Oblique tear is seen in posterior body/ posterior horn junction region of medial meniscus. Rest of medial and lateral menisci appear grossly normal.

Mild medial and lateral meniscocapsular sprain changes are seen.

Ligaments:

Full thickness tear of ACL is seen with attenuated and wavy fibres. PCL appears grossly intact.

Grade II sprain changes of medial collateral ligament is seen. No complete tear is seen. Patellar retinacula appear grossly intact.  LCL appears grossly intact.

Grade I/ II sprain of posterolateral and posteromedial corner ligament complexes is seen.

Rest of soft tissues:

Extensor mechanism appears grossly intact. Myofascial strain changes are seen involving muscles, fascia and soft tissue around knee joint region. Rest of the surrounding muscles, tendons and neurovascular structures are grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Bone contusions, trabecular injuries with effusion as detailed.

Full thickness tear of ACL and other ligament injuries as detailed.

Meniscal tears and meniscocapsular sprain changes as detailed.

Myofascial strain changes in soft tissue around knee joint as mentioned.

reports.fullText:
Dr Rajiv S Menon

MRI SCAN OF LEFT THIGH REGION

Clinical Profile: C/o swelling in left thigh x 2 months/ Incisional biopsy done with HPE- atypical lipomatous tumor/ well differentiated liposarcoma. For detailed evaluation.

Technique:  T2, T1, IR, DWI, GRE and PC T1 in all planes. CT correlation.

Left thigh:

Primary tumor:

A large moderately delineated, lobulated fat containing mass lesion measuring approximately 29.2 x 14.9 x 10.4 cm (CC x TRA x AP) is seen in the posteromedial aspect of left thigh region, probably arising from posterior aspect of adductor magnus muscle.

The lesion shows significant fat suppression and heterogeneously IR hyperintensity within. The lesion shows patchy areas of diffusion restriction along the anterior aspect of the mass lesion. Mild patchy and septal enhancement is also seen within the lesion.

No matrix mineralization/ cystic component are seen. Mild post procedural changes with few hemorrhagic foci are seen.

Extent of lesion:

Superiorly, the margin of the lesion is seen about 1.5 cm inferior to lesser trochanter of femur. Inferiorly, the distal margin is seen about 7 cm proximal to articular surface of medial femoral condyle.

Anteriorly, the lesion is causing smooth indentation and stretching of adductor magnus muscle over the mass. The posterior aspect of muscle is involved by the tumor. Adductor brevis and longus muscles appear grossly normal.

Posteriorly, the mass is causing smooth indentation and deformation of the anterior aspects of semimembranosus, semitendinosus and biceps muscles with loss of fat planes. The possibility of invasion could not be ruled out.

In medial aspect, the lesion is protruding through the gaps between sartorius and gracilis and gracilis and semimembranosus muscles. Indentation and stretching of gracilis is seen with loss of fat plane.

In lateral aspect, the lesion is indenting and stretching the biceps muscle as well as extending upto the deep fascia.

No other similar focal lesion is seen.

Neurovascular structures:

The sciatic nerve is completely encased by the mass lesion for a length of approximately 20 cm in mid and lower thigh regions. Mass effect and posterior displacement of sciatic nerve is also seen in upper thigh region.

The lipomatous mass is seen indenting the posterior aspect of distal femoral and popliteal vessels. However, no significant encasement is seen.

The femoral nerve appears grossly normal.

Lymph nodes:

No significant sized lymphadenopathy is seen in left inguinal or iliac regions.

Bones and joints:

The visualised bones of bony pelvis and thigh regions appear grossly normal.

No significant focal lesion or signal abnormality seen.

Mild osteoarthrosis is seen in left knee joint. Left hip joint appears grossly normal.

Rest of the soft tissue:

Rest of the visualised soft tissue appear normal.

Right thigh appears normal.

IMPRESSION:

In this known HPE proven case of atypical lipomatous tumor/ well differentiated liposarcoma, present scan shows

Large lobulated fat containing mass lesion in posteromedial aspect of left thigh region with extensions and mass effect as detailed.

Encasement of left sciatic nerve and mass effect over vascular structures as detailed.

No other significant abnormality seen.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF DORSAL SPINE AND SCREENING OF REST OF SPINE

Clinical Profile: C/o numbness of both legs. Initially started with paraesthesia, cramps of bilateral leg and thigh 2 months back, then developed gait abnormalities 2 weeks back, decreased/ absent sensation over both legs and difficulty in walking.

MRI scans done outside – s/o dorso lumbar transverse myelitis, nerve conduction study s/o peripheral neuropathy, GCS 15/15, muscle power 4/5, working diagnosis – demyelinating polyneuropathy.

Patient is not willing for brain screening.

Technique: Sagittal, T1, T2, IR, Axial T2, DWI and PC T1.

Screening of rest of the spine: T2 and PC T1 sagittal

Spinal cord:

Diffuse long segment central T2/ IR intramedullary hyperintensity is seen in the spinal cord extending from D5-6 disc to D12 vertebral levels and involving the conus medullaris. Mild swelling of the cord is seen with subtle post contrast enhancement.

Sparing of the thin rim of periphery of the cord is seen in the involved segments. No significant intramedullary focal lesion or haemorrhage seen in the present study.

Few prominent serpiginous intradural extramedullary flow voids is seen along the dorsal surface of the involved cord. Serpentine enhancing veins are seen on the cord surface in the involved spinal cord region.

No abnormal enhancement of the cauda equina or nerve roots is seen.

Rest of the dorsal spine:

The dorsal spine displays a normal curvature and vertebral column alignment.

The individual vertebrae are normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities.

Disc desiccation is seen at all levels with small chronic Schmorl’s nodes and endplate signal changes at multiple levels. No significant mass effect over cord or nerve roots seen.

The intervertebral discs are normal in heights. Rest of the vertebral end-plates are normal.

The prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues are grossly normal.

Rest of the spinal cord appears grossly normal. The conus medullaris ends at D12 level and cauda equina appear grossly normal.

Screening of cervical spine:

Disc desiccation is seen at all levels with reduced disc height and endplate changes at few levels. Uncovertebral arthropathy and disc bulge causing indentation of anterior thecal sac is seen at multiple levels and mild cord indentation at C5-6 and C6-7 levels. No spinal cord signal changes are seen.

No other significant abnormality seen in cervical spine.

Screening of lumbar spine:

Grade I anterolisthesis is seen at L5-S1 level.  Disc desiccation is seen at all levels with endplate changes at multiple levels, more severe at L5-S1 level with reduced disc height.

Disc bulge and facetal arthropathy are seen at multiple levels, more severe at L4-5 and L-S1 levels causing mass effect over traversing nerve roots.

Significant degenerative changes are seen between spinous processes of lumbar vertebrae, likely Baastrup disease.

No other significant abnormality seen in lumbar spine.

IMPRESSION:

Suspected case of transverse myelitis on treatment.

Diffuse long segment central T2/ IR intramedullary hyperintensity in spinal cord from D5-6 to D12 levels with imaging characteristics as detailed.

Few prominent serpiginous intradural extramedullary flow voids as detailed.

Diffuse severe degenerative changes of spine with mass effect over cord and nerve roots at few cervical and lumbar levels as detailed.

In view of clinical and imaging features, the possibility of occult spinal dural arteriovenous fistula with congestive myelopathy has to be ruled out. Suggested clinical correlation/ DSA for further evaluation as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF LEFT FOOT

Clinical profile: Known case of DM. History of left leg cellulitis. S/p left forefoot and midfoot radical wound debridement done on 19.7.2026 and left fifth toe amputation done on 26.7.26. Decompressive fasciotomy of entire side of left foot and skin grafting done on 10.08.2026. Now  with pus discharge from wound.

Technique: T1, IR, T2, DWI and PC T1 in all planes. CT correlation.

Compared with previous MRI dated 05.08.2026.

Bones and joints:

Postsurgical changes are noted with non-visualisation of 5th toe phalanges and distal/ anterior portion of 5th metatarsal, consistent with prior 5th ray amputation.

The 5th metatarsal stump demonstrates reactive postoperative marrow changes, with no convincing MRI evidence of osteomyelitis at the amputation stump.

Persistent marrow signal changes with enhancement are seen involving head of 4th metatarsal and proximal phalanx of 4th toe represent reactive osteitis/ postoperative reactive marrow changes than early osteomyelitis.

Mild stress related/ reactive marrow changes are seen in inferior aspect of calcaneus.

Mild osteoarthrosis changes are also seen in few foot joints.

Rest of the visualised bones and joints appear grossly normal for age.

No imaging features of septic arthritis seen in the present study.

Ligament complex:

Medial and lateral ligament complex appears intact. No significant tear is seen.

Rest of the visualised ligaments appears grossly normal. 

Tendons and rest of soft tissue:

Post procedural changes with soft tissue defects involving skin and subcutaneous fat plane are seen along plantar aspect of proximal and mid foot regions.

Small ill-defined infected fluid collections with restricted diffusion are seen in heel pad and plantar aspect of forefoot regions, largest measuring 2.3 x 2 x 0.5 cm in heel pad region.

Few persistent patchy areas of inflammation and non-enhancement are seen around these infected fluid collections along heel pad and plantar aspect of fore foot regions. Features are most consistent with fat necrosis/ devitalised plantar soft tissues.

Surrounding soft tissue inflammation and enhancement is seen around these collections in fore foot and heel pad regions.

Diabetic myoneuropathy changes are seen in foot muscles.

Plantar fasciitis with focal partial thickness tear redemonstrated.

Diffuse subcutaneous edema and inflammation is seen along dorsum of foot and ankle regions. No other significant fluid collection is seen in the present study.

Rest of the soft tissue appears grossly normal. 

IMPRESSION:

Compared with previous MRI dated 05.08.2026, present study shows,

Postsurgical changes of left 5th ray amputation and plantar debridement.

Persistent mild reactive postoperative marrow changes involving 5th metatarsal stump, 4th metatarsal head and proximal phalanx of 4th toe as detailed.

Extensive postoperative plantar soft tissue defects with small ill-defined infected fluid collections, fat necrosis and soft tissue inflammation involving plantar forefoot and heel pad regions as detailed.

Diffuse cellulitis soft tissue edema involving the foot and ankle.

Diabetic myoneuropathy changes involving intrinsic foot muscles.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF LEFT WRIST

Clinical profile: Pain and mild swelling in left wrist joint for past few months. Numbness along thumb and index finger for past few weeks. For detailed evaluation:

Technique: T1, PDfs, IR, DWI, GRE and post contrast T1 in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Chronic scaphoid fracture with non-union, rotation of scaphoid, pseudo arthrosis, proximal pole avascular necrosis and cystic degeneration of distal pole are seen. Severe degenerative changes with large subarticular cysts, cartilage loss and edema are seen in radio scaphoid joint.

Degenerative changes are also seen in scaphocapitate and capitolunate joints. (SNAC wrist).

Carpal height index ratio is abnormal measuring 0.39 (normal above 0.5). DISI pattern is seen with dorsal tilt of lunate, mild dorsal subluxation of capitate and abnormal angles.

Ulnocarpal, rest of intercarpal and carpometacarpal joints appear normal.

Ligaments:

Chronic sprain with attenuation of radioscaphocapitate and radiolunotriquetral ligaments are seen. Chronic sprain is also seen in scapholunate ligament. However, no complete disruption is seen. Mild adjacent synovitis is seen.

The lunotriquetral ligament is intact. Dorsal radiotriquetral and dorsal intercarpal ligaments appear intact.

TFCC appears normal for age. Rest of the ligaments appear intact.

Tendons:

Chronic stenosing tenosynovitis involving extensor pollicis longus (EPL), extensor carpi radialis brevis (ECRB) and longus (ECRL) tendons over left wrist is seen with large fluid collection in tendon sheaths.

No abnormal post contrast enhancement, tendon tears or retraction are seen in the present study. Features are likely due to distal intersection tenosynovitis of wrist.

Rest of the flexor and extensor tendons appear normal.

Rest of soft tissue:

Segmental thickening, increased signal intensity and post contrast enhancement is seen in median nerve at the level of hook of hamate. Flattening of the nerve is seen with palmar bowing of flexor retinaculum.

IR hyperintensity is seen in thenar muscles. No atrophy is seen. Features are suggestive of early carpal tunnel syndrome.

Rest of the soft tissue appears grossly normal. No abnormal inflammation, soft tissue swelling or collection is seen.

IMPRESSION:

Non-union of scaphoid fracture with degenerative changes and instability as detailed. (SNAC wrist).

Chronic ligament sprain with adjacent synovitis as detailed.

Chronic distal intersection tenosynovitis of wrist as detailed.

Features of early carpal tunnel syndrome.

MRI SCAN OF CERVICAL SPINE AND SCREENING OF REST OF SPINE

Clinical profile: Cervical spondylosis for evaluation:

Technique: Sagittal T1, IR and T2, IR coronal, Axial T2.

Screening of rest of the spine: T2 sagittal.

Grade I anterolisthesis of C7 over D1 vertebra is seen. Severe bilateral facetal hypertrophy with marrow edema is seen at this level. Rest of cervical spine shows loss of lordosis and normal vertebral column alignment.

Rest of the individual vertebrae are grossly normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities for age.

Disc desiccation at all levels with reduced disc height and endplate changes at multiple levels. Uncovertebral and facetal arthropathy are also seen at multiple levels.

C2-3: Facetal arthropathy is seen. No significant mass effect over nerve roots.

C3-4: Disc bulge with small central protrusion and bilateral uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy are seen causing spinal canal stenosis and mild indentation of cord and bilateral exiting C4 nerve roots. Residual thecal sac measures 7.9 mm in midsagittal dimension.

C4-5: Mild disc bulge and uncovertebral arthropathy are seen. No significant mass effect over exiting nerve roots.

C5-6: Disc bulge with bilateral uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy are seen causing spinal canal stenosis and mild indentation of cord and bilateral exiting C6 nerve roots. Residual thecal sac measures 8.2 mm in midsagittal dimension.

C6-7: Disc bulge with bilateral uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy are seen causing spinal canal stenosis and indentation of cord and bilateral exiting C7 nerve roots. Residual thecal sac measures 7 mm in midsagittal dimension.

C7-D1: Uncovered disc with posterior bulge and facetal hypertrophy are seen causing indentation of bilateral exiting C8 nerve roots.

Spinal cord shows normal signal intensity.

The prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues are grossly normal for age.

The craniovertebral junction and atlantoaxial joint are grossly normal for age.

Screening of dorsal spine:

Disc desiccation is seen at multiple levels with small disc protrusions and mild flaval thickening at few levels. Spinal cord appears normal.

No other significant abnormalities are seen.

Screening of lumbar spine:

The conus medullaris ends at L1 level and the cauda equine is normal in appearance.

Disc desiccation is seen at all levels with mild reduced disc height, endplate irregularity and Modic changes at L3-4 and L5-S1 levels.

Disc bulge and facetal arthropathy are seen at few levels, more severe at L3-4 and L5-S1 levels causing mass effect over nerve roots.

No other significant abnormalities are seen in lumbar spine.

IMPRESSION:

Diffuse degenerative changes of spine with C7-D1 anterolisthesis as detailed.

Disc changes and arthropathy causing canal stenosis and mass effect over cord and bilateral nerve roots at C3-4, C5-6, C6-7 and C7-D1 levels as detailed.

Lumbar spondylosis as mentioned.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Mild expansion of vertebra, cortical thickening, and coarsened trabeculae and mild post contrast enhancement is seen involving entire L2 vertebra including body and posterior elements. No obvious destructive lesion or extra osseous soft tissue component seen in the present study, likely suggestive of Paget’s disease of L2 vertebra. No significant diffusion restriction or collection is seen.

Dr Neethu

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT LEG WITH SCREENING OF ANKLE

Clinical profile: RTA – bike versus pillion rider on 23.05.2015, bamboo stick piercing wound, traumatic necrosis right leg – right leg anterolateral compartment muscle excision + slough excision + right leg posterior compartment – necrotic muscle excision (06.06.2015)

Right leg wound debridement + slough excision

Right leg anterior lateral skin + fascio cut – advanced flap and SSG.

Right leg post fasciocut, advancement flap and SSG.

Right leg below POP SLAB (18.06.2015)

Tendoachilles lengthening by Z plasty – wound closure by advancement flaps done on 16.02.2017.

Technique: IR, T1, T2 – coronal and axial, DWI, GRE, PD fs - axial. Screening of ankle: PDfs in all planes. 

Soft tissue:

Chronic post-operative changes with overlying skin/ subcutaneous and soft tissue defect is seen along anterolateral and posteromedial aspects of left regions. No fluid collection is seen.

Absent muscle bulk with severe atrophy is seen involving anterior compartment muscles including tibialis anterior, extensor hallucis longus and extensor digitorum muslces in the lower half region.

Absent muscle bulk with severe atrophy is also seen involving (deep and superficial) posterior compartment muslces involving soleus, gastrocnemius, tibialis posterior, and flexor hallucis longus and flexor digitorum muscles.

Extensive peritendinous adhesion and fibrosis is seen in the posterior compartment. All the flexor and Achilles tendons are adherent to each other for a length of approximately 13 cm in distal half of leg region with altered course of tendons.

Anterior compartment tendons are only appreciated in the ankle joint region and not seen separately in leg region.

Chronic post-operative changes with thickening of Achilles tendon are seen. Achilles tendon is adherent to flexor tendons as detailed above.

Rest of the visualised lateral compartment muscles, tendons and soft tissue appear grossly intact. Asymmetrical atrophy is seen involving right leg muslces as compared to left leg region.

Well delineated fusiform T2/ IR hyperintense lesion, measuring about 2.1 x 1 x 0.9 cm is seen along tibial nerve in mid third region of leg, likely post traumatic neuroma in continuity.

Denervation changes are seen involving posterior compartment muscles of right leg region.

Bones and joints:

Mild smooth cortical/ periosteal thickening is seen along lateral part of right tibia involving distal half. No aggressive periosteal changes or lytic areas are seen.

No focal lesion or marrow signal abnormality is seen in the present study.

Rest of the visualised bones and joints appear normal.

The knee and ankle joints are normal with respect to alignment and joint space.

No significant joint effusion or synovitis is seen.

Screening of ankle:

Denervation changes are seen involving all the foot muslces.

Minimal joint effusion is seen. No osteochondral abnormality is seen.

Patchy soft tissue edema is seen involving posteromedial aspect of heel pad region, likely due to altered walking and stress related changes. 

IMPRESSION:

Chronic post-operative changes with soft tissue defect, absent muscle bulk and severe atrophy involving anterior and posterior compartment muscles as detailed.

Extensive peritendinous adhesion/ fibrosis involving flexor and Achilles tendons in distal half of leg region with altered course of tendons as detailed.

Denervation changes in right leg and foot muscles as mentioned.

Well delineated fusiform lesion along tibial nerve in mid third region of leg, likely post traumatic neuroma in continuity.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Dr. Anushuya/ Dr Sherene

reports.fullText:
MRI SCAN OF LEFT KNEE JOINT

Clinical profile: C/o Acute onset of pain in left knee joint since few weeks? Cause.

Technique: T1, T1fs, IR, T2, DWI, GRE, PC T1fs in all planes with limited CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Eccentric lytic mass lesion with slightly lobulated margin is seen in epimetaphyseal region of distal femur towards anterolateral aspect, measuring about 6.1 x 5.7 x 5 cm (CC x TRA x AP) . The lesion is extending to the subarticular region of distal femur with narrow zone of transition. No sclerotic margin is seen around the lesion. Thinned out cortex with multiple foci of deossification is seen around the lesion.

The lesion appears hyper intense in IR, intermediate in T1, heterointense with areas of hypointensity in T2 images. The soft tissue component shows moderate enhancement, significant diffusion restriction (0.9 to 1.1 x 10−3 mm2/s) and mild blooming in gradient images.

Multiloculated cystic area with fluid levels and hemorrhage is seen in anterior part of the lesion, measuring about 2.1 x 2.8 x 0.8 cm, likely suggestive of secondary ABC component.

Mild adjacent bone marrow edema is seen in distal femur towards articular aspect. No significant fracture is seen.

No matrix mineralization or periosteal reaction is seen. No obvious intraarticular extension of soft tissue component is seen.

Focal extra osseous soft tissue components are seen along the anterior and posterior aspects of the lesion, measuring about 1 x 1.2 x 0.6 cm and 3.3 x 2.4 x 1.2 cm respectively. Mild edema is seen in the adjacent soft tissue and fascial planes. Prefemoral fat pad edema is also seen.

Mild joint effusion with synovitis is seen in left knee joint.

Rest of the visualised bones and joints appear grossly normal. No other focal lesion is seen.

No significant sized lymphadenopathy is seen in popliteal fossa region.

Rest of soft tissue:

Ligaments and menisci appear grossly normal. No significant abnormality seen.

Rest of the soft tissue appears normal. No other significant inflammation, any other soft tissue swelling or collection is seen.

Rest of visualised muscles and tendons appear normal.

IMPRESSION:

Eccentric epimetaphyseal lytic lesion in distal femur with extensions and small extra osseous soft tissue component as detailed.

Diffuse altered signal intensity in distal quadriceps and medial gastrocnemius muscles as detailed.

No other significant abnormality seen.

In view of clinical and imaging characteristics, the possibility of giant cell tumor is more likely than other neoplastic etiologies (like Sarcoma). Suggested clinical and HPE correlation/ review as indicated.

No significant soft-tissue collection or haematoma.

Median and radial nerves appear grossly unremarkable.

Remaining visualized muscles, tendons and neurovascular structures are grossly preserved.

Screening of wrist:

Postoperative changes of distal radius fracture fixation with metallic hardware are noted, with associated susceptibility artefacts limiting local assessment.

No significant periarticular fluid collection or postoperative haematoma is identified.

Resolving marrow edema is seen involving the distal radius and ulna, in keeping with the known healing fractures. Mild regional osteopenic changes are seen involving the carpal bones.

Diffuse synovial thickening is noted around the wrist joint without significant joint effusion.

Peripheral nerves and muscles:

No focal mass, collection or obvious extrinsic compressive lesion is seen along the visualized median or ulnar nerves.

Diffuse mild IR hyper intensity involving the intrinsic muscles of the hand is noted, with associated atrophy predominantly involving the hypothenar muscle group.

The combination of muscle signal abnormality and atrophy is compatible with sub-acute denervation changes in the ulnar nerve distribution.

No focal tendon tear or significant soft-tissue collection is identified.

IMPRESSION:

Mild smooth thickening and increased IR signal of left ulnar nerve extending from distal arm across cubital tunnel into proximal forearm, consistent with ulnar neuropathy/ neuritis.

Sub-acute denervation changes involving ulnar-innervated muscles, particularly the flexor carpi ulnaris and intrinsic muscles of hand as detailed.

Mild resolving low-grade myofascial strain changes involving portions of flexor and extensor muscle groups, without significant muscle tear or haematoma.

Postoperative changes of distal radius fracture fixation with resolving marrow edema in distal radius and ulna. No significant fluid collection or haematoma.

Mild wrist synovial thickening and regional carpal osteopenic changes.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT ANKLE

Clinical profile: C/o Pain and swelling in right ankle x 6 months, severe and unable to walk x 10 days. H/o trauma 10 years back.

Technique: PD fs, T1, T2, IR, DWI, post contrast T1 in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Extensive destruction and erosions of articular parts of ankle, subtalar and distal tibiofibular joints are seen involving distal tibia, fibula, talus and calcaneus with multiple loose bodies and joint deformity.

Mild diffuse sclerosis is also seen in involved bones. Mild effusion with diffuse hypertrophic synovitis is seen in ankle and subtalar joints.

Abnormal signal intensity and post contrast enhancement is seen in involving distal tibia, fibula, lateral and medial malleolus, talus and calcaneus with patchy areas of marrow necrosis. No significant intraosseous collection with restricted diffusion is seen in the present study.

Mild diffuse subarticular IR hyperintensity and post contrast enhancement is seen involving all inter tarsal and tarsometatarsal joints without focal erosions. Trabecular stress fracture is seen in proximal part of 5th metatarsal bone.

No other significant abnormality seen in rest of the visualized bones and joints.

Soft tissue:

Diffuse tenosynovitis of all medial and lateral tendons is seen with hypertrophic synovial thickening and fluid collection. Extension of tenosynovitis is seen in foot and great toe regions also.

Tendinosis with longitudinal tears of peroneal longus and brevis tendons are seen.

Diffuse IR hyperintensity is seen in all the visualized muscles in foot regions, suggestive of myoneuropathy changes. However, no significant necrosis is seen. Rest of the visualized tendons appears grossly intact.

Diffuse edematous changes are seen in subcutaneous fat planes in ankle and foot regions. No significant skin/ soft tissue defect or enhancing sinus tract seen in the present study. No other soft tissue fluid collection or diffusion restriction is seen.

Rest of the visualized soft tissue appears grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Features are suggestive of Charcot neuro-osteoarthropathy involving ankle and foot regions as detailed.

Diffuse tenosynovitis of medial and peroneal tendons, peroneal tendinosis with longitudinal tears as detailed.

Diffuse soft tissue edema and myoneuropathy changes in foot muslces as detailed. No sinus tract or skin defect seen.

The possibility of superimposed infection with osteomyelitis and septic arthritis has to be ruled out. Suggested clinical correlation, fluid analysis, further evaluation and review as indicated.

Screening of rest of the spine: IR sagittal. CT correlation.

The lumbosacral spine displays a normal lordotic curvature and vertebral column alignment.

Mild acute to subacute anterior wedge compression fracture along the inferior endplate is seen at L5 vertebral level with marrow edema. No significant lytic areas, soft tissue component diffusion restriction or fluid collection seen in the present study.  About 20% height reduction is seen without posterior cortical retropulsion or spinal canal compromise.  Likely benign osteoporotic vertebral compression fracture.

Post-treatment changes are seen in the pelvis region.

Rest of the individual vertebrae are normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities. No significant focal lesion is seen in vertebrae.

Multilevel disc desiccation is seen with mild facetal arthropathy at few levels. The intervertebral discs are normal in heights. Rest of the vertebral end-plates are normal.

L5-S1: Mild disc bulge is seen. No mass effect over nerve roots.

The conus medullaris ends at L1 level and the cauda equine is normal in appearance.

The prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues are grossly normal.

Both SI joints show mild degenerative changes.

Multilevel disc desiccation is seen. Uncovertebral arthropathy and disc changes causing mild anterior thecal sac indentation are seen at C5-6 and C6-7 levels. No spinal cord signal changes are seen.

No other significant abnormalities are seen.

Screening of dorsal spine:

Disc desiccation and ligamentum flavum thickening are seen at few levels. Spinal cord appears normal.

No other significant abnormalities are seen.

IMPRESSION:

Mild acute to subacute compression fracture of L5 vertebral body as detailed, likely benign osteoporotic compression fracture.

Mild diffus7e degenerative changes of spine as detailed.

No significant focal lesion in spine.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Dr.P.Silambarasi

MRI SCAN OF DORSAL SPINE AND SCREENING OF REST OF SPINE

Clinical Profile: H/o fall, c/o low backache since then for 3 weeks (MRI elsewhere on 14.04.2022 –Old D12 compression fracture), c/o left lower limb pain

Technique: Sagittal T1, T2, IR, Axial T2, IR Coronal for SI joints, IR coronal

Screening of rest of the spine: T2/ IR sagittal

D12 vertebra:

Acute burst fracture involving superior and inferior endplates and posterior cortex is seen involving D12 vertebral body with about <25% height reduction. No significant lytic area/ soft tissue component or fluid collection seen in the present study.

Mild retropulsion of posterior cortex, small disc extrusion, thin epidural soft tissue edema and haemorrhage are seen causing secondary spinal canal stenosis at D12 and D12-L1 levels and compression of conus medullaris and bilateral nerve roots. Residual thecal sac measures about 9.3 x 6 mm (TRA x AP).

Mild edema and small annular tears are seen in D11-12 and D12-L1 discs. Mild sprain of anterior and posterior ligament complex is seen.  No complete disruption is seen.

Mild soft tissue contusion changes are seen in pre and bilateral paravertebral soft tissue and psoas muscles.

Rest of the dorsal spine:

Mild trabecular compression with minimal edema is seen along the superior endplates of D10 and D11 vertebrae. Mild marrow oedema is also seen in L1 vertebral body.

Diffuse heterogeneous marrow signal is seen in the visualised vertebrae without significant IR hyperintensity or focal lesion, likely red marrow reconversion changes.

Multilevel disc desiccation is seen. Rest of the intervertebral discs are normal in heights. Rest of the vertebral end-plates are normal.

Ligamentum flavum hypertrophy is seen at D10-11 level indenting the spinal cord.

Subtle suspicious T2/ IR hyperintensity is seen in the conus medullaris region, may represent edema/ contusion. Rest of the spinal cord appears grossly normal.

The conus medullaris ends at L1 level and the cauda equine is grossly normal in appearance.

Rest of the prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues are grossly normal.

Screening of cervical spine:

Straightening of cervical spine is seen with disc desiccation at all levels and mild disc bulge at C5-6 level. No spinal cord signal changes are seen.

No other significant abnormality seen in cervical spine.

A nodule measuring approximately 1.2 x 0.6 cm is seen in left lobe of thyroid.  Suggested ultrasound correlation.

Screening of lumbar spine:

Grade I anterolisthesis of L4 over L5 vertebra is seen. Severe facetal arthropathy is seen at this level. No spondylolysis is seen.

Disc desiccation is seen at all levels with mild endplate changes, disc bulge and facetal arthropathy at multiple levels. Mild indentation of traversing nerve roots is seen at L4-5 level.

No other significant abnormality seen in lumbar spine.

IMPRESSION:

Burst fracture of D12 vertebra with ligament/ soft tissue changes as detailed.

Secondary spinal canal stenosis causing compression of conus medullaris and bilateral nerve roots as detailed.

Subtle suspicious T2/ IR hyperintensity in conus medullaris region, may represent edema/ contusion.

Diffuse degenerative changes of spine with L4-5 anterolisthesis as mentioned.

No other significant abnormality in spine.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Dr. Arrthe

MRI SCAN OF LEFT FOOT

Clinical profile: H/o left great toe amputation few weeks back. Now with gangrene of left 2nd and 3rd toes with superadded infection. K/c/o DM, HTN.

Technique: PD fs, T1, IR, DWI, GRE and PC T1 in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Left great toe and anterior half of 1st metatarsal bones are not visualized with loss of adjacent soft tissue, consistent with post-surgical status.

Multiple air pockets with abnormal marrow signal are seen in all the phalanges of 2nd toe, suggestive of emphysematous osteomyelitis.

Small fracture with edema is seen involving head of 5th metatarsal bone with arthritis of 5th MTP joint.

Mild degenerative changes are seen in ankle ad foot joints.

Soft tissue:

Acute post-operative changes with soft tissue defect are seen in forefoot region. Extensive adjacent soft tissue inflammatory/ edematous changes are seen in forefoot region around 1st, 2nd and 3rd toe regions with multiple small air pockets. Patchy areas of non-enhancing soft tissue are seen, suggestive of necrosis around 2nd and 3rd toes.

Minimal fluid is seen in the post-operative site. However, no significant fluid collection is seen in the present study.

Diffuse myoneuropathy changes are seen in visualized muscles of foot region. Mild tenosynovitis of flexor tendons is seen.

Diffuse edematous changes are seen in subcutaneous fat planes and soft tissue in ankle and foot regions.

IMPRESSION:

Post-operative status with soft tissue changes as mentioned.

Features of emphysematous osteomyelitis, soft tissue necrosis and infection in left forefoot region as detailed. No significant fluid collection.

Midfoot joint and bone changes as mentioned, may represent early Charcot neuro-osteoarthropathy features.

Extensive soft tissue edematous changes in ankle and foot regions.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Dr.Abdulla

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: Pain and reduced movements in right shoulder joint for past 1 year.  No h/o injury.

Technique: PD fs, T1, T2 fs, GRE in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joint:

Minimal joint fluid is seen with extension to biceps tendon sheath. Mild synovial thickening is also seen in the joint.

Rest of shoulder joint and articulating bones appear grossly normal for age.

Rotator cuff:

Chronic full thickness tear is seen involving supraspinatus tendon (AP dimension of 2.5 cm). Retracted torn end is attenuated, frayed and is seen at joint level, about 3.5 cm from insertion. Small anterior part of supraspinatus tendon appears intact with severe tendinosis and attenuation.

Subscapularis tendinosis is seen with partial thickness articular tear with intrasubstance extension. Partial thickness tear is also seen in infraspinatus tendon with extension to MTJ.

Mild atrophy of supraspinatus and mild to moderate atrophy of subscapularis muscles is seen with stage I/ II fatty changes (Goutallier’s classification).

Teres minor tendon and muscle appears normal. Mild fatty changes are seen in deltoid muscle also.

Tendinosis of LHBT is seen with medial subluxation between fibres of subscapularis tendon.

Labrum and ligamentous structures:

Degenerative changes with chronic tear are seen in anterosuperior part of glenoid labrum. No acute tear or displaced fragment is seen.

Chronic disruption of biceps pulley is seen. No other definite capsular or ligamentous disruption seen.

AC joint:

AC joint appears grossly normal. The acromion is of type II morphology and is laterally sloping with prominent acromial spur.

Grossly reduced sub acromial space is seen (2 mm) with mild subacromial bursitis.

IMPRESSION:

Chronic full thickness tear of supraspinatus tendon as detailed.

Tendinosis, partial thickness tears and muscle changes of rotator cuff as detailed.

Minimal joint effusion and labroligamentous changes as detailed.

Laterally sloping acromion with spur, reduced subacromial space and bursitis. Imaging features are likely due to subacromial impingement. Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: C/o right shoulder pain for 2 months, more severe for 1 week, not able to lift right shoulder, also c/o pain in both lower limbs, radiating to left lower limb, associated with numbness? CVA

Technique: PD fs, T1, T2 fs, GRE in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joint:

Osteoarthrosis is seen with cartilage loss in superior aspect, osteophytes and tiny subarticular cysts. Superior migration of humeral head is seen against under surface of acromion process. Increased sclerosis of acromion is seen, suggestive of Rotator cuff tear arthropathy

Mild joint effusion is seen with mild synovitis. No osteochondral loos body is seen.

Rest of shoulder joint and articulating bones appear grossly normal for age.

Rotator cuff:

Chronic full thickness tear is seen involving entire supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendons (AP dimension of 4.5 cm). Retracted torn end is attenuated, frayed and is seen at joint level, about 3.5 cm from insertion.

Severe tendinosis with high grade partial to full thickness tear are seen in cranial part of subscapularis tendon.

Moderate atrophy of supraspinatus (grade II/ III fatty changes), severe atrophy of infraspinatus and teres minor muslces (grade IV fatty changes) and mild atrophy of subscapularis muscle (grade I fatty changes) is seen. (Goutallier’s classification).

Small tear of fibres of deltoid muscle is seen at its attachment to acromion process with mild retraction and adjacent soft tissue strain changes. Rest of the deltoid muscle appears grossly normal.

Chronic full thickness tear of LHBT is seen with distal retracted end in arm region.

Labrum and ligamentous structures:

Degenerative changes with chronic tear are seen in superior glenoid labrum. Diffuse attenuated labrum is seen. Labral ossification is seen in posterosuperior aspect, measuring about 3.3 x 1.9 x 1.3 cm. No acute tear or displaced fragment is seen.

Chronic disruption of biceps pulley is seen. No other definite capsular or ligamentous disruption seen.

AC joint:

Grossly reduced sub acromial space is seen with mild subacromial bursitis.

IMPRESSION:

Chronic massive full thickness tears of rotator cuff tendons with muscle changes and rotator cuff tear arthropathy as detailed.

Mild joint effusion, synovitis, labroligamentous changes, labral ossification and LHBT tear as detailed.

Severe AC joint arthropathy with multiloculated ganglion cysts as detailed.

Small tear of deltoid muscle with adjacent soft tissue strain changes.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
MRI SCAN OF LUMBOSACRAL SPINE AND SCREENING OF REST OF SPINE

Clinical Profile: Low back pain since 1 year with recent behavioural disturbances? AS, No known comorbidities.

Technique: Sagittal T1, T2, IR, Axial T2, IR Coronal for SI joints, PC T1 fs axial and coronal

Screening of rest of the spine: T2 sagittal, IR sagittal and axial, T2 space, DWI, PC T1 fs axial and coronal.

The lumbosacral spine displays a normal lordotic curvature and vertebral column alignment.

Imaging features of multifocal osteomyelitis/ spondylitis are seen involving body of posterior elements of multiple vertebrae and pelvis bones. Diffuse sclerosis is seen in the regions of involved bones.

Multilevel spondylodiscitis changes with infected fluid collections (abscesses) are also seen as detailed below:

L5-S1 level:

Abnormal marrow signal changes with post contrast enhancement are seen involving L5 and S1 vertebra with L5-S1 disc involvement. The signal changes are seen extending to the upper sacral vertebrae also. Destruction of superior endplate of S1 vertebra is seen.

Infected fluid collection with diffusion restriction and smooth rim enhancement is seen in anterior epidural space, pre and paravertebral regions as follows:

The paravertebral fluid collection extends from L3 to S3 levels and measures about 15.1 x 5.8 x 1.2 cm (CC x TR x AP). There is extension of the collection into bilateral (L>R) psoas muscles [3.6 x 2.8 x 1.6 cm on the right side & 11.3 x 4.6 x 3.7 cm on the left side], along right iliacus and also into the left gluteal compartment through the S1, S2 and S3 neural foramina.

The anterior epidural component measures 2.7 x 2.1 x 0.7 cm (TR x CC x AP) in this level and also into bilateral neural foramen. It causes secondary spinal canal narrowing and bilateral narrowing of neural foramen and compression of bilateral traversing and exiting nerve roots.

D7-8 level:

Similar signal changes with involvement of intervening intervertebral disc is seen at D7-D8 level. Anterior prevertebral collection with diffusion restriction is seen extending between D7 to D9 levels measuring about 3.7 x 3.2 x 1.1 cm (TR x CC x AP). It is seen extending to right neural foramen and epidural region at D8-9 level compressing exiting nerve roots and further extension along D7-8 and D8-9 intercostal spaces on right side.

Mild inflammatory changes are also noted in D10 level along its posterior elements and transverse processes.

Small collections are also noted adjacent to lamina of D8 vertebra on right side.

C5-6 level:

Abnormal marrow changes are seen in C5 and C6 vertebrae with diffuse sclerosis and destruction of superior part of C6 vertebra and involvement of C5-6 disc.

Anterior epidural and right paravertebral collection/ abscess are seen as follows: The anterior epidural component is more on the right side and measures 1.7 x 1.5 x 0.5 cm (CC x TR x AP). It is causing mass effect with indentation of right hemi cord and compressing right exiting nerve root. It is seen communicating with right anterior paravertebral collection which extends from C4 to D1 vertebral levels and measuring about 7.8 x 0.7 x 0.9 (CC x AP x TR).

Rest of the vertebrae and discs appear normal.

Spinal cord appears grossly normal in thickness and signal intensity. The conus medullaris ends at L1 level and the cauda equine is normal in appearance.

No abnormal of nerve roots or spinal meninges is seen.

Both SI joints appear grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Multilevel spondylodiscitis with epidural and pre/ paravertebral infected fluid collections at cervical, dorsal and lumbosacral levels causing mass effect over spinal cord and nerve roots as detailed.

Multifocal osteomyelitis/ spondylitis in multiple vertebrae and pelvis bones as detailed.

Bilateral psoas and left gluteal abscess as detailed.

Features are consistent with infective etiology (Likely Tuberculosis). Suggested clinical correlation and further evaluation as indicated.

Rest of the extensor tendons appear normal.   

Rest of soft tissue:

Rest of the visualised soft tissue appear grossly normal.

Screening of left wrist:

Similar changes are also seen in left wrist joint.

IMPRESSION:

Focal erosions with bone changes, extensive synovitis, joint effusion and ankylosis in right wrist region as detailed.

Mild synovitis in 3rd MCP joint with mild flexor and extensor tendon sheath inflammation as detailed.

No other significant abnormality seen.

Rotator cuff:

Supraspinatus tendinosis is seen with partial-thickness articular surface (<50% thickness) tear is seen at foot print region of anterior margin and small partial-thickness interstitial tear involving posterior supraspinatus.

Mild subscapularis tendinosis is seen with small chronic intrasubstance tear. No full-thickness rotator cuff tear or tendon retraction.

LHBT tendinosis is seen. The deltoid muscle is also normal.

Labroligamentous structures:

Degenerative labral changes  are seen with small chronic tears involving anteroinferior, anterosuperior, superior and posterosuperior quadrants. No displaced fragment is seen.

Mild capsular and synovial thickening is seen in rotator interval and axillary recess regions. Thickening with increased signal intensity of biceps pulley and anterior IGHL are seen.

Mild disc bulges and uncovertebral arthropathy are seen at few levels causing mild indentation over the anterior thecal sac. No significant mass effect over cord or nerve roots seen.

Spinal cord appears normal.

No other significant abnormality seen in screening of cervical spine.

Rotator cuff tendinosis with small partial thickness tears as detailed.

Mild capsulitis, minimal effusion and labroligamentous changes as detailed.

AC joint arthropathy with reduced subacromial space and subacromial bursitis, likely suggestive of subacromial impingement.

MRI SCAN OF BONY PELVIS (PLAIN)

Clinical profile: H/o fall injury and femur fractures. For detailed evaluation.

Technique:  T1, IR, T2, DWI, PDfs, GRE for bony pelvis in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

An ill-defined mass lesion with significant diffusion restriction and measuring approximately 8.5 x 6.7 x 5.3 cm is seen in right iliac bone. Patchy mixed lytic/ sclerotic area is seen in involved bone with periosteal reaction/ matrix mineralisation. No significant fluid collection is seen.  Indentation, edema and mass effect over adjacent right iliopsoas and gluteal muscles is seen.

Multiple lytic/ sclerotic lesions of varying sizes are seen involving all the bilateral pelvic bones, visualised lower lumbar vertebrae and bilateral proximal femurs.

Displaced fracture is seen in right proximal femur at sub trochanteric region and involving lesser trochanter also. Mixed lytic/ sclerotic lesion is seen in the region of fracture, consistent with pathological fracture. Similar pathological fracture is also seen in left femora neck in sub capital position.

Fracture with mild reduction of vertebral height (about 25%) is seen involving L4 vertebral body. Bilateral chronic L5 spondylolysis is seen.

Minimal effusion is seen in left hip joint.

Right hip joint appears grossly normal.

Soft tissue:

Heterotopic ossification is seen involving left iliopsoas muscles upto insertion.

Soft tissue contusion changes are seen in bilateral thigh muscles with strain and oedema along the fascial planes.  Mild oedematous changes are also seen in bilateral gluteal muscles. No other significant fluid collection is seen in the present study.

Visualised pelvic structures:

Abnormal ill-defined T2 hypo intensity with diffusion restriction is seen in both halves of prostate gland involving central gland and peripheral zones. Focal capsular bulge is also seen on right side.

A lymph node measuring 1.2 cm in SAD is seen along left common iliac vessels.

No other significant abnormality seen in the visualised lower abdominal and pelvic region.

IMPRESSION:

Multiple focal lesions of varying sizes in pelvic bones, proximal femurs and lumbar vertebrae, largest in right iliac bone as detailed.  Imaging features suggest the possibility of bone metastasis.

Pathological fractures in bilateral proximal femurs and L4 vertebra as detailed.

Soft tissue contusion and myofascial strain changes in bilateral thigh regions as detailed.

Heterotopic ossification involving left iliopsoas muscles.

Abnormal signal intensity in prostate gland with left iliac node as detailed. The possibility of prostate malignancy has to be ruled out.

Early reversal of cervical spine is seen with disc desiccation and uncovertebral arthropathy at few levels. Disc protrusion and uncovertebral arthropathy causing mild indentation of cord is seen at C5-6 level.

Screening of lumbar spine:

Small chronic Schmorl's nodes are seen at multiple levels with mild disc bulge at few levels.

No significant mass effect over nerve roots.

No other significant abnormality seen in lumbar spine.

Screening of orbits:

No significant abnormality is seen in both orbits.

Screening of brain:

(Suboptimal study due to susceptibility artefacts):

No obvious enhancing foci/ leptomeningeal enhancement is seen

IMPRESSION:

Multifocal T2/ IR signal changes in spinal cord involving cervical, upper dorsal and conus medullaris regions without significant enhancement as detailed.

Mild degenerative changes of spine as mentioned.

In view of imaging features, the possibility of acute demyelination/ myelitis can be considered, likely of para infectious/ autoimmune etiology. Suggested clinical and CSF correlation and further evaluation as indicated.

Rest of the visualized osseous structures and joint spaces are unremarkable.

Ligament complex:

The anterior talofibular ligament, calcaneofibular ligament, posterior talofibular ligament, deltoid ligament complex, distal tibiofibular syndesmotic ligaments, and remaining visualized ligaments are intact.

No significant sinus tarsi inflammatory changes.

Rest of the soft tissue appears normal.

Mild lateral/ posterolateral ankle synovitis, predominantly along ATFL/ PTFL region, with minimal ankle and subtalar joint effusion.

Mild diffuse subcutaneous edema involving right ankle and dorsum of foot, without focal collection or abscess.

No significant abnormality in Achilles tendon.

No acute osseous or significant ligamentous abnormality.

MRI OF LUMBOSACRAL SPINE AND SCREENING OF REST OF THE SPINE

Clinical Profile: C/o neck stiffness while turning to left side and looking up for 1 year? Ankylosing spondylitis.

Technique: Sagittal, T1, T2, IR, Axial T2, T1 and IR Coronal for SI joints, Screening of rest of the spine – T2 and IR sagittal, CT correlation.

Findings:

Features of axial spondyloarthropathy:

Extensive bilateral facet joint ankylosis involving the cervical, thoracic and multiple lumbar vertebral levels is seen.

Ankylosis of multiple bilateral costovertebral and costotransverse articulations is seen throughout the thoracic spine.

Thin flowing ossification of anterior and posterior longitudinal ligaments is seen at multiple cervical levels.

Bilateral sacroiliac joint ankylosis is seen, more pronounced on the left.

Bilateral ankylosis of atlanto-occipital joints is seen.

Active inflammatory lesions:

Multiple anterior vertebral corner marrow oedematous lesions involving thoracic and lumbar spine demonstrating STIR hyper intensity, consistent with active Romanus lesions.

Active disco vertebral inflammatory change (Andersson-type disco vertebral lesion) is seen at the D7-D8 level, characterised by adjacent endplate marrow edema.

Mild active inflammatory marrow oedema is seen involving a few costovertebral and costotransverse articulations.

Overall appearances are consistent with mild active inflammation superimposed on advanced chronic structural changes of Ankylosing spondylitis.

Rest of the lumbar spine:

Sacralisation of L5 vertebra is seen with fusion of left transverse process and sacrum, suggestive of Castellvi type IIIa lumbosacral transitional vertebra.

The lumbosacral spine displays a normal mild loss of normal lordosis and with normal vertebral column alignment.

Rest of the individual vertebrae are normal in heights, morphology.

The intervertebral discs are normal in heights and hydration. Rest of the vertebral end-plates are normal.

D12-L1 to L3-4: No significant disc bulge or mass effect over nerve roots seen.

L4-5: Mild diffuse disc bugle and facetal arthropathy are seen. No significant mass effect over nerve roots seen.

L5-S1: No significant abnormality seen.

The conus medullaris ends at D12-L1 level and the cauda equine is normal in appearance.

The prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues are grossly normal.

Screening of rest of cervical and dorsal spine:

Mild loss of cervical lordosis is seen with mild disc desiccation at few levels. Mild exaggerated kyphosis of upper dorsal spine is seen.

Flaval hypertrophy is seen at few dorsal levels.

Spinal cord appears normal. No other significant abnormality seen.

IMPRESSION:

Advanced Ankylosing spondylitis (axial spondyloarthritis) with extensive chronic structural ankylosis in vertebrae and SI joints as detailed.

Mild superimposed active inflammatory disease in vertebrae and SI joints.

Castellvi Type IIIA lumbosacral transitional vertebra.

No spinal cord abnormality, epidural inflammatory mass, significant spinal canal stenosis, or acute vertebral fracture.

Mild degenerative changes of spine as mentioned.

Suggested clinical correlation/ further evaluation and review as indicated.

No focal herniation of meninges or neural contents beyond the spinal canal is seen.

Spinal cord appears grossly normal. No significant abnormality is seen.

Features are suggestive of closed spinal dysraphism with spinal bifida, intradural lipoma with focal extra spinal extension and low lying tethered spinal cord as detailed.

Clinical profile: H/o RTA with CV Junction fractures.

CV junction:

Minimally displaced, mild comminuted fractures are seen involving bilateral occipital condyles (L>R). Anterior extension of fracture to basilar part of occipital bone is seen. No other significant fractures are seen in craniovertebral junction.

Minimal fluid is seen in both lateral Atlanto-axial joints. However, no abnormal widening of joint is seen. Atlantodental joint appears normal.

Mild sprain with subtle waviness of apical and cruciate ligaments are seen. However no complete disruption is seen.

Grade I sprain of posterior atlantooccipital membrane, posterior atlantoaxial ligament is seen. No disruption is seen.

Anterior atlantooccipital membrane, anterior atlantoaxial ligament, alar ligaments, transverse ligament and tectorial membranes are intact. ALL and PLL appear intact.

Rest of the cervical spine:

Prevertebral hematoma is seen from base of skull to C4 vertebral level with maximum thickness of 1 cm.

Thin anterior epidural haemorrhage/ soft tissue thickening are seen from C1-2 to D1-2 levels with maximum thickness of 3 mm. Mild mass effect is seen over the dural sac with partial effacement of anterior CSF space in these levels. No significant mass effect over spinal cord is seen.

No significant abnormalities are seen. No fracture/ dislocation seen.

Screening of lumbar spine:

The conus medullaris ends at D12 level and the cauda equine is normal in appearance.

Posterior annular fissure is seen at L3-4 and L4-5 levels. No fracture/ dislocation seen.

No other significant abnormalities are seen.

IMPRESSION:

Minimally displaced bilateral occipital condyle fractures with mild sprain of CVJ ligaments and prevertebral hematoma as detailed.

reports.fullText:
Dr.Aathithya

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT SHOULDER JOINT WITH C-SPINE SCREENING

Clinical profile: Recurrent right shoulder dislocation, for evaluation.

Technique: PD fs, T1, GRE, T2 fs in all planes and CT correlation

Bones and joints:

A Hill-Sachs impaction defect is seen along the posterolateral aspect of the humeral head, measuring approximately 25 × 17 × 6.4 mm (CC × transverse × depth), with associated marrow edema, suggesting a recent/recurrent impaction injury.

No acute bony Bankart fracture or associated marrow edema is seen.

Chronic osseous bone loss of the anteroinferior glenoid is noted, measuring approximately 14.1% of the glenoid width by the width method.

No osseous bridge is seen between the rotator cuff footprint and the lateral margin of the Hill-Sachs defect. The calculated glenoid track measures 18.6 mm, while the Hill-Sachs interval measures 17 mm. Thus, the Hill-Sachs interval remains within the glenoid track, with approximately 1.6 mm of residual track, consistent with an on-track bipolar bone-loss lesion.

Mild to moderate joint effusion is seen. Cartilage injury is seen in anteroinferior aspect.

A fat-containing soft-tissue component is seen within the anterior axillary recess, measuring approximately 23 × 12 × 7 mm demonstrating internal fat signal with mild susceptibility blooming on GRE images. No corresponding osseous or osteochondral fragment is identified on CT.

Rest of articulating bones are normal in outline and marrow signal.

Rotator cuff:

Mild strain changes are seen in supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendons with a small intrasubstance tear in supraspinatus tendon. No other significant tear or retraction of fibres is seen.

Mild grade I/ II myofascial strain changes are seen involving subscapularis muscle and adjacent fascial planes with tendinosis and few small intrasubstance tears.

Long head of biceps appears grossly intact with strain changes. Rest of muscles and tendons of rotator cuff appear grossly normal. The deltoid muscle is normal.

Labroligamentous structures:

Chronic tear is seen involving anteroinferior labrum with adjacent periosteal injury.  The tear is also seen extending into the anterosuperior, superior and posterosuperior aspect of the labrum.

Sprain of anterior band of IGHL, biceps pulley and adjacent capsule are seen. No complete disruption or waviness is seen.

AC joint:

Mild AC joint arthropathy is seen. Type I acromion is seen and is laterally sloping.

Sub acromial space measures 5.6 mm. No other significant abnormality seen. Rest of the soft tissue appear grossly normal.

Screening of cervical spine:

Loss of cervical lordosis is seen with disc desiccation at almost all levels.

Multilevel disc bulge and uncovertebral arthropathy noted, more prominent at C3-4 and C5-6 levels.

C3-4: Disc bulge and right uncovertebral arthropathy are seen causing mild indentation of right exiting C4 nerve root.

C5-6: Disc bulge and uncovertebral arthropathy are seen causing mild indentation of cord and bilateral ventral C6 nerve roots.

Spinal cord appears normal. No other significant abnormality is noted in the cervical spine.

IMPRESSION:

Features of chronic anterior glenohumeral instability with labral tear, glenoid bone loss, Hill Sachs lesion and joint effusion as detailed, suggestive of on-track bipolar bone-loss lesion.

Mild rotator cuff strain changes with small intrasubstance tears and capsuloligamentous injuries as detailed.

Mild AC joint arthropathy and myofascial strain changes as detailed.

Small focal fatty synovial proliferation within anterior axillary recess as detailed.

Cervical spondylosis with mass effect over nerve roots at C3-4 and C5-6 levels as mentioned.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Dr Sherene

CT OF LEFT KNEE

Clinical profile: H/o injury.

Acute comminuted split-depression fracture of the lateral tibial plateau is seen, with a maximum articular surface depression of approximately 6.7 mm. Findings are consistent with a Schatzker type II tibial plateau fracture.

An additional undisplaced fracture of the medial tibial spine (medial intercondylar eminence) is seen.

Moderate lipohemarthrosis is present within the knee joint. Two small intra-articular osseous loose bodies/ fragments are seen, the larger measuring approximately 6 × 4 mm.

Mild surrounding soft-tissue contusion/edema is seen adjacent to the fracture. No significant soft-tissue defect or loss is identified.

Few superficial varicose veins are noted around the knee and visualized leg.

A small benign-appearing sclerotic focus is seen in the proximal tibia, likely representing a bone island. Focal periosteal thickening is noted along the proximal fibula, without aggressive features.

The remainder of the visualized osseous structures and joint articulations show no significant abnormality.

IMPRESSION:

Acute comminuted split-depression fracture of lateral tibial plateau as detailed. (Schatzker type II tibial plateau fracture).

Associated undisplaced fracture of medial tibial spine.

Moderate knee joint lipohemarthrosis and small loose bodies.

Mild surrounding post-traumatic soft-tissue contusion/ edema.

MRI SCAN OF LEFT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: H/o left shoulder dislocation. H/o numbness, left shoulder pain and difficulty in lifting left upper limb.

Technique: PD fs in all planes, T1 sag, GRE axial, T2 IR coronal and CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Chronic healed partially fused bony Bankart lesion is seen involving the anteroinferior glenoid rim with irregular osseous remodeling and articular irregularity. The osseous fragment measures 13 × 5.5 × 4.5 mm (CC × TRA x AP). No displaced fragment or marrow edema is seen.

Quantitative assessment demonstrates approximately 13.8% anteroinferior glenoid bone loss by the glenoid width method excluding the fragment.

A Hill-Sachs impaction defect is present involving the posterolateral aspect of the humeral head, measuring approximately 21 × 21 × 6 mm (TRA x CC x Depth). Mild marrow edema is also seen, suggestive of recent dislocation.

No significant bone bridge is seen between rotator cuff attachment and lateral aspect of Hill-Sachs lesion. Glenoid track measures 18.5 mm. Hill-sachs interval measures 21 mm. Bipolar lesion is engaging, off-track lesion.

Old fractures are seen in mid third of right clavicle and lateral third of left clavicle.

Rest of the articulating bones is normal in outline and marrow signal intensities.

Rotator cuff:

Supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendinosis is seen.

Full thickness tear is seen involving posterior part of supraspinatus and anterior part of infraspinatus tendons (conjoined tendon region) from its insertion footprint region (AP dimension of 1 cm) and with retraction of fibres of about 6 mm from insertion.

Mild subscapularis tendinosis is seen with small chronic intrasubstance tear.

Rest of the rotator cuff tendons and muscles appear grossly normal. The deltoid muscle appears grossly normal.

Long head of biceps appears intact. The deltoid muscle is also normal.

Labroligamentous structures:

Anteroinferior labral tear of is seen extending to anterosuperior, superior and posterosuperior quadrants. Injury of adjacent scapular periosteum is seen. However, no significant medial displacement of labrum is seen.

Rest of the glenoid labrum appear grossly intact.

Chronic sprain/ scarring of the anterior band of the inferior glenohumeral ligament (IGHL), adjacent anterior capsule, and biceps pulley is seen.

No other definite capsular or ligamentous disruption noted.

AC joint:

Moderate AC joint arthropathy is noted. The acromion is of type II morphology

The sub acromial space is reduced (4.1 mm) with minimal sub acromial bursitis.

Rest of the soft tissue appears grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Chronic healed partially fused osseous Bankart lesion as detailed.

Hill-Sachs impaction defect with mild marrow edema, compatible with recent recurrent anterior shoulder dislocation.

Rotator cuff tendinosis with full thickness tear as detailed.

Labral tear and capsuloligamentous changes as detailed.

AC joint arthropathy, reduced subacromial space and minimal sub acromial bursitis as detailed, likely subacromial impingement.

Imaging features are suggestive of Off-track (engaging) bipolar instability lesion.  Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Chronic sprain of biceps pulley with synovial thickening in rotator interval space is seen.

No other definite capsular or ligamentous disruption noted.

Degenerative changes are seen in acromio-clavicular joint and the acromion is type 2 morphology.  Acromial spur and thickened coracoacromial ligament is seen with reduced sub acromial space measuring 4 mm.
