Chronic tear with attenuation, PASTA lesion, intramuscular cyst and muscle atrophy in supraspinatus muscle/ tendon as detailed.

Calcific tendinitis of infraspinatus with sub acromial bursitis.

Clinical profile: C/o pain in right shoulder with difficulty in initiation of abduction - 6 months. Impingement of right shoulder, rotator cuff/ supraspinatus tear. No h/o recent trauma.

Rotator cuff:

Chronic full thickness tear is seen involving entire supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendons (AP dimension of 4.3 cm). Retracted torn end is attenuated, frayed and is seen at mid humeral head level, about 2.3 cm from insertion.

Severe subscapularis tendinosis is seen with partial thickness articular surface tears (about 25-50% thickness). Mild teres minor tendinosis is also seen.

Mild atrophy with grade I fatty changes of supraspinatus, and mild to moderate atrophy with grade II fatty changes of infraspinatus muscles are seen. (Goutallier’s classification).

Chronic full thickness tear of supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendons with muscles changes as detailed.

reports.fullText:
Dr Prakhyath

MRI SCAN OF LEFT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: H/o acute onset pain in left shoulder region since 15 days. H/o uncontrolled DM since 10 years. No h/o trauma, weakness or numbness.

Technique: PD fs, T1, GRE, T2 fs in all planes, DWI axial and sagittal, T2 axial, post contrast T1, IR. 

Bones and joints:

Abnormal ill-defined marrow signal with post contrast enhancement is seen in left proximal femur suggestive of acute osteomyelitis. Multiple discrete and serpiginous intramedullary collections with diffusion restriction are seen in the region of osteomyelitis, suggestive of intramedullary abscess formation. No significant cortical destruction is seen.

Mild similar abnormal marrow signal and contrast enhancement is also seen involving spine/ adjacent part of body of left scapula, suggestive of acute osteomyelitis.

Mild synovitis is seen in AC joint with possible extension to the adjacent collection. The possibility of septic arthritis of AC joint has to be ruled out.  No sinus tract or skin opening is seen in the present study.

Mild joint effusion without diffusion restriction and mild synovitis is seen. The possibility of early infection could not be ruled out.

The shoulder joint is normal with respect to joint space and alignment.

Rest of the visualized bones appears grossly normal.

Rotator cuff and subacromial bursa:

Large ill defined, likely communicating, fluid collection is seen involving the entire extent the subacromial/ sub deltoid bursa in anterior, posterior and lateral aspects. The fluid collection shows central diffusion restriction and rim enhancement and measures approximately 8 x 6.3 x 4 cm, suggestive of abscess formation. No air pockets are seen.

Multiple extensions of the collection is seen medially all around the supraspinatus muscle, along the infraspinatus muscle, both sides of spine of scapula and anteromedially along the neurovascular bundle, largest collection measuring about 5 x 2.6 x 2.5 cm along anteromedial aspect.

Myositis features are seen involving supraspinatus, infraspinatus, deltoid and parts of trapezius, teres minor, short head and biceps and coracobrachialis muscles.

Extensive soft tissue inflammation is seen in the adjacent fat planes, fascia and biceps tendon sheath.

No significant full thickness tear of rotator cuff tendons is seen.

Labroligamentous structures:

The glenoid labrum appears normal. No tear or displaced fragment is seen. 

Biceps pulley is intact. No definite capsular or ligamentous disruption seen.

Screening of right shoulder:

No abnormal IR hyperintense signal changes/ fluid collection seen. 

IMPRESSION:

Features are suggestive of acute osteomyelitis involving left proximal humerus and parts of left scapula with possible AC joint infective arthritis.

Multiple small intra osseous abscess formation in left proximal humerus.

Large abscess formation in subacromial bursa with extensions along the fascia of rotator cuff muscles and neurovascular structures as detailed.

Features of myositis involving rotator cuff and adjacent left shoulder region muscles and adjacent soft tissue inflammation as detailed.

Mild left shoulder joint effusion and synovitis.

Clinical profile: H/o left shoulder dislocation while playing pickle ball at around 10 PM  on 29.08.2026. H/o previous shoulder dislocation 4 years back.

Technique: PD fs, T1, GRE, T2 fs in all planes and CT correlation.

Chronic osseous Bankart lesion is seen involving the anteroinferior glenoid rim with cortical irregularity and mild anteroinferior glenoid bone loss measuring approximately 7.1% by the width method.

Chronic Hill-Sachs impaction defect is present involving the posterosuperior humeral head, measuring approximately 18.2 x 24 × 7.8 mm (TR x CC x depth). Bone bridge between rotator cuff attachment and lateral aspect of Hill-Sachs lesion measures 4.5 mm.

Glenoid track measures 21.4 mm. Hill-Sachs interval measures 22.7 mm. The Hill-Sachs interval is more than the glenoid track, consistent with an engaging bipolar (off-track) lesion.

Mild acute marrow edema is noted in the posterosuperior aspect of humeral head adjacent to the hill sachs defect.

No acute fracture is identified within the humeral head or glenoid.

Mild glenohumeral joint effusion is present.

Remaining visualized osseous structures demonstrate preserved marrow signal.

Rotator cuff:

Mild supra and infraspinatus tendinosis is seen with small chronic intrasubstance tear.

No other significant acute tear or retraction of fibres is seen.

LHBT is intact. The deltoid muscle is also normal.

Chronic tear is seen involving anteroinferior labrum with periosteal stripping and focal cartilage injury. Extension of tear to anterosuperior and inferior quadrants is also seen. Rest of the glenoid labrum appears grossly normal.

Mild AC joint arthropathy is seen. The acromion is of type II morphology and is laterally sloping. Subacromial bursa appears grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

LIMITED MRI SCAN OF RIGHT FOOT (PLAIN)

Clinical profile: C/o right hallux toe ulcer x  1 month, No h/o DM, No h/o trauma.

Technique: T1, IR, T2, PDfs and DWI in all planes. CT correlation.

Suboptimal evaluation due to movement artefacts.

Bones and joints: 

Non visualisation of middle, distal phalanges and small part of head of proximal phalanx of 3rd toe is seen, consistent with post-operative changes.

Abnormal marrow IR hyperintensity with subtle cortical erosion along the plantar aspect is seen in distal phalanx of great toe, underlying the soft tissue ulcer.

Severe osteoarthrosis changes with subchondral cysts, reduced joint space, osteophytes, erosions, subarticular sclerosis, small loose bodies and loss of cartilage are seen involving multiple mid and hind foot joints, very severe in talonavicular articulation. Subluxation of talonavicular joint is seen with loss of arches and rocker bottom foot.

Extensive marrow edema is also seen in the involved bones with mild synovitis and minimal joint fluid in joints.

Rest of the visualised bones and joints appear grossly normal.

Tendons and rest of soft tissue:

Sinus tarsi inflammation is seen. 

Small soft tissue ulcer is seen in the plantar aspect of 1st toe with adjacent soft tissue inflammation. No e/o underlying fluid collection or sinus tract seen.

Diffuse and extensive edematous and inflammatory changes are seen in subcutaneous fat planes, predominantly in dorsolateral aspect of foot and ankle regions. No significant fluid collection is seen.

Diffuse IR hyperintensity, mild atrophy with fatty changes is seen involving the foot muscles, suggestive of myoneuropathy changes.

IMPRESSION:

Non visualisation of phalanges of 3rd toe, consistent with post-operative changes.

Patchy IR hyperintensity with subtle cortical erosions in distal phalanx of great toe, likely represent early acute osteomyelitis.

Severe osteoarthrosis changes involving mid and hind foot joints as detailed, likely suggestive of Charcot neuroosteo arthropathy.

Few patchy areas of blooming are seen in gradient images. No fluid levels are seen.

No matrix mineralisation or thickened trabecular seen within the lesion. Cortical breakthrough is seen at multiple points with extra osseous extension of soft tissue component. The zone is transition is narrow and the adjacent bone marrow appears normal.

The soft tissue component forms smooth lobulated contour and is seen causing mass effect/ compression of adjacent muscles like soleus and anterolateral compartment of muscles with altered fat planes. The possibility of involvement of the muscles could not be ruled out.

The mass lesion causes mass effect over peroneal and tibial nerves also. Acute tibial and peroneal nerve denervation changes are seen in soleus and anterolateral compartment muscles. Effacement of the intermuscular fat planes is seen with edema. No obvious invasion of neurovascular structures is seen.

Mild stress changes with edema are seen in lateral tibial plateau.

No other similar focal lesions are seen.

The knee joint is normal with respect to alignment and joint space.

No significant joint effusion noted.

Rest of the articulating bones are normal in outline and bone marrow signal intensity characteristics.

Meniscus:

The medial and lateral menisci are normal in configuration and signal intensities. No evidence of displaced tear or degeneration.

Collateral ligaments:

Altered signal intensity is seen in fibular insertion of lateral collateral ligament and biceps tendon. No significant tear is seen.

The medial collateral ligament along with the medial and lateral patellar retinacula is normal.

Cruciate ligaments:

The anterior cruciate and posterior cruciate ligaments are grossly intact and normal in signal intensity. No significant tear is seen.

The intermeniscal and meniscofemoral ligaments are also normal.

Posterolateral and posteromedial corner ligament complex appear normal.

Rest of soft tissue:

Mild thickening of quadriceps tendon is seen.

Rest of the extensor mechanism appears normal. Rest of the surrounding muscles and tendons and the neurovascular structures are grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

	Large expansile lytic lesion in proximal fibula with extensions, soft tissue component and mass effect as detailed.

	Acute tibial and common peroneal denervation changes in muscles, secondary to mass effect over nerves.

	No significant abnormality in knee joint/ rest of the bones.

In view of age of patient and imaging characteristics, the possibility of giant cell tumor is more likely. Suggested HPE correlation to rule out any malignant etiology.

Dr Naveen kumar

MRI SCAN OF LEFT ARM (WITH CONTRAST)

Clinical Profile: Known case of intramuscular Low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma involving the left triceps. Status post local excision in January 2026. Histopathology dated 16/02/2026 confirmed low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma. Follow-up PET/CT performed on 06/03/2026 showed no metabolically active disease. Present study is for surveillance. No new complaints of pain or swelling.

Comparison: Pre-operative MRI images are not available for comparison.

Technique:

Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the left arm performed using T1, STIR/IR, PD fat-suppressed, T2, GRE and DWI sequences. Pre- and post-contrast T1 fat-suppressed images were obtained in all three planes.

Findings:

Bones and Joints:

Visualized humerus and adjacent osseous structures demonstrate normal marrow signal intensity without focal osseous lesion.

The Ulnohumeral, radiocapitellar and proximal radioulnar joints are normally aligned.

Elbow joint is unremarkable without significant joint effusion or synovitis.

Ligaments:

The radial and ulnar collateral ligament complexes are intact.

No ligament tear or abnormal laxity is identified.

Soft Tissues:

Chronic postoperative changes are seen along the posterior aspect of the distal arm, approximately 5–6 cm proximal to the elbow joint, involving the skin, subcutaneous tissues and extending into the distal triceps muscle, consistent with postoperative scar tissue.

Areas of chronic hemosiderin deposition with blooming in gradient images are present within the distal triceps muscle and along the postoperative bed.

No focal soft tissue mass, diffusion restriction, abnormal nodular or mass-like enhancement, or other imaging evidence of residual or recurrent tumour is identified at the operative site.

No postoperative fluid collection or abscess is seen.

The visualized radial, median and ulnar nerves demonstrate normal calibre and signal intensity.

Remaining visualized muscles, tendons and soft tissues are unremarkable.

No significant regional lymphadenopathy is identified.

IMPRESSION:

Stable chronic postoperative changes involving posterior aspect of distal left arm and distal triceps muscle with associated postoperative scarring and chronic hemosiderin deposition.

No MRI evidence of residual or recurrent low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma at the operative site. No abnormal diffusion restriction or suspicious enhancing lesion.

No postoperative fluid collection or significant regional lymphadenopathy.

No osseous abnormality identified in the visualized left arm.

Recommendation:

Suggested clinical correlation and review/ follow up imaging as clinically indicated.

Varicose veins are seen in the left lower limb.

reports.fullText:
LIMITED MRI SCAN OF BRAIN AND ORBITS (PLAIN)

Clinical profile: C/o sudden reduced vision in both eyes, since 3 months. Completed ATT for pulmonary Tuberculosis in April. For detailed evaluation.

Technique: FLAIR axial, MPR T1, MRA, DWI for brain, IR and T1 coronal, T2 fs axial for orbits:

Contrast could not be given, due to abnormal renal function.

Brain:

Diffuse age related cerebral atrophy with extensive small vessel ischemic changes is seen.

Rest of the brain parenchyma shows normal signal on all sequences.

No acute infarct or haemorrhage is seen.

No other significant focal lesion or signal abnormality seen.

Ventricles, basal cisterns and cortical sulci appear normal for age.

Sella and suprasellar regions appear normal. No chiasmal compression is seen.

Orbits:

T1 hypo intensity/ T2 hyper intensity is seen in bilateral optic nerves involving prechiasmatic segments, optic chiasm and bilateral optic tracts, predominantly in central parts and in symmetrical fashion, suggestive of optic neuropathy. No diffusion restriction is seen. Peripheral rim is relatively spared. In view of history, the possibility of toxic optic neuropathy can be considered.

No abnormal thickening or thinning of the nerves is seen. No chiasmal compression is seen.

Both eyeballs appear normal in size and contour.

Bilateral extra ocular muscles appear normal.

Rest of the bilateral orbital contents appear normal.

IMPRESSION:

Abnormal signal intensity in optic pathway as detailed, likely toxic optic neuropathy.  Suggested clinical correlation.

Diffuse cerebral atrophy with extensive small vessel ischemic changes.

No other significant abnormality in brain and orbits.

reports.fullText:
MRI SCAN OF ORBITS AND BRAIN

Clinical profile: Known case of bilateral retinoblastoma, for detailed evaluation:

Technique: FLAIR axial for brain, obl sag, axial, coronal T2 and fs T2, T1 cor, post contrast T1 in all planes for orbits and post contrast MPR T1 for brain:

Orbits:

Right orbit:

Lobulated combined endophytic/ exophytic lesion is seen in postero-infero medial aspect of right eyeball which appear hyper in T1 and hypo in T2 when compared to vitreous and  measuring approximately 14.8 x 11.4 x 8.3 mm. The lesion shows heterogenous enhancement on post contrast images. Focal secondary retinal detachment is also seen which appears thickened. Involvement of partial thickness of adjacent choroid is seen. Abnormal smooth enhancement is also seen along anterior aspect of lens.

Another endophytic mass lesion measuring approximately 3.9 x 3 x 1.5 mm is seen in the anterosuperior quadrant.

No significant disruption of normal signal intensity/ enhancement of rest of choroid are seen.

Sclera appears normal.  No obvious extra slceral or orbital extension is seen.

Normal depth of the anterior chamber is seen. No abnormal expansion of the eyeball seen.

No abnormal enhancement of the optic nerve/ optic nerve sheath complex seen.

Rest of the right orbital contents appears normal.

Left orbit:

Multiple, at least 3, endophytic lesions of varying sizes are seen in posterosuperior part ( 5.5 x 5 x 4.1 mm), medial aspect of anteroinferior part ( 5.7 x 3.2 x 2 mm) and lateral aspect of anteroinferior part ( 6.9 x 4.3 x 2.5 mm) of eyeball.  Two of these lesions show possible involvement of enhancing choroid.

Small suspicious extra scleral soft tissue nodule with similar signal intensity is seen at the junction of medial rectus and eyeball causing mild focal inward indentation of sclera, measuring about 3 x 2 mm. (Best appreciated in T2 space).

Two tiny similar enhancing nodules are seen along the inferomedial aspect of left lens near ciliary body, likely deposits.

Rest of the choroid shows normal signal intensity/ enhancement.

Sclera appears normal.  No other obvious extra scleral or orbital extension is seen.

Normal depth of the anterior chamber is seen. No abnormal expansion of the eyeball seen.

No abnormal enhancement of the optic nerve/ optic nerve sheath complex seen.

Rest of the left orbital contents appears normal.

Brain:

No significant pineal/ suprasellar mass lesion seen.

The brain parenchyma shows normal signal on all sequences.

No other significant focal / diffuse altered signal noted.

Ventricles are normal.

Basal cisterns and cortical sulci are normal.

No significant leptomeningeal lesions are seen in the present study.

Multiple discrete lymph nodes are seen in the bilateral upper cervical regions, largest measuring approximately 6.1 mm in short axis diameter.  (Insignificant by size criteria).

IMPRESSION:

Bilateral, multifocal enhancing mass lesions with extensions/ and confined to eyeballs as detailed, consistent with retinoblastomas (R>L).

Small suspicious extra scleral nodule in left orbit as detailed.

No other significant abnormality in both orbits.

No significant abnormality in brain.

LIMITED MRI SCAN OF BRAIN AND ORBITS

Clinical profile: Pain followed by drooping of right upper eye lid 50 days back, underwent treatment, recurrent episode of eye lid pain and partial drooping.

Technique: FLAIR axial, MPR T1, MRA for brain, IR and T1 coronal, DWI, T2 fs axial for orbits, Post contrast T1 for brain and orbits. USG correlation.

Brain:

Brain parenchyma shows normal signal on all sequences.

Few scattered small vessel ischemic changes are seen in bilateral white matter.

No acute infarct or haemorrhage is seen.

Ventricles, basal cisterns and cortical sulci are normal for age.

Sella and suprasellar regions appear normal. No chiasmal compression is seen.

MRA: Bilateral prominent Pcoms are seen. No significant abnormality in intracranial arteries.

Dural venous sinuses appear normal. No features of venous thrombosis.

No abnormal parenchymal or meningeal enhancement is seen.

Orbits:

Right upper eyelid:

A well-defined smooth rim enhancing cystic lesion measuring approximately 10 x 8 x 8 mm is seen in the media aspect of upper eyelid. The cyst has thin hypointense wall and smooth rim enhancement. No calcification is seen. USG correlation showed multiple live worms inside the cyst.

Mild adjacent soft tissue inflammation is seen in adjacent preseptal soft tissue. No abnormal collection is seen.

Rest of the right orbital contents appear normal.

Left orbital contents appear normal.

Both eyeballs appear normal in size and contour.

Bilateral extra ocular muscles appear normal.

The optic nerves appear normal in thickness and signal intensity. No significant focal lesion or signal abnormality seen. Rest of the optic pathway appears normal.

Mild mucosal thickening is seen in bilateral maxillary, right frontal and bilateral anterior ethmoid sinuses, suggestive of sinusitis.

IMPRESSION:

Small well defined cystic lesion in right upper eyelid with adjacent inflammation as detailed. Features are suggestive of Filarial cyst.

Mild small vessel ischemic changes in brain.

No other significant abnormality in brain and orbits.

LIMITED MRI SCAN OF BRAIN AND ORBITS

Clinical profile: Multiple cranial nerve palsies on right side involving right II, V and VI? Orbital apex syndrome/ SOL. Known diabetic for many years. C/o pain on right side.        

Technique: FLAIR axial, MPR T1, MRA and DWI for brain, IR coronal, T2 fs axial for orbits, Post contrast T1 for brain and orbits. T2 Dixon for upper neck region. Limited CT correlation.

Brain:

Small chronic infarct with gliosis is seen in right frontal lobe.

Rest of the brain parenchyma shows normal signal on all sequences.

No acute infarct or hemorrhage is seen.

Ventricles are normal for age.

Sella and suprasellar regions appear normal.

MRA: Hypoplastic right vertebral artery and aplasia of right A1 segment are seen. Mild smooth narrowing is seen in cavernous segment of right ICA. However normal flow related signal is seen in distal vessels. No other significant abnormality in intracranial arteries for age.

Dural venous sinuses appear grossly normal. No features of venous thrombosis.

No abnormal parenchymal or leptomeningeal enhancement is seen.

Orbits and Para nasal sinuses:

Bilateral sphenoid and ethmoid sinusitis is seen. Cortical breaks involving walls of right sphenoid and posterior ethmoid sinuses and right  is seen, consistent with acute invasive sinusitis. No obvious T2 hypointense contents are seen.

Extension of acute inflammatory changes with contrast enhancement is seen extending to right orbital apex/ superior orbital fissure, right cavernous sinus, and masticator space and pterygopalatine fossa.  No abnormal fluid collection is seen.

Mild inflammation and edematous changes are seen in right orbital contents.

Smooth pachymeningeal enhancement is seen in right basifrontal and anterior temporal regions.

Both eyeballs appear normal in size and contour.

Left orbital contents appear normal. 

Bilateral optic nerve appears normal in thickness and signal intensity. No significant focal lesion or signal abnormality seen. No chiasmal compression is seen.

IMPRESSION:

Features of sinusitis and extensive inflammation in right upper neck spaces as detailed. In view of clinical and imaging features, to consider the possibility of acute invasive fungal sinusitis.

Extension of inflammation to right orbital apex/ cavernous sinus regions as detailed.

Small chronic infarct in right frontal lobe.

No other significant abnormality in brain and orbits.

reports.fullText:
MRI SCAN OF BRAIN

Clinical profile:

Technique: MPR T1, FLAIR Axial, T2 Coronal, DWI, SWI, 3D TOF MRA, T2 space.

The brain parenchyma is normal in signal intensity, morphology and gray-white matter differentiation.

No significant focal lesion or signal abnormality seen.

The deep gray matter and internal capsules are symmetrical and normal in signal intensity.

The periventricular and deep white matter display normal volume and signals.

The midbrain, pons and medulla are normal in morphology and signals.

The imaged cranial nerves are also normal.

The cerebellum and cerebellar peduncles are also normal.

The ventricular system is normal in size and appearance.

The sella turcica, pituitary gland and infundibulum appear normal. The suprasellar cistern and hypothalamic region are unremarkable for any pathology.

MRA: No significant abnormality seen in intracranial arteries.

The orbits and their contents are grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

No significant abnormality in brain.

Diffuse mild age-related atrophic changes of brain are seen with prominent sulci, fissures and cisterns.

Small vessel ischaemic changes are seen in bilateral white matter.  Small chronic lacunar infarcts are seen in left corona radiata.   

No acute infarct or haemorrhage is seen.

Dural venous sinuses appear normal. No features of venous thrombosis.

No abnormal parenchymal or meningeal enhancement is seen.

Bilateral hippocampal regions appear normal in volume, signal intensity, internal architecture and T2 relaxometry values.

Bilateral inner ear structures appear grossly normal. The endolymphatic duct and sac could not be clearly visualised. No mastoiditis or otitis media features are seen. (Meniere disease).

No significant abnormality seen in CP angle region.

Increased mineralisation is seen in bilateral deep gray matter. Nigrosome 1 (Dorsal nigral hyperintensity) could not be adequately assessed due to poor mineralisation of substantia nigra. No selective midbrain atrophy/ brainstem signal changes or cerebellar atrophy. No putaminal rim sign or putaminal atrophy seen.

Asymmetrical thinning of dorsal substantia nigra with indistinct visualization of nigrosome-1 on both sides - likely nigro-striatal dopaminergic neurodegeneration.

MSA:  No ‘hot cross bun sign’ or abnormal T2 hyperintensity in cerebellar peduncles and cerebellum. No significant putaminal atrophy or putaminal rim sign seen. No disproportionate atrophy of cerebellum and brainstem seen.

Left superior cerebellar artery is seen indenting root exit zone of left trigeminal nerve in the superomedial aspect. Mild deviation of nerve course is seen. No thinning of nerve is seen. Features are suggestive of grade II neurovascular conflict.

CSF flow studies however show aqueductal stroke volume - 16.5 ul (non-elevated)

CSF flow studies - value given above (16ul represents maximal forward volume while stroke volume ranges between 9-11.5 ul) - non elevated

Prominent CSF flow void is noted within posterior third ventricle and aqueduct.

Disproportionate ventriculomegaly with tight medial convexity sulcal spaces and reduced callosal angle with prominent CSF flow void - features s/o NPH

Suggested clinical and CSF correlation

MRI SCAN OF BRAIN

Clinical profile: C/o giddiness and memory loss for 8 months? Early Alzheimer’s disease? Corticobasal degeneration (CBD).

Technique: MPR T1, FLAIR Axial, T2 Coronal, DWI, SWI, 3D TOF MRA, T2 space.

Few scattered punctate T2/ FLAIR hyper intensities are seen in bilateral white matter and pons, s/o Fazekas grade I small vessel ischemic changes.

Hippocampus: Mild widening of B/L choroidal fissures is seen without dilatation of temporal horns or volume loss, s/o medial temporal lobe atrophy score 1.

Substantial parietal atrophy with widening of sulci is seen, suggestive of grade 2 Koedam parietal atrophy.

Global cerebral atrophy (GCA scale I/ II) is seen. No significant atrophy of frontal lobe or temporal pole is seen. No asymmetric cortical parietal atrophy is seen. No significant strategic area infarct is seen.

No acute infarct or hemorrhage is seen.

Small calcific focus is seen in left occipital cortex without surrounding edema, suggestive of calcified granuloma.

Rest of the brain parenchyma is normal in signal intensity pattern and morphology and displays a normal gray-white matter differentiation.

The deep gray matter and the internal capsules appear normal.

Rest of the white matter display normal volume and signals.

Rest of the brainstem appears normal in morphology and signals.

The imaged cranial nerves are also normal.

The cerebellum and cerebellar peduncles are also normal.

Mega cisterna magna is seen.

The ventricular system is normal in size and appearance for age.

The sella turcica, pituitary gland and infundibulum appear grossly normal for age. The suprasellar cistern and hypothalamic region are unremarkable for any pathology.

MRA: Small saccular out pouching measuring 2.0 x 1.7 mm is noted in postero lateral aspect of left paraclinoid ICA, projecting inferolaterally. No other significant abnormality seen in intracranial arteries.

The orbits and their contents are grossly normal.

Mild mucosal thickening is noted in right maxillary sinus, s/o sinusitis.

IMPRESSION:

Fazekas grade I small vessel ischemic changes, medial temporal lobe atrophy score 1 and grade II koedam parietal atrophy score, likely early Alzheimer’s disease.

Small saccular aneurysm in left paraclinoid ICA.

Small calcified granuloma in left occipital lobe.

No other significant abnormality in brain.

Suggested clinical correlation.

MRI SCAN OF BRAIN

Clinical profile: K/c/o Alzheimer’s disease with memory loss for 2 years.

Technique: MPR T1, FLAIR Axial, T2 Coronal, DWI, SWI, 3D TOF MRA, T2 space.

Mild small vessel ischemic changes (Fazekas I) are seen in white matter. Few chronic lacunar infarcts are seen in bilateral corona radiata and right side of midbrain and pons.

No acute infarct or hemorrhage is seen.

Global cerebral atrophy (GCA scale II) is seen. Mild widening of B/L choroidal fissures is seen without dilatation of temporal horns or volume loss, s/o medial temporal lobe atrophy score 1.

Substantial parietal atrophy with widening of sulci is seen, suggestive of grade 2 Koedam parietal atrophy.

No significant atrophy of temporal pole is seen. No asymmetric cortical parietal atrophy is seen. No significant strategic area infarct is seen.

Rest of the brain parenchyma is normal in signal intensity pattern and morphology and displays a normal gray-white matter differentiation.

The deep gray matter and internal capsules appear normal. Rest of the white matter display normal volume and signals.

Rest of the brainstem appears normal in morphology and signals. The imaged cranial nerves are also normal.

The cerebellum and cerebellar peduncles are also normal.

The ventricular system is normal in size and appearance for age.

The sella turcica, pituitary gland and infundibulum appear grossly normal for age. The suprasellar cistern and hypothalamic region are unremarkable for any pathology.

MRA: No significant abnormality is seen in neck and intracranial arteries for age.

The orbits and their contents are grossly normal.

Mild mucosal thickening is noted in left maxillary sinus, s/o sinusitis.

IMPRESSION:

Diffuse cerebral atrophy with small vessel ischemic changes and chronic lacunar infarcts as detailed.

MTA score 1 and grade II parietal atrophy as detailed.

No other significant abnormality in brain.

Suggested clinical correlation.

MRI SCAN OF PITUITARY

Clinical profile – K/c/o pituitary macro adenoma.

Compared to previous MRI done on 26.09.2011

Technique: T1 coronal and sag, T2 coronal for pituitary, T2 FLAIR axial, Post contrast T1 for pituitary and brain.

Well delineated lobulated, mild heterogeneously enhancing mass lesion is seen in sella/ suprasellar and parasellar regions, measuring approximately 3.7 x 2.8 x 3.2 cm (TRA x CC x AP). No hemorrhage or cystic changes are seen.

In left lateral aspect, invasion of left cavernous sinus and encasement of left ICA is seen. On the right side, lateral margin of lesion is seen beyond lateral intercarotid line.

No significant interval changes are seen when compared to previous MRI done on 26/09/2011.

Brain parenchyma shows normal signal on all sequences.

Incomplete inversion of both hippocampi is seen.

No focal / diffuse altered signal noted.

Ventricles are normal.

Basal cisterns and cortical sulci are normal.

The orbits and their contents are grossly normal.

Rest of the dural venous sinuses and intracranial arteries appear normal.

IMPRESSION:

Features of pituitary macroadenoma with extensions as detailed.  No significant interval changes are seen.

No other significant abnormality in brain.

reports.fullText:
MRI SCAN OF BRAIN WITH CERVICAL SPINE SCREENING

Clinical profile: Giddiness and unable to stand. H/o swaying to left.

Technique: MPR T1, FLAIR Axial, T2 Coronal, DWI, SWI, 3D TOF MRA, T1 post contrast.

Screening of spine: T2 and post contrast T1 sagittal.

A well-defined, lobulated extra axial mass lesion, measuring approximately 3.8 x 3.6 x 2.9 cm (AP x CC x TRA) is seen in left CP angle cistern. The lesion appears hyperintense in T2, no significant diffusion restriction, few hemorrhagic foci and moderate enhancement. No calcification or cystic changes are seen in the lesion.  MRS shows reduced NAA and increased choline peak.

Cisternal segments of CN 7/ 8 complex could not be made out separately from the lesion. Mild widening of the internal acoustic meatus is seen with subtle chronic bone erosion. Small tongue like extension to the IAC is also seen.  No hyperostosis is seen. No dural tail is seen.

The lesion is causing compression of left cerebellar hemisphere, left middle cerebellar peduncle, fourth ventricle and rotation of brainstem with edema in adjacent brain. Mass effect over the adjacent cranial nerves is also seen.

Few perilesional arachnoid cysts are seen around the lesion, largest measuring 1.7 x 1.1 cm.

Obstructive upstream hydrocephalus is seen with periventricular CSF seepage.

Diffuse age related cerebral atrophy with extensive small vessel ischemic changes is seen. Effacement of the sulci is also seen.

Rest of the deep gray matter and internal capsules appear normal.

The right cerebellum and cerebellar peduncles are also normal.

Features of increased intracranial tension are seen with partial empty sella, dilated optic nerve sheath complexes, intra ocular protrusion of optic nerve heads and few focal brain herniations into calvarium.

The suprasellar cistern and hypothalamic region are unremarkable for any pathology.

MRA: No significant abnormality seen in intracranial arteries for age.

Hypoplastic transverse and sigmoid sinuses are seen.  Rest of the dural venous sinuses appears normal.

No other abnormal parenchymal or meningeal enhancement seen.

Screening of whole spine:

Straightening of cervical spine is seen with multilevel disc dessication. No significant mass effect over nerve roots or spinal cord seen.

No abnormal enhancing lesion is seen in the spine. Hemangioma is seen in D11 vertebral body.

No other significant abnormality seen in the spine.

IMPRESSION:

Well defined extra axial mass lesion in left CPA cistern with extensions, mass effect, and hydrocephalus as detailed.

Diffuse age related cerebral atrophy with small vessel ischemic changes.

In view of imaging features, the possibility of Acoustic neuroma is more likely than meningioma. Suggested HPE correlation.

reports.fullText:
Dr Soumya

MRI SCAN OF ELBOW

Clinical profile: Past h/o ulnar nerve repair. Now with c/o fall injury and swelling in left elbow joint region:

Technique: T1, IR, PD fs and GRE in all planes.

Bones and joint:

Small avulsion fracture is seen from medial epicondyle. Bone contusion with edema is seen in posterior capitulum and anterior radial head. Tiny bony fragments are seen near radiocapitellar joint. (With CT correlation).

Ulnohumeral and proximal radio ulnar joints appears normal in alignment.

Rest of the bones show no alteration in signal intensity.

Mild joint effusion is seen. Capsular injury is seen in posterior aspect of lateral compartment.

Ligaments:

Medial collateral ligament:

Humeral avulsion of anterior band of medial collateral ligament is seen. High grade partial tear (Grade II/ III) is seen involving proximal part of posterior band.

Lateral collateral ligament complex:

High grade partial injury of posterior part of radial collateral ligament tear is seen with intact anterior fibres. Injury of proximal LUCL is also seen with lax distal part.

Mild sprain of annular ligament is also seen.

Soft tissue:

Avulsion injury of humeral attachment of common flexor tendon is seen.

Chronic atrophy with fatty changes is seen in anterior muscles in flexor group, more severe in pronator teres, flexor carpi radialis, biceps and brachialis.

Contusion with grade I/II strain of anconeus, common extensor tendon and muscles and triceps is seen. Partial tear of proximal extensor carpi ulnaris extensor digitorum tendons is seen.

Extensive soft tissue contusion changes are seen in the left elbow region.

Ulnar nerve appears intact. Mild edema is seen around the nerve.

IMPRESSION:

MRI SCAN OF LEFT ELBOW (PLAIN)

Clinical profile: Alleged H/o RTA on 14.07.2019, Known case of dislocation of elbow joint with fractures in radial head - post reduction status

Technique: T1, IR, T2, PD fs and GRE in all planes, CT correlation.

Bones and joint:

Posterior dislocation of ulna and radius are seen relative to humerus.

Minimally displaced intracapsular fracture of radial head is seen in anterolateral aspect with displaced fractured fragment noted adjacent to it. Compression fracture is seen in capitellum with cortical irregularity. Contusions are seen in radial head and posterolateral aspect of capitellum.

Small bony fragment is seen in coronoid fossa; measuring 8.7 x 4.7 x 4 mm. Small avulsion fracture of distal LUCL attachment of ulna is seen.

Moderate joint effusion is seen with capsular disruption in posterior aspect.

Rest of the bones shows no alteration in signal intensity.

Ligaments:

Lateral collateral ligament complex: Complete disruption of humeral attachment of radial collateral ligament and LUCL are seen with waviness. Tear of annular ligament is also seen.

Medial collateral ligament complex:  High grade partial/ near complete disruption of medial collateral ligament complex is seen.

Soft tissue:

Full thickness tear involving posterior part of common extensor tendon is seen from humeral attachment with intact anterior part.

Contusion and grade I/ II strain are seen in anterior or and posterior compartment muscles. Grade II injury of the distal triceps muscle is seen.

Mild strain of common flexor tendon attachment is seen.  No complete tear is seen.

Diffuse subcutaneous edema is seen, more prominent in the posterior aspect.

Post traumatic changes are seen in short segment of subluxed ulnar nerve with thickening and altered signal intensity.

IMPRESSION:

Traumatic posterior dislocation of left elbow joint with fractures/ bone contusion as detailed.

Moderate joint effusion with posterior capsular injury and bony loose body.

Complete tear of lateral ligament complex and medial ligament complex tear as detailed.

Common extensor tendon tear and other muscle injuries as detailed.

Extensive post traumatic soft tissue changes.

Suggested clinical correlation.

MRI SCAN RIGHT TIBIA

Clinical Profile: Known case of chronic osteomyelitis with discharging sinuses in right knee region. H/o RTA and surgery in right knee region. Details not available.

Suboptimal evaluation of the right knee region due to extensive artefacts:

Technique: T1, T2, IR, DWI and post contrast T1 in all planes. CT correlation.

Post-operative changes are seen in right knee joint region with fixations screws in situ in proximal tibia and parts of distal femur.

Chronic ill-defined osteolysis is seen in condylar/ supracondylar regions of distal femur with cortical thickening/ sclerosis and periosteal reaction. Multiple small bone chips are seen in this region. Mild osteolysis is also seen along tibial screw in the lateral aspect.

Osseous fusion is seen between parts of lateral femoral condyle, medial femoral condyle, patella with proximal tibia.

Post contrast enhancement is seen in the region of osteolysis. Few draining sinus openings are seen along anterior aspect of knee joint.  No significant fluid collection could be appreciated due to artefacts.

Rest of the visualised bones appear grossly normal. No other significant marrow abnormalities.

Diffuse atrophic changes are seen in visualised right lower limb muscles. IR hyperintensity with edema is seen in gastrocnemius muscles.

Mild subcutaneous edema is also seen. No other significant collection is seen.

IMPRESSION:

Post-operative changes with screws and bony fusion in right knee joint region as detailed.

Ill-defined osteolysis with bone changes, enhancement, bone chips and sinuses as detailed, consistent with chronic osteomyelitis.

Diffuse atrophic changes of right lower limb muscles.

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT ANKLE JOINT

Clinical profile: H/o recent inversion injury of right ankle joint. C/o persistent pain and swelling of ankle. For detailed evaluation.

Technique: PD fs, T1, GRE, DWI and IR in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Ankle joint alignment is normal. No joint widening or subluxation is seen.

Bone contusions/ marrow edema are seen in talus and both malleoli. No obvious osteochondral fragment is seen.

Mild ankle joint effusion is seen. Edema with synovial thickening is seen in medial, lateral and anterolateral gutter regions.

Rest of the visualized bones and joints appear normal.

Lateral ligament complex:

Disruption of ATFL is seen with tiny avulsed fragment from talus. CFL is also not seen in continuity, suggestive of grade II/ III sprain. Mild periosteal stripping is seen in lateral malleolus. Mild sprain of PTFL without disruption of fibers is also seen.

Medial ligament complex:

Contusion with partial tear (Grade II sprain) is seen in medial ligament complex, predominantly involving the deep fibers in posterior aspect. Mild periosteal stripping is also seen in medial malleolus.

No complete disruption of fibers is seen.

Distal tibiofibular articulation:

Grade I sprain of AITF and PITF ligaments is seen. No complete disruption or widening of syndesmosis is seen.

Rest of the visualized ligaments appears normal.

Rest of the structures:

Minimal fluid is seen in tibialis posterior tendon sheath. Flexor and peroneal retinaculum appear intact. The visualized tendons appear normal. No tear or retraction is seen.

Sinus tarsi appear normal. The visualized muscles and rest of the soft tissue appear normal.

Mild subcutaneous edema is seen at ankle joint region. No abnormal collection is seen.

IMPRESSION:

Grade II/ III sprain of lateral ligament complex as detailed.

Grade II deltoid ligament sprain and grade I syndesmosis sprain.

Mild ankle joint effusion, synovial/ soft tissue thickening and bone changes as detailed. No significant osteochondral fragment seen.

No other significant abnormality in right ankle joint.

MRI SCAN OF ANKLE AND FOOT

Clinical profile: Recurrent mild swelling in left foot? Left midfoot synovitis.

Technique: T1, T2fs, PDfs, IR, DWI, GRE and post contrast T1 in all planes. With CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Mild uniform joint narrowing, extensive subchondral edema/ inflammation and synovial thickening are seen in midfoot joints involving the Talocalcaneonavicular, calcaneocuboid, cuneonavicular, intercunieform and lateral four tarsometatarsal joints.  A small ganglion cyst measuring 4 x 4 mm is seen in dorsum of foot arising from medial intercunieform joint.

No significant joint effusion or erosion/ destruction of bones are seen. No significant subchondral cysts, fracture or osteophytes are seen. No features to suggest osteomyelitis.

Extensive synovial thickening and inflammation is seen along extensor hallucis longus, peroneus longus tendon in the plantar aspect and the distal insertion part of tibialis posterior tendon. Mild extension of inflammation along the roots of extensor retinaculum to the lateral aspects of sinus tarsi is also seen.

Ankle and rest of visualised joint alignment is normal.

Rest of the visualised bones show no alteration in signal intensity.

Prominent dorsal calcaneal enthesophytes are seen. Mild chronic insertional Achilles tendinopathy is seen with Haglund deformity. Mild retro calcaneal bursitis is seen with tiny calcific foci.

Type II accessory navicular bone is seen.

Ligaments:

Medial and lateral ligament complex appear normal. Rest of the visualised ligaments appear normal.

Tendons and muscles:

Rest of the anterior, medial, posterior and lateral tendons appear normal. No features of tendon tear or retraction seen. Peroneal, extensor and flexor retinaculum are intact.

Rest of structures:

Mild diffuse subcutaneous edema is seen in dorsum of foot, medial and lateral aspects of ankle joint region. No abnormal collection is seen.

Rest of the soft tissue appears normal.

IMPRESSION:

Extensive midfoot arthritis with synovitis, tenosynovial inflammation and small ganglion cyst as detailed.

Haglund deformity with mild retro calcaneal bursitis.

Diffuse subcutaneous edema in ankle and dorsum of foot regions.

In view of imaging and clinical features, to consider the possibility of inflammatory etiology.

MRI SCAN OF ANKLE

Clinical profile: C/o swelling and pain in lateral aspect of right ankle joint for few years, for evaluation.

No obvious bony tarsal bony coalition is seen. The joint space between involving the middle facet of talocalcaneal joint is narrow. The possibility of fibrous or cartilaginous coalition could not be ruled out.

Rest of the bones and joints of ankle and foot appear normal.

Mild joint effusion is seen with reactive chronic synovitis.

Elongated lateral tubercle of posterior process of talus (Stieda process) is seen with edema. Adjacent synovitis is seen.

No complete tear or waviness is seen in lateral ligament complex.

Muscles, tendons and rest of structures:

Peroneus brevis tendinopathy with longitudinal tear is seen. Mild tendinopathy changes are also seen in peroneus longus tendon near the peroneal tubercle. No complete tear or retraction or fluid in the tendon sheath is seen.

Sinus tarsi inflammation is seen. No significant cysts or collections are seen.

The anterior, medial and posterior tendons appear normal. No features of tenosynovitis are seen. Peroneal and flexor retinaculum is intact.

Rest of the soft tissue appears normal. There is no evidence of fluid collection seen.

IMPRESSION:

Degenerative arthrosis in subtalar, calcaneocuboid and ankle joint as detailed.

Sinus tarsi inflammation with ankle joint effusion and synovitis.

Stress changes in lateral gutter/ lateral ligament complex with peroneal tendinopathy.

Stieda process with adjacent synovitis.

Inflammation/ edema are also seen in adjacent soft tissue in the anterolateral aspect. No collection is seen in the soft tissue.

Ankle joint alignment is normal. The articular cartilage appears normal.

Rest of the visualised bones and joints show no significant abnormality.

Rest of the soft tissue appear normal. Tendons and ligaments appear grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Features are suggestive of acute right distal fibula osteomyelitis with small sub periosteal collection as detailed.

Right femoral head:

Geographic area of fat signal intensity with T1 hypointense rim is seen in femoral head region involving the antero-superior aspect, with area of involvement of >50% (R>L). Edema is seen in the adjacent femoral neck and inter trochanteric regions. (Mitchell Class A).

Double line sign is seen with subchondral collapse and flattening of contour of femoral head is seen.  Thinning of articular cartilage, narrowing of joint space is seen in the superior aspect with secondary acetabular changes and mild joint effusion, consistent with Ficat Arlet Stage 4.

Left femoral head:

Geographic area of fat signal intensity with T1 hypointense rim is seen in femoral head region involving the antero-superior aspect, with area of involvement of >50% (R>L). (Mitchell Class A).

Double line sign is seen. Small focal flattening of contour is seen in posterosuperior aspect of the head. No significant abnormality in joint or in the acetabulum, suggestive of early Ficat Arlet Stage 3.

Rest of the visualised bones appears normal in signal intensity. No significant focal lesions are seen.

Transplant kidney is seen in right iliac fossa region. No other significant abnormality seen in the visualised structures.

IMPRESSION:

Bilateral avascular necrosis, Stage IV on right side and early stage III on left side involving > 50% of femoral heads (R>L) as detailed.

Acute comminuted fracture of the right proximal femur involving the intertrochanteric region, lesser trochanter, adjacent basicervical/ femoral neck region, and the anterior aspect of the greater trochanter is seen. CT OF BONY PELVIS

Clinical Profile: H/o slip and fall at home, sustained injury to left side lower limb, X-ray left intertrochanteric fracture.

Acute comminuted fracture of the left proximal femur involving the intertrochanteric region, lesser trochanter and greater trochanter regions. No underlying lytic lesion, cortical destruction, or suspicious osseous mass is identified to suggest a pathological fracture.

The fracture fragments demonstrate displacement and varus angulation.

No extension of the fracture line into the femoral head articular surface is identified.

The left femoral head remains congruent with the acetabulum without evidence of dislocation.

Mild left hip joint effusion is present. No intra-articular fracture fragments are seen.

The right hip joint appears unremarkable for age.

No additional acute fracture is identified in the visualized pelvic bones or hip girdle structures.

Soft tissues:

Mild surrounding soft tissue contusion with edema is noted around the left hip region.

No organized soft tissue collection or soft tissue gas is seen.

IMPRESSION:

Acute comminuted displaced and angulated left proximal femoral fracture involving intertrochanteric region with extension into lesser and greater trochanters as detailed.

Mild associated left hip joint effusion and surrounding soft tissue contusion.

No hip dislocation or intra-articular fracture fragments.

No additional acute pelvic fractures identified.

CT OF LEFT ANKLE

Clinical profile: History of a slip and fall on 16/6/26, closed displaced medial malleolus left ankle fracture.

Acute comminuted displaced oblique fracture of the distal fibula is seen at the level of the syndesmosis (trans-syndesmotic), extending distally to involve lateral malleolus, consistent with Weber B fibular fracture.

Acute mildly displaced avulsion fracture of the medial malleolus is present.

Acute undisplaced fracture involves the posterior malleolus.

The constellation of fractures is consistent with a trimalleolar ankle fracture (Lauge-Hansen supination-external rotation stage IV / Weber B injury).

Mild subluxation of the talus with widening of medial space is seen.

Mild ankle joint effusion is present. No significant intra-articular fracture fragments are identified.

Surrounding soft tissue edema and contusion are noted without evidence of open injury or soft tissue defect.

Mild osteoarthrosis is noted involving the tibiotalar joint and a few visualized joints of the foot.

The remaining visualized bones demonstrate preserved alignment without additional acute fracture.

IMPRESSION:

Acute unstable trimalleolar fracture of left ankle (Weber B stage IV) as detailed.

Mild tibiotalar subluxation with joint effusion and surrounding soft tissue contusion/ edema as detailed.

No significant intra-articular fracture fragments.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Clinical Profile: K/c/o bilateral femoral head AVN with pain.

Technique: T1, IR, T2, PDfs, GRE and DWI in all planes. CT correlation.

The necrotic segment involves >2/3 of the weight-bearing portion of the femoral head, without extension to the lateral acetabular edge, corresponding to JIC type C1.

A small subchondral fracture is seen involving anterosuperior aspect of the femoral head. No significant flattening or complete collapse of the femoral head is identified.

Associated bone marrow edema is seen involving the subchondral femoral head and extending into the femoral neck, representing reactive edema.

Minimal right hip joint effusion with mild reactive synovial thickening.

No significant secondary osteoarthritic changes. Articular cartilage is relatively preserved.

Left hip joint:

A geographic, serpiginous area of abnormal marrow signal is seen involving weight-bearing portion of the left femoral head, consistent with osteonecrosis.

The necrotic segment involves >2/3 of the weight-bearing portion of the femoral head, without extension to the lateral acetabular edge, corresponding to JIC type C1.

The combined modified Kerboul angle measures approximately 210°, corresponding to a medium-sized osteonecrotic lesion. The estimated extent of involvement is approximately 50% of the femoral head.

A small subchondral fracture is seen involving the anterosuperior aspect of femoral head. No significant flattening or complete collapse of the femoral head is identified.

Associated subchondral and femoral neck marrow edema is present.

Minimal left hip joint effusion with mild reactive synovial thickening.

No significant secondary osteoarthritic changes. Articular cartilage is relatively preserved.

Remaining osseous structures:

The remaining visualized bony pelvis, proximal femora and visualized sacroiliac joints demonstrate preserved marrow signal and cortical outlines.

No additional focal osseous lesion or acute fracture.

The visualized periarticular muscles, tendons and soft-tissue structures are unremarkable. No significant periarticular collection or focal soft-tissue mass.

reports.fullText:
Dr Pragadesh

MRI SCAN OF BONY PELVIS AND RIGHT HIP

Clinical details: H/o Trauma 1 week back with extensive pelvic bone fractures, surgery done for fixation of shaft of femur.

Technique:  T2 axial and coronal, T1 axial, T2 FS axial, DWI for both hips. PD FS in 3 planes, T1 coronal and sagittal for right hip joint.

Right hip joint:

Femoral head:

Bone marrow contusion is noted in epiphysis of head of right femur in the inferomedial aspect. Suspicious subtle surface indentation is seen along the inferior aspect of fovea, suggestive of impaction injury. Trabecular micro fractures are also seen running parallel along growth plate in the epiphysis. Micro fractures are also seen in the neck region.

Focal alteration of thickness and signal intensity of the growth plate is seen under the bone contusion, suggestive of focal impaction injury. No significant widening/ distraction of growth plate are seen. Rest of the growth plate appears normal in thickness.

Acetabulum, articular cartilage, labrum, ligament and capsule:

Focal irregularity of cortex with minimal edema is seen in posterior acetabular margin/ wall. Rest of the bony acetabulum appears normal.

Articular cartilage injury with fissures and cartilage loss is seen along the posterior wall. Traumatic, displaced posterior labral tear is seen. Rest of the labrum appears grossly normal. These changes are probably secondary to posterior hip dislocation/ subluxation.

An osteochondral fragment measuring approximately 13 x 8 x 4 mm is seen in the posteromedial aspect, probably from the posterior acetabular wall injury.

Intrasubstance injury with thickening and altered signal intensity is seen in in ligamentum teres. No obvious complete disruption is seen.

Partial capsular injury with contusion of the adjacent soft tissue is seen along the posterior aspect. No complete disruption is seen. Minimal joint fluid is seen.

Rest of bones and soft tissue:

Extensive fractures of the pelvic bones are seen, which are as detailed in the previous CT. Soft tissue contusion changes are seen near the fractures.

Diffuse subcutaneous edema with layering of thin fluid collections are noted in bilateral groin, hip and proximal thigh.

Large fluid collection measuring approximately 10 x 6.3 x 2.5 cm is noted in the right proximal thigh lateral aspect in subcutaneous plane – suggestive of degloving injury with hemolymphatic fluid.

No other interval changes in the bony injuries and fragments compared to previous CT dated 01.01.2017.

Metallic fixation screw with susceptibility artifacts are noted in shaft of right femur.

Visualised pelvis:

The bladder is empty with Foleys’ bulb in situ.

Uterus and ovaries appear grossly normal.

Diffuse edematous changes with mild fluid are seen in the pelvis and visualised parts of lower abdomen.

IMPRESSION:

	Impaction changes in right femoral head/ posterior acetabular wall, injuries in articular cartilage, labrum with intra articular osteochondral fragment as detailed.

	Micro fractures in right femoral head, neck with focal physeal injury as detailed.

	Post-surgical changes with large hemolymphatic collection as detailed.

MRI OF BONY PELVIS

Clinical profile: C/o pain in left hip region? AVN? Trochanteric bursitis.

Technique: IR, T1, T2, PDfs, DWI and GRE in all planes. CT correlation.

Screening of lumbar spine: T2 sagittal.

Bones and joints:

Both femoral heads demonstrate normal contour and preserved marrow signal intensity. No serpiginous subchondral abnormality, bone marrow edema, collapse or other imaging features of avascular necrosis are seen.

Bilateral hip joint spaces are maintained with trace physiological joint fluid. No significant hip joint effusion or synovial thickening is seen.

Mild degenerative changes are seen involving both sacroiliac joints, with minimal focal subarticular marrow edema on the left, suggestive of mild active degenerative change.

The pubic symphysis is unremarkable.

The remaining visualized pelvic bones demonstrate preserved marrow signal without focal osseous lesion, fracture or significant marrow edema.

Muscles and Tendons:

Bilateral gluteus medius insertional tendinosis with partial-thickness insertional tears at the greater trochanters, more pronounced on the left.

Mild bilateral gluteus minimus insertional tendinosis is also seen without significant tendon tear.

There is associated mild greater trochanteric bursitis bilaterally, more pronounced on the left, with minimal bursal fluid and adjacent inflammatory edema.

Mild asymmetric fatty atrophy of the left gluteus minimus muscle is noted without associated muscle edema, suggesting a chronic process.

The remaining visualized muscles and tendons are grossly preserved.

Nerves and Soft Tissues:

The visualized sciatic, femoral and obturator nerves are normal in calibre and signal intensity.

No significant soft-tissue collection or mass lesion is identified.

The visualized pelvic viscera are grossly unremarkable for the patient's age. No significant free fluid is seen in the pelvis.

Screening of lumbar spine:

Considering last discrete vertebra as L5, conus medullaris ends at L1-2 level and the cauda equina nerve fibres appear normal.

Disc desiccation and facetal arthropathy is seen at multiple lumbar levels.

Disc bulge and facetal arthropathy causing indentation of bilateral traversing nerve roots are seen at L4-5 and L5-S1 levels.

IMPRESSION:

Bilateral gluteus medius tendinosis with partial-thickness tears (L>R).

Mild bilateral greater trochanteric bursitis (L>R) with minimal associated bursal fluid on left side as detailed.

Mild bilateral gluteus minimus tendinosis and chronic fatty atrophy of left gluteus minimus muscle as detailed.

Mild bilateral sacroiliac joint osteoarthrosis.

No other significant abnormality seen in bony pelvis.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF BONY PELVIS AND LEFT HIP

Clinical details: H/o Trauma with pelvic fractures. For detailed evaluation.

Technique: IR, T1, PDfs and GRE in all planes. CT correlation.

Left hip joint:

Femoral head:

Bone contusion is seen around fovea, suggestive of impaction injury. Trabecular micro fractures are seen along growth and in femoral neck region.

No significant widening/ distraction of growth plate are seen. No avulsion/ displaced fracture.

Bony Acetabulum and articular cartilage:

Displaced fracture involving posterior acetabular wall is seen measuring approximately 3.6 x 1.9 x 0.5 cm. The fragment is rotated, flipping through the space between piriformis and obturator internus muscles/ tendons and lying posterior to obturator internus tendon. Cartilage injury is also seen along posterior aspect.

Rest of bony acetabulum and cartilage appears normal.

Labrum, ligaments and joint and capsule:

Inferior aspect of posterior labrum is torn and is attached to displaced fracture fragment. The labrum is continuous superiorly with rest of labrum towards anterior aspect.

Widening of labral sulcus is seen in posterosuperior quadrant, likely partial under surface detachment. Partial injury of transverse acetabular ligament is seen at its bony attachments. No complete disruption is seen. Rest of labrum appears normal.

Sprain is seen in ischiofemoral ligament and ligamentum teres. No complete disruption is seen.

Capsular injury with contusion of adjacent soft tissue is seen along posterior aspect.

Mild joint effusion is seen. A bony fragment measuring approximately 1.5 x 0.8 x 0.5 cm is seen in hip joint.  Another tiny one is also seen.

Rest of visualised ligaments appear normal.

Rest of bones and soft tissue:

Comminuted fractures are seen in left iliac bone extending to left sacroiliac joint and in right superior pubic ramus. Mild diastasis of left sacroiliac joint is also seen in inferior aspect near the fracture.

Trabecular injuries are seen in bilateral sacral ala and right iliac bones. Soft tissue contusion changes are seen adjacent to fractures.

Contusions are also seen in flexors and gluteal muscles on left side.

Rest of the visualised muscles and tendons appear normal.

The urinary bladder appears normal.

IMPRESSION:

Left posterior hip dislocation with displaced bone fragment, contusions and labral tear as detailed.

Mild joint effusion, intraarticular fragment and ligament/ capsular injury.

Multiple fractures and soft tissue injuries in pelvis as detailed.

MRI OF BONY PELVIS (PLAIN)

Clinical profile: H/o RTA with head injury 3 years back. C/o left hip pain for past 1 year? Osteoarthrosis? Septic arthritis. For detailed evaluation.

Suboptimal evaluation due to patient factors and movement artefacts.

Technique: IR, T1, T2, GRE and DWI in all planes. CT correlation.

Left Hip Joint:

Marked flattening and deformity of the left femoral head are noted, consistent with chronic post-traumatic remodelling.

Advanced secondary osteoarthrosis is present with diffuse full-thickness articular cartilage loss, prominent marginal osteophytes, subchondral marrow edema and cystic degenerative changes involving the femoral head and adjacent acetabulum.

Widening of hip joint space with superolateral migration/ subluxation of femoral head is seen. Mild to moderate joint effusion is seen. No diffusion restriction is seen in joint fluid.

A small ossific intra-articular loose body is present within the posterior aspect of the joint, measuring approximately 1.3 × 0.3 cm.

No erosive osseous destruction, periarticular abscess, sinus tract, or significant periarticular soft tissue inflammatory changes are identified to suggest active septic arthritis.

Heterotopic Ossification:

Ill-defined focal areas of mature heterotopic ossification are seen surrounding left proximal femur, predominantly along anterior and lateral aspects of femoral neck.

Small focus of heterotopic ossification is also seen in left obturator internus muscle.

Muscles:

Asymmetric diffuse volume loss with fatty infiltration is seen involving the left gluteal, pelvic girdle and proximal thigh musculature compared with contralateral side, consistent with chronic denervation/ disuse atrophy.

No muscle edema or STIR hyperintensity is identified to suggest active myositis or acute denervation.

Right Hip:

Right hip joint is preserved without significant abnormality.

Remaining Osseous Structures:

The remaining visualized pelvic bones and proximal femora demonstrate preserved marrow signal without acute osseous abnormality.

No sacroiliac joint abnormality is identified.

Rest of soft tissues:

No significant abnormality is seen in the remaining visualized pelvic soft tissues.

IMPRESSION:

Advanced post-traumatic secondary osteoarthritis of left hip joint with chronic deformity/ flattening and superolateral migration of left femoral head as detailed.

Left hip joint effusion with small loose body as mentioned.

Mature heterotopic ossification surrounding left femoral neck region.

Asymmetric chronic atrophy of left gluteal, pelvic and proximal thigh musculature, likely representing chronic denervation and/ or disuse changes.

No MRI evidence of active septic arthritis or osteomyelitis.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF LEFT ANKLE AND FOOT

Clinical profile: Known case of diabetes, previous h/o surgery in foot, for detailed evaluation:

Technique: PD fs, T1, IR, DWI, post contrast T1 in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Extensive destruction of bones/ joints with multiple loose bodies, joint deformity and subluxation of bones are seen involving in ankle, subtalar and midfoot joints. Sclerosis and periosteal reaction is also seen in involved bones. Smooth synovial thickening is seen in involved joints.

Collapse of arches, gross deformity of foot and ankle with rocker bottom foot is seen.  Bony ankylosis of talus and calcaneus is also seen.

Abnormal signal intensity and post contrast enhancement is seen in involving calcaneus, talus, navicular, cuboid bones, lateral and medial malleolus. Small intraosseous collections are also seen in calcaneus.

Fractures with edema are seen in first and second metatarsal bones and proximal phalanx of little toe.

Soft tissue:

Two large skin/ soft tissue defects are seen opposite medial malleolus and along posterolateral aspect of foot extending upto the bones.  Another smaller similar defect is seen in posteromedial aspect.

Multiple collections are seen as follows

Collection measuring approximately 3.6 x 2.3 x 2 cm is seen along FHL tendon and extends to posterior small defect.

Collection measuring about 3 x 2 x 1.5 cm is seen at medial soft tissue defect and appears to be continuous with ankle joint.

Another one measuring about 2.5 x 1.5 x 1 is seen at plantar soft tissue defect.

One more collection measuring about 3.5 x 1.8 x 1.5 cm is seen along Flexor hallucis longus tendon at the level of first MTP joint.

Tenosynovitis of all the tendons is seen with synovial thickening and minimal fluid.

Diffuse IR hyperintensity is seen in all the visualized muscles in distal leg, ankle and foot regions. However, no significant necrosis is seen. The visualized tendons appear grossly intact.

Diffuse edematous changes are seen in subcutaneous fat planes and soft tissue in ankle and foot regions.

Rest of the visualized bones appears grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Features are suggestive of chronic Charcot neuro-osteoarthropathy with superimposed infection and osteomyelitis.

Extensive soft tissue inflammation and collections in ankle/ foot as detailed.

Post-operative changes with soft tissue defects as detailed.

Dr Akila

MR RENAL ANGIO (PLAIN)

Clinical profile: Young hypertensive, to rule out renal artery stenosis.

Technique: MRA for renal arteries, T2/ IR in axial and coronal.

Both kidneys appear normal in size and contour. Right and left kidney measures 9.9 x 5.3 cm and 11.4 x 5.6 cm respectively. No significant focal lesion is seen.

Mild altered signal intensity is seen in renal parenchyma, may be renal parenchymal disease.

Right side: Single main renal artery is seen measuring 6.3 mm at origin.

Left side: Single main renal artery measuring 6.5 mm at origin. Another small accessory artery supplying inferior pole is also seen measuring 2 mm at origin.

No significant renal artery stenosis or aneurysm is seen.

Retro aortic left renal venin is seen.

Rest of the visualized abdomen shows no significant abnormality.

IMPRESSION:

	Single renal artery on right side and two renal arteries on left side.

	No significant stenosis in the present study.

In carpal tunnel, palmar bowing of flexor retinaculum, enlargement of median nerve proximal to flexor retinaculum, and flattening of median nerve at level of hook of hamate (Flattening ratio of >4) and increased signal intensity of nerve are seen.

Subtle increased signal intensity is seen in thenar muscles, suggestive of carpal tunnel syndrome.

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT KNEE JOINT REGION

Clinical profile: C/o Recurrent soft tissue swelling in right knee joint region, for detailed evaluation. H/o surgical excision few months back.

Technique: T1, IR, DWI, GRE, Pre and Post contrast T1 in all planes. PD fs sagittal and coronal for knee joint.

A soft tissue mass lesion with ill-defined margins and measuring approximately 5.4 x 4.3 x 2.8 cm (TRA x CC x AP) is seen in right proximal leg abutting anteromedial cortex of proximal tibia and extending upto the subcutaneous fat plane. The upper margin of the lesion is about 1.4 cm from medial tibial plateau. Mild adjacent subcutaneous edema is also seen. The lesion abutting medial margin of distal patellar tendon and anterior aspect of MCL.

The lesion appears heterogeneously hyperintense in IR/ isointense to hypointense T1 with few scattered small haemorrhagic foci. Contrast study shows moderate and heterogeneous enhancement with areas of necrosis. The enhancing component shows significant diffusion restriction. No significant satellite nodules are seen.

No calcification/ ossification or fat component seen in the lesion. No fluid levels are seen.

No significant periosteal reaction/ cortical destruction or marrow involvement seen.

No other similar lesions are seen in the visualised parts of right lower limb.

Visualised knee joint:

Medial tibiofemoral joint predominant osteoarthrosis is seen with cartilage loss, subchondral edema and cysts. Small intra articular fragment is seen in intercondylar notch region. (With CT correlation).

Chronic Grade II/ III tear is seen in ACL with waviness and attenuation of proximal part. Mild anterior translation of tibia is seen (8.5 mm).

Medial meniscus: Complex tear with oblique and radial components is seen in posterior body and posterior horn of medial meniscus. Small flipped component is seen in meniscofemoral recess.

Lateral meniscus: Chronic horizontal tear is seen in body and horns. Small flap tear with flipped fragment is seen in anterior horn. A parameniscal cyst measuring approximately 1.7 x 1.4 x 0.6 cm is seen.

Rest of the knee joint is grossly normal.

Extensor mechanism appears normal. Rest of the surrounding muscles, tendons and the neurovascular structures are grossly normal.

No significant abnormality seen in the distal leg and ankle joint regions.

IMPRESSION:

Enhancing soft tissue mass lesion with ill-defined margins in anteromedial aspect of right proximal leg region with extensions as detailed.

Osteoarthrosis of right knee joint with meniscal and ACL tears.

In view of age and imaging features, the possibility of soft tissue sarcoma is more likely. Suggested HPE correlation.

MRI SCAN OF LEFT FOREARM

Clinical profile: H/o painless swelling in left forearm region, for detailed evaluation.

Technique: T1, IR, DWI, GRE, Pre and Post contrast T1 in all planes.

A well-defined lobulated soft tissue mass lesion is seen in anterior aspect of proximal forearm, measuring approximately 4.8 x 3.8 x 3.2 cm (CC x TRA x AP).

The lesion appears iso to slightly hyperintense in T1 and hyperintense in IR/ T2 with band like areas of low signal intensity and shows mild diffusion restriction. No cystic changes/ hemorrhage/ calcification or ossification/ necrosis seen now. The lesion shows moderate patchy and peripheral enhancement.

Extent:

The proximal margin of the lesion is at elbow joint level and distal margin is seen at level of biceps tendon insertion.

The lesion is encasing the distal biceps tendon. The margin of the lesion is ill-defined in few areas with loss of fat plane between lesion and adjacent parts of brachialis, pronator teres and supinator muscles.

The lesion is indenting and causing mild mass effect over brachial vessels and median nerve. However, no definite encasement is seen.

The lesion is abutting short segment of proximal radius. However, no erosion or bone marrow changes are seen.

No extension to joint seen. No other similar lesion seen in the visualised parts of upper limb. No significant sized regional lymphadenopathy.

Bones and joint:

Ulnohumeral, radiocapitellar and proximal radio ulnar joints appears normal in alignment.

No joint effusion or synovial thickening is seen. The ligaments appear normal.

The bones show no significant abnormality. No significant focal lesion or abnormality seen.

Rest of the soft tissue:

The ulnar nerve and radial nerves appear normal in thickness and course.

The common flexor and extensor tendons appear normal.

Rest of the muscles, intermuscular and subcutaneous fat planes appear normal.

IMPRESSION:

Well defined lobulated soft tissue mass lesion in anterior aspect of proximal forearm with extensions and imaging characteristics as detailed.

To consider the possibilities of 1. Benign fibromatous lesion. 2. Soft tissue sarcoma has to be ruled out in view of age and deep location. Suggested HPE correlation for further detailed evaluation.

Clinical profile: H/o fall injury 3 weeks. C/o persistent pain and swelling in lateral aspect of left thigh region.

Lateral intermuscular septum and gluteal aponeurotic fascia appear intact.

Left hip joint appears grossly normal.

Rest of the visualized muscles and tendons appear normal.

Bilateral sacroiliac joints appear normal.

Diffuse subcutaneous edematous changes are seen in left lower limb. No collection is seen.

IMPRESSION:

Partial injury of iliotibial band (ITB)/ deep fascia of thigh as detailed.

Grade II strain in vastus lateralis muscle and grade I strain in other thigh muscles as detailed.

Mild left knee joint effusion and diffuse edema in left lower limb.

No other significant abnormality seen.

reports.fullText:
MRI SCAN OF PELVIS

Technique:  T2 sagittal, obl axial and coronal, T1 obl axial, DWI, T2 HASTE axial - upper abdomen, IR axial.

Anorectal region:

Abnormal proliferative growth is seen in mid and lower rectum in a semicircular pattern in left lateral, anterior and right anterolateral aspects with relative sparing of right posterolateral aspect for a length of approximately 7.5 cm and maximum thickness of 2.2 cm in the left lateral aspect. Significant perirectal fat stranding with subtle nodularity is seen at multiple areas.

The lesion infiltrates muscularis propria and serosa at few regions in lower rectum, with nodular growth into mesorectal fat plane at 2 to 5 o’clock position. The extramural depth of invasion in this position is about 8.4 mm. Extramural vascular invasion is also seen in this region. Definite invasion of left levator ani muscle involving pubococcygeus with minimal fat stranding extending into ischiorectal fat plane. The minimum distance to the MRF is 0 in this region.

Anteriorly, possible focal invasion of posterior wall of vagina is seen in the left paramedian position with loss of fat plane with the mass.

No obvious extension to the lateral pelvic walls/ obturator internus or piriformis muscle involvement seen now.

The lower end of the tumour is about 1.6 cm from the anal verge at and just below the level of puborectalis. At this level, the lesion is involving the mucosa, internal sphincter and just extends to the interspincteric fat plane.

Few discrete suspicious lymph nodes with irregular margin and mixed signal intensity (at least 5 in number) are seen in the mesorectal fat on both sides, largest measuring 10.7 mm in short axis.  Few discrete lymph nodes are seen in the presacral region; largest measuring approximately 4.1 mm is seen.

Uterus and ovaries are not seen, consistent with post-surgical status.

Urinary bladder, bilateral vesicoureteric junctions is normal. No hydroureteronephrosis.

No significant free fluid is seen in the pelvis.

Visualized bones:

Multiple small IR hyperintense foci are seen in the pelvic bones, both femurs and lower vertebrae.

Screening of the upper abdomen:

Few T1 hyperintense focal lesions of varying sizes are seen in the liver, atleast 6 in no, largest measuring approximately 9.8 mm in segment 4.

No significant sized para aortic lymph nodes are seen.

Few simple cortical cysts are seen in both kidneys, largest measuring 3.1 x 2.5 cm in left kidney.

Hiatal hernia is seen.

No other significant abnormality is noted in the abdomen.

IMPRESSION:

Mid and lower rectal growth with extension to anal canal, mesorectal fat plane, left levator ani and possibly posterior wall of vagina (T4) with pelvic lymphadenopathy as detailed.

Focal lesions in liver and visualised bones as detailed.

Features are consistent with rectal malignancy with liver and bone metastases.
