reports.fullText:
MRI SCAN OF PELVIS (PLAIN)

Clinical profile – Known case of carcinoma rectum, for detailed evaluation:

Technique:  T2 all three planes, T1 axial, DWI, T2 HASTE and DWI of upper abdomen.

RECTUM AND ANAL CANAL:

Tumor:

Above the level of puborectalis:

Abnormal asymmetric circumferential wall thickening, intermediate signal intensity and diffusion restriction is seen in the mid and lower rectum, for a length of approximately 8.5 cm and with maximum thickness of 1.6 cm. The lower margin of the tumor is about 1.9 cm from anal verge.

Loss of T2 hypointense serosa with significant perirectal fat infiltration is seen, in anterior, bilateral lateral and left posterior aspects.

The lesion is involving the mesorectal fascia in the anterior aspect. The distance is also about 1-3 mm between abnormal thickening and MRF in right and left anterolateral and left posterolateral aspects.

Loss of fat plane with posterior vagina wall is seen, with mild altered T2 hypointensity of vaginal wall, likely invasion. No significant rectovaginal fistula is seen.  (T4).

The fat plane between the rectum and uterus is not clearly seen, may be adherent to it.  However, no obvious invasion of uterus is seen. No obvious extension to pelvic lateral wall or levator ani muscle seen.

At and below the level of puborectalis:

The lesion is extending to involve the anorectal junction and adjacent upper part of anal canal, predominantly in anterior and lateral aspects. Extension to the intersphincteric plane is seen in the right lateral aspect.

Nodes:

Few discrete nodes, at least 4 in number, are seen in the perirectal region, largest measuring approximately 17 mm in SAD on left side. The largest node shows perinodal infiltration and appears to be involving the adjacent peritoneum.

Few small discrete nodes are also seen along the inferior mesenteric vessels, largest measuring approximately 4 mm in SAD. No significant sized lymph nodes are seen along the external/ internal iliac vessels and in inguinal regions.

Rest of the pelvis:

Uterus:  Multiple fibroids of varying sizes are seen in anterior and posterior walls, largest measuring approximately 23 x 20 mm in anterior wall.

The ovaries are grossly normal.

Urinary bladder appears normal. Bilateral vesicoureteric junctions are normal. No hydroureteronephrosis.

Minimal free fluid is seen in the pelvis.

Chronic degenerative tear/ enthesopathy changes are seen in bilateral hamstring muscles attachments in ischial tuberosity.

Visualized bones show normal signal intensity. No significant focal lesions are seen.

Screening of the upper abdomen:

A well-defined T2 hyperintense lesion with thin hypointense rim and measuring approximately 16 x 15 mm is seen in segment 6 of right lobe of the liver without diffusion restriction. USG shows hyperechoic lesion, likely hemangioma (hepatic venous malformation). Multiple small similar cysts are also seen in the liver.

Two small suspicious T2 hyperintense lesions, largest measuring approximately 8 x 6 mm is seen in the liver, indeterminate in etiology.

No significant sized retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy seen.

Multiple simple renal cortical cysts of varying sizes are seen in both kidneys, largest measuring approximately 18 x 15 mm.

No other significant abnormality seen in the visulaised upper abdominal structures.

IMPRESSION:

Abnormal rectal wall thickening with extensions as detailed.

Pelvic lymphadenopathy as detailed.

Small suspicious focal liver lesions as detailed, likely indeterminate in etiology.

Imaging features are consistent with rectal malignancy with lymph nodal metastases, likely stage T4bN2Mx. Suggested clinical correlation/ further evaluation if clinically indicated.

MRI SCAN OF LEFT SHOULDER AND ARM

Clinical profile? Septic arthritis of left shoulder joint, for evaluation:

Technique: T1, IR, DWI, PD fs, DWI, Pre and Post contrast T1 in all planes.

Left humerus:

Abnormal, extensive ill-defined IR hyper/ T1 hypo intensity is seen in marrow of left humerus extending from proximal metaphysis to distal metaphysis. Abnormal marrow enhancement is seen in distal metaphyseal region, consistent with osteomyelitis.

However, no appreciable marrow enhancement is seen in proximal two thirds of the humerus, consistent with marrow ischemia, secondary to periosteal stripping.

Small trabecular fracture is also seen in proximal humerus. No Intraosseous collection is seen.

A large sub periosteal collection with diffusion restriction and measuring approximately 11.8 x 3.6 x 3.3 cm (CC x AP x TRA) is seen all around the proximal humerus, extending from proximal physeal plate upto distal metaphyseal region, ending about 4 cm above elbow joint line. Proximally, stripped periosteum is seen attached to the perichondrium.

Transphyseal spread to infection with physeal separation and medial subluxation of proximal humeral epiphysis is seen. Abnormal enhancement is also seen in proximal epiphysis and secondary ossification centre, consistent with epiphyseal involvement.

Extension of inflammation to adjacent soft tissue is also seen with features of myositis. No feature of necrosis or collection is seen in the soft tissue.

Joints:

Minimal fluid is seen in left shoulder joint. Mild smooth synovial enhancement is seen in left shoulder and elbow joints. The possibility of early mild infection to joint space could not be ruled out.

Left shoulder and elbow joint alignment is normal. Joint space and articular cartilage appear grossly normal.

Multiple axillary nodes are seen, largest measuring 9 m in SAD.

Rest of the visualised bones show no alteration in signal intensity.

Rest of the soft tissue appear normal.

Few patchy consolidations are seen in lower lobes of both lungs.

IMPRESSION:

Features of acute left humeral osteomyelitis with marrow ischemia and transphyseal extension to epiphysis.

Septic physeal separation with medial subluxation of proximal humeral epiphysis.

Large sub periosteal collection and soft tissue inflammation as detailed.

Minimal left shoulder joint effusion and synovial thickening in left shoulder and elbow joints. The possibility of early infection could not be ruled out.

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT KNEE JOINT REGION

Clinical profile: H/o benign hamartomatous lesion/ hemangioma in lateral aspect of right distal thigh, operated on 20/04/2018.  Now c/o pain in right knee region for past 1 month.

Technique: PD fs, IR, T1, T2, DWI, GRE, post contrast T1 in all planes. CT correlation. Whole body IR/ T1 screening. Preoperative MRI is not available for comparison.

Old post-operative changes are seen in lateral aspect of distal thigh region.

Mild diffuse reduced volume of thigh muscles and relatively smaller bones is seen on right side, when compared to left side. Fatty atrophy is seen involving right vastus lateralis muscle in the distal part. However, no abnormal signal intensity is seen in muscles.

Bones and joints:

A well-defined lobulated lesion measuring approximately 1.6 x 1.4 x 0.8 cm is seen in anterior suprapatellar fat pad region in superolateral aspect. The lesion shows progressive post contrast enhancement. No calcification or cystic areas are seen, suggestive of residual/ recurrent lesion.

Minimal joint effusion is seen.

Right distal femur: Extensive heterogeneous marrow PDfs/ IR hyperintensity/ T1 hyperintensity with post contrast enhancement are seen involving distal metaphyseal region of right distal femur. Few small punctate/ serpigineous lytic foci with T2 hyperintensity and without post contrast enhancement are seen with surrounding mild diffuse sclerosis. No definite sclerotic rim or collection seen in the present study.  No periosteal reaction or bony destruction seen. No significant diffusion restriction or extra osseous soft tissue mass lesion is seen.

Mild irregularity of distal femoral growth plate is seen with altered enhancement when compared to other visualised physis. Mild similar marrow changes are also seen in epiphysis. However, no abnormal enhancement is seen in epiphysis.

Left distal femur: Small similar focus of altered signal intensity and sclerosis is seen in left distal femoral metaphysis in posterolateral aspect.

No other similar marrow signal abnormality seen in rest of the visualised bones in screening of whole body.

The knee joint is normal with respect to alignment and joint space.

The medial and lateral menisci are normal in configuration and signal intensities.

The medial and lateral collateral ligaments and patellar retinaculi are normal.

Anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact and normal in signal intensity.

The intermeniscal and meniscofemoral ligaments are also normal.

Posterolateral and posteromedial corner ligament complex appear normal.

Extensor mechanism appears normal. Rest of the surrounding muscles, tendons and neurovascular structures are normal.

IMPRESSION:

Old post-operative changes and relatively reduced muscle volume and smaller bones on right side as detailed.

Well-defined lobulated enhancing lesion in superolateral aspect of patella as detailed, suggestive of residual/ recurrent lesion.

Extensive marrow changes with small lytic foci, sclerosis and enhancement in right distal femoral metaphysis with growth plate changes as detailed.

Small similar focus in left distal femoral metaphysis.

In view of imaging and clinical features, to consider the possibility of multifocal sub-acute osteomyelitis. However, suggested HPE correlation/ further evaluation to rule out the possibility of neoplastic etiology.

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT ANKLE (P+C)

Clinical profile: C/o ulceroproliferative soft tissue mass lesion in lateral aspect of right ankle for the past 6 to 7 years ? Squamous cell carcinoma.

Technique: PD fs, IR, T1, T2, DWI, GRE and Post contrast T1 in all planes. 

Bones and joints: 

Mild osteoarthrosis changes are seen in ankle, posterior subtalar and few joints in foot region.

Rest of the visualised bones and joints appear grossly normal for age.

Ligament complex:

Medial and lateral ligament complex appear grossly intact. No significant tear is seen.  

Tendons and rest of soft tissue:

Mild chronic insertional Achilles tendinopathy is seen with small tears and intratendinous calcification. No full thickness tear is seen.

No significant sinus tarsi inflammation is seen. 

Rest of the anterior, medial, peroneal and posterior tendons appear normal. No features of tenosynovitis are seen. Peroneal and flexor retinaculum is intact.

Primary soft-tissue lesion:

There is a poorly marginated exophytic soft-tissue mass centered predominantly in the skin and immediately subjacent subcutaneous tissues along the lateral aspect of the distal leg/ankle, measuring approximately 3.1 × 2.9 × 1.4 cm (AP × CC × depth).

The lesion is T1 isointense and heterogeneously T2/IR hyperintense and demonstrates marked diffusion restriction (ADC approximately 0.7–1.1 × 10⁻³ mm²/s) with moderate heterogeneous post-contrast enhancement.

No macroscopic fat, internal cystic/ necrotic component, matrix mineralisation or prominent intralesional vascular channels are identified.

The lesion extends through the subcutaneous tissues with infiltration of the underlying deep fascia and extension into the immediately deep fascial/ fat planes, indicating violation of the deep fascial compartment.

There is focal loss of the intervening fat plane with short segments of the adjacent Sural nerve and small saphenous vein, suspicious for local involvement. Definite nerve enlargement or proximal extension is not demonstrated on the present study.

No definite involvement of the adjacent muscles, peroneal tendons or tendon sheaths is identified.

No underlying cortical erosion or marrow abnormality is seen.

Additional soft tissues:

Mild diffuse skin thickening and subtle enhancement with subcutaneous edema along the lateral distal leg and ankle, without associated diffusion restriction, likely representing reactive inflammatory change.

No additional enhancing soft-tissue nodule or mass is identified.

No significant regional lymphadenopathy is visualized within the field of examination.

No drainable fluid collection.

IMPRESSION:

Ulceroproliferative exophytic cutaneous/ subcutaneous mass along lateral aspect of distal right leg/ ankle as detailed.

Local extension through deep fascia into immediately deep fascial/ fat planes and focal loss of intervening fat plane with adjacent Sural nerve and small saphenous vein  as detailed, suspicious for involvement.

No definite involvement of adjacent muscles, peroneal tendon sheaths or bone.

No additional soft-tissue lesion or significant regional lymphadenopathy seen.

Given clinical history and imaging morphology, the lesion is highly suspicious for cutaneous malignancy, like squamous cell carcinoma. Suggested clinical/ HPE correlation and follow up as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr Arrthe

MRI SCAN OF LEFT KNEE JOINT

Clinical Profile: H/o left knee pain for past few years; now with sudden onset of pain? Sub-acute osteomyelitis? Monoarticular rheumatoid arthritis of left knee joint. For detailed evaluation.

Technique: PDfs, T1, T2, IR, DWI, GRE, Post contrast T1 in al planes. CT correlation.

The knee joint is normal with respect to alignment and joint space.

Large lobulated mass lesion with focal ill-defined margins at few areas and measuring approximately 7.1 x 5.3 x 2.2 cm (CC x TRA x AP) is seen in medial aspect of Hoffa fat pad and extending superiorly along medial aspect of patella. The lesion appears heterogeneously hyperintense in T2/ IR images with few fibrous septa, small scattered hemorrhagic components and small calcific foci and altered diffusivity. The hyperintensity of the lesion is almost equal to joint fluid. The lesion shows intense heterogeneous post contrast enhancement with progressive filling in of contrast.

Focal bulging and herniation of the lesion is seen in anteromedial aspect between patellar tendon and medial patellar retinaculum and is seen extending upto deep fascia.

Subtle similar signal intensity changes are seen in inferomedial aspect of patella. Rest of the bones and fat planes appear normal.

Moderate joint effusion is seen. Diffuse irregular thickening and enhancement of the synovium is seen with blooming on T2* gradient echo images, suggestive of siderotic/ hypertrophic synovitis, probably secondary to repeated hemarthrosis.

Rest of the articulating bones are normal in outline and bone marrow signal intensity. No imaging features of osteomyelitis are seen.

The medial and lateral menisci are normal in configuration and signal intensities. No evidence of tear or degeneration.

The medial and lateral collateral ligaments and patellar retinaculi are normal.

Anterior cruciate and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact and normal in signal intensity.

The intermeniscal and meniscofemoral ligaments are also normal.

Extensor mechanism appears normal. Rest of the surrounding muscles, tendons and neurovascular structures are normal.

IMPRESSION:

Lobulated heterogeneously enhancing soft tissue mass lesion in anteromedial aspect of Hoffa fat pad with extensions and characteristics as detailed.

Moderate joint effusion with siderotic/ hypertrophic synovitis.

No other significant abnormality in left knee joint.

In view of clinical and imaging features, the possibility of synovial hemangioma is more likely than synovial sarcoma (less likely). Suggested HPE correlation.

IMPRESSION:

Significant soft tissue inflammation in anterior chest wall (right>left) with abscess as detailed.

Subtle altered marrow signal in adjacent right 3rd rib- may represent osteomyelitis. Suggested post contrast MR study.

Small T2 hyperintense focus with diffusion restriction and no significant post contrast enhancement is seen along the anterolateral aspect of fluid collection and abutting the adjacent bone. The lesion measures approximately 2.2 x 1.4 x 1 (CC x TRA x AP). Thin rim of diffusion restriction is also seen along the adjacent posterolateral wall of fluid the above mentioned fluid collection.

No other similar focal lesion is seen.

Atrophy with IR hyperintensity and post contrast enhancement involving adductor, quadriceps and hamstring group of muscles, likely due to denervation/ radiation induced changes.

Mild diffuse subcutaneous edema is seen in left thigh region, predominantly in anteromedial and medial aspects. No other significant fluid collection is seen.

Post-operative changes with large well defined fluid collection (likely seroma) in medial compartment of left upper thigh region as detailed.

MRI SCAN OF LEFT FOOT

Clinical profile: Known h/o hyperuricemia on treatment. C/o acute onset of left foot pain and unable to bear weight. No h/o recent injury.

Technique: PD fs, T1, T2, GRE, IR and PC T1 in all planes. Limited DECT correlation. 

Bones and joints: 

Mild acute periarticular soft tissue inflammation is seen along dorsomedial aspects of 4th and 5th toe regions. A tiny calcific focus is seen in lateral periarticular region of PIP joint region of 5th toe. DECT analysis does not show uric acid deposit pattern. No cortical erosion/ subarticular marrow changes are seen in the present study.

No other significant articular or periarticular calcific foci are seen in the foot region.

Minimal joint effusion and smooth synovitis is seen in ankle, posterior subtalar, intertarsal, cuboid-metatarsal and few metatarsophalangeal joints.

No fracture/ displaced fragment or callus formation is seen. 

No imaging features of acute osteomyelitis or septic arthritis are seen.

Ligaments:

Medial and lateral ligament complexes appear grossly intact. 

Rest of the visualized ligaments appears intact.

Tendons and rest of soft tissue:  

Diffuse subcutaneous edema is seen in dorsum of foot and ankle regions. No abnormal fluid collection or diffusion restriction is seen. Visualised muscles of foot appear normal.  
 
The anterior, medial and posterior tendons appear intact. No significant tendon tear or tenosynovitis is seen. Peroneal and flexor retinaculum is intact. 

Rest of the soft tissue appears grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Mild acute periarticular soft tissue inflammation in 4th and 5th toes with tiny calcific focus in 5th toe as detailed.

Smooth synovitis and minimal effusion in ankle and other foot joints as detailed.

Diffuse subcutaneous edema in foot and ankle regions as detailed.

No other significant abnormality seen.

In view of clinical and imaging features, the possibility of acute gouty arthritis and periarthritis is more likely than other inflammatory causes. Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT FOOT

Clinical profile: H/o right foot swelling S/p wound debridement done 13 years back, surgery details not available, now c/o swelling over the dorsal aspect of foot for 3 months.

Technique: T1, IR, T2, DWI, GRE Fat sat T2 axial, T1 axial, fat sat PD - sagittal, coronal; T1 and inversion recovery coronal, post contrast images in all three planes. CT correlation

Bones and joints:

Features of chronic osteomyelitis are seen involving 4th metatarsal bone with multiple lytic foci with surrounding sclerosis, cortical thickening, marrow signal changes and enhancement.

Healing stress fracture is seen involving the distal part of proximal phalanx of great toe with sclerosis and marrow edema.

Osteoarthrosis changes are seen in 1st MTP joint with mild hallux valgus deformity. Mild degenerative changes with minimal joint effusion are seen in ankle and posterior subtalar joints.

Ankle joint alignment is normal. Rest of the bones and joints appear grossly normal for age.

Soft tissue and tendons:

Large ill-defined enhancing soft tissue inflammatory mass lesion with multiple subcentimetric sized focal lesions appearing hyperintense with central hypointense dot and peripheral hypointense rim on T2-weighted images is seen involving the subcutaneous plane of antero-lateral aspect of dorsum of foot in mid and forefoot regions. This lesion is seen extending to involve and surround the 4th metatarsal bone and also the adjacent interossei muscles. The inflammatory soft tissue mass lesion measures about 4.7 x 3.5 x 2.7 cm.

Similar inflammatory mass lesion with focal lesions are also seen involving the plantar aspect of mid and fore foot regions and involving flexor digitorum brevis, quadratus plantae, interosseous muscles and lumbricals and extending to the subcutaneous fat plane. Mild diffuse subcutaneous edema and inflammation is seen in dorsum of foot region. No other significant infected fluid collection of sinus tract is seen.

Peroneal brevis tendinopathy is seen with longitudinal split. Rest of the tendons appear grossly intact. No other significant tendon tear is seen. Peroneal and flexor retinaculum is intact. 

Rest of the visualised soft tissues are grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Features of chronic osteomyelitis involving 4th metatarsal bone with multiple focal lesions and extensive soft tissue inflammatory mass formation in dorsal and plantar aspects of foot region and its extensions as detailed.

Healing stress fracture in proximal phalanx of great toe.

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT KNEE JOINT

Clinical profile: H/o fall injury with patellar dislocation 3 weeks back. For detailed evaluation.

Technique: PD fs, T1, IR, T2 and GRE in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and Articular Cartilage:

Typical sequelae of recent transient lateral patellar dislocation are noted with impaction-related osteochondral injuries/ bone marrow contusions involving anterolateral aspect of lateral femoral condyle and Inferomedial facet of patella.

Additional small focus of marrow edema is noted within posteromedial femoral condyle.

Focal chondral injury with superficial-to-deep chondral fissuring is seen along inferomedial patellar facet. No full-thickness cartilage defect or exposed subchondral bone identified.

Minimal joint effusion is noted. No displaced osteochondral fragment or intra-articular loose body is seen.

Remaining osseous structures and articular cartilage surfaces are preserved.

Patellofemoral Instability Risk Factor Assessment:

Patella morphology: Wiberg Type II.

Lateral trochlear inclination angle: 23° (normal; >11°).

Trochlear sulcus angle: 143° (normal; <154°).

Trochlear facet ratio: 61% (normal; >40%).

Trochlear depth: 5 mm (normal; >3 mm).

Insall-Salvati index: 1.2 (no patella Alta).

TT-TG distance: 16 mm (borderline increased).

Overall, no significant trochlear dysplasia or patella Alta is identified. Borderline increased TT-TG distance is noted.

Menisci:

Mild medial meniscocapsular sprain changes are seen with minimal medial meniscal signal changes. Rest of the medial and lateral menisci are normal in morphology and signal intensity.

No significant meniscal tear or displaced fragment is identified.

Ligaments:

Medial Patellofemoral Stabilizers:

High-grade partial to near-complete tear of femoral attachment of medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) with associated tearing of adjacent medial patellar retinaculum is seen. Ligament fibers appear edematous and mildly wavy.

Medial Collateral Ligament:

Grade I/ II sprain involving the femoral attachment of the superficial medial collateral ligament is seen. No complete ligament disruption.

Other Ligaments:

Lateral patellar retinaculum is intact.

Anterior and posterior ruciate ligaments are intact.

Lateral collateral ligament complex is intact.

Posterolateral and posteromedial corner structures are intact.

Extensor Mechanism and Soft Tissues:

Quadriceps tendon, patellar tendon, and remaining extensor mechanism are intact.

Surrounding muscles, tendons, and visualised neurovascular structures are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

MRI findings are consistent with recent transient lateral patellar dislocation with bone contusions/ osteochondral impaction injuries as detailed.

High-grade partial to near-complete tear of femoral attachment of medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) with associated medial patellar retinaculum.

Mild medial meniscocapsular sprain without meniscal tear.

Grade I/ I sprain of femoral attachment of medial collateral ligament.

No displaced osteochondral fragment, intra-articular loose body, cruciate ligament injury, or significant trochlear dysplasia.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT KNEE JOINT

Clinical profile: C/o right knee pain and crepitus? Chondromalacia patella. H/o obesity and severe exercise and running for weight reduction for past few years. No h/o recent injury or patellar dislocation.

Technique: PDfs, IR, T1, T2, T2 *MAP and GRE in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and articular cartilage:

Patellofemoral compartment:

Marked focal abnormality of articular cartilage of the medial patellar facet is seen, with surface irregularity, fraying, fissuring and partial to full-thickness cartilage loss.

A displaced chondral flap measuring about 14 × 8 × 2 mm (CC × TRA × thickness) is seen arising from medial patellar facet, with only a small residual focal attachment to the parent cartilage.

Associated cartilage delamination extends from the medial patellar facet toward the lateral patellar articular cartilage.

Chronic cortical hypertrophy, irregularity, remodeling and marginal osteophyte formation are seen along the medial patellar facet and medial aspect of the patella. Minimal subjacent subchondral marrow edema is present.

Overall, the medial patellar facet demonstrates advanced focal chondral injury/ degeneration with deep partial-thickness to focal full-thickness cartilage loss, corresponding to ICRS grade 3–4 / Outerbridge grade III–IV.

No significant osteochondral loose body is identified.

Clinical profile:  RTA on 02/06/2026 with penetrating muscle injury (steel prick), On 05/06/2026 - underwent right thigh wound exploration, debridement, muscle repair, and soft tissue repair, follow-up review on 09/07/2026 - pain and localized tenderness at the post-surgical wound site. Bones and joints:

Mild osteoarthrosis changes are seen in bilateral knee joints with mild joint effusion.

Well define paralabral cyst measuring 1.4 x 1 cm is seen in anteromedial aspect of left hip joint.

The visualised right femur appears grossly normal for age. No evidence of cortical thickening, periosteal reaction, or underlying bone marrow signal abnormality is seen in the adjacent bone.

No imaging features of acute osteomyelitis/ septic arthritis seen.

Soft tissue:

Right thigh region:

Resolving post-operative changes with edema are seen in skin, subcutaneous and deep subcutaneous fat planes in the anterolateral aspect of the right mid and lower thigh regions.

Few (three) irregular amorphous calcific foci are seen within the vastus intermedius muscle in intramuscular plane adjacent to the femur, the largest calcific focus abutting the periosteum , measures about 1.4 x 1.0 x 0.8 cm.

Resolving postoperative/ post-traumatic changes in anterolateral mid and distal right thigh regions involving muscles and subcutaneous plane with persistent edema and enhancement as detailed.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Sternoclavicular joints, sternocostal and costochondral articulations appears normal

Clinical profile: Swelling in the lateral aspect of lower thigh region for 4 years. No h/o injury or 

Technique: T1, IR in all planes, T2 axial, DWI, pre and post contrast T1 fs axial and coronal. Limited CT correlation.

Ill-defined, infiltrative slow-flow vascular malformations are seen involving the left gluteus maximus muscle and distal biceps femoris muscle, extending inferiorly towards the posterolateral aspect of the distal thigh and knee region.

The vascular malformation demonstrates predominantly fluid-sensitive hyperintense signal with post-contrast enhancement, in keeping with a low-flow, predominantly venous vascular malformation.

There is transfascial extension into the adjacent subcutaneous fat planes. No discrete solid soft-tissue component is identified.

Minimal similar vascular malformation components are seen deep to the tensor fascia lata and along the iliotibial band in the proximal thigh.

No significant non-enhancing macrocystic lymphatic component is seen.

Technique: PDfs axial and coronal, IR axial and coronal, T1, GRE, DWI in axial and coronal, Pre contrast T1fs axial, PC T1fs in all planes. CT correlation.

Postoperative / Tumor bed

Mild irregular soft tissue thickening and enhancement are seen at the operative bed between the lateral femoral condyle and iliotibial band, without significant diffusion restriction. Associated small foci of susceptibility blooming on GRE are consistent with postoperative hemosiderin deposition.

No discrete measurable enhancing soft tissue mass demonstrating restricted diffusion is identified to suggest definite residual/ recurrent tumor on the present MRI.

Diffuse adjacent synovial thickening and enhancement are noted predominantly along the lateral aspect of the knee joint.

Postoperative fibrotic changes with enhancement extend along the anterior aspect of the biceps femoris and into the posterolateral aspect of the popliteal fossa.

Perivenous postoperative fibrosis is seen around the popliteal vein, with associated lateral displacement. Intraluminal filling defect/ altered signal within the popliteal vein is suspicious for partial thrombosis.

Popliteal artery, sciatic nerve, common peroneal nerve and tibial nerve are grossly preserved.

Small indeterminate popliteal lymph node measuring approximately 7.3 × 5.6 mm is seen.

Joint / Synovium:

Moderate knee joint effusion with diffuse, relatively smooth enhancing synovial thickening is seen, predominantly along the lateral compartment.

No nodular synovial mass or focal area of diffusion restriction is identified.

Mild degenerative osteoarthritic changes are seen.

Osseous structures:

No focal marrow signal abnormality, cortical destruction, osseous erosion or abnormal marrow enhancement.

No evidence of osseous metastatic involvement on the present examination.

Alignment is maintained.

Meniscus:

Mild degenerative changes of menisci are seen. Rest of the medial and lateral menisci is grossly normal for age. No acute tear or displaced fragment seen.

Ligaments:

Postoperative changes are seen along the lateral patellar retinaculum. The medial and lateral collateral ligaments and medial patellar retinaculum appear intact.

Mild degenerative changes and thinning are noted in ACL.

The posterior cruciate ligaments appear intact. The intermeniscal and meniscofemoral ligaments are also normal.

Mildly diffuse edema is seen around the knee joint and the proximal leg regions. No loculated fluid collection noted.

Known case of biopsy-proven synovial sarcoma of left knee, status post excisional biopsy (compared with outside MRI dated 29/07/2026):

No discrete enhancing soft tissue mass with significant diffusion restriction is identified to suggest definite residual/ recurrent tumor on the present MRI.

Irregular mild enhancing soft tissue thickening at operative bed between lateral femoral condyle and iliotibial band, without restricted diffusion and with susceptibility blooming, favored to represent postoperative granulation/ fibrotic change and hemosiderin deposition.

MRI SCAN OF LEFT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: H/o fall injury yesterday. C/o severe pain and unable to lift arm.

Technique: PDfs, T1, T2, IR and GRE in in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Mild joint effusion is seen. No significant acute fracture or displaced fragment is seen.

Mild degenerative changes are seen in humeral head region. Rest of articulating bones are grossly normal in outline and marrow signal.

Rotator cuff:

Acute full thickness tear of subscapularis tendon is seen from its attachment to lesser tuberosity (CC dimension of 2.2 cm). Torn tendon is oedematous and wavy and is seen at the level of medial third of humeral head region with varying retraction. Maximum retraction is about 2.5 cm from insertion point. Small calcific focus is seen within the retraced subscapularis tendon, likely chronic calcific tendinosis changes.

Acute full thickness tear is seen involving the supraspinatus tendon (AP dimension of 1.8 cm). Torn tendon fibres are oedematous and wavy and with retraction of about 0.8 cm from insertion. Mild tendinosis with attenuation of supraspinatus tendon are seen.

Mild infraspinatus tendinosis is seen. Rest of rotator cuff muscles and tendons appear grossly normal.

LHBT is not seen, likely chronic tear. Deltoid muscle appears grossly normal.

Labroligamentous structures:

Degenerative changes are seen in the labrum with chronic tears in the anterosuperior and superior quadrants. Rest of the labrum appears grossly intact. No other significant acute tear or displaced fragment seen.

Sprain changes of anterior IGHL and adjacent capsule is seen. Disruption of biceps pulley is seen.

AC joint:

AC joint arthropathy is seen. The acromion is of type II morphology and is laterally sloping. Subacromial space is reduced measuring 4.7 mm. Mild sub acromial bursitis is seen. Features of subacromial impingement are seen.

Myofascial strain changes are seen involving subscapularis and supraspinatus muscles. Significant oedema is seen along the anterior aspect of the shoulder joint with minimal fluid along the fascia.

Rest of the soft tissue appear grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Acute full thickness tears of subscapularis and supraspinatus tendons with retracted oedematous fibres as detailed.

Mild joint effusion, LHBT and labral tears and capsuloligamentous injuries as detailed.

AC joint arthropathy with features of subacromial impingement and subacromial bursitis as detailed.

Myofascial strain changes involving subscapularis and supraspinatus muscles and adjacent soft tissue edema as detailed.

Chronic calcific tendinosis changes of subscapularis tendon.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT KNEE JOINT

Clinical profile: C/o right knee pain for 1 year, swelling for 6 months ? Meniscal tear. No h/o recent trauma.

Technique: PDfs, IR, T1, T2 and GRE in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Medial and patellofemoral joint predominant osteoarthrosis is seen with partial to full thickness cartilage loss, chondral fissure and osteophytes.

Mild to moderate joint effusion is seen with chronic reactive synovitis, lipoma arborescens and suprapatellar plica. No osteochondral fragment is seen.

Rest of knee joint and articulating bones appear grossly normal for age.

Meniscus:

Mild degenerative changes are seen in medial and lateral menisci.

Small chronic oblique tear is seen in posterior horn of medial meniscus. Mild extrusion of medial meniscus is seen. No significant posterior root tear is seen.

Mild stress and inflammatory changes are seen in MCL and pes anserinus bursae.

Rest of the medial and lateral menisci appears grossly normal.

Ligaments:

Mild degenerative changes are seen in ACL. No significant tear or waviness seen. The posterior cruciate ligament appears normal for age.

Medial and lateral collateral ligaments and patellar retinacula appear grossly intact. No significant tear or waviness seen.

Posterolateral and posteromedial corner ligament complexes appear grossly intact.

Rest of soft tissue:

Extensor mechanism appears grossly normal for age. Degenerative changes are seen at proximal femoral attachment of medial and lateral gastrocnemius muscles. Mild semimembranosus tendinosis is seen.

Rest of surrounding muscles, tendons and neurovascular structures are grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Right knee osteoarthrosis with effusion as detailed.

Small chronic medial meniscal tear, mild medial meniscal extrusion and stress/ inflammatory changes in MCL and pes anserinus bursae as detailed.

Mild degeneration of ACL and myotendinous changes as mentioned.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Muscles and Soft Tissues:

Visualized muscles of the neck, shoulder girdles and upper chest appear normal in bulk and signal intensity.

No evidence of muscle denervation changes, including involving the left trapezius muscle.

Mild cutaneous/ subcutaneous edema with mild enhancement is noted in left side of neck region, overlying left trapezius muscle, without underlying intramuscular edema, collection or mass lesion.

CT OF RIGHT KNEE

Clinical History: Alleged h/o slip and fall and sustained injury to right lower limb.

Bones and joints:

Acute comminuted displaced fracture involving the distal metadiaphyseal region of the right femur is seen, with mild posterior angulation of the distal fracture fragment.

The fracture demonstrates focal intra-articular extension along the anterior aspect of the distal femur, extending into the patellofemoral joint space. No gross articular surface depression is identified on the provided images.

Mild lipohemarthrosis is present, consistent with intra-articular fracture extension.

Proximal tibia, proximal fibula and patella are intact.

Overall knee alignment is maintained, with no dislocation.

Soft Tissues:

Surrounding soft-tissue swelling, contusion and edema are seen predominantly around the distal thigh/ knee region.

Diffuse muscle atrophy with fatty infiltration is noted in the visualized proximal leg, involving the anterior, medial and posterior compartments.

Similar chronic atrophic/ fatty changes are seen involving the visualized distal semimembranosus and posteromedial compartment musculature of the distal thigh.

These muscle changes appear chronic in nature.

Degenerative Changes:

Moderate degenerative osteoarthritic changes of the right knee joint is seen, predominantly involving medial tibiofemoral compartment, characterized by joint-space narrowing, marginal osteophyte formation and subchondral sclerosis.

No significant erosive osseous change.

IMPRESSION:

Acute comminuted displaced fracture of distal metadiaphyseal region of right femur with mild posterior angulation of distal fragment.

Focal intra-articular extension of fracture into patellofemoral joint space, with associated mild lipohemarthrosis.

Surrounding acute soft-tissue contusion and edema.

Chronic diffuse muscular atrophy with fatty replacement involving visualized proximal leg compartments and distal thigh musculature as described.

Moderate degenerative osteoarthritis of right knee.

MRI SCAN OF BONY PELVIS AND SCREENING OF LUMBAR SPINE

Clinical profile: Old case of CA left breast post-treatment (2018), suspected case of sub-acute hypersensitive pneumonitis (on steroids since 07/01/2025), osteopenia on injection Denosumab. Now complaints of back and left hip pain.

Technique:

Pelvis with Hip: IR, T1, T2, PDfs, DWI and GRE in all planes. CT correlation.

Screening of lumbar spine and lumbosacral plexus: T2 Sagittal and axial and 3D IR coronal.

Bones and joints:

Both femoral heads demonstrate normal contour, smooth articular surface, and normal bone marrow signal intensity.

No imaging features of avascular necrosis (AVN), subchondral fracture, or femoral head collapse are seen.

Bilateral hip joints appear grossly normal with preserved joint spaces and alignment. Trace of joint fluid is seen.

No significant joint effusion, cartilage erosion, or synovitis is noted.

The visualized pelvic bones and bilateral proximal femurs show normal marrow signal characteristics without focal lytic or sclerotic lesions to suggest skeletal metastasis.

Bilateral sacroiliac joints show osteoarthrosis changes with vacuum phenomenon.

Pubic symphysis appears grossly normal.

Soft tissues:

Altered signal intensity appearing hyper intense on T2/IR sequences with minimal fluid is noted in the left greater trochanteric bursa region, suggestive of mild left greater trochanteric bursitis. Minimal sub gluteus medius bursal inflammation is also seen.

Mild thickening and altered signal intensity in the form of IR/T2 hyper intensity are noted involving the tendon insertion sites of bilateral gluteus medius and minimus tendons (L>R), consistent with tendinosis. Partial thickness tear is seen in left gluteus medius tendon.

Rest of the visualized pelvic musculature and soft tissue planes appear grossly normal.

Screening of Lumbar Spine and Lumbar Plexus:

Screening sequences through the lumbar spine demonstrate normal vertebral alignment and body heights with no gross disc protrusion causing significant canal stenosis.

Mild disc desiccation, disc bulge and facetal arthropathy are seen at few levels. No significant mass effect over nerve roots seen.

Screening of the lumbosacral plexus demonstrates normal symmetry, course, and signal intensity of the visualized nerve roots without neural thickening, edema, or mass effect.

IMPRESSION:

Mild left greater trochanteric bursitis as detailed.

Bilateral gluteus medius and minimus tendinosis (L>R) as detailed.

No MRI evidence of focal skeletal metastasis in bony pelvis and femurs.

Mild lumbar spondylosis and SI joint osteoarthrosis.

No significant abnormality in lumbosacral plexus.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr Praveen

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT ANKLE JOINT

Clinical profile: Known DM. c/o swelling and pain in right ankle and foot region for the past 15 days. No h/o injury/ fever/ soft tissue ulcer. For detailed evaluation.

Technique: IR, T1, T2, PDfs, GRE and DWI in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Severe destructive neuropathic arthropathy (Charcot neuroarthropathy) is seen involving the midfoot, with extensive osseous fragmentation, irregularity, erosive/ destructive changes and multiple fractures involving the navicular, cuneiforms, anterolateral calcaneus and bases of the 2nd, 3rd and 4th metatarsals.

Extensive involvement of the intertarsal and tarsometatarsal articulations is seen, with marked joint incongruity, subluxation/ dislocation and osseous fragmentation.

Collapse of longitudinal plantar arch with rocker-bottom configuration of foot is seen.

Extensive marrow edema is seen involving the affected midfoot and adjacent hind foot bones, with associated joint effusions, compatible with active Charcot arthropathy.

Mild degenerative changes with minimal effusion are seen involving the ankle, posterior subtalar and first metatarsophalangeal joints.

No definite focal intraosseous abscess or drainable osseous collection identified. No convincing diffusion restriction within the abnormal marrow to specifically suggest an intraosseous abscess.

Soft Tissues:

Extensive diffuse soft-tissue edema is seen involving the midfoot, predominantly surrounding the involved joints and fracture fragments.

Diffuse skin and subcutaneous edema involving the dorsum of the foot, ankle and distal leg regions.

Diffuse fatty atrophy with increased T2/STIR signal involving the visualized distal leg and intrinsic foot musculature, in keeping with diabetic neuropathic muscular changes.

A thin fluid collection is seen along the medial aspect of the midfoot, communicating with the first tarsometatarsal joint. It demonstrates no significant diffusion restriction.

Minimal fluid within the flexor and peroneal tendon sheaths, without significant diffusion restriction.

No soft-tissue abscess or other drainable collection identified.

No soft-tissue ulcer, sinus tract or definite cutaneous breach identified.

No significant diffusion restriction within the visualized soft tissues.

Tendons:

Visualized flexor, extensor, peroneal and Achilles tendons are grossly intact.

Minimal tenosynovial fluid as described above, without features of infective tenosynovitis.

IMPRESSION:

Severe active Charcot neuroarthropathy of right midfoot, with extensive osseous fragmentation, fractures and marked disorganization of intertarsal and tarsometatarsal joints as detailed.

Marked midfoot collapse, loss of plantar arch and rocker-bottom foot deformity.

Extensive marrow edema and joint effusions involving affected midfoot/ hind foot bones, compatible with active neuropathic arthropathy.

No definite MRI evidence of intraosseous abscess or soft-tissue abscess. No soft-tissue ulcer or sinus tract. No significant diffusion restriction.

Diffuse skin/ subcutaneous edema and diabetic myoneuropathy changes involving the visualized distal leg and foot.

Minimal flexor and peroneal tenosynovial fluid without diffusion restriction.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT KNEE JOINT

Clinical profile: C/o severe knee pain for past 3 days, lateral meniscus tear in previously taken MRI(2024)

Technique: PDfs, IR, T1, T2 and GRE in all planes.

Joint and Synovium:

Mild to moderate right knee joint effusion is seen.

Diffuse synovial thickening with multiple nodular synovial proliferations is noted.

Numerous intra-articular calcific/ ossified nodules of varying sizes are seen within the knee joint, in association with the nodular synovial proliferation. The largest measures approximately 1.2 × 1.0 × 0.6 cm.

The nodular synovial lesions demonstrate blooming on gradient-echo images, corresponding to their calcific/ ossified composition.

Ligaments:

Mild degenerative signal changes of ACL are seen without significant fiber discontinuity or tear.

The medial and lateral collateral ligaments and patellar retinaculum appear intact.

Posterolateral and posteromedial corner ligament complex appear normal.

The extensor mechanism appears normal. Rest of the surrounding muscles, tendons and neurovascular structures are normal.

IMPRESSION:

Mild to moderate knee joint effusion with diffuse nodular synovial thickening and numerous intra articular loose bides as detailed, consistent with primary synovial chondromatosis.

Mild osteoarthrosis with partial-thickness articular cartilage loss.

Small chronic tear in anterior root of the lateral meniscus.

Mild degenerative changes of ACL without significant tear.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr Praveen

CT SCAN OF LUMBOSACRAL SPINE (PLAIN)

Clinical Profile: C/o low back pain for 3 months. No h/o trauma.

Cortical erosions and destruction of inferior endplate of L1 and superior endplate of L2 vertebrae are seen with adjacent sclerosis of the involved vertebrae. Grossly reduced L1-2 intervertebral disc space is seen.

Pre and bilateral anterior paravertebral soft tissue thickening and fluid collections are seen at this level, with maximum thickness of 1.7 cm on the right side. Few tiny calcific foci are seen within the collections.

Abnormal anterior epidural inflammatory soft tissue thickening is seen at this level causing indentation of the thecal sac and causing secondary spinal canal stenosis at this level.

Multiple discrete enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the retroperitoneum, largest measuring approximately 1.2 cm in short axis dimension.

Features are likely suggestive of infective spondylodiscitis. The possibility of tuberculous aetiology has to be considered.

Chronic right L5 spondylolysis is seen.

Rest of the vertebrae appear grossly normal.

Bulky uterus with few calcified fibroids is seen.

Rest of the visualised structures are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

Features of L1-L2 infective spondylodiscitis with destructive endplate changes, marked L1-2 disc-space narrowing, and adjacent vertebral sclerosis.

Bilateral anterior paravertebral/ prevertebral collections at L1-2 level with few internal calcific foci.

Anterior epidural inflammatory soft-tissue component at L1-2 level causing thecal sac indentation and secondary spinal canal stenosis.

Mild retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.

Chronic right L5 spondylolysis.

Bulky fibroid uterus.

Given the chronicity, paravertebral collections with internal calcific foci and associated lymphadenopathy, tuberculous spondylodiscitis is more likely. Suggested MRI for further detailed evaluation.

reports.fullText:
MRI SCAN OF LEFT FOOT (PLAIN)

Clinical profile: C/o DM, left foot plantar aspect unhealthy wound for 6 months. Treated elsewhere with wound debridement/ dressing. H/o left great toe amputation status 1 year before.

Technique: T1, IR, T2, DWI, PDfs, GRE in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Cortical erosions and ill-defined osteolytic changes are noted along the plantar aspect of the calcaneus, predominantly involving its lateral aspect, with associated abnormal marrow signal changes, suggestive of acute osteomyelitis. A small intraosseous collection measuring approximately 1.2 × 0.8 × 0.8 cm is seen within the calcaneus, consistent with an intraosseous abscess.

Associated irregular plantar soft tissue ulceration and contiguous infected fluid collections are noted, as described below.

Healing fracture of the base of the fifth metatarsal is noted, without significant associated marrow signal abnormalities to suggest acute osteomyelitis.

Chronic post-amputation changes of the great toe are noted, with a small residual stump of the base of the proximal phalanx.

Osteoarthritic changes are noted involving the ankle, a few midfoot joints and the first metatarsophalangeal joint.

No imaging features of septic arthritis are identified.

Ankle joint alignment is maintained. The remaining visualised bones and joints are otherwise unremarkable.

Soft tissue:

An irregular soft tissue ulcer is noted along the plantar aspect of midfoot and hind foot.

Irregular, diffusion-restricting fluid collections are noted along the medial and lateral plantar aspects of the foot, communicating with or extending from the region of the underlying calcaneal osteomyelitis. These measure approximately:

Medial plantar collection: 4.1 × 1.7 × 0.6 cm (TR × AP × CC).

Lateral plantar collection: 4.1 × 1.9 × 1.0 cm (AP × CC × TR).

Minimal additional infected fluid is noted along the plantar fascia.

A segment of the plantar fascia is not distinctly visualised near its lateral calcaneal attachment, likely related to inflammatory destruction and post procedural changes.

Extensive surrounding inflammatory changes are noted in the plantar soft tissues, particularly around the ulcer, calcaneal insertion and adjacent fluid collections.

Diffuse fatty atrophy and oedematous signal changes are noted in the intrinsic muscles of the foot, consistent with diabetic myopathy/myoneuropathy changes.

Diffuse inflammatory oedematous changes are noted in the skin and subcutaneous tissues along the dorsum of the foot, ankle and distal leg.

No other significant drainable fluid collection is identified.

IMPRESSION:

Acute calcaneal osteomyelitis, predominantly involving plantar aspect, with osteolytic changes and small intraosseous abscess as detailed.

Extensive plantar soft tissue infection with abscess formation, extending along the medial and lateral plantar aspects of the foot, with associated plantar ulceration and surrounding inflammatory changes.

Diffuse cellulitis changes involving dorsum of the foot, ankle and distal leg.

Healing fracture of base of fifth metatarsal, without convincing MRI evidence of associated acute osteomyelitis.

Chronic post-amputation changes of left great toe.

Diabetic myoneuropathy changes involving the intrinsic muscles of the foot.

No MRI evidence of septic arthritis.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF LEFT FOOT (PLAIN + CONTRAST)

Clinical profile: C/o swelling and discharge from left foot for 3 days. Known DM on treatment. H/o left 5th toe amputation + foreign body removal? Osteomyelitis.

Technique: T1, IR, T2, DWI and PC T1 in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Post-amputation changes of the left fifth toe are noted, with non-visualisation of the phalanges.

Mild abnormal marrow signal hyper intensity on IR sequences with mild post-contrast enhancement is noted in the head of the fifth metatarsal. No significant cortical erosion or destruction is identified. In the given clinical setting, these findings are suspicious for early acute osteomyelitis.

Degenerative arthropathy changes are noted in the midfoot joints, with prominent marginal osteophytes and subchondral marrow signal changes.

Prominent dorsal and plantar calcaneal enthesophytes are noted.

The ankle joint alignment is maintained. The remaining visualised bones and joints are otherwise unremarkable.

Soft tissue:

Few small, ill-defined, diffusion-restricting fluid collections are noted along the dorsal, lateral and plantar aspects of fifth metatarsal head, largest measuring approximately 1.3 × 0.8 × 0.4 cm, suspicious for small abscesses. A small cutaneous opening is noted along the plantar aspect of the foot in this region.

Significant surrounding soft tissue oedema and post-contrast enhancement are noted around the fifth metatarsal head and adjacent fluid collections, consistent with infective inflammatory changes.

Three small hyper dense foci are noted on CT correlation along the lateroplantar aspect of the midfoot, associated with susceptibility artefacts. These may represent retained foreign bodies or postoperative material. Clinical and surgical correlation is advised.

Diffuse skin thickening and subcutaneous oedema with mild post-contrast enhancement are noted over the dorsum of the foot, consistent with cellulitis.

Diffuse fatty atrophy and signal alterations of the visualised intrinsic foot muscles are noted, consistent with diabetic myopathy/ myoneuropathy changes.

Mild distal Achilles tendinopathy and plantar fasciitis are noted.

The visualised anterior, medial and posterior tendons are otherwise intact. No significant tenosynovitis is seen.

The peroneal and flexor retinacula are intact.

No significant inflammatory changes are noted in the sinus tarsi.

IMPRESSION:

Mild marrow signal abnormality and enhancement in head of fifth metatarsal as detailed, suspicious for early acute osteomyelitis.

Small adjacent soft tissue abscesses along dorsal, lateral and plantar aspects of fifth metatarsal head and surrounding infective inflammatory changes.

Diffuse dorsal foot cellulitis as mentioned.

Three small hyper dense foci with susceptibility artefacts along lateroplantar aspect of midfoot, possibly retained foreign bodies or postoperative material.

Post-amputation changes of left fifth toe.

Midfoot osteoarthritis, mild Achilles tendinopathy and plantar fasciitis.

Diabetic myoneuropathy changes of the intrinsic foot muscles.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI OF CERVICAL SPINE WITH SCREENING OF REST OF SPINE AND RIGHT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical Profile: C/o neck pain and right shoulder pain.

Technique: Sagittal T1, T2, IR, Axial T2.

Screening of rest of the spine: T2 sagittal

Screening of right shoulder joint: PDfs in all planes.

The cervical spine shows normal lordotic curvature and vertebral column alignment.

The individual vertebrae are normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities. Small vertebral body haemangioma is seen at C7 level.

Disc desiccation is seen at almost all levels with mild uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy at few levels. The vertebral end-plates are normal. The intervertebral discs are normal in heights.

C2-3: No significant abnormality seen.

C3-4: Mild disc bulge is seen. No significant mass effect over nerve roots seen.

C4-5: Disc bulge and uncovertebral arthropathy (R>L) are seen causing mild indentation of cord and right ventral C5 nerve root. No significant mass effect over exiting nerve roots seen.  

C5-6: Disc bulge and uncovertebral arthropathy are seen causing mild indentation of cord and ventral C6 nerve roots. No significant mass effect over exiting nerve roots seen.

C6-7: Small central protrusion is seen. No significant mass effect or nerve roots seen.

C7-D1: Normal.  

Spinal cord shows normal signal intensity.

The prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues are normal.

The Craniovertebral junction and atlantoaxial joint are normal.

Screening of dorsal spine:

Mild disc desiccation and flaval thickening are seen at few levels.

Spinal cord appears normal. No other significant abnormality seen.

Screening of lumbar spine:

Complete sacralisation of L5 vertebra is seen.

The conus medullaris ends at D12-L1 level and the cauda equine is normal in appearance.

Mild disc desiccation and facetal arthropathy are seen at few levels, more significant at L4-5 level with endplate changes.

Mild disc bulge is seen at few levels more significant at L4-5 level with posterior annular fissure. No significant mass effect over nerve roots seen.

No other significant abnormality seen in lumbar spine.

Screening of right shoulder joint:

Minimal right shoulder joint effusion is seen.

Mild supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendinosis is seen with small chronic partial thickness intrasubstance tears. Small chronic partial thickness articular surface tear is also seen in cranial part of subscapularis tendon. No full thickness tear seen.

Mild AC joint arthropathy is seen. Type I acromion is seen and is laterally sloping.

Reduced subacromial space is seen (4.2 mm) with mild subacromial bursitis and minimal fluid collection. Features are suggestive of suggestive of subacromial impingement.

No other significant abnormality seen in screening images of right shoulder joint.

IMPRESSION:

Complete sacralisation of L5 vertebra.

Mild diffuse degenerative changes of spine as detailed.

Disc bulge and uncovertebral arthropathy causing mild indentation of cord and ventral nerve roots at C4-5 and C5-6 levels as detailed.

Rotator cuff tendinosis with small chronic tears and features of subacromial impingement in right shoulder joint as mentioned.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF LEFT FOOT

Clinical profile: 12-year-old football player presented with left heel pain for 2 days.

Technique: PDfs, T1, T2, GRE, IR and DWI in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

The calcaneal apophysis demonstrates no significant abnormality. No abnormal marrow edema, fracture line or other evidence of acute trabecular injury is identified in the calcaneus.

Few nonspecific patchy foci of marrow hyper intensities are noted in visualized bones. No focal marrow edema pattern suggestive of acute fracture or significant trabecular injury is identified.

Rest of the visualized bones demonstrate preserved alignment and marrow signal.

Trace fluid is noted in the ankle, a few midfoot joints and the first metatarsophalangeal joint, without significant joint effusion or associated synovial thickening.

The visualized articular surfaces are preserved.

Ligaments:

The visualized medial and lateral ligamentous complexes are intact, without significant thickening, edema or discontinuity.

The remaining visualized ligamentous structures appear unremarkable.

Tendons and rest of soft tissue:

Mild thickening and edema-like signal alteration are noted in the plantar heel pad overlying the calcaneus, without a discrete fluid collection.

The Achilles tendon is intact, with preserved thickness and signal. The plantar fascia is intact at its calcaneal attachment, without significant thickening, perifascial edema or tear.

The remaining visualized tendons and soft tissue structures appear unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

Mild heel fat pad edema as detailed, likely represents pressure-related or mechanical soft-tissue changes.

Few nonspecific patchy marrow hyper intensities in visualized bones, without evidence of acute fracture or significant trabecular injury.

No MRI evidence of calcaneal apophysitis.

Trace fluid in ankle and few other joints without significant effusion or synovitis.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF LEFT ANKLE AND FOOT

Clinical profile: Suspected plantar fasciitis with mild swelling of ankle region.

Technique: PDfs, T1, T2, IR, GRE and DWI in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

The ankle joint alignment is maintained.

A prominent plantar calcaneal enthesophyte is noted, with subtle adjacent marrow edema at the plantar fascial attachment.

Trace joint fluid is noted in the ankle, subtalar and first metatarsophalangeal joints, without significant joint effusion or synovial thickening.

The remaining visualized bones demonstrate preserved alignment and marrow signal. No acute fracture or focal osteochondral lesion is identified.

Ligament complex:

The visualized medial and lateral ligamentous complexes are intact, without evidence of significant sprain or tear.

Tendons:

Trace fluid is noted within the tendon sheaths of the tibialis posterior and flexor digitorum tendons, suggesting mild tenosynovial fluid.

The remaining visualized tendons, including the Achilles and peroneal tendons, demonstrate preserved thickness and signal, without significant tear.

Plantar fascia and soft tissues:

Mild thickening and increased signal intensity of the plantar fascia is seen at its calcaneal attachment, with mild adjacent perifascial edema, consistent with plantar fasciitis. No discrete partial- or full-thickness tear is identified.

Mild subcutaneous soft tissue edema is noted around the ankle, predominantly along the medial aspect. No organized fluid collection is seen.

A small ganglion cyst measuring approximately 7.5 × 3.5 × 2.8 mm is noted along the dorsal aspect of the talonavicular articulation.

The remaining visualized soft tissue structures are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

Plantar fasciitis with mild perifascial edema and subtle reactive marrow edema at calcaneal attachment. No discrete plantar fascial tear.

Prominent plantar calcaneal enthesophyte with minimal marrow edema.

Trace tendon sheath fluid involving tibialis posterior and FDL tendons.

Mild predominantly medial perimalleolar subcutaneous soft tissue edema.

Small dorsal talonavicular ganglion cyst as mentioned.

reports.fullText:
Dr Praveen

MRI OF LEFT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: H/o seizure followed by fall on 07.10.2026. C/o left shoulder pain with restricted movements.

Technique: PDfs, T1, GRE, T2 and IR in all planes and CT correlation

Bones and Glenohumeral Joint:

An acute Hill-Sachs impaction injury is noted along the posterolateral aspect of the humeral head, characterized by subtle cortical flattening and associated marrow edema.

No acute bony Bankart fracture is identified.

Mild marrow edema is noted in the coracoid process without a definite fracture line or displaced osseous fragment, favouring a bone contusion.

Mild glenohumeral joint effusion is present. No intra-articular osteochondral loose body is identified.

The glenohumeral alignment is currently maintained.

Rotator Cuff:

Subscapularis: Near-complete full-thickness tear of subscapularis tendon is seen at its lesser tuberosity attachment, with a few suspicious residual intact fibers along its inferior aspect. The torn tendon end is edematous and lax, with approximately 1.7 cm of retraction, extending to the medial third of the humeral head. A tiny associated cortical avulsion fragment is suspected at the lesser tuberosity.

Significant strain-related edema is noted in the subscapularis muscle, with a partial-thickness intrasubstance tear.

Supraspinatus and infraspinatus: Mild acute strain-related and tendinopathy signal changes with small partial-thickness tears involving the supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendons. No additional full-thickness tear is identified.

Teres minor: Mild myofascial strain-related edema is noted.

Deltoid and short head of biceps: Mild strain-related edema is present.

Adjacent fascial edema and minimal fluid are noted around the infraspinatus and teres minor muscles. No significant intramuscular hematoma or organized fluid collection is identified.

The long head of the biceps tendon is grossly intact.

Labroligamentous structures and joint capsule:

A soft-tissue Bankart lesion is noted, with tearing of the anteroinferior glenoid labrum. The labral tear extends into the anterosuperior, superior and posterosuperior quadrants. No displaced labral fragment is identified.

High-grade sprain of the biceps pulley complex is present.

Sprain of the inferior glenohumeral ligament (IGHL) and inferior joint capsule is noted, with a partial-thickness tear of anterior band of IGHL at its humeral attachment, consistent with a partial humeral avulsion of the glenohumeral ligament (HAGL lesion).

Disruption of the anterior joint capsule is noted, with extensive adjacent soft tissue and fascial edema and fluid tracking along the adjacent fascial planes into the proximal arm, axilla and visualized thoracic region.

Extensive soft tissue edema is also noted along the anteroinferior aspect of the glenohumeral joint. No organized collection or significant hematoma is identified.

Acromioclavicular Joint:

AC joint appears grossly intact. Type II acromion is seen. Acromiohumeral interval is maintained. Mild subacromial-bursal fluid is seen.

IMPRESSION:

Acute Hill-Sachs impaction injury as detailed. No acute bony Bankart fracture.

Near-complete full-thickness tear of subscapularis tendon from its lesser tuberosity attachment, muscle strain and tiny cortical avulsion fragment.

Mild acute strain-related changes with small partial-thickness tears of supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendons.

Soft-tissue Bankart with extension of tear and ligamentous injuries as detailed.

Anterior joint capsular disruption with extensive pericapsular and interfascial edema/ fluid tracking into proximal arm, axilla and visualized thoracic region.

Multifocal acute periarticular muscle strains involving the subscapularis, infraspinatus, teres minor, deltoid and short head of biceps muscles.

Mild glenohumeral joint effusion and subacromial-subdeltoid bursitis.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF BILATERAL LOWER LIMBS (PLAIN)

Clinical profile: C/o bilateral leg pain and difficulty in walking x 4 days, fever.  K/c/o renal dysfunction, CAD, native drug intake for skin allergy.

Technique: T2, IR, T1 and DWI in all planes. Hip joint: T1 and IR coronal, CT correlation.

Bilateral hip joints:

Advanced osteoarthritic changes are noted in both hip joints, characterized by diffuse full-thickness articular cartilage loss, extensive subchondral cystic changes, sclerosis and marrow edema, with marginal osteophyte formation.

Mild alteration of the femoral head contours is noted bilaterally, with mild features of protrusio acetabuli.

Minimal bilateral hip joint effusions are present, likely reactive.

No focal marrow changes or periarticular findings specifically suggestive of acute osteomyelitis or septic arthritis are identified on the present study.

Bilateral knee joints:

Mild osteoarthritic changes are noted in both knee joints, with associated joint effusions.

Bones:

The remaining visualized osseous structures demonstrate no significant focal marrow lesion or other focal marrow signal abnormality.

Muscles and soft tissues:

Diffuse patchy edema-like signal hyper intensities are noted involving multiple muscle groups bilaterally, predominantly the iliacus and gluteal muscles, anterior, medial and posterior compartments of the thighs, and anterior and posterior compartments of the legs.

Associated mild diffuse edema is noted along the superficial and intermuscular fascial planes.

Mild diffuse subcutaneous edema is present in the visualized abdominal wall, pelvis and bilateral lower limbs, more pronounced in the distal legs, around the ankles and over the dorsum of the feet.

No discrete intramuscular or subcutaneous fluid collection is identified. No convincing restricted diffusion is seen within the affected muscles or soft tissues to suggest a drainable abscess.

Mild diffuse muscle atrophy with fatty infiltration is noted in the bilateral gluteal and lower limb muscles, predominantly involving the posterior compartments.

Mild ascites is noted in the visualized abdomen and pelvis.

The remaining visualized muscles and soft tissues are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

Diffuse multifocal bilateral lower limb muscle edema involving pelvic, gluteal, and thigh and leg muscles with associated fascial edema, may represent inflammatory/ toxic myopathy and systemic edema-related changes.

Diffuse bilateral subcutaneous edema pelvis and lower limbs, more pronounced in distal legs, ankles and dorsum of the feet, with mild ascites.

No discrete intramuscular collection or restricted diffusion to suggest abscess.

No definite MRI evidence of acute osteomyelitis or septic arthritis.

Advanced bilateral hip osteoarthritis and mild knee osteoarthritis.

Mild diffuse fatty atrophy of bilateral gluteal and lower limb muscles, predominantly involving posterior compartments.

Suggested clinical correlation/ further evaluation and review as indicated.

Clinical profile: C/o pain in right knee joint. No h/o recent trauma.

Technique: PDfs, IR, T1, T2 and GRE in all planes. CT correlation.

Medial and patellofemoral joint predominant osteoarthrosis is seen with partial thickness cartilage loss, chondral fissure, subchondral edema/ cysts and small osteophytes.

Mild joint effusion is seen with chronic reactive synovitis, lipoma arborescens and suprapatellar plica. Small Baker cyst is seen. No loose bodies are seen.

Rest of knee joint and articulating bones appear grossly normal for age.

Meniscus:

Degenerative changes are seen in medial and lateral menisci.

Chronic complex tear with horizontal and oblique components are seen involving body, anterior and posterior horns of medial meniscus. Mild extrusion of the inferior flap fragment is seen causing mild stress and inflammatory changes in MCL bursa.

Rest of the medial and lateral menisci appears grossly normal for age. No other significant tear are displaced fragment seen.

Ligaments:

Mucoid degenerative changes are seen in ACL with few small cruciate ligament cysts. Mild degenerative changes of posterior cruciate ligament are also seen. No significant tear or waviness seen.

Medial and lateral collateral ligaments and patellar retinacula appear grossly intact. No significant tear or waviness seen.

Posterolateral and posteromedial corner ligament complexes appear grossly intact.

Rest of soft tissue:

Extensor mechanism appears grossly normal for age. Mild degenerative changes are seen at proximal femoral attachment of medial and lateral gastrocnemius muscles.

Rest of surrounding muscles, tendons and neurovascular structures are grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Right knee osteoarthrosis with effusion and small Baker cyst as detailed.

Chronic complex medial meniscal tear with mild extrusion of inferior flap fragment causing stress/ inflammatory changes as detailed.

Mucoid degeneration of ACL and myotendinous changes as mentioned.

No other significant abnormality seen.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF CERVICAL SPINE AND SCREENING OF REST OF THE SPINE AND BRAIN

Clinical Profile: Known case of L4-L5-S1 disc disease with L5-S1 recurrent disc prolapse and L4-L5 instability, early cauda equina syndrome. L4-L5-S1 decompression, discectomy and TLIF done on 12.01.2023. Now c/o inability to walk, imbalance and left upper limb tremors

Technique: Sagittal T1, T2, IR, Axial T2. T2/ IR sagittal for whole spine screening. FLAIR and DWI axial for brain. CT correlation.

Mild loss of cervical lordosis is seen with grossly normal vertebral column alignment.

The individual vertebrae are normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities.

Disc desiccation is seen at all levels and uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy at multiple levels. The intervertebral discs are normal in heights. The vertebral end-plates are normal.

C2-3: No significant disc bulge is seen.

C3-4: Diffuse disc bulge and bilateral uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy (R>L) are seen causing secondary spinal canal stenosis (residual thecal sac measures 7.1 mm in midline sagittal dimension) and compression of cord and bilateral exiting C4 nerve roots.

C4-5: Diffuse disc bulge with central protrusion and bilateral uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy are seen causing secondary spinal canal stenosis (residual thecal sac measures 5.9 mm in midsagittal dimension) and compression of cord and bilateral exiting C5 nerve roots.

C5-6: Diffuse disc bulge and uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy are seen causing secondary spinal canal stenosis (residual thecal sac measures 8.5 mm in midsagittal dimension) and compression of cord and bilateral exiting C6 nerve roots.

C6-7: Mild disc bulge with bilateral uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy are seen causing mild indentation of cord and compression of bilateral exiting C7 nerve roots.

Spinal cord: Abnormal T2/ IR hyper intensities with thinning of the cord are seen from C3-4 to C5-6 levels, consistent with chronic compressive myelopathy changes. Similar changes are also seen in cervical spinal cord at C1-C2 level predominantly involving the right half of the cord.  Rest of the spinal cord shows normal signal intensity.

The prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues are grossly normal.

The craniovertebral junction and atlantoaxial joints are normal for age.

Screening of dorsal spine:

Disc desiccation is seen at all levels with flaval thickening and small disc protrusions at few levels. Disc protrusion causing mild indentation of the cord is seen at D3-D4 level. No abnormal cord signal changes are seen.

Small vertebral body haemangioma is seen at D3 level. No other significant abnormality seen in screening dorsal spine.

Screening of lumbar spine:

Loss of lumbar lordosis is seen. Chronic postoperative changes are seen at L4-L5-S1 levels with metallic pedicle screws, and interbody disc spacers in situ. Orthopaedic hardware is in satisfactory position. Mild chronic endplate changes are seen at these levels. Postoperative changes are seen in the adjacent soft tissue.

Diffuse disc bulge with posterior annular fissure, facetal arthropathy and flaval thickening are seen at L3-4 level causing severe secondary spinal canal stenosis and compression of bilateral traversing L4 nerve roots and cauda equina nerve fibres.

Conus medullaris ends at L1 level. No other significant abnormality seen in the lumbar spine.

Brain screening:

Mild diffuse age related atrophic changes of brain are seen.

No significant acute infarct or haemorrhage seen.

No other significant abnormality seen in the screening brain sequences.

IMPRESSION:

Diffuse degenerative changes of spine as detailed.

Disc changes and arthropathy causing canal stenosis and mass effect over cord and bilateral nerve roots from C3-4 to C6-7 levels, more severe at C3-4 and C4-5 levels as detailed.

Chronic compressive myelopathy changes in cervical spinal cord as detailed.

Chronic postoperative changes at L4-L5-S1 levels with metallic screws, and interbody disc spacer in situ.

Disc bulge with facetal arthropathy and flaval thickening are seen causing severe canal stenosis and compression of bilateral L4 nerve roots and cauda equina nerve fibres at L3-4 level as detailed.

Mild diffuse age related cerebral atrophy. No acute infarct or haemorrhage seen.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
MRI SCAN OF BRACHIAL PLEXUS

Clinical Profile: H/o polytrauma in June/ 2026. Closed displaced fracture of left clavicle, C5-C7 transverse process fracture, left brachial plexus injury with complete weakness and sensory loss in left upper limb.

Technique: 3DIR, T2, T1, DWI in all planes. Screening of cervical spine: T2/ IR sagittal and axial.

Brachial plexus

Preganglionic nerve root avulsion injuries involving the left C7 and C8 nerve roots is seen, with associated pseudomeningocele formation.

Gross attenuation of left C5 and C6 nerve roots is seen, consistent with severe postganglionic nerve injury. Postganglionic injury of the left D1 nerve root is also noted.

Distal retraction of the left brachial plexus nerve elements is seen, with thickening and oedematous signal changes involving the retracted nerve end in the infraclavicular region. Mild beaded morphology is noted along a few of the retracted nerve ends.

Diffuse increased T2-weighted signal intensity is seen involving the remaining visualised left brachial plexus trunks, divisions, cords and terminal nerves, consistent with associated traumatic neuropathic changes.

Mild perineural fibrosis is noted in the infraclavicular region surrounding the retracted nerve ends.

No significant haematoma or organised fluid collection is identified along the course of the left brachial plexus.

The right brachial plexus appears unremarkable.

Cervical spine screening:

Disc desiccation is seen at multiple levels and uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy at few levels. The intervertebral discs are normal in heights.

C3-4: Mild uncovertebral arthropathy (R>L) and small central protrusion are seen causing indentation of right exiting C4 nerve root.

C4-5: Disc bulge with uncovertebral arthropathy are seen causing indentation of cord and bilateral exiting C5 nerve roots (R>L).

C5-6: Mild disc bulge and uncovertebral arthropathy are seen. No mass effect over nerve roots seen.

Spinal cord shows normal signal intensity.

Muscles and tendons:

Diffuse atrophy with increased IR signal intensity and fatty changes is seen involving the left shoulder girdle muscles, trapezius and visualised left hemi thoracic muscles, consistent with sub-acute-to-chronic denervation changes secondary to the known left brachial plexus injury.

The visualised right-sided muscles and tendons around the thoracic outlet demonstrate preserved morphology and signal intensity.

Bones:

Healing left clavicle fracture is seen with orthopaedic implant noted in-situ.

Old healed fractures of C5-C7 left transverse process are seen.

No obvious mass lesion / other significant finding are noted.

IMPRESSION:

Severe traumatic left brachial plexus injury with combination of preganglionic and postganglionic nerve injuries as detailed.

Preganglionic avulsion of left C7 and C8 nerve roots with pseudomeningocele formation and post ganglionic injury of left C5, C6 and D1 nerve roots with attenuation as detailed.

Distal retraction of left brachial plexus nerve elements, with thickening, edema and mild beaded morphology of few retracted nerve ends, associated with mild infraclavicular perineural fibrosis.

Diffuse denervation changes involving left shoulder girdle, trapezius and visualised left hemi thoracic muscles, with atrophy and fatty replacement, consistent with sub-acute-to-chronic denervation.

Cervical spondylosis changes, most pronounced at C4-5 level as detailed.

No abnormal cervical cord signal changes.

Healing left clavicular fracture with fixation hardware in situ and old healed left C5–C7 transverse process fractures.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.
