MRI SCAN OF LEFT FOOT

Clinical profile: Known diabetic for more than 10 years. C/o infected wound with exposed bone over left foot for 2 weeks with osteomyelitis and septic arthritis. H/o nail prick injury 2-3 weeks back. Wound debridement, great toe and 2nd toe amputation done few days back.

Technique: T2, DWI, GRE - axial, T1, IR, PC T1 in all planes, Leg screening – T1 IR coronal and axial, CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Recent postoperative changes of amputation of the great and second toes are seen, with non-visualization of the phalanges and distal portions of the first and second metatarsals.

Minimal marrow edema is noted in the residual first and second metatarsal stumps, without significant abnormal post-contrast enhancement. No convincing MRI evidence of residual osteomyelitis is identified in the visualized osseous stumps.

No significant cortical destruction or intraosseous collection is identified in the described residual metatarsal stumps.

Mild osteoarthritic changes are noted involving the ankle, posterior subtalar and few midfoot joints.

Minimal joint effusions are seen in the ankle, subtalar and midfoot joints.

No acute fracture or displaced osseous fragment is identified in the visualized bones.

Tendons and soft tissue:

Postoperative soft-tissue defects are noted in the great and second toe amputation beds, with surrounding soft-tissue edema.

Minimal ill-defined fluid is noted within the postoperative bed, without significant diffusion restriction. No definite drainable abscess is identified in the described region.

The flexor hallucis longus tendon is retracted into the midfoot, with mild fluid within its tendon sheath in the distal leg, suggestive of associated tenosynovitis.

Diffuse fatty atrophy and signal alterations of the visualized foot muscles are noted, consistent with diabetic myopathy/ diabetic myoneuropathy changes.

Diffuse inflammatory edema is seen involving the skin and subcutaneous soft tissues of the foot and ankle, consistent with cellulitis changes in the appropriate clinical setting.

No other significant soft-tissue abnormality is identified in the visualized region.

IMPRESSION:

Recent postoperative changes of amputation of left great and second toes, with associated soft-tissue defects and diffuse surrounding inflammatory edema.

Minimal marrow edema in residual first and second metatarsal stumps, without convincing MRI evidence of residual osteomyelitis at the time of examination.

Minimal ill-defined fluid in postoperative bed without significant diffusion restriction; no definite drainable abscess identified in the described region.

Diffuse cellulitis changes involving the left foot and ankle soft tissues.

Retracted flexor hallucis longus tendon with mild associated tenosynovitis.

Diffuse diabetic myoneuropathy changes in intrinsic foot muscles.

Mild ankle, subtalar and midfoot osteoarthrosis with minimal joint effusions.

Dr Thapasya

MRI OF LUMBOSACRAL SPINE AND SCREENING OF REST OF THE SPINE AND HIP JOINTS

Clinical Profile: Left hip pain for 1 year. H/o frequent self-falls while working and intake of native medications for hip pain.

Technique: Sagittal T1, T2, IR, Axial T2. T1 and IR Coronal for SI joints, CT correlation.

Screening of rest of the spine: T2/ IR sagittal

Screening of hip joints: IR axial and coronal, T1 axial

The lumbosacral spine displays a normal lordotic curvature and vertebral column alignment.

Thin smooth ossification of anterior longitudinal (ALL) and posterior longitudinal ligaments (PLL) are seen at multiple contiguous levels of the dorsolumbar spine, giving a bamboo spine appearance. Reduced intervertebral disc spaces are seen at most levels of the dorsolumbar spine with intradiscal calcification.

Bony fusion and ankylosis involving facet joints are noted at multiple dorsolumbar levels. Anterior vertebral corner and endplate changes with fat deposition are seen at multiple levels.

Vertebral body haemangiomas are noted at a few levels.

L1-2: Diffuse disc bulge and facetal arthropathy are seen. No significant mass effect over nerve roots noted.

L2-3 & L3-4: Disc bulge, ligamentum flavum thickening and facetal arthropathy are seen. No significant mass effect over nerve roots.

L4-5: Disc bulge, ligamentum flavum thickening and facetal arthropathy are seen causing indentation of right traversing L5 nerve root.

L5-S1: Diffuse disc bulge with left subarticular osteophyte, ligamentum flavum thickening, and facetal arthropathy causing compression of left traversing S1 nerve root.

The conus medullaris ends at D12-L1 level and the cauda equina is grossly normal in appearance.

The prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues are grossly normal for age.

Urachal cyst measuring 1.9 x 1.3 x 1.3 cm is seen in the midline at the dome of the urinary bladder.

Osteoarthrosis changes with intra-articular vacuum phenomenon are seen in the bilateral sacro-iliac joints. No imaging features of bony ankylosis are seen.

Screening of cervical spine:

Straightening of cervical spine is seen with disc desiccation at all levels and facetal/ uncovertebral arthropathy at multiple levels. Endplate changes are seen at few levels.

Disc bulge and uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy causing mild indentation of the cord and nerve roots are seen at few levels more significant at C2-3 and C4-5 levels.

No spinal cord signal changes are seen in the present study.

No other significant abnormality is seen in the cervical spine.

Screening of dorsal spine:

Reduced disc space with bony ankylosis of the vertebrae is seen at multiple levels. Rest of the disc shows disc desiccation.

Disc bulge and ligamentum flavum thickening are seen at multiple levels, more significant at D11-12 level, causing mild indentation of cord.

Vertebral body haemangiomas are noted at a few levels.

No abnormal spinal cord signal changes are noted.

No other significant abnormality is seen in the dorsal spine.

A well-defined soft tissue mass lesion measuring 5.2 x 4.9 x 2.5 cm is seen in the anterior mediastinum, anterior to the aorta. No calcification or cystic changes seen within the lesion, indeterminate in etiology. Suggested further detailed evaluation.

No significant mediastinal or abdominal lymphadenopathy seen in the present study.

Screening of Hip joints:

Severe advanced osteoarthrosis changes are seen in the left hip joint with severe joint space narrowing and full-thickness loss of articular cartilage. Altered contour of the femoral head with flattening of the articular surface is also seen.

Extensive altered marrow IR hyper intense signal (marrow edema) is noted involving articular surfaces of both the femoral head and acetabulum on the left side.

Extensive subchondral edema with sclerosis, and multiple subchondral cystic changes are noted in the left femoral head and acetabular margins.

Mild synovitis and minimal effusion are seen in the left hip joint.

Chronic osteitis pubis changes are seen.

Rest of the visualized soft tissue structures appears otherwise unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

Features of chronic inflammatory spondyloarthropathy as detailed.

Severe advanced osteoarthrosis of left hip joint with full-thickness cartilage loss, extensive subarticular marrow edema/ cysts and altered contour as detailed, likely secondary to chronic inflammatory arthritis.

Degenerative disc disease and spondyloarthropathy of cervical, dorsal, and lumbar spine causing spinal cord indentation at few levels and nerve roots at L4–5 and L5-S1 levels as detailed.

Bilateral sacroiliac joint osteoarthrosis, without definite osseous ankylosis.

Indeterminate anterior mediastinal soft-tissue mass as detailed. Suggested dedicated evaluation for further characterization of the lesion.

Small midline Urachal cyst at the dome of urinary bladder.

Suggested clinical correlation/ further evaluation and review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr Praveen

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: H/o recurrent shoulder dislocation, last episode 2 days ago? Bankart / Hill-Sachs lesion.

Technique: PDfs, T1, T2, IR and GRE in all planes and CT correlation

Bones and joints:

A focal impaction defect involving the anteromedial aspect of the humeral head, measuring approximately 1.6 × 1.5 × 0.3 cm (CC × TRA × Depth), is noted, with associated bone marrow edema, consistent with a reverse Hill-Sachs lesion in the setting of posterior shoulder dislocation.

No acute displaced fracture or deficiency involving the postero inferior aspect of the bony glenoid margin is seen.

Mild to moderate glenohumeral joint effusion is seen. No intra articular osteochondral fragment is seen.

Rest of the articulating bones appears normal in outline and marrow signal intensities.

Rotator cuff:

Supraspinatus and subscapularis strain changes are seen. No significant tear is seen.

Small partial-thickness articular surface tear is seen in the cranial part of the subscapularis tendon (25-50%thickness, measuring 4 mm in CC dimension). No full-thickness tear or retracted tendon fibers seen in subscapularis.

No evidence of muscle atrophy or fatty infiltration is noted in the rotator cuff muscles.

Rest of the rotator cuff muscles and tendons appear normal.

Long head of biceps appears intact. The deltoid muscle is also normal.

Labroligamentous structures:

Small tears are seen in posterior and posteroinferior quadrants. Rest of the glenoid labrum appears grossly normal for age. No other significant tear or displaced fragment is seen.

The middle glenohumeral ligament is prominent and cord-like in morphology, consistent with a possible Buford-type variant.

Sprain changes of biceps pulley, IGHL and capsule are seen. No definite capsular or ligamentous disruption noted.

AC joint:

Mild AC joint arthropathy/ sprain are seen. The acromion is of type II morphology and is laterally sloping. Minimal subacromial bursitis is seen.

Myofascial strain changes and edema are seen involving subscapularis muscle. No significant fluid collection or hematoma seen.

Rest of the soft tissue appears grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Reverse Hill-Sachs lesion involving the anteromedial aspect of the humeral head with bone marrow edema as detailed, indicative of an impaction injury secondary to a posterior dislocation mechanism.

Glenohumeral joint effusion with labroligamentous changes as detailed.

Rotator cuff strain, partial-thickness tear and myofascial strain as detailed.

AC joint arthropathy/ sprain and minimal subacromial bursitis as detailed.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr Praveen

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: C/o right shoulder pain with restriction of movements for 1 week. History of daily weightlifting occupation. No recent history of trauma. Not a known diabetic.

Technique: PDfs, T1, T2, IR and GRE in all planes. CT correlation

Bones and joints:

Mild osteoarthrosis is seen in the glenohumeral joint with subchondral cyst formation, and subarticular bone marrow edema in the humeral head region.

Diffuse hypertrophic synovitis is seen with mild joint effusion. No osteochondral fragment is seen.

Rest of the shoulder joint appears grossly normal with respect to joint space and alignment.

No bony Bankart/ Hill-Sachs lesion is seen. Rest of the articulating bones appears normal in outline and marrow signal intensities.

Rotator cuff:

Supraspinatus, infraspinatus, and subscapularis tendinosis is seen.

Near complete full-thickness tear is seen involving the supraspinatus tendon from its insertion footprint (AP dimension of 2.2 cm). The torn tendon fibres are seen medially retracted and with varying severity, measuring approximately 2 cm from insertion.

High grade partial thickness articular surface tear is seen in subscapularis tendon in its cranial part (>75% thickness and measuring 1.2 mm in CC dimension). Partial thickness articular surface tear is also seen in anterior part of infraspinatus tendon.

Myofascial edema is seen around supraspinatus and subscapularis muscles.

No significant muscle atrophy/ fatty infiltration noted. Few fatty streaks are seen in supraspinatus and subscapularis muscles.

Rest of the rotator cuff muscles and tendons appear grossly intact.

Mild tendinosis of LHBT is seen with intrasubstance longitudinal tear and medial dislocation. The deltoid muscle is also normal.

Labroligamentous structures:

Degenerative changes are seen in labrum with small chronic labral tears in superior, posterosuperior, anterior and inferior quadrants. Rest of the glenoid labrum appears grossly normal. No acute tear or displaced fragment is seen.

Mild synovial/ capsular thickening is seen in rotator interval and axillary recess regions. Thickening with increased signal intensity of biceps pulley and IGHL are seen.

Complete disruption of biceps pulley is seen. No other definite capsular or ligamentous disruption noted.

AC joint:

Mild AC joint arthropathy is seen. The acromion is of type III morphology and is laterally sloping.

The subacromial space is mildly reduced (4.6 mm). Subacromial bursitis is seen with significant fluid and synovial thickening.

Rest of the soft tissue appears normal.

IMPRESSION:

Rotator cuff tendinosis with full thickness tear of supraspinatus tendon and retraction of torn fibres as detailed.

High grade partial thickness tear in subscapularis tendon and partial thickness tear in infraspinatus tendon as detailed.

Diffuse hypertrophic synovitis with mild effusion, disruption of biceps pulley and medial dislocation of LHBT and degenerative labral tears as detailed.

AC joint arthropathy with features of subacromial impingement and subacromial bursitis as detailed.

Myofascial strain changes involving subscapularis and supraspinatus muscles and adjacent soft tissue edema as detailed.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr Praveen

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT SHOULDER JOINT AND UPPER ARM WITH SCREENING OF CERVICAL SPINE

Clinical profile: C/o right shoulder swelling for 1.5 years

Technique: PDfs, T1, T2, GRE and T2fs in all planes and CT correlation.

Screening of cervical spine: T2/ IR sagittal and T2 axial. 

Bones and joints:

The shoulder joint is normal with respect to joint space and alignment.

No significant joint effusion is noted.

No bony Bankart/ Hill-Sachs lesion is seen. Rest of the articulating bones is normal in outline and marrow signal intensities.

Rotator cuff:

Supraspinatus, infraspinatus and subscapularis tendinosis is seen. Small chronic intrasubstance tear is seen in the supraspinatus tendon at its insertion foot print region (AP dimension of 5.7 mm).

Another small intrasubstance tear is also seen in the infraspinatus tendon extending to MTJ region.

Rest of the rotator cuff muscles and tendons appear normal. No significant atrophy or fatty changes seen in the present study. No full thickness tear is seen.

Mild intraarticular tendinosis of LHBT is seen.

Labroligamentous structures:

Degenerative changes with chronic tears are seen in labrum, predominantly in anterior, anteroinferior and anterosuperior quadrants. Small tear is also seen in superior quadrant.

A small septated paralabral cyst measuring 1.2 x 1.2 x 1.1 cm with intraosseous extension is noted in the anterior aspect. Few other small subarticular cysts are noted in the glenoid bone.

Biceps pulley is intact. No definite capsular or ligamentous disruption noted.

AC joint:

AC joint arthropathy is noted. The acromion is of type 1 morphology. The subacromial space measures 5.6 mm. No subacromial bursitis is seen.

Right shoulder/ upper arm soft tissues:

A large, well-defined, lobulated fat-signal intensity mass lesion is seen in the sub deltoid region, measuring approximately 12.0 × 9.2 × 6.3 cm (AP × CC × TR) in maximum dimensions.

The lesion demonstrates signal characteristics similar to subcutaneous fat with complete/ suppressed signal on fat-suppressed sequences. It contains a few thin, smooth internal septations and minimal subtle nodular signal alterations. Few traversing vessels are seen.

The internal septations demonstrate only smooth, subtle enhancement. No definite enhancing nodular soft-tissue component, irregular or thickened septations, significant diffusion restriction or other suspicious enhancing component is identified.

The lesion extends extensively from the anterior to posterior aspect along the deep/ inner aspect of deltoid muscle, producing smooth mass effect with displacement and stretching of the deltoid muscle, more pronounced anteriorly. The anterior deltoid fibres are markedly stretched and thinned out.

Inferiorly, the lesion extends up to the level of the deltoid insertion on the proximal humerus.

Smooth indentation/ mass effect is seen on the adjacent pectoralis major muscle anteromedially and the axillary neurovascular bundle posteriorly, without evidence of invasion.

No surrounding soft-tissue edema or inflammatory change is seen.

No extension into the overlying subcutaneous tissues is identified.

The adjacent proximal humerus shows preserved cortical outline and marrow signal, without cortical erosion, marrow edema or osseous invasion.

No significant regional lymphadenopathy is seen.

Rest of the visualized soft tissues is unremarkable.

Screening of cervical spine:

Loss of cervical lordosis is seen with disc desiccation at all levels. Mild disc bulge and uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy are seen at few levels.

C5-6: Disc bulge and uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy are seen causing mild indentation of the cord and bilateral exiting C6 nerve roots (L>R). No spinal cord signal changes are seen.

No other significant abnormality seen in the screening cervical spine.

IMPRESSION:

Large well-defined deep lipomatous mass in right sub deltoid region, with few thin smooth septations and minimal septal enhancement. No definite thick/ irregular septations, enhancing nodular non-fat component, significant diffusion restriction, infiltrative margins or adjacent osseous involvement.

Rotator cuff tendinosis with small chronic intrasubstance tears as mentioned.

Mild LHBT tendinosis, degenerative labral tears and paralabral cysts as mentioned.

Mild AC joint arthropathy.

Cervical spondylosis, more significant at C5-6 level as mentioned.

Imaging features favor benign lipomatous mass lesion. However, given the large size and deep location, an atypical lipomatous tumor/ well-differentiated liposarcoma has to be ruled out. Suggested HPE correlation and review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr. Aathithya

MRI SCAN OF BONY PELVIS

Clinical Profile: C/o pain in left hip following injury on 02.10.2026 / Left femur fracture.

Technique: IR, T1, T2, PDfs, GRE and DWI in all planes. CT correlation.

Left proximal femur and hip:

An acute to sub-acute mildly comminuted and displaced fracture involving the intertrochanteric region of the left proximal femur is seen, with associated mild marrow edema at the fracture margins.

No focal marrow-replacing lesion, significant lytic/destructive component or associated soft-tissue mass centered on the fracture ends is identified to suggest an underlying pathological fracture.

The fracture does not extend into the femoral head articular surface.

The left femoral head remains congruent with the acetabulum. No hip dislocation is seen.

Mild left hip joint effusion is noted.

No MRI evidence of avascular necrosis of the femoral head is identified at present.

Perifracture soft tissues:

A large ill-defined, irregular and lobulated hemorrhagic collection/ hematoma is seen centered around and extending across the fracture site, measuring approximately 14.5 × 10.7 × 6.7 cm (CC × AP × TR).

The collection demonstrates predominantly T2/I R hyper intense signal with heterogeneous internal signal characteristics and a peripheral rim of diffusion restriction, compatible with organizing blood products.

The collection extends into and along the adjacent musculature, involving the gluteus medius, adductor longus, adductor brevis, pectineus and iliopsoas muscles.

Multiple amorphous nodular and curvilinear T2 hypo intense areas with corresponding susceptibility/ blooming on GRE are seen along the periphery of the collection. On CT correlation, these correspond to peripheral calcific/ossific foci, likely representing evolving post-traumatic mineralization/ heterotopic ossification.

No definite solid enhancing soft-tissue component is identified on the provided sequences.

Extensive surrounding post-traumatic soft-tissue contusion, myofascial edema and muscle strain are seen involving the left gluteal, pelvic and proximal thigh musculature.

A high-grade partial tear involving the iliopsoas insertion is noted. Associated high-grade partial tear/ strain of the pectineus muscle is also seen.

Diffuse fascial and subcutaneous edema is present throughout the left gluteal and thigh regions.

No additional significant organized fluid collection is identified.

Right hip:

Right hip joint alignment is maintained. No significant joint effusion or focal marrow abnormality is identified.

Remaining bony pelvis:

The remaining visualized pelvic bones and right femur show preserved marrow signal without focal osseous lesion.

Bilateral sacroiliac joints and pubic symphysis are unremarkable.

No additional acute fracture is identified.

IMPRESSION:

Acute to sub-acute mildly comminuted and displaced intertrochanteric fracture of left proximal femur as detailed. No evidence of underlying pathological lesion.

Large post-traumatic haemorrhagic collection/ hematoma centered around the fracture site with extension into the adjacent soft tissue as detailed.

Peripheral calcific/ ossific foci within the hematoma, likely representing evolving post-traumatic mineralization/ heterotopic ossification.

Extensive surrounding post-traumatic myofascial edema/ contusion and muscle strain, with high-grade partial tears of iliopsoas insertion and pectineus muscle.

Mild left hip joint effusion. No intra-articular fracture extension/ hip dislocation.

No MRI evidence of avascular necrosis of left femoral head at present.

Suggested clinical correlation/ follow up and review as indicated.

Dr. Aathithya

Dr. Aravind

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT KNEE JOINT

Clinical profile: C/o right knee pain.

Technique: PDfs in all planes, IR coronal, T1, T2 sagittal, GRE axial. CT correlation. 

Bones and joints:

Osteoarthrosis with partial to near full thickness articular cartilage loss and subchondral edema are seen in lateral compartment. Prominent marginal osteophytes are seen.

Mild joint effusion is seen with reactive synovitis. Small loose body is seen measuring 3 x 2 mm. No other significant osteochondral loose body is seen.  

Mild anterior translation of tibia is seen (8 mm). Subluxation of proximal tibiofibular joint is seen. Rest of the articulating bones and joints appear grossly normal.

Meniscus:

Horizontal tear is seen in posterior body and posterior horn of medial meniscus. Few tiny small parameniscal cysts are seen, largest measuring 3 x 2 mm along posterior horn region.

Small chronic tear with tiny parameniscal cysts are seen in anterior root of medial meniscus. 

Chronic oblique tear is seen in posterior horn of lateral meniscus. Chronic horizontal tear is seen in body region of lateral meniscus with small parameniscal cysts, measuring about 7 x 5 x 3 mm. 

Rest of medial and lateral menisci appears grossly normal. No other significant tear or displaced fragment seen. 

Ligaments:

Chronic full thickness tear of ACL is seen with attenuated, retracted and wavy fibres. PCL appears grossly intact.  

Medial and lateral collateral ligaments appear grossly intact. No complete tear is seen. Patellar retinacula appear grossly intact.  

Posterolateral and posteromedial corner ligament complexes appear grossly intact with chronic sprain changes. 

Rest of soft tissues: 

Rest of the extensor mechanism appears intact. Mild degenerative changes are seen at femoral insertion of medial and lateral gastrocnemius muscle with few small cysts.

Rest of the surrounding muscles, tendons and neurovascular structures are grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Right knee osteoarthrosis with joint effusion and loose body as detailed.

Full thickness tear of ACL as detailed.

Medial and lateral meniscal tears with few parameniscal cysts as detailed.

No other significant abnormality seen. 

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF LEFT FOOT

Clinical profile: C/o left big toe pain - left 1st MTP joint arthritis.

Technique: PDfs in 3 planes, T1 sag, IR, T2 axial, GRE axial, and CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

First metatarsophalangeal joint:

Moderate-to-severe osteoarthrosis of first MTP joint is seen, characterized by partial to near full-thickness articular cartilage loss, reduction of joint space, prominent marginal osteophyte formation and subchondral marrow edema involving opposing articular surfaces, more pronounced along the lateral aspect.

A small focal area of subchondral marrow edema with subtle cortical flattening is seen involving the first metatarsal head, likely representing focal degenerative/ pressure-related osteochondral remodelling.

No definite displaced osteochondral fragment or loose body is identified.

Mild joint effusion and synovial thickening/synovitis are noted.

The alignment of the first MTP joint is maintained.

Rest of the visualized osseous structures demonstrate preserved marrow signal without focal acute osseous abnormality.

Tendons and ligaments:

Mild stenosing tenosynovitis of the flexor hallucis longus tendon is seen at the visualized tendon sheath. The tendon itself maintains normal thickness and signal without tendinosis or tear.

The remaining visualized flexor and extensor tendons are intact.

The visualized collateral ligament complexes, including the medial and lateral first MTP collateral ligaments, are preserved.

No significant plantar plate abnormality is identified.

Soft tissues:

No significant soft-tissue collection, focal mass or abnormal soft-tissue edema is seen.

Visualized intrinsic foot muscles are grossly preserved.

IMPRESSION:

Osteoarthrosis of left first MTP joint with effusion and synovitis as detailed.

Small focal subchondral marrow edema with subtle cortical flattening involving first metatarsal head, likely degenerative/ pressure-related osteochondral remodeling. No definite displaced osteochondral fragment or loose body.

Mild stenosing tenosynovitis of FHL tendon, without tendon tear.

No other significant osseous or soft-tissue abnormality identified.

reports.fullText:
Dr. Aathithya

MRI OF LUMBOSACRAL SPINE AND SCREENING OF REST OF THE SPINE AND BONY PELVIS

Clinical Profile: C/o low back ache; H/o RTA x 4 years back.

Technique: Sagittal T1, T2, IR, Axial and sagittal T2, T1 and IR Coronal for SI joints, DWI,

Screening of rest of spine: T2/ IR and PC T1 sagittal.

Screening of bony pelvis: IR/ T1 coronal, PC T1. CT correlation.

Bone marrow:

Diffuse, extensive and heterogeneous marrow signal abnormality/ replacement is seen involving the visualized vertebral bodies and posterior elements, visualized cranial and thoracic osseous structures, pelvic bones and proximal femora.

The abnormal marrow demonstrates mild to moderate post-contrast enhancement and altered diffusion with areas of restricted diffusion.

Associated marked generalized osteopenia is noted, with multiple small focal lytic-appearing osseous lesions on CT correlation.

A more conspicuous focal lytic lesion involving left sacral ala measures approximately 3.7 × 2.6 × 1.8 cm. It demonstrates associated abnormal marrow signal, enhancement and mild diffusion restriction, with focal cortical deossification/ destruction of the anterior cortex. No significant extra osseous soft-tissue component is identified.

No significant epidural soft-tissue component, spinal canal compromise or cord compression is seen.

The overall pattern of diffuse marrow replacement with multifocal lytic lesions is suspicious for an infiltrative marrow neoplastic process, like plasma-cell dyscrasia/ multiple myeloma.

Rest of the lumbar spine:

Grade I retrolisthesis of L5 over S1 vertebra is seen. Rest of the lumbosacral spine displays a normal lordotic curvature and vertebral column alignment.

The individual vertebrae are normal in heights and morphology. .

Mild disc desiccation and facetal arthropathy are seen at few levels more significant at L5-S1 level. The intervertebral discs are normal in heights. The vertebral end-plates are normal.

D12-L1 to L3-4: No significant disc bulge or protrusion seen.

L4-5: Mild disc bulge and facetal arthropathy are seen causing partial effacement of lateral recess. No significant mass effect or nerve roots.

L5-S1: L5 retrolisthesis, uncovered disc with posterior bulge and facetal arthropathy are seen abutting bilateral traversing S1 nerve roots.

The conus medullaris ends at L1-2 level and the cauda equine is normal in appearance. No abnormal thickening or enhancement along the nerve roots seen.

The prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues are grossly normal.

Bilateral SI joints are normal in joint space and signal intensities.

Bilateral kidneys appear slightly hyper intense in T2 images.

Screening of rest of cervical spine:

Mild loss of cervical lordosis is seen. Mild disc desiccation and early uncovertebral arthropathy are seen at few levels. No mass effect over spinal cord or nerve roots seen.

Spinal cord appears normal. No other significant abnormalities are seen.

Screening of dorsal spine:

Mild chronic axial compression fracture with about < 20% height reduction is seen involving D9 vertebra. No spinal canal compromise seen in the present study.

Mild disc desiccation and flaval thickening are seen at few levels. Spinal cord appears normal. No other significant abnormalities are seen.

IMPRESSION:

Diffuse extensive marrow signal abnormality/ replacement involving visualized axial and appendicular skeleton with imaging characteristics as detailed.

Focal lytic lesion in left sacral ala with focal anterior cortical destruction as detailed, likely part of above-mentioned infiltrative process.

No epidural / paravertebral soft-tissue component. No spinal cord/ nerve root compression seen.

Mild diffuse degenerative changes of spine with L5-S1 retrolisthesis as detailed.

Mild chronic axial compression fracture involving D9 vertebra as detailed.

L5 retrolisthesis, uncovered disc and facetal arthropathy abutting bilateral S1 nerve roots at L5-S1 level as detailed.

Imaging features are suggestive of a diffuse marrow infiltrative disorder, with plasma-cell dyscrasia/ multiple myeloma being an important consideration. Clinical and laboratory correlation with further haematological evaluation is advised.

reports.fullText:
Dr. Christina

MRI SCAN OF DORSAL SPINE & SCREENING OF REST OF SPINE

Clinical profile: Known case of tubercular spondylodiscitis on ATT for follow up.

Technique: Sagittal T1, T2, IR, Axial T2, DWI, pre and post contrast T1 FS axial and sagittal. CT correlation. Screening of rest of the spine: T2/ IR.

As compared with previous scan dated 04.06.2026,

D4, D5 and D6 vertebrae:

There is mild interval reduction in the abnormal marrow IR hyper intensity and post-contrast enhancement involving the D4, D5 and D6 vertebral bodies, consistent with interval response to treatment.

There is significant interval resolution of the previously noted marrow abnormality involving the posterior elements, with only minimal residual signal alteration and enhancement.

Persistent reduction in height of the D5 vertebral body with chronic endplate erosive changes is noted.

On CT correlation, there is increased sclerosis involving the affected vertebral bodies with focal osseous fusion across the D4–D6 vertebral bodies, representing chronic healing changes.

No new vertebral erosion, collapse or acute osseous abnormality is identified.

There is partial interval reduction in the prevertebral and paravertebral inflammatory soft tissue, with residual right paravertebral soft-tissue thickening measuring up to approximately 1.0 cm in maximum thickness.

No significant residual drainable/ infected fluid collection is identified.

No significant anterior epidural inflammatory soft tissue or epidural collection is seen.

No significant spinal canal stenosis or cord compression is present at these levels.

The dorsal spinal cord demonstrates normal signal intensity without evidence of myelopathy.

Rest of the dorsal spine:

The dorsal spine displays grossly normal curvature and vertebral column alignment.

Rest of the individual vertebrae are grossly normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities.

Disc desiccation is seen at almost all levels with flaval thickening at multiple levels. Small chronic Schmorl's nodes and disc protrusions/ disc bulge are seen at few levels.

The intervertebral discs are normal in heights. Rest of the vertebral end-plates are normal.

The spinal cord appears normal. The conus medullaris ends at L1 level and the cauda equine is normal in appearance.

Screening of cervical spine:

Loss of cervical lordosis is seen with disc desiccation at all levels. OPLL is seen at C2 and C3 levels causing indentation over the cord.

Disc bulge and uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy causing indentation of cord and nerve roots are seen at C5-6 and C6-7 levels.

Spinal cord shows normal T2 signal intensity. No other significant abnormalities are seen.

Screening of lumbar spine:

Grade I retrolisthesis of L5 over S1 vertebra is seen.

Disc desiccation is seen at all the levels with disc bulge and facetal arthropathy at multiple levels.

L5-S1: Uncovered disc with posterior bulge and disc protrusion, facetal arthropathy are seen causing compression of left S1 nerve root and indentation of right S1 and bilateral exiting L5 nerve roots.

No other significant abnormalities are seen.

IMPRESSION:

Known tubercular spondylodiscitis involving D4–D6, demonstrating interval response to treatment, with reduction in vertebral marrow edema/ enhancement and near-complete resolution of posterior element involvement.

Chronic residual D5 vertebral body height loss and endplate erosive changes, with increased sclerosis and focal D4–D6 vertebral body fusion, consistent with chronic healing/post-treatment changes. No new erosion or vertebral collapse.

Partial interval regression of pre-/paravertebral inflammatory soft tissue as detailed. No significant residual drainable collection or epidural abscess.

No spinal canal compromise or cord changes seen.

Cervical and lumbar spondylosis as mentioned.

reports.fullText:
Dr. Saravanan.

MRI SCAN OF BONY PELVIS

Clinical Profile: C/o right sided hip pain radiating to thigh for past 9 years? Avascular necrosis of head.

Technique: IR, T1, T2, PDfs, GRE and DWI in all planes. CT correlation.

Right hip joint:

Mild diffuse chronic synovial thickening is seen involving the right hip joint, associated with minimal joint effusion.

No significant acute articular erosions, destructive osseous changes or focal marrow edema are identified.

There is mild-to-moderate osteoarthrosis of the right hip joint, characterized by diffuse articular cartilage thinning/ loss, reduced joint space, minimal subchondral marrow edema involving the acetabular side and prominent marginal osteophytes.

No focal subchondral collapse or serpiginous abnormal marrow signal is seen in the right femoral head.

No MRI evidence of avascular necrosis of the right femoral head at present.

No significant periarticular soft-tissue collection, abscess or abnormal muscular edema is identified.

Left hip joint:

Left hip joint alignment is maintained. Trace joint effusion is present.

No significant synovial thickening, cartilage loss, osteoarthrosis or articular erosion is identified.

No evidence of avascular necrosis.

Remaining bony pelvis and soft tissues:

The remaining visualized pelvic bones and proximal femora demonstrate preserved marrow signal and cortical outlines.

No focal osseous lesion or acute fracture is identified.

Bilateral sacroiliac joints and pubic symphysis are unremarkable.

The visualized muscles and tendons are intact.

No significant periarticular or intramuscular collection is seen.

IMPRESSION:

Mild diffuse chronic synovial thickening of right hip joint with minimal effusion, without significant active erosive/ destructive changes or periarticular collection.

Mild-to-moderate right hip osteoarthrosis as detailed.

No MRI evidence of avascular necrosis or femoral-head collapse.

No other significant abnormality in bony pelvis.

Features are suggestive of chronic right hip synovitis with secondary osteoarthrosis; no current MRI evidence of AVN or active septic arthritis. Suggested clinical correlation/ synovial evaluation and review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr. Christina

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: HC/o right shoulder pain while lifting weights? Rotator cuff injury

Technique: PDfs, T1, T2, IR and GRE in all planes. CT correlation. 

Bones and joints:

Right shoulder joint appears grossly normal. Minimal joint effusion is seen.

Tiny subchondral cysts are seen head of humerus.

No bony Bankart/ Hill-Sachs lesion is seen. Rest of the articulating bones is normal in outline and marrow signal intensities.

Rotator cuff:

Supraspinatus tendinosis is seen with fraying of fibres. High grade partial thickness articular surface tear (>50% thickness) with delamination and retraction of torn fibres is seen involving the supraspinatus tendon (AP dimension of 1.3 cm). The retracted fibres are seen at the mid third of humeral head level, consistent with a PASTA-type tear.

Mild tendinosis with a small chronic partial thickness articular surface tear is seen in the anterior part of infraspinatus tendon. Small chronic intrasubstance tear is also seen in subscapularis tendon. No full thickness tears are seen.

Rest of the rotator cuff muscles and tendons appear grossly normal. No atrophy or fatty changes are seen in the present study.

Long head of biceps appears intact. The deltoid muscle is also normal.

Labroligamentous structures:

Degenerative changes are seen in labrum with small chronic tear in anterosuperior, superior and anteroinferior quadrants. Rest of the glenoid labrum appears grossly normal for age. No acute tear or displaced fragment is seen. 

Diffuse synovial/ capsular thickening is seen in rotator interval and axillary recess regions. Thickening with increased signal intensity of biceps pulley and IGHL are seen. No definite capsular or ligamentous disruption seen.

AC joint:

Moderate AC joint arthropathy is seen. The acromion is of type II morphology and is laterally sloping.

The subacromial space is mildly reduced (4.5 mm). Mild subacromial bursitis is seen with minimal fluid.  Rest of the soft tissue appears normal.

IMPRESSION:

High-grade partial-thickness articular-sided (PASTA-type) tear of supraspinatus tendon with delamination and retraction of torn fibres.

Other rotator cuff tendinosis with small partial thickness tears as detailed.

Mild adhesive capsulitis and degenerative labral tears as detailed.

AC joint arthropathy with reduced subacromial space and minimal subacromial bursitis, suggestive of sub acromial impingement.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
MRI SCAN OF LEFT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: H/o RTA few days back? Rotator cuff tear.

Technique: PDfs, T1, T2, IR and GRE in all planes and CT correlation

Bones and joints:

Persistent posterior dislocation of the glenohumeral articulation is seen with the posterior glenoid engaging with the reverse Hill-Sachs bony defect.

Reverse Hill-Sachs impaction defect involving the anteromedial aspect of the humeral head with associated bone marrow edema is seen, measuring approximately 2.2 x 1.5 × 0.9 cm (CC × TRA × Depth).

No acute displaced fracture or deficiency involving the postero inferior aspect of the bony glenoid margin is seen.

Mild glenohumeral joint effusion is seen. No intra articular osteochondral fragment is seen.

Rest of the articulating bones appears normal in outline and marrow signal intensities.

Rotator cuff:

Supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendons show strain/ tendinosis with interstitial and partial-thickness articular-sided fibre tears.

Significant strain of the subscapularis tendon with associated edema and a partial-thickness articular-sided tear involving its cranial fibres. No full-thickness tear or significant tendon retraction is seen.

Diffuse myofascial strain changes with edema involving the rotator cuff musculature, more pronounced in the infraspinatus and teres minor muscles. Minimal fluid is seen tracking along the adjacent fascial planes. No significant intramuscular collection or hematoma.

Mild atrophy and fatty infiltration of the teres minor muscle, compatible with chronic denervation change. No significant atrophy or fatty infiltration of the remaining rotator cuff muscles.

Long head of biceps appears intact with strain changes. Mild strain is seen in deltoid muscle.

Labroligamentous structures:

Reverse soft-tissue Bankart lesion is seen, characterized by a tear involving the posteroinferior labrum with injury of adjacent periosteum.

The labral tear extends superiorly and circumferentially to involve the inferior, anteroinferior, anterosuperior, superior and posterosuperior quadrants.

Sprain/partial-thickness tears involving the inferior glenohumeral ligament (IGHL), joint capsule and biceps pulley complex. No complete capsuloligamentous disruption is identified.

AC joint:

Mild AC joint arthropathy/ sprain are seen. The acromion is of type IV morphology and is laterally sloping. Mild subacromial bursitis is seen.

Rest of the soft tissue appears grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Persistent posterior dislocation of left glenohumeral joint, with posterior glenoid engaging the anteromedial humeral head impaction defect.

Reverse soft-tissue Bankart lesion involving posteroinferior labrum with periosteal injury and extension of tears as detailed.

Rotator cuff strain with partial-thickness tears as detailed. No full-thickness rotator cuff tear or significant tendon retraction.

Diffuse rotator cuff myofascial strain, most pronounced involving infraspinatus and teres minor muscles.

Mild chronic fatty atrophy/ denervation change of teres minor muscle.

Sprain/ partial tears of IGHL, joint capsule and biceps pulley complex.

Mild glenohumeral joint effusion and mild subacromial-subdeltoid bursitis.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT KNEE JOINT

Clinical profile: C/o knee pain. No h/o recent injury. To r/o meniscal tear.

Technique: PDfs, IR, T1, T2 and GRE in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Medial tibiofemoral and patellofemoral joint predominant osteoarthrosis is seen with partial to near full thickness articular cartilage loss, chondral fissure, subarticular cysts/ edema and marginal osteophytes. Chondral flaps are seen in medial femoral condyle.

Mild knee joint effusion is seen with reactive synovitis and lipoma arborescens. No acute fracture or osteochondral loose body seen.

Few proximal tibiofibular joint ganglion cysts are seen, largest measuring 1.2 x 0.7 x 0.5 cm along the anterior aspect.

Rest of knee joint and articulating bones appear grossly normal for age.

Meniscus:

Degenerative changes are seen in medial and lateral menisci.

Chronic horizontal tear is seen in the posterior body and posterior horn of medial meniscus. Small chronic tears are also seen in anterior and posterior roots of medial meniscus. Minimal extrusion of medial meniscus is seen.

Multilobulated parameniscal cyst measuring 10 x 9 mm is seen near the anterior root tear. Another tiny parameniscal cyst is seen along the posterior horn of medial meniscus measuring 2.5 x 2.5 mm.

Small chronic tear is seen in the anterior root of lateral meniscus with few adjacent parameniscal cysts, largest measuring 4.5 x 3.5 mm.

Rest of the menisci is grossly intact. No other significant tear or displaced fragment seen.

Ligaments:

Mucoid degenerative changes are seen in anterior cruciate ligament. No significant tear or waviness is seen. The posterior cruciate ligament appears intact.

Medial and lateral collateral ligaments and patellar retinaculum appear grossly intact with mild degenerative changes. The intermeniscal and meniscofemoral ligaments are also normal.

Posterolateral and posteromedial corner ligament complexes appear intact.

Rest of soft tissues:

Mild degenerative changes with few cysts are seen at proximal femoral attachment of gastrocnemius muscles. Popliteus tendinosis is seen. Few varicose veins are seen around knee joint.

The extensor mechanism appears normal. Rest of the surrounding muscles, tendons and neurovascular structures are normal for age.

IMPRESSION:

Right knee osteoarthrosis with mild effusion as detailed.

Chronic medial and lateral meniscal tears, minimal medial meniscal extrusion and parameniscal cysts as detailed.

Mucoid degenerative changes in ACL and myotendinous changes as mentioned.

Few proximal tibiofibular joint ganglion cysts.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
MRI SCAN OF LEFT FOOT

Clinical profile: 53-year-old male with geographic plantar pigmentation persisting for approximately 30 years without significant change in size or shape but with occasional mild pain. C/o mild recent onset of pain. Biopsy performed for diagnostic evaluation. The visible ulceration is post biopsy status.

Technique: T1, IR, T2, DWI, PDfs, GRE and PC T1 in all planes. CT correlation.

Soft tissue:

There is smooth, diffuse thickening of the plantar skin corresponding to the clinically evident pigmented lesion, measuring approximately 7.2 × 5.2 cm and with maximum thickness of 5 mm. The thickened skin demonstrates predominantly T1 and T2-hypointense signal intensity with subtle delayed post-contrast enhancement.

A thin rim of adjacent subcutaneous soft-tissue edema with mild enhancement is seen along the deep aspect of the thickened skin.

No discrete cystic component, significant intralesional fluid collection or prominent abnormal perilesional vascular channels are identified. No definite calcification is evident within the lesion on CT correlation. No significant diffusion restriction is demonstrated.

A small focal superficial soft-tissue defect is seen involving thickened skin, corresponding to the recent biopsy site. Mild adjacent post-procedural inflammatory change is noted. No drainable/ infected fluid collection is identified.

The abnormality appears predominantly confined to the skin, without convincing extension into the deeper subcutaneous tissues, underlying fascia, muscles or osseous structures.

Few prominent/varicose veins are noted in the distal leg and ankle regions.

Mild diffuse subcutaneous edema is seen involving the dorsum of the foot, ankle and distal leg. No associated drainable fluid collection.

Bones and joints:

Mild osteoarthrosis involving ankle, midfoot and first metatarsophalangeal joints is seen.

Minimal ankle and posterior subtalar joint effusion.

reports.fullText:
Dr Praveen

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT THIGH

Clinical profile: Swelling in the medial aspect of right mid-thigh for 8 years. History of sudden increase in size in past few months.

Technique: T1, T2, IR, DWI, pre and post contrast T1 in all planes. CT correlation.

A large, well-delineated, lobulated fat-containing mass lesion measuring approximately 20.3 x 15.6 x 11.3 cm (CC x TRA x AP) is seen in the medial compartment of the right thigh, situated deep to the subcutaneous fat within the intermuscular and intramuscular planes.

The mass demonstrates predominant T1 and T2 hyperintensity with near-complete suppression on fat-saturated / IR sequences, consistent with macroscopic fat content.

Multiple internal lobulations, thin and thick septations are noted within the lesion.

A thick irregular nodular enhancing locule measuring approximately 6.7 x 5.9 x 0.3 cm (CC x TRA x AP) with an eccentric nodular enhancing and mild diffusion-restricting solid component is seen in the superior posterior aspect of the lesion.

Coarse chunky calcifications noted within one of the locules in posterosuperior aspect on limited CT correlation.

Another thick irregular nodular enhancing locule with an eccentric nodular enhancing and mild diffusion-restricting solid component measuring approximately 5.8 x 3.7 x 3.8 cm (CC x TRA x AP) is seen in the inferior posterior aspect of the lesion.

The mass exerts significant mass effect upon surrounding musculature with effacement of adjacent fat planes, displacing the gracilis muscle anteromedially and sartorius muscle anteriorly with flattening at mid and lower thigh levels. Laterally, the lesion splays and extends between the adductor group of muscles.

Laterally, the lesion extends to abut the right femoral neurovascular bundle and the sciatic nerve. A small focal lobular protrusion of fat extends anterior to the hamstring muscles into contact with the sciatic nerve, displacing it slightly laterally.

The visualized thigh musculature demonstrates no intrinsic signal edema or invasive muscle destruction.

No significantly enlarged right inguinal lymph nodes are seen.

Visualized pelvic bones and right femur demonstrate normal marrow signal intensity with no focal osseous lesion.

Visualized soft tissues of the left thigh appear grossly unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

Large, well-delineated, lobulated fat-containing intermuscular and intramuscular mass lesion in the medial compartment of the right mid-thigh with thick septations and two distinct focal eccentric nodular enhancing, diffusion-restricting soft tissue components causing mass effect on adjacent musculature and close abutment with displacement of the sciatic nerve and femoral neurovascular bundle as detailed

Imaging features are suggestive of Atypical Lipomatous Tumor / Well-Differentiated Liposarcoma, Suggested HPE correlation.

reports.fullText:
MRI SCAN OF RIGHT THIGH REGION

Clinical profile: Swelling in the medial aspect of right mid-thigh for 8 years. History of sudden increase in size in past few months. For detailed evaluation.

Technique: T2, T1, IR, DWI, GRE and PC T1 in all planes. CT correlation.

Right thigh:

Primary tumor:

A large, moderately defined, lobulated predominantly fat-containing mass lesion is seen in the posteromedial aspect of the right mid-thigh, measuring approximately 20.5 × 14.9 × 10.0 cm (CC × TR × AP) in maximum dimensions.

The lesion demonstrates predominant macroscopic fat signal with significant suppression on fat-saturated sequences. Within the fatty component, there are multiple irregular/ ill-defined patchy and nodular non-fatty areas, along with multiple internal septations.

These non-fatty nodular components and septations demonstrate restricted diffusion and mild-to-moderate post-contrast enhancement.

An intralesional calcific focus measuring approximately 3.9 × 2.2 × 1.0 cm is seen along the lateral aspect of the lesion on CT correlation.

No definite cystic/ necrotic component is identified.

The overall imaging morphology, particularly large size, internal thickened/ irregular septations, enhancing diffusion-restricting non-fatty nodular components, calcification and recent increase in size, is suggestive of lipomatous neoplasm with atypical/ high-grade components.

Extent of lesion:

Superiorly, the margin of the lesion is seen about 7 cm inferior to lesser trochanter of femur.

Inferiorly, the distal margin is seen about 4.5 cm proximal to superior patellar cortex.

Anteriorly, the lesion is causing smooth indentation and stretching of adductor magnus muscle over the mass. The posterior aspect of muscle is involved by the tumor. Adductor brevis and longus muscles appear grossly normal.

Anteromedially, the lesion is causing smooth indentation and displacement of gracilis and Sartorius muscles.

Posteriorly and posteromedially, the mass is seen extending up to the deep fascia and causing its smooth stretching of deep fascia and causing visible soft tissue bulge. No significant extension beyond the deep fascia is seen in the present study.

Posterolaterally, the mass lesion is causing smooth indentation and lateral displacement of all hamstring muscles. In addition the lesion is extending along the anterior, medial and posterior aspects of semi membranosus and semi tendinosis muscle and with sparing of lateral aspect and encasing for about >180 degrees.

Mild deformation of the anterior aspects of semimembranosus muscle is seen with loss of fat planes. The possibility of invasion could not be ruled out.

Medially, the lesion is protruding through the gaps between Sartorius and gracilis muscles. Indentation and stretching of Sartorius is seen with loss of fat plane.

No other similar focal lesion is seen.

Neurovascular structures:

The mass lesion is seen causing smooth indentation and flattening of the medial aspect of sciatic nerve for a length of approximately 8.2 cm in the mid-thigh region. Mild lateral displacement of the fatty nerve is seen. However, no complete encasement is seen in the present study. No abnormal thickening or enhancement or increased signal intensity is seen in the sciatic nerve.

The lipomatous mass is seen abutting the posterior aspect of distal femoral and popliteal vessels. However, no significant encasement is seen.

The femoral nerve appears grossly normal.

Lymph nodes:

No significant sized lymphadenopathy is seen in right inguinal or iliac regions.

Bones and joints:

The visualised bones of bony pelvis and thigh regions appear grossly normal.

No significant focal lesion or signal abnormality seen.

Rest of the soft tissue:

Rest of the visualised soft tissue appear normal.

Left thigh appears normal.

IMPRESSION:

Large lobulated predominantly fat-containing mass in posteromedial right thigh with multiple internal septations and irregular non-fatty nodular components demonstrating diffusion restriction and post-contrast enhancement. Associated intralesional calcific focus.

The lesion predominantly occupies posteromedial muscular compartment, with focal loss of fat planes and possible involvement of muscles.

Smooth indentation and flattening of sciatic nerve over approximately 8.2 cm without neural encasement or intrinsic nerve abnormality.

Lesion abuts the distal femoral/ popliteal vessels without significant encasement or definite vascular invasion.

No definite osseous involvement or significant regional lymphadenopathy.

Imaging features are suggestive of an atypical lipomatous tumour/ well-differentiated liposarcoma (ALT/WDLPS), with progression for dedifferentiated/ high-grade non-fatty components. The recent increase in size further raises suspicion for malignant transformation/ progression. Suggested clinical and HPE correlation/ review as indicated.

Extensor tenosynovitis involving the second and sixth extensor compartments, involving the extensor carpi radialis and extensor carpi ulnaris tendon sheaths, respectively.

No significant tendon tear, discontinuity or retraction.

Palmar bursa / soft tissues:

Mild inflammatory thickening and fluid distension of the radial palmar bursa with synovial thickening and enhancement, extending along the flexor tendon sheath region, consistent with palmar bursitis.

No discrete soft-tissue abscess or drainable collection. No significant diffusion restriction within the described inflammatory changes.

No significant focal subcutaneous soft-tissue mass.

Nerves:

Median and ulnar nerves demonstrate preserved course, calibre and signal intensity without focal abnormality.

IMPRESSION:

Multicompartment inflammatory synovitis involving distal radio ulnar, intercarpal, carpometacarpal, MCP and interphalangeal joints as detailed.

Extensive flexor tenosynovitis, most pronounced involving first through fourth flexor tendon sheaths, with additional flexor carpi radialis tenosynovitis.

Extensor tenosynovitis involving second and sixth extensor compartments.

Mild radial palmar bursitis/ inflammatory tenosynovial change.

No definite osseous erosions, subchondral marrow edema, significant cartilage loss, joint-space narrowing or static subluxation identified.

No tendon tear or retraction. No drainable soft-tissue collection or abscess.

In view of clinical history and imaging features, findings are consistent with active inflammatory rheumatoid arthritis with tenosynovitis, mild synovitis and palmar bursitis. Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT KNEE JOINT

Clinical profile: H/o trauma. Diagnosed as acute ACL tear in February at outside MRI. Managed conservatively. Presenting for follow-up evaluation. Currently asymptomatic with no specific complaints.

Bones and joints:

Resolving bone contusions/ trabecular injuries with minimal residual marrow oedema are seen in the posterior aspect of lateral tibial plateau and in the distal femur.

The knee joint is normal with respect to alignment and joint space. Mild anterior translation of tibia is seen (6 mm)

Minimal knee joint effusion is seen. No acute fracture or osteochondral loose body seen.

Articular cartilage across the medial, lateral, and patellofemoral compartments appears grossly preserved.

Meniscus:

Small chronic tear involving the junction of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus is seen, with adjacent chronic meniscocapsular sprain changes.

Mild attenuation of the body of the medial meniscus, likely related to chronic injury.

Full-thickness tear of ACL with attenuated and wavy residual distal fibres.

Resolving post-traumatic bone contusions/ trabecular injuries involving tibia and distal femur, with minimal residual marrow edema.

Small chronic medial meniscal tear with ligaments sprain changes as detailed.

No acute fracture, osteochondral lesion or displaced meniscal fragment.

reports.fullText:
Dr Praveen

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT FOOT (PLAIN)

Clinical profile: Known diabetic foot patient with h/o surgery about few weeks back. For detailed evaluation. Status post right lower limb angioplasty.

Technique: T1, IR, T2, DWI and PDfs in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

There is non-visualization of the phalanges of all toes and the distal portions of the metatarsal bones, consistent with post-amputation changes.

Mild residual marrow edema-like IR hyper intensity is seen involving the distal metatarsal stumps, with mild surrounding callus formation, likely representing postoperative/reactive changes.

No focal intraosseous fluid collection, significant cortical destruction or gross osseous erosion is identified.

No definite MRI evidence of acute osteomyelitis at the visualized metatarsal stumps.

Mild osteoarthritic changes are seen involving the midfoot articulations.

Minimal ankle and subtalar joint effusions are seen.

Ankle alignment is maintained. Remaining visualized osseous structures demonstrate no significant focal abnormality.

Ligament complex:

Medial and lateral ligament complex appears intact. No significant tear is seen.

Rest of the visualised ligaments appears grossly normal.

Tendons:

The distal cut ends of the flexor hallucis longus and flexor digitorum longus tendons are visualized, consistent with the postoperative/ amputation status.

No significant infective tenosynovitis is identified.

Remaining visualized tendons are grossly maintained without significant tear.

Soft tissue:

Extensive postoperative soft-tissue changes with soft-tissue defect are seen in distal foot.

An ill-defined fluid collection with internal diffusion restriction and multiple air foci is seen along the medioplantar aspect of the foot, centered around the abductor hallucis muscle. It measures approximately 10.0 × 0.9 × 0.3 cm (CC x TRA x Thickness)

The collection tracks along the abductor hallucis muscle from the postoperative site towards the hind foot.

A small plantar soft-tissue ulcer is seen along the medial plantar aspect of the hind foot, which communicates with the above-described infected collection.

An additional small fluid collection with diffusion restriction is seen along the plantar aspect of the midfoot at the postoperative site, suspicious for another localized infected collection.

Marked surrounding inflammatory changes and edema are seen within the postoperative soft tissues, particularly around the collections and along the plantar and medial plantar aspects of the midfoot and hind foot.

Mild diffuse subcutaneous edema and inflammatory changes extend into the distal leg, ankle and foot.

No other significant drainable fluid collection is identified.

Muscles:

Diffuse edema-like IR hyper intensity with fatty infiltration involving the intrinsic muscles of the foot and visualized distal leg muscles, in keeping with chronic diabetic myopathy/ neuropathic changes.

IMPRESSION:

Postoperative/ post-amputation changes involving forefoot, with non-visualization of phalanges and distal portions of all metatarsal bones.

Ill-defined infected fluid collection/ abscess in medioplantar aspect of foot with extensions and small medial plantar ulcer communicating with it as detailed.

Extensive postoperative inflammatory soft-tissue edema/ cellulitis changes.

Mild residual marrow edema at distal metatarsal stumps with callus formation, favoured to represent postoperative/ reactive changes. No definite cortical destruction, intraosseous abscess.

Mild midfoot osteoarthrosis with minimal ankle and subtalar joint effusions.

Diffuse chronic diabetic myoneuropathy changes.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr. Christina

CT OF LEFT ELBOW

Clinical profile: Alleged H/o injury to left upper limb while lifting by son from the chair 2 days back.

Bones and joints:

Acute comminuted displaced fracture of distal humerus involving supracondylar region is seen. The fracture extends through the distal humeral metaphysis without definite extension into the articular surface.

There is posterior displacement of the distal fracture fragment, with associated comminution.

The distal humeral condyles are maintained. No definite intra-articular fracture extension is identified.

The proximal radius and ulna demonstrate preserved cortical outlines without acute fracture.

Ulnohumeral, radiocapitellar and proximal radioulnar joint alignments are maintained. No dislocation is seen.

Multiple small, well-defined lytic/ mottled lucent foci are seen involving the visualized distal humerus, proximal radius and ulna. In view of the patient's age, these findings raise the possibility of an underlying marrow-replacing process such as multiple myeloma or osseous metastatic disease.

Soft tissue:

Soft-tissue swelling and edema are seen surrounding the distal humeral fracture.

No discrete soft-tissue mass or significant hematoma is identified.

A nodular calcific focus measuring approximately 1.6 × 1.5 × 0.7 cm is seen within the subcutaneous fat of the posterior proximal forearm. This is nonspecific/ indeterminate on the present examination and may represent a chronic calcified soft-tissue focus.

IMPRESSION:

Acute comminuted displaced supracondylar fracture of left distal humerus as detailed. No definite intra-articular extension.

Maintained Ulnohumeral, radiocapitellar and proximal radioulnar alignment. No associated proximal radius or ulna fracture.

Multiple small lytic lesions involving visualized bones, suspicious for underlying marrow-replacing disorder such as multiple myeloma/ metastatic disease.

Perifracture soft-tissue edema/ swelling.

Indeterminate calcified subcutaneous nodule in posterior proximal forearm.

Suggested clinical correlation/ further evaluation and review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
CT SCAN OF RIGHT HIP AND THIGH REGIONS

Clinical profile: H/o RTA with multiple trauma and surgeries, now c/o right hip pain and restricted ROM.

Bones and joints:

Intramedullary nail is noted within right femoral shaft with proximal/ distal interlocking screws in situ.

Old united fracture of the shaft of the right femur is noted, with maintained alignment.

The femoroacetabular articulation is maintained. No acute fracture or dislocation. No significant focal articular surface abnormality identified.

Heterotopic ossification:

Extensive mature heterotopic ossification is seen along the posterior aspect of the right hip joint, involving the adjacent gluteus medius and gluteus minimus musculature. The ossification is contiguous with/ attached to the posterior aspect of the iliac bone and posterior wall of the acetabulum and extends inferiorly towards the proximal femur.

The mature ossified component measures approximately 9.4 × 7.4 × 3 cm (TR × CC × AP).

Additional smaller ossific foci are seen along the proximal iliotibial band.

Another focus of mature heterotopic ossification is seen along the medial aspect of the distal thigh, involving the vastus intermedius muscle.

An additional focus of heterotopic ossification is seen in the right paravertebral soft tissues at approximately the L3–L4 level.

The described areas demonstrate mature cortical/ trabecular ossification, compatible with chronic post-traumatic/ postoperative heterotopic ossification.

No aggressive osseous destruction or associated soft-tissue mass is identified.

Soft Tissues:

Mild asymmetric atrophy of the right pelvic, gluteal and thigh musculature is noted compared with the contralateral side, likely related to chronic post-traumatic/ postoperative changes and disuse.

No significant acute soft-tissue collection is identified.

IMPRESSION:

Extensive mature post-traumatic/ postoperative heterotopic ossification along posterior aspect of right hip joint region as detailed.

Additional mature heterotopic ossifications in proximal iliotibial band, medial distal thigh/ vastus intermedius and right paravertebral soft tissues at L3–L4.

Old united fracture of right femoral shaft with intramedullary nail and interlocking screws in situ.

Mild chronic asymmetric atrophy of right pelvic, gluteal and thigh musculature.

No acute fracture or dislocation. Femoroacetabular alignment is maintained.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI OF LUMBOSACRAL SPINE AND SCREENING OF REST OF THE SPINE

Clinical Profile: Known case of CA breast, completed treatment, now complaints of lower back pain and stiffness.

Technique: Sagittal T1, T2, IR, Axial T2. T1 and IR Coronal for SI joints

Screening of rest of the spine: T2/ IR sagittal

Grade I anterolisthesis of L5 over S1 vertebra is seen. Severe facetal arthropathy is seen at this level. No spondylolysis is seen.

Rest of the lumbosacral spine displays a vertebral column alignment.

Significant facetal arthropathy is seen at L4-L5 and L5-S1 levels on both sides with marrow and adjacent periarticular soft tissue edema. No fluid collection is seen.

Rest of the individual vertebrae are normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities. No significant focal lesion or marrow signal changes seen in the present study.

Disc desiccation is seen at all the levels and facet arthropathy at multiple levels. The intervertebral discs are normal in heights. The vertebral end-plates are normal for age.

D12-L1 to L2-3: Mild disc bulge and facetal arthropathy are seen. No significant mass effect over nerve roots.

L3-4: Diffuse disc bulge and facetal arthropathy are seen causing partial effacement of lateral recess. No significant mass effect over nerve roots seen.

L4-5: Diffuse annular disc bulge, facetal arthropathy and flavum thickening are seen causing secondary spinal canal stenosis and compression of bilateral traversing L5 nerve roots. Residual thecal sac measures 7.9 mm in midsagittal dimension.

L5-S1: Uncovered disc with posterior bulge, ligamentum flavum thickening and severe facetal arthropathy (L>R) are seen causing indentation of bilateral traversing S1 and left exiting L5 nerve roots.

The conus medullaris ends at L1 level and the cauda equina is normal in appearance.

Rest of the prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues are grossly normal.

Both SI joints show features of mild osteoarthrosis.

A large uterine fibroid measuring 9.9 x 9.7 cm is seen. Suggested clinical and ultrasound correlation.

Screening of cervical spine:

Mild loss of cervical lordosis is noted.

Disc desiccation is seen at all levels with uncovertebral and facetal arthropathy at few levels. Disc bulge, protrusion and uncovertebral arthropathy causing anterior thecal sac indentation are seen at few levels more significant at C5-6 and C6-7 levels. No significant mass effect over spinal cord or nerve roots seen.

Spinal cord appears normal. No other significant abnormality is seen in the cervical spine.

Few thyroid nodules are seen. Suggested ultrasound correlation.

Screening of dorsal spine:

Disc desiccation is seen at all the levels with mild flaval thickening at few levels. Disc osteophyte complex causing mild indentation of anterior thecal sac/ cord are seen at D4-5 and D5-6 levels. No spinal cord signal changes are seen.

No other significant abnormality is seen in the dorsal spine.

IMPRESSION:

Diffuse degenerative changes of the spine with L5-S1 anterolisthesis as detailed.

Significant bilateral facetal arthropathy at L4-5 and L5-S1 levels with marrow and periarticular soft tissue oedema. No collection seen.

Disc bulge and facet arthropathy causing canal stenosis and mass effect over bilateral L5 and S1 nerve roots at L4-5 and L5-S1 levels as detailed.

Cervical and dorsal spondylosis as mentioned.

No significant focal lesion or marrow abnormality in the vertebrae.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Suspected DPN palsy secondary to compartment syndrome. Status post left leg fasciotomy done on 15/10/2026 (POD 1).

Technique: T1, T2, IR, DWI, GRE, and post contrast T1 FS in axial, sagittal, and coronal planes with CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Left tibial intramedullary nail with proximal and distal interlocking screws is noted in situ, with associated susceptibility artefacts.

No acute fracture, cortical destruction or focal suspicious osseous lesion is identified.

Visualized left knee and ankle joints are grossly maintained for age, without significant joint effusion or acute osseous abnormality.

Soft tissue/ muscles:

Postoperative changes of recent fasciotomy are seen along the anterolateral aspect of the left leg, with associated defects involving the skin, subcutaneous tissues and deep fascial planes.

Mild diffuse postoperative edema involving the skin, subcutaneous tissues and adjacent fascial planes is seen.

No significant postoperative hematoma, drainable fluid collection or abscess is identified. No intramuscular air is seen.

Anterior compartment:

The tibialis anterior, extensor hallucis longus and extensor digitorum longus muscles are diffusely bulky and demonstrate extensive abnormal T2/ IR hyper intensity, with associated altered diffusivity and mild corresponding T1 fat-saturated hyper intensity.

There are large confluent areas of abnormal T2/IR hyper intensity involving almost the entire circumference of the anterior compartment musculature, predominantly involving the mid and distal thirds, for an approximate length of about 20 cms.

These confluent areas demonstrate absent post-contrast enhancement with facilitated diffusion, consistent with extensive myonecrosis.

Additional patchy areas of similar non-enhancing myonecrotic change are present in the proximal third of the anterior compartment musculature.

The intervening deep fascial planes are stretched and demonstrate mild postoperative/ inflammatory edema.

Posterior and lateral compartment muscles and tendons appear normal.

Neurovascular structures:

The deep peroneal nerve and anterior tibial vessels are displaced/ compressed by the edematous anterior compartment musculature, with effacement of the intervening fat planes along their course.

Subtle smooth thickening and enhancement of the deep peroneal nerve are noted within the anterior compartment, without focal discontinuity or focal mass lesion, suggestive of reactive neuritis/ neuropathy secondary to compression.

Rest of the visualized muscles, tendons and neurovascular structures are grossly unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

Extensive ischemic myonecrosis involving left anterior compartment musculature, predominantly mid and distal thirds as detailed, likely sequelae of recent compartment syndrome.

Post-fasciotomy changes along anterolateral aspect of the left leg region. No significant hematoma, drainable fluid collection, abscess or intramuscular air.

Smooth mild thickening and enhancement of deep peroneal nerve with effacement of surrounding fat planes and mass effect from edematous anterior-compartment musculature, consistent with compressive neuropathy changes.

Left tibial intramedullary nail with proximal and distal interlocking screws in situ. No new acute fracture or cortical destruction.

Overall imaging findings are consistent with sequelae of anterior compartment syndrome with extensive ischemic myonecrosis and secondary deep peroneal nerve compressive neuropathy/ reactive neuritis.

MRI SCAN OF BILATERAL LOWER LIMBS

Clinical profile: K/c/o beta thalassemia major on treatment since six months of age, pre-transplant immunosuppressive chemotherapy (29/01/2026 to 03/02/2026) and desferal chelation therapy (10/02/2026 to 16/02/2026), followed by an allogeneic matched unrelated donor (MUD) hematopoietic stem cell transplantation on 10/07/2026. Now c/o left hip and thigh pain associated with a limping gait, requested for imaging evaluation to rule out avascular necrosis (AVN), osteomyelitis, or infective myositis.

Technique: T1, T2, IR, GRE, DWI and pre and post contrast T1 images in all planes.

Bones and joints:

Diffuse paucity of fatty marrow signal with predominantly low T1-weighted signal intensity is seen throughout the visualized osseous structures, in keeping with predominant hematopoietic marrow/ treatment-related marrow alteration in the given clinical setting.

Symmetric STIR hyper intensity is seen involving the physeal regions of the bilateral distal femora and proximal and distal tibiae. The proximal femoral and fibular physes are relatively spared.

The involved physes maintain their normal morphology without significant physeal widening, irregularity or focal destruction.

A thin rim of sub periosteal STIR hyper intensity with subtle post-contrast enhancement is seen along the metaphyseal aspects of the involved bones. No associated focal cortical disruption or aggressive periosteal reaction is identified.

No abnormal restricted diffusion is seen within the involved physeal, osseous or soft-tissue regions.

No focal abnormal physeal enhancement, cortical erosion or focal marrow-replacing abnormality is identified.

No intraosseous, subperiosteal or soft-tissue fluid collection/ abscess is seen.

No discrete focal marrow-replacing lesion or osseous mass is identified.

No imaging features of avascular necrosis/osteonecrosis are seen in the visualized epiphyses, including the bilateral femoral heads.

Mild bilateral knee and ankle synovial thickening with trace joint effusions is seen.

No significant articular erosions or destructive osseous changes are identified.

Muscles and soft tissues:

Mild adjacent soft-tissue/ muscle edema and subtle enhancement are seen around the involved physeal-metaphyseal regions.

The visualized muscles demonstrate preserved bulk and normal signal intensity.

No focal intramuscular edema, abnormal enhancement or fluid collection is seen.

No imaging evidence of significant myositis.

No discrete soft-tissue mass is identified.

IMPRESSION:

Symmetric multifocal physeal IR hyper intensity involving bilateral distal femoral, proximal tibial and distal tibial physes, with thin adjacent metaphyseal subperiosteal edema and subtle enhancement.

The involved physes maintain preserved morphology without significant widening, irregularity or destruction.

Diffuse low T1 marrow signal in all visualized bones, likely predominant hematopoietic marrow/ treatment-related marrow alteration.

No MRI evidence of osteomyelitis, osteonecrosis/ AVN or significant myositis.

No cortical destruction, restricted diffusion or fluid collection seen.

Mild bilateral knee and ankle synovitis with trace joint effusions, likely reactive.

In the given clinical setting of beta thalassemia major with recent hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation, findings favor multifocal treatment-related/ metabolic physeal stress changes with reactive subperiosteal and adjacent soft-tissue edema. Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.
