reports.fullText:
MRI OF LEFT ANKLE

Clinical profile: H/o inversion injury to left ankle 3 months back, treated outside. Presenting with persistent pain and swelling.

Technique: PDfs, T1, T2, GRE, IR and DWI in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Diffuse osteopenia of the visualized bones of the left ankle and foot is noted, relatively more pronounced compared with the contralateral side. No abnormal bone marrow edema is identified in the visualized osseous structures.

No acute or healing fracture, focal cortical disruption or displaced osteochondral fragment is seen.

Ankle joint alignment is maintained.

Minimal ankle and subtalar joint effusions are noted.

No significant articular erosions or destructive osseous changes are identified.

Ligament complex:

Anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL) is mildly thickened with altered intrasubstance hyper intense signal, consistent with low-grade sprain / partial-thickness injury. No complete tear or retracted fibers are seen.

Mild intrasubstance hyper intensity of the calcaneofibular ligament (CFL), consistent with Grade I sprain. Mild sprain changes are also seen involving the bifurcate ligament.

Posterior talofibular ligament is intact.

Anterior and posterior inferior tibiofibular ligaments are intact.

Mild intrasubstance signal alteration of the deltoid ligament complex, consistent with Grade I sprain.

Tendons and retinacula:

Mild Achilles and peroneus longus tendinopathy is seen without significant partial/ full-thickness tear or tendon retraction.

Mild sprain-related signal alteration is seen involving peroneal and extensor retinacula.

The remaining visualized tendons are intact with preserved signal and morphology.

Muscles and soft tissues:

Mild diffuse edema-like signal is seen involving the intrinsic muscles of the foot, without focal collection.

The remaining visualized muscles demonstrate preserved bulk and signal intensity.

Diffuse subcutaneous edema is seen involving the distal leg, ankle and dorsum of the foot, appearing disproportionate to the degree of focal ligamentous/tendinous injury.

No focal soft-tissue collection, abscess or hematoma is seen.

No abnormal restricted diffusion is identified within the soft tissues.

IMPRESSION:

Diffuse unilateral osteopenia involving visualized left ankle and foot bones, without associated marrow edema, acute/ healing fracture or focal osseous lesion.

Diffuse disproportionate subcutaneous edema involving distal leg, ankle and dorsum of foot, with mild edema-like signal involving intrinsic foot muscles.

Low-grade sprain/ partial-thickness injury of ATFL, with associated Grade I sprain of the CFL, bifurcate ligament and deltoid ligament complex.

Mild Achilles and peroneus longus tendinopathy without significant tear. Mild sprain-related changes of the peroneal and extensor retinacula.

Minimal ankle and subtalar joint effusions.

In the appropriate clinical setting, the combination of regional osteopenia, disproportionate soft-tissue edema and mild intrinsic muscle edema may represent a post-traumatic complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS) pattern. Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF LEFT HIP JOINT

Clinical Profile: C/o acute onset of pain in left hip and left lower limb since 3:00 pm? Septic arthritis? Hemarthrosis. Post CABG status done few weeks back.

Technique: IR, T1, DWI, PDfs, DWI, GRE and post contrast T1 in all planes. CT correlation.

Bone marrow:

Mild diffuse red marrow reconversion changes are seen involving the visualized vertebral bodies and pelvic bones.

Subtle early Paget-like osseous changes are noted involving the left iliac bone, with mild cortical thickening and coarse/ trabecular prominence. No aggressive marrow signal abnormality, cortical destruction or extra osseous soft-tissue component is seen.

No acute fracture or significant focal marrow edema is identified.

Right hip joint:

Right hip joint alignment is maintained.

Minimal joint effusion is seen without significant synovial thickening or abnormal synovial enhancement.

No articular erosion, subchondral marrow edema or other features of inflammatory/infective arthropathy.

No imaging evidence of avascular necrosis of the right femoral head.

Left hip joint:

Mild left hip joint effusion is seen with mild smooth diffuse synovial thickening and enhancement. No internal susceptibility/ blood-product signal to suggest significant hemarthrosis. No restricted diffusion within the joint fluid.

No significant articular surface irregularity or erosions. No subchondral marrow edema or destructive osseous change.

No abnormal marrow signal or enhancement involving the femoral head, neck or acetabulum to suggest osteomyelitis.

No drainable intra-articular or periarticular collection/ abscess is identified.

Significant periarticular soft-tissue edema with mild associated enhancement is seen around the left hip, predominantly involving the adjacent soft tissues. No focal collection is seen.

No imaging evidence of avascular necrosis of the left femoral head.

Rest of bony pelvis:

Visualized pelvic bones are otherwise unremarkable for age.

Bilateral sacroiliac joints and pubic symphysis are preserved.

Soft tissues / pelvic viscera:

Mild soft-tissue edema is seen in the left inguinal region within the subcutaneous fat planes.

Visualized muscles and tendons are otherwise maintained without focal tear or collection.

Prostatomegaly is seen with median lobe hypertrophy and few nodules.

Foley catheter is seen in situ within the urinary bladder.

Mild diffuse urinary bladder wall thickening with mild surrounding perivesical fat stranding/ edema is noted.

Rest of the visualized muscles and tendons appear normal for age. Rest of the soft tissue appears normal for age.

IMPRESSION:

Mild left hip joint effusion with mild smooth synovitis, associated periarticular soft-tissue edema and enhancement. Features favor acute nonspecific inflammatory synovitis with periarticular inflammatory changes.

No convincing MRI features of septic arthritis/ osteomyelitis at present.

No significant hemarthrosis identified.

Subtle early Paget-like osseous changes involving the left iliac bone.

Mild diffuse red marrow reconversion changes in the visualized axial skeleton.

Prostatomegaly with median lobe hypertrophy. Foley catheter in situ. Mild diffuse urinary bladder wall thickening and perivesical edema; correlate clinically/ with urine analysis for possible cystitis.

Suggested clinical correlation/ follow up and left joint fluid evaluation as clinically indicated.

Technique: T1, T2, IR, DWI, GRE, pre and post-contrast T1 fat-saturated in all planes with CT correlation.

Soft tissue:

A well-defined, slightly lobulated T2/ IR heterogeneously hyper intense intramuscular soft tissue mass lesion measuring 2.2 x 1.8 x 1.4 cm (CC x TRA x AP) is noted within the superficial part of supinator muscle in the anterior aspect of the proximal forearm region.

The lesion demonstrates moderate heterogeneous post-contrast enhancement with areas of altered diffusivity. A thin peripheral T2 hypo intense rim is noted without significant susceptibility blooming on gradient sequences.

On CT correlation, a characteristic lamellar pattern of peripheral ossification is identified with relative sparing of the central portion of the lesion.

Marked adjacent myofascial edema, soft tissue inflammation, and bulky T2/ IR hyper intense signal changes are noted involving the supinator muscle and extending along the adjacent intermuscular and deep fascial planes. Minimal subcutaneous edema is also seen.

Rest of the visualized forearm muscles, flexor/ extensor tendons, and major neurovascular structures appear grossly normal.

No loculated fluid collection or abscess formation is identified.

Bones and joints:

The visualized proximal radius and ulna display normal cortical outline and bone marrow signal intensity.

No evidence of cortical defect, bone erosion, periosteal reaction, or adjacent bone marrow edema is seen.

Proximal radioulnar and radiocapitellar joints appear normal in alignment.

IMPRESSION:

Well-defined intramuscular lesion within supinator muscle demonstrating peripheral lamellar/ zonal ossification with relative central sparing on CT, peripheral T2-hypointense rim and marked surrounding myofascial inflammatory edema. Imaging features are characteristic of evolving/ maturing myositis Ossificans.

No involvement of adjacent radius or ulna, with no cortical erosion, osseous destruction or marrow edema.

No drainable collection or abscess seen.

Given the characteristic peripheral zonal ossification and absence of adjacent osseous involvement, myositis Ossificans is favoured over a primary soft-tissue neoplasm. Clinical and imaging follow-up may be considered to document maturation of the lesion.

Dr Praveen

MRI OF BONY PELVIS AND BOTH HIP JOINTS (PLAIN & CONTRAST)

Clinical Profile: Right hip pain for 3 months.

Technique: T1, T2, IR, DWI, GRE, pre and post-contrast T1fs in all planes for bony pelvis. CT correlation.

Bones and bone marrow:

A geographic ill-defined patchy marrow signal abnormality measuring approximately 4.5 × 3.3 × 2.8 cm (CC × TR × AP) is seen involving the right iliac bone, extending inferiorly into the right acetabular roof and up to the subarticular region.

The involved marrow demonstrates low signal intensity on T1- and T2-weighted images compared to the adjacent normal marrow, while remaining mildly hyper intense relative to skeletal muscle. Few scattered foci of preserved intralesional marrow fat are seen within the abnormality.

Mild associated hyper intensity is seen on fluid-sensitive/ PD fat-saturated sequences with mild diffuse post-contrast enhancement. No significant surrounding marrow edema is identified.

No abnormal trabecular thickening/coarsening, cortical thickening, cortical breach or destruction is seen. No focal lytic component, cortical erosion or periosteal reaction is identified.

No associated extra osseous soft-tissue component is seen. Adjacent periosteum and surrounding soft tissues appear unremarkable.

Few additional small, ill-defined patchy areas of similar marrow signal alteration are seen in the visualized pelvic and bones and proximal femurs.

No acute fracture or collapse is identified.

Bilateral femoral heads are maintained in contour without evidence of avascular necrosis.

Hip joints:

Bilateral hip joints appear grossly normal with preserved joint spaces and articulating margins. Trace of joint fluid is seen. No significant synovitis is seen.

No imaging features of avascular necrosis (AVN) are seen.

Rest of bony pelvis:

Small bony island is seen in right sacral ala measuring 5 x 4.5mm.

Bilateral sacroiliac joints and pubic symphysis appear grossly normal for age.

Rest of the visualized pelvic bones and proximal femurs show normal marrow signal intensity with no other focal lesion or signal abnormality.

Muscles and soft tissues:

Visualized muscles demonstrate normal bulk and signal intensity.

No focal intramuscular or soft-tissue mass or collection.

Lumbosacral plexus:

Visualized lumbosacral plexus appears normal in course, caliber and signal intensity.

Sacroiliac joints:

Bilateral sacroiliac joints are maintained without significant erosive or inflammatory changes.

IMPRESSION:

Ill-defined geographic patchy marrow signal alteration involving right iliac bone with extension to roof of acetabulum showing preserved intralesional marrow fat and mild enhancement.

Few additional small similar-appearing marrow foci in visualized pelvic bones.

No cortical destruction, aggressive lytic change, abnormal trabecular thickening, periosteal reaction, significant marrow edema or extra osseous soft-tissue component.

Bilateral hip joints are unremarkable.

Overall non aggressive features favor benign focal marrow variation/ reconversion. Lymphoma or plasma-cell dyscrasia is less likely based on current imaging morphology.

Suggested clinical correlation/ further evaluation and review as indicated.

Dr Prakhyath/ Dr Deepikha

MRI OF BONY PELVIS (PLAIN WITH CONTRAST)

Clinical Profile: Pregnancy-associated pelvic girdle stress and bone marrow edema, 15-days H/o lower back pain radiating to the lower limbs and gluteal pain with an inability to stand or walk developing after a normal vaginal delivery on 22/09/2026.

Outside MRI Whole Spine dated 11/10/2026: Significant marrow edema in the iliac and sacral aspects of bilateral sacroiliac joints (R > L) with minimal right-sided effusion and soft tissue edema in the right iliopsoas muscle - bilateral sacroiliitis.

Technique: T1, IR, T2, T1 pre and post contrast in all planes, GRE and DWI, SI joint - T1 and IR oblique coronal, Lumbar spine T1 and T2 sagittal, CT correlation.

Hip joints:

The hip joints are normal with respect to alignment and joint space.

Minimal joint effusion is seen. No cartilage loss or osteochondral loose body is seen.

The articulating bones are normal in outline and bone marrow signal intensity characteristics.

No features of avascular necrosis are seen in the visualized parts of femoral head regions.

Sacroiliac joints:

Extensive confluent marrow edema-like signal alteration involving the subarticular regions of the right sacroiliac joint is seen, involving the right sacral ala and adjacent iliac bone. The involved marrow demonstrates associated diffusion signal alteration and post-contrast enhancement.

No significant right sacroiliac joint effusion is identified.

Periarticular inflammatory soft-tissue edema and enhancement are seen predominantly along the anterior aspect of the right SI joint, extending along the adjacent iliopsoas myofascial planes.

No discrete rim-enhancing fluid collection or intramuscular abscess is identified. No definite focal drainable collection or convincing restricted-diffusion focus is seen.

Small patchy area of subarticular marrow edema-like signal alteration and enhancement is also noted along the sacral aspect of the left sacroiliac joint.

CT demonstrates extensive chronic-appearing subarticular sclerosis with fatty deposition involving both sacroiliac joints. Focal cortical erosive changes are noted along the right SI joint. Few small intra-articular gas locules are seen within the left SI joint. No definite bony ankylosis.

Rest of the bony pelvis:

Minimal fluid is seen in pubic symphysis.

Abnormal IR hyper intense edematous changes are noted in the bilateral lower paravertebral muscles (R > L) and bilateral gluteal muscles (R > L). Minimal edema is also seen in bilateral adductor muscles.

No frank intramuscular fluid collection or abscess formation is seen in present study.

No other significant focal lesion is seen in the visualized bones.

Postpartum changes of the uterus are noted.

IMPRESSION:

Bilateral sacroiliitis (R>L) with extensive active inflammatory marrow edema involving right sacral ala and iliac bone, with focal right SI joint cortical erosions and adjacent anterior periarticular/ iliopsoas inflammatory edema.

Chronic structural changes of bilateral sacroiliac joints with subarticular sclerosis and fatty deposition. No bony ankylosis.

No significant SI joint effusion, drainable collection or intramuscular abscess identified.

Associated bilateral paravertebral, gluteal and mild adductor muscle edema, likely related to the acute inflammatory/ postpartum musculoskeletal process.

Minimal bilateral hip joint effusions without significant hip joint abnormality.

Postpartum changes of the uterus.

Suggested clinical correlation / review as indicated.

Dr. Thamaraikkannan/ Dr.Deepikha

These lesions appear predominantly lytic with patchy sclerosis involving D5, D10, L3 and S1 vertebrae. These lesions are seen involving the vertebral body and the posterior elements also.

No significant fluid collection seen in the present study. No significant epidural fluid collection or spinal canal compromise seen in the present study.

Small extra osseous soft tissue component is seen at few levels, more significant at S2 and S3 vertebral levels along the anterior aspect. Foraminal narrowing with indentation over right S1 and S2 nerve roots are seen.

Mild presacral soft tissue inflammation and enhancement is seen with maximum thickness of with maximum thickness of 4.1 mm.

Multiple enhancing discrete retroperitoneal lymph nodes are seen.

Ret of the lumbar spine:

The lumbosacral spine displays a normal lordotic curvature and vertebral column alignment.

Multilevel disc desiccation and facetal arthropathy changes are noted. Mild endplate changes are seen at few levels with reduced disc height at L5-S1 level.

L3-L4: Mild disc bulge and facetal arthropathy are seen causing partial effacement of right lateral recess. No significant mass effect over nerve roots seen.

Multilevel disc desiccation is seen with mild uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy at few levels. The intervertebral discs are normal in heights. The vertebral end-plates are normal.

IMPRESSION:

Multifocal marrow-replacing lesions involving multiple vertebrae and pelvic bones with imaging characteristics as detailed.

Associated mild presacral inflammatory soft-tissue thickening and multiple enhancing retroperitoneal lymph nodes.

Dr. Thamaraikkannan

MRI SCAN OF BRACHIAL PLEXUS

Clinical Profile: H/o left C7-C8 nerve root avulsion and pseudomeningocele on 2023 MRI, Now presenting with suspected left Erb's palsy For follow-up scan.

Technique: 3DIR, T2, T1, DWI. Screening of cervical spine: T2 sag and axial.

Left Brachial plexus:

Left C5 and C6 nerve roots: Abnormal thickening with increased T2/STIR hyper intensity involving left C5 and C6 nerve roots and the upper trunk without preganglionic root avulsion or pseudomeningocele formation, consistent with postganglionic nerve injury / traction injury.

Left C7 nerve root: Preganglionic nerve root avulsion injury with pseudomeningocele formation and disruption of left C7 nerve root is seen. Suspicious retracted nerve ends are noted in the infraclavicular region.

Left C8 nerve root: Preganglionic nerve root avulsion injury involving the left C8 nerve root with associated pseudomeningocele formation. Thickening with increased T2/STIR signal intensity of residual C8 nerve root fibers and lower trunk is noted.

No significant haematoma or organised fluid collection is identified along the course of the left brachial plexus.

Right Brachial Plexus:

Right brachial plexus appears normal in course, caliber and signal intensity.

Cervical spine screening:

Cervical spinal cord appears normal in caliber and signal intensity. No syrinx, cord edema or focal intraspinal lesion identified.

No significant abnormality seen in the remainder of the cervical spine.

Visualised muscles:

Asymmetric atrophic changes of muscles are seen in the left side of neck and shoulder regions, consistent with chronic denervation changes.

Remaining visualized muscles and soft tissues appear grossly unremarkable.

Bones:

No cervical rib is noted. No obvious fracture/ lesion seen.

IMPRESSION:

Preganglionic nerve root avulsion injuries involving the left C7 and C8 nerve roots with pseudomeningocele formation as detailed

Abnormal thickening and T2 hyper intensity involving left C5 and C6 nerve roots and upper trunk, suggestive of postganglionic injury as detailed.

Chronic denervation-related muscular atrophy involving left neck and shoulder girdle.

No significant abnormality in the right brachial plexus/cervical spinal cord.

Suggested clinical correlation / review as indicated.

Dr Praveen/Dr.Deepikha

MRI SCAN OF LEFT KNEE JOINT

Clinical profile: History of injury to left knee 1 month back with c/o swelling and pain.

Technique: PDfs, IR, T1, T2 and GRE in all planes.

Bones and joints:

Small resolving bone contusion with minimal residual edema is seen in the anteromedial aspect of proximal tibia. No fracture or displaced fragment seen. No full thickness cartilage loss is seen.

Mild medial tibiofemoral predominant osteoarthrosis is seen with partial thickness articular cartilage loss.

Moderate joint effusion is seen with reactive synovitis and lipoma arborescens.

Rest of knee joint and articulating bones appear grossly normal for age.

Meniscus:

Mild degenerative changes are noted in medial meniscus with small horizontal tear in outer third of body posterior horn junction region.

Rest of the medial and lateral menisci appear normal. No other significant tear or displaced fragment seen.

Ligaments:

The medial and lateral collateral ligaments and patellar retinacula appear intact.

The anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments appear intact. No significant tear or waviness is seen.

The intermeniscal and meniscofemoral ligaments are also normal.

Posterolateral and posteromedial corner ligament complexes appear grossly intact.

Rest of soft tissues:

Mild diffuse soft tissue oedema is seen in the pre and infrapatellar regions. No significant fluid collection or haematoma seen.

Mild diffuse periarticular soft tissue oedema is also seen. Mild degenerative changes are seen at proximal femoral attachment of medial gastrocnemius muscle.

Mild chronic enthesopathic changes are seen involving prepatellar extension of quadriceps tendon. Rest of the extensor mechanism appears normal. Rest of the surrounding muscles, tendons and neurovascular structures are normal.

IMPRESSION:

Small resolving bone contusion with minimal residual edema in proximal tibia.

Mild osteoarthrosis with effusion and periarticular edema.

Small medial meniscal tear as detailed. No displaced fragment.

Mild pre/ infrapatellar and periarticular soft-tissue edema, likely post-traumatic. No significant collection or hematoma.

No other significant abnormality seen.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Dr Praveen

MRI OF BILATERAL LOWER LIMB NEUROGRAPHY (P + C)

Clinical Profile: K/c/o relapsing remitting IgG4-related disease with mononeuritis multiplex involving sciatic nerve, C/o left lower limb pain, itching, cramps, unsteady gait, and radiating lower back pain for 2 weeks

Technique: Thigh and leg – T1, IR coronal, T2, DWI - axial. Post contrast T1.

Compared to previous MRI dated on 23-02-2026, present scan shows,

Bones and joints:

Interval appearance of IR hyper intense marrow edema is seen in left distal femur.

Mild interval reduction/ persistent IR hyper intense bone marrow edema is seen involving the neck and intertrochanteric regions of bilateral proximal femurs and tibia.

Interval decrease in IR hyper intense marrow edema involving left calcaneum is seen.

Visualized hip, knee, and ankle joints appear grossly normal with no significant joint effusion or synovitis. No acute cortical fracture or focal bone lesion identified.

Nerves and soft tissue:

Interval appearance of diffuse smooth thickening with mild IR hyper intensity and post-contrast enhancement is seen involving the left sciatic nerve in distal thigh region, common peroneal and posterior tibial nerves along their courses in popliteal fossa and leg regions.

Diffuse and extensive perineural soft tissue inflammation and edema are noted along the involved nerves in distal thigh, popliteal fossa and leg regions. No abnormal fluid collection or diffusion restriction seen in the present study.

Bilateral lumbar sacral plexus appear grossly normal. Bilateral femoral and obturator nerves appear grossly normal in caliber and signal intensity.

Right sciatic nerve common peroneal and tibial nerves appear normal.

No significant denervation changes (muscle edema, atrophy, or fatty infiltration) are seen in the thigh and leg musculature.

IMPRESSION:

Compared to previous MRI dated 23-02-2026, present scan shows:

Interval development of diffuse smooth thickening, IR hyper intensity and enhancement of left sciatic nerve in distal thigh and left common peroneal and tibial nerves in popliteal fossa and leg, with extensive surrounding perineural inflammatory edema. Findings are suggestive of active peripheral neuritis/ perineuritis compatible with active IgG4-related mononeuritis multiplex.

No focal nerve abscess, collection or significant diffusion restriction. No associated muscle denervation changes identified.

Interval appearance of marrow edema in left distal femur, with persistent/ mild reduced marrow edema involving bilateral proximal femora and tibiae. Interval reduction of marrow edema in left calcaneum.

No other significant abnormality seen.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Dr Praveen

MRI OF LUMBOSACRAL SPINE AND SCREENING OF REST OF THE SPINE

Clinical Profile: Complaints of lower back pain and right hip pain for 10 days.

Technique: Sagittal T1, T2, IR, Axial T2. T1 and IR Coronal for SI joints

Screening of rest of the spine: T2 sagittal

Grade I retrolisthesis is seen at L3-L4 and L4-L5 levels. Significant facetal arthropathy is seen at these levels. No spondylolysis is seen.

Rest of the lumbosacral spine displays a normal lordotic curvature and vertebral column alignment.

The individual vertebrae are normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities.

Multilevel disc desiccation and facetal arthropathy are seen with mild endplate changes at few levels. The intervertebral discs are normal in heights. Rest of the vertebral end-plates are normal.

D12-L1 and L1-2: No significant abnormality seen.

L2-3: Diffuse disc bulge with posterior annular fissure, facetal arthropathy and flaval thickening are seen. No significant mass effect over nerve roots seen.

L3-4: Uncovered disc with diffuse annular disc bulge and right subarticular disc protrusion, flaval thickening and facetal arthropathy are seen causing effacement of lateral recess and indentation of bilateral traversing L4 nerve roots (R>L). Residual thecal sac measures 8.6 mm in midsagittal dimension.

L4-5: Uncovered disc with diffuse annular disc bulge and left subarticular disc protrusion, flaval thickening and facetal arthropathy are seen causing effacement of lateral recess and compression of bilateral traversing L5 nerve roots (L>R). Residual thecal sac measures 10 mm in midsagittal dimension.

L5-S1: Diffuse disc bulge with facetal arthropathy are noted. No significant mass effect over nerve roots noted.

The conus medullaris ends at L1 level and the cauda equina is normal in appearance.

The prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues are normal.

Both SI joints are grossly normal for age in joint space and signal intensities.

Screening of cervical spine:

Loss of cervical lordosis is seen with normal vertebral column alignment.

Disc desiccation is seen at all levels. Vertebral endplate changes and uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy are noted at few levels.

Disc bulge and uncovertebral arthropathy causing indentation of cord and nerve roots are seen at few levels, more significant at C3-4 and C6-7 levels. No spinal cord signal changes are seen.

No other significant abnormality is seen in the cervical spine.

Screening of dorsal spine:

Mild disc desiccation and flaval thickening are seen at few levels.

Spinal cord appears normal. No other significant abnormality is seen in the dorsal spine.

IMPRESSION:

Degenerative changes of spine with L3-4 and L4-5 retrolisthesis as detailed.

Uncovered disc with small protrusions and facetal arthropathy causing mass effect over bilateral L4 and L5 nerve roots at L3-4 and L4-5 levels as detailed.

Cervical spondylosis with mass effect over cord and nerve roots as mentioned.

No other significant abnormality in spine.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Dr Praveen

MRI OF LUMBOSACRAL SPINE AND SCREENING OF REST OF THE SPINE

Clinical Profile: Complaints of lower back and left lower limb pain.

Technique: Sagittal T1, T2, IR, Axial T2. T1 and IR Coronal for SI joints. CT correlation.

Screening of rest of the spine: T2 sagittal

Chronic left L5 spondylolysis is seen without significant anterolisthesis. The lumbosacral spine displays a normal lordotic curvature and vertebral column alignment.

Limbus vertebra is seen at L4 level. Rest of the individual vertebrae are normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities.

Disc desiccation and facetal arthropathy are seen at almost all levels with endplate changes at multiple levels. The intervertebral discs are normal in heights.

D12-L1 and L1-2: Mild disc bulge with posterior annular fissure and facetal arthropathy are seen. No mass effect over nerve roots.

L2-3: Diffuse disc bulge and facetal arthropathy are seen. No mass effect over nerve roots.

L3-4: Diffuse disc bulge with facetal arthropathy and flaval thickening are seen causing effacement of lateral recess and mild indentation of bilateral traversing L4 nerve roots.

L4-5: Disc bulge with facetal arthropathy and flaval thickening are seen causing partial effacement of lateral recess and mild indentation of traversing L5 nerve roots (R>L).

L5-S1: Disc bulge with facetal arthropathy are seen. No significant mass effect over nerve roots.

The conus medullaris ends at L1 level and the cauda equina is normal in appearance.

Mild atrophy with subtle oedema and fatty changes are seen involving bilateral posterior paravertebral and gluteal muscles.

Both SI joints show mild degenerative changes.

Screening of cervical spine:

Mild early reversal of cervical lordosis is seen with normal vertebral column alignment.

Disc desiccation is seen at all levels with disc bulge and uncovertebral arthropathy at multiple levels. The vertebral end-plates are normal. The intervertebral discs are normal in heights.

Mild retro flexion of tip of odontoid process is noted with degenerative changes at anterior atlantodental joint. No evidence of mass effect over cervicomedullary junction noted.

Mild indentation of cord is seen at C5-C6 level. No spinal cord signal changes are seen. No other significant abnormality is seen.

Screening of dorsal spine:

Small vertebral body haemangioma noted at D11 level.

Mild disc desiccation with ligamentum flaval thickening is noted at few levels.

Spinal cord appears normal. No other significant abnormality is seen in the dorsal spine.

IMPRESSION:

Diffuse degenerative changes of spine with chronic L5 spondylolysis as detailed.

Disc bulge with facetal arthropathy causing mild indentation of bilateral L4 and L5 nerve roots at L3-4 and L4-5 levels as detailed.

Cervical spondylosis as mentioned.

Mild atrophy with subtle edema and fatty changes involving bilateral posterior paravertebral and gluteal muscles.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Dr Praveen/ Dr. Deepikha

Dr. Suresh

MRI SCAN OF LEFT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: A/h/o RTA 2 days back and sustained injury to left shoulder. C/o pain and restricted range of movements.

Technique: PDfs, T1, T2, GRE and T2 s in all planes.

Bones and joints:

Mild static posterosuperior subluxation of the humeral head is seen.

Mild to moderate joint effusion is seen. Capsular injury is seen in postero-superior aspect. Diffuse synovial/ capsular thickening is seen in the joint, predominantly in rotator cuff and the axillary recess regions.

No acute bony Bankart/ Hill-Sachs lesion is seen. No acute fracture or displaced osteochondral fragments seen.

Rest of the articulating bones appear grossly normal for age. 

Rotator cuff:

Acute full thickness tears are seen involving entire width of supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendons (AP dimension of about 4 cm) from its insertion foot print region.

Retracted torn end is severely edematous and wavy with varying levels of retraction. The torn ends are seen predominantly at the level of medial 1/3 of humeral head/ joint and with maximum retraction of about 3.8 cm from insertion. Synovitis is seen in the region of tears.

Extension of tear to the myotendinous junction of infraspinatus is seen.

Mild strain changes with small intrasubstance tear are seen in teres minor tendon.

Subscapularis tendinosis is seen with chronic partial thickness tears are seen in the cranial part of the tendon.

Significant contusion and grade II myofascial strain changes are seen involving infraspinatus and teres minor muscles and adjacent fascia. Grade I myofascial strain changes are seen involving the supraspinatus and subscapularis muscles.

Grade I / II strain changes are also seen in involving the deltoid, teres major and other shoulder girdle muscles also.

Mild atrophy is seen in supraspinatus muscle. No significant atrophy is seen in rest of the rotator cuff muscles. Stage I fatty changes (Goutallier's classification) are seen.

LHBT appears intact with tendinosis with intrasubstance tear.

Labroligamentous structures:

Degenerative changes are seen in glenoid labrum with chronic tears in superior and anterosuperior, anteroinferior and posterosuperior quadrants. No displaced fragment is seen.

Disruption of biceps pulley is seen.

AC joint:

AC joint arthropathy is seen. Type II acromion is seen and is laterally sloping. Sub acromial space measures 3.4 mm with subacromial bursitis. Synovial thickening with minimal haemorrhagic fluid is seen in the bursa.

Posterosuperior capsular injury with extra articular fluid collection measuring 2.5 x 1.2 x 0.6 cm is seen just posterior to the infraspinatus muscle/ tendon.

Rest of the soft tissue appears grossly normal.

Torn tendon | Supraspinatus | Infraspinatus
Tear width ( Anteroposterior) | 4 cm
Tendon retraction ( Mediolateral) | 3.8 cm
Tendon degeneration ( Grade 0-3 ) | 3 | 3
Muscle atrophy ( Grade 0-3 ) | 1 | 0
Muscle fatty infiltration (Grade 0-4) | 1 | 1

IMPRESSION:

Acute traumatic full-thickness, full-width tears of supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendons as detailed.

Acute infraspinatus and teres minor muscle contusions and grade II myofascial strain, with rotator cuff and shoulder girdle muscles strain changes as detailed.

Posterosuperior glenohumeral capsular injury/ disruption with associated extra-articular fluid collection posterior to the infraspinatus.

Mild posterosuperior subluxation of humeral head with effusion and synovitis.

Other rotator cuff and LHBT changes and labral tears as detailed.

AC joint arthropathy with reduced subacromial space and subacromial bursitis.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr Akila

MRI SCAN OF LEFT FOOT

Clinical profile: H/o left infected corn foot excision done on 22.07.26 (lateral aspect of planar forefoot). Now c/o swelling and pain at the site of surgery for 2 weeks

Technique: T1, IR, T2, DWI and PC T1 in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Minimal fluid is seen within the ankle, posterior subtalar, and first metatarsophalangeal joints.

Ankle joint alignment is maintained.

The visualized bones demonstrate normal marrow signal intensity without focal marrow edema, cortical destruction, erosions, or aggressive osseous lesion.

No MRI evidence of acute osteomyelitis. No other significant joint effusion, synovial thickening, or post-contrast synovial enhancement to suggest septic arthritis.

Ligament complex:

The medial and lateral ligament complexes of the ankle are intact.

The visualized ligamentous structures of the foot appear unremarkable without evidence of tear or disruption.

Tendons:

The anterior, medial, lateral, and posterior tendon groups are intact and demonstrate normal signal intensity.

No evidence of tendinosis, tendon tear, or tenosynovitis.

The peroneal and flexor retinacula are intact.

Soft tissue:

Post procedural changes are noted in the plantar aspect of foot opposite left 4th metatarsophalangeal joint. Focal soft tissue thickening with IR signal changes and post contrast enhancement is seen at this region.

No abnormal focal fluid collection or restricted diffusion is seen.

Diffuse mild edema are seen involving the subcutaneous fat planes along the dorsum of the foot, predominantly overlying the second through fourth metatarsal regions, appearing hyper intense on T2-weighted and STIR images with no significant post-contrast enhancement.

Additional diffuse mild subcutaneous edema is seen around the ankle and distal leg regions.

No focal fluid collection or drainable abscess or sinus tract formation is seen.

No extension into deep fascial planes, muscles, tendons, joints, or osseous structures is identified.

The visualized muscles demonstrate normal bulk and signal intensity.

IMPRESSION:

Post procedural changes with mild soft tissue thickening in plantar aspect of foot opposite left 4th MTP joint, likely of post-operative inflammatory etiology.

Diffuse subcutaneous inflammatory edema in dorsum of left foot, ankle and distal leg regions, suggestive of inflammatory cellulitis with associated lymphedematous changes.

No infected fluid collection or features of acute osteomyelitis/ septic arthritis.

Suggested clinical correlation/ further evaluation and review as indicated.

Dr. Aathithya

MRI SCAN OF LEFT FOOT WITH ANKLE

Clinical profile: K/c/o DCLD. H/o scald injury to left lower limb 2 months back, c/o swelling of left leg for the past 2 months. C/o fever with chills for 1 week? Left leg cellulitis? SBP.

Technique: PDfs, T1, T2, GRE, IR, DWI and PC T1 in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Minimal ankle joint effusion is noted.

Ankle alignment is maintained. The visualized bones demonstrate preserved marrow signal without focal marrow edema, cortical destruction or abnormal enhancement.

No MRI evidence of acute osteomyelitis.

No significant articular erosions or synovial enhancement to suggest septic arthritis.

The remaining visualized bones and joints are unremarkable for age.

Tendons and ligaments:

The anterior, medial and posterior compartment tendons are intact with preserved signal and morphology.

No significant tenosynovitis is identified.

Peroneal and flexor retinacula are intact.

The medial and lateral ligament complexes are intact. The remaining visualized ligamentous structures are also preserved.

Skin, subcutaneous tissues and muscles:

Diffuse skin thickening and extensive subcutaneous edema/ inflammatory signal is seen involving the toes, dorsum of the foot, ankle and distal leg, appearing hyper intense on T2/IR sequences with associated post-contrast enhancement, consistent with acute cellulitis.

No organized rim-enhancing collection or significant drainable abscess is identified. No sinus tract or soft-tissue ulcer is seen.

No focal diffusion restriction is identified within the involved soft tissues to suggest a drainable collection.

The visualized muscles demonstrate preserved bulk and signal without focal intramuscular collection or significant myositis.

IMPRESSION:

Diffuse cellulitis involving toes, dorsum of left foot, ankle and distal leg, with extensive skin/ subcutaneous edema and mild enhancement.

No drainable soft-tissue abscess, sinus tract or soft-tissue ulcer.

No MRI evidence of acute osteomyelitis or septic arthritis.

Minimal ankle joint effusion.

No significant tenosynovitis or focal intramuscular collection.

Dr. Akhildev

MRI OF RIGHT UPPER LIMB WITH BRACHIAL PLEXUS SCREENING (PLAIN)

Clinical Profile: C/o progressive finger stiffness of right hand and weakness. No history of sensory loss (PIN syndrome).

Technique: 3D IR coronal for brachial plexus, T1, T2, IR, and limited DWI axial sequences for right upper limb, coronal and sagittal IR of right elbow with USG and CT correlation. Screening of cervical spine: T2 sagittal and axial.

Bones and joints:

Moderate ulnohumeral osteoarthrosis is seen with joint-space narrowing, subchondral cystic changes, marginal osteophytes and few small intra-articular loose bodies. Minimal associated joint effusion is seen.

Radiocapitellar and proximal radioulnar joints are maintained in alignment.

Moderate osteoarthrosis of the right glenohumeral joint is seen with subchondral sclerosis and associated joint effusion.

Visualized osseous structures otherwise show preserved marrow signal. No acute fracture, focal marrow lesion or destructive osseous abnormality is seen.

Soft tissue and Nerves:

A well-defined, intramuscular fat-containing lesion measuring approximately 2.5 × 2.0 × 1.3 cm (AP × CC × TR) is seen within the deep aspect of the right supinator muscle, predominantly along its lateral/ posterior aspects and closely surrounding the proximal radius.

The lesion demonstrates signal characteristics identical to subcutaneous fat, appearing hyper intense on T1- and T2-weighted images with complete suppression on IR/STIR sequences. It shows no diffusion restriction or internal calcification. Few residual supinator muscle fibres are seen traversing the lesion.

The lesion closely abuts the proximal radial cortex; however, no cortical thickening, cortical erosion, periosteal reaction, osseous excrescence or adjacent marrow signal abnormality is identified, favoring an intramuscular lipoma rather than a parosteal lipoma.

The lesion produces smooth focal mass effect upon the posterior interosseous nerve (PIN) at its course through the supinator, with resultant focal compression.

On USG correlation, the PIN demonstrates mild smooth fusiform thickening along its intramuscular course through the supinator, with subtle involvement of the immediately adjacent proximal and distal segments, compatible with compressive neuropathy.

Subtle diffuse STIR hyper intensity involving the visualized extensor compartment muscles of the forearm with relative preservation of muscle bulk and without significant fatty atrophy is noted, compatible with sub-acute denervation changes. No focal intramuscular collection or mass lesion is identified.

Rest of the visualized muscles, tendons and soft tissue planes are unremarkable.

Screening of Brachial plexus:

The roots, trunks, divisions, and cords of the bilateral brachial plexus appear normal in thickness and signal intensity. No preganglionic avulsion, pseudomeningocele, or focal nerve sheath lesion is seen.

Rest of the visualized muscles, tendons, and soft tissue planes appear grossly normal.

Screening Of Cervical Spine:

Mild loss of cervical lordosis is seen with disc desiccation at all levels and reduced disc height /endplate changes at C5-6 and C6-7 levels.

Disc bulge and uncovertebral arthropathy causing indentation of cord and bilateral ventral nerve roots (R>L) is seen at C5-C6 level.

No spinal cord signal changes are seen. No other significant abnormality seen in cervical spine.

IMPRESSION:

Well-delineated intramuscular lipoma within right supinator muscle causing mass effect and compression over posterior interosseous nerve (PIN) as detailed.

Mild smooth thickening of posterior interosseous nerve at and around the level of the supinator, consistent with focal compressive PIN neuropathy.

Subtle diffuse denervation edema of visualized extensor compartment muscles, without significant fatty atrophy, compatible with sub-acute denervation changes secondary to PIN neuropathy.

Moderate ulnohumeral joint osteoarthrosis with subchondral cysts, osteophytes, and minimal joint effusion as detailed.

Right shoulder joint osteoarthrosis with subchondral sclerosis and joint effusion.

No significant abnormality identified in brachial plexus.

Cervical spondylosis, more significant at C6-7 level as mentioned.

Suggested clinical, electromyography (EMG/ NCS) correlation and review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF LEFT ARM (PLAIN AND CONTRAST)

Clinical Profile: Known case of progressive quadriparesis, chronic neuropathy? CIDP. Complaints of pain and swelling over left upper limb region.

Technique: T1, T2, IR, DWI, GRE, pre and post contrast T1fs in all planes and CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Visualised bones of left arm (humerus, radius, and ulna) and elbow / shoulder joints show normal morphology and bone marrow signal intensity. No cortical erosion, bone destruction, or periosteal reaction seen.

Visualised shoulder and elbow joints appear normal in alignment with minimal joint effusion.

No imaging features of acute osteomyelitis or septic arthritis seen.

Soft tissue:

A well-defined, lobulated intramuscular soft-tissue lesion measuring approximately 5.0 × 4.5 × 4.2 cm (CC × TR × AP) is seen within the proximal left triceps muscle.

The lesion demonstrates heterogeneous intermediate-to-high signal intensity on T2/IR sequences and heterogeneous intermediate signal intensity on T1-weighted images, with moderate heterogeneous post-contrast enhancement and areas of altered diffusion.

A thin peripheral T2-hypointense rim is noted with significant susceptibility blooming seen on GRE sequences.

On CT correlation, the lesion demonstrates peripheral, mature-appearing lamellar ossification with relative central sparing, producing a characteristic zonal pattern of mineralization.

Marked surrounding myofascial edema and inflammatory signal abnormality are seen involving the triceps muscle, with extension along the adjacent intermuscular and deep fascial planes. Minimal overlying subcutaneous edema is present.

The visualized radial and brachial nerves and adjacent neurovascular structures are preserved, without direct encasement or infiltration by the lesion.

Diffuse severe fatty atrophy of the visualized muscles of the arm and forearm is noted, in keeping with the background chronic neuromuscular disorder/ denervation.

IMPRESSION:

Well-defined intramuscular ossifying lesion within proximal left triceps muscle, demonstrating characteristic peripheral zonal/ lamellar ossification with relative central sparing on CT, associated with marked surrounding myofascial edema and inflammatory change. Imaging features are characteristic of myositis Ossificans (early/ intermediate stage).

No cortical destruction, marrow involvement or aggressive osseous abnormality.

No definite features to suggest aggressive soft-tissue sarcoma in present study.

Marked surrounding triceps myofascial edema/ inflammation, likely representing the active phase of the lesion.

Diffuse severe fatty atrophy of visualized arm and forearm musculature, consistent with chronic denervation/ neuromuscular disease.

Suggested clinical correlation / review as indicated.

Dr Praveen

CT SCAN OF BONY PELVIS (PLAIN)

Clinical profile: H/o fracture shaft of left femur on 07.10.2026. ? Myositis Ossificans. Planned for fixation.

Old displaced non-united fracture of left femoral shaft is seen with mild surrounding callus formation.

Extensive, mature-appearing heterotopic ossification is seen along the anterior aspects of left hemi pelvis, hip joint and proximal femur, involving the anterior compartment musculature and iliopsoas region.

There is bridging heterotopic ossification between the anterior aspect of the left iliac bone and the proximal femur, resulting in partial osseous bridging across the anterior hip region.

The overall extent of the mature heterotopic ossification measures approximately 28.0 × 8.7 × 6.5 cm (CC × TR × AP).

The ossification demonstrates a mature peripheral/ lamellar appearance. There is smooth mass effect upon the adjacent muscles and soft tissues.

The anterior compartment muscles of the proximal left thigh are bulky and edematous, likely representing associated reactive myositis/ soft-tissue inflammatory change.

No focal soft-tissue collection or drainable fluid collection is identified.

The left acetabulum and hip joint are maintained without significant articular surface destruction. No intra-articular osseous fragment is identified.

Bilateral sacroiliac joints and pubic symphysis are preserved.

Bilateral superior and inferior pubic rami are intact.

The remaining visualized pelvic bones demonstrate preserved morphology without acute fracture or destructive osseous lesion.

Visualized proximal shaft of the right femur is intact.

IMPRESSION:

Extensive mature heterotopic ossification/ ossifying myositis involving anterior left hemi pelvis, periarticular left hip and proximal femur, with involvement of the iliopsoas and anterior compartment musculature.

Prominent osseous bridging between left iliac bone and anterior aspect of proximal femur measuring approximately 28.0 × 8.7 × 6.5 cm.

Associated bulky edematous changes of anterior compartment musculature of the proximal left thigh, without drainable soft-tissue collection.

Displaced non-united fracture of left femoral shaft with mild callus formation.

No acute fracture involving remaining visualized pelvic bones/ right femur.

Dr Jayaprakash

MRI SCAN OF LEFT FOOT (PLAIN + CONTRAST)

Clinical profile: Known case of longstanding diabetes mellitus, complaints of left midfoot ulcer for 1 month. No history of discharge / pain.

Technique: IR, T1, T2, PDfs, GRE and DWI in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Old post-amputation changes are noted involving the great toe, with absence of the distal phalanx and distal part of proximal phalanx, with small residual proximal phalanx (consistent with left great toe amputation).

Chronic destructive neuropathic arthropathy (Charcot neuroarthropathy) is seen involving the midfoot region with severe osteoarthrosis changes, reduced joint spaces, articular irregularity and erosions, extensive subarticular cysts, and prominent osteophytes, periosteal reaction and osseous fragmentation. Mild subarticular marrow edema is seen. No significant joint effusion or synovitis is seen.

These changes are seen involving navicular, cuneiforms, cuboid and bases of 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th metatarsals. Mild incongruity and subluxation of few joints are seen.

Mild degenerative changes with minimal effusion are seen involving the ankle, posterior subtalar and mid foot joints.

No imaging features of acute osteomyelitis or septic arthritis seen. No definite focal intraosseous abscess seen.

Rest of the visualized bones and joints appear grossly normal for age.

Prominent plantar and dorsal calcaneal enthesophytes are seen.

Soft Tissues:

A plantar soft tissue ulcer is seen at the level of the cuboid. Diffuse surrounding soft tissue inflammatory changes, edema and enhancement are seen in the midfoot, particularly around the ulcer.

Diffuse edema with mild volume loss and fatty atrophy involving the intrinsic muscles of the foot and visualized distal leg musculature, in keeping with diabetic myopathy/ neuropathic muscular changes.

Diffuse skin and subcutaneous edema involving the dorsum of the foot and ankle.

Features of plantar fasciitis are seen.

No significant soft-tissue abscess or other drainable collection identified.

IMPRESSION:

Features are suggestive of chronic Charcot neuro-osteoarthropathy involving midfoot region as detailed.

Plantar soft tissue ulcer at level of cuboid bone with soft tissue inflammation and cellulitis as detailed. No drainable intraosseous/ soft tissue abscess.

No definite MRI evidence of acute osteomyelitis/ septic arthritis seen.

Diffuse skin and subcutaneous edema with diabetic myoneuropathy changes involving intrinsic foot musculature.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Dr Praveen

MRI OF BONY THORAX (PLAIN WITH CONTRAST)

Clinical profile: Recurrent sternal wound and pus discharge, H/o two times sternal wires removal outside. Now persistent pus discharge, to rule out osteomyelitis of the ribs and cartilage destruction.

Technique: Axial and coronal IR, T2 and T1, IR, GRE, DWI, PC T1 in all planes, CT correlation.

Sternum and sternotomy site:

Chronic post-operative changes related to prior median sternotomy and sternal wire removal is noted. No retained sternal wire fragments or definite osseous sequestrum identified.

No abnormal marrow signal, cortical destruction or abnormal post-contrast enhancement involving the sternum to suggest active sternal osteomyelitis.

Ribs and costochondral structures:

Patchy marrow signal abnormality with cortical irregularity/ erosion and associated sclerosis involving the anterior aspect of the right 2nd rib, with corresponding post-contrast enhancement, consistent with active osteomyelitis.

Mild adjacent inflammatory change extends up to the right 2nd costochondral junction. The visualized costal cartilage and sternocostal/ costochondral junctions do not show definite abnormal marrow/ cartilage signal or significant enhancement to suggest frank cartilage destruction.

Pleural thickening and enhancement are noted along the anterior right 2nd–4th ribs and adjacent costochondral regions, most pronounced at the right 2nd rib, likely representing reactive/ inflammatory pleural involvement.

Perichondral/ presternal soft tissues:

Multiple small loculated peripheral rim-enhancing fluid collections with diffusion restriction are seen within the anterior and posterior perichondral soft tissues adjacent to the right 2nd and 3rd costal cartilages/ costochondral junctions, as well as within the presternal soft tissue plane at the level of the right 3rd costal cartilage insertion, consistent with small abscesses.

The largest collection measures approximately 2.6 × 1.6 × 1.0 cm.

Muscles and soft tissues:

Diffuse T2/ IR hyper intense signal and post-contrast enhancement involving portions of the right pectoralis major and minor muscles adjacent to the right 2nd–4th ribs, costal cartilages and costochondral junctions, with medial extension into the presternal and parasternal soft tissues.

These findings are consistent with acute myofascitis with associated phlegmonous inflammatory change.

No significant additional drainable collection or inflammatory extension into the anterior mediastinum is identified.

Pleura and lungs:

Mild reactive pleural thickening and enhancement as described above. Visualized lung fields are grossly clear.

Mediastinum:

Visualized mediastinal structures are unremarkable. No significant mediastinal lymphadenopathy.

Upper abdomen:

Visualized upper abdominal structures are grossly unremarkable.

Additional skeletal findings:

Bilateral partial/ incomplete cervical ribs are noted, with fusion of the left cervical rib to the first rib.

Remaining visualized osseous structures and joints show no significant abnormality.

IMPRESSION:

Active osteomyelitis involving anterior right 2nd rib, with cortical erosions and marrow signal abnormality/ enhancement.

Multiple small perichondral and presternal abscesses adjacent to right 2nd–3rd costochondral regions, largest measuring approximately 2.6 × 1.6 × 1.0 cm.

Adjacent right pectoralis major/ minor myofascitis with presternal/ parasternal phlegmonous inflammatory change.

Mild reactive inflammatory pleural thickening/ enhancement along anterior right 2nd–4th ribs.

No definite MRI evidence of active sternal osteomyelitis or frank costal cartilage destruction. No retained sternal wire fragments or definite sequestrum.

Bilateral incomplete cervical ribs, with fusion of left cervical rib to first rib.

Suggested clinical correlation / review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
MRI SCAN OF LEFT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: H/o trauma, right shoulder dislocation. For detailed evaluation 

Technique: PDfs, T1, IR, T2 and GRE in all planes.

Bones and joints:

Large acute Hill-Sachs impaction defect is seen involving the posterolateral aspect of the humeral head, measuring approximately 28 × 21 × 15 mm (TR × CC × depth), with surrounding bone marrow edema/contusion.

No definite bony Bankart lesion is identified.

Mildly comminuted fracture involving the greater tuberosity of the humerus is noted, with associated marrow edema/ contusion.

Mild glenohumeral joint effusion is present. No intra-articular osteochondral loose fragment is identified.

Rest of the visualized osseous structures and articular surfaces are maintained.

Rotator cuff:

Acute full-thickness tear involving posterior supraspinatus and anterior infraspinatus tendon fibres, spanning approximately 1.5 cm in AP dimension. The torn tendon margins are edematous and mildly wavy, with approximately 8 mm medial retraction from the humeral insertion.

The remaining anterior supraspinatus and posterior infraspinatus fibres show marked strain/ tendinopathy changes with small partial-thickness intrasubstance tears. Minor extension of the tear/strain changes towards the respective myotendinous junctions is noted.

Subscapularis tendon demonstrates strain/ tendinopathy changes with small partial-thickness articular-sided and intrasubstance tears.

Teres minor tendon is intact.

Long head of biceps tendon is maintained in position and remains continuous, with mild tendinopathy/ strain changes.

Muscles and Soft Tissues:

Extensive peri-muscular and myofascial strain changes with diffuse edema and small amounts of fluid along the fascial planes are seen involving the rotator cuff musculature and anterior shoulder soft tissues, most pronounced around the subscapularis muscle.

Associated soft-tissue/ fascial edema extend into the axilla and proximal arm.

Mild strain changes are also seen involving the deltoid muscle.

No significant intramuscular hematoma or drainable soft-tissue collection is identified.

Labroligamentous Structures:

Anterior labral tear with associated soft-tissue Bankart lesion is noted, with adjacent periosteal injury. The tear extends from the anteroinferior region into the anterosuperior and superior labral quadrants.

No displaced labral fragment is identified.

Sprain/ partial tear of the anterior capsuloligamentous structures is noted, including a partial tear of the anterior band of the inferior glenohumeral ligament (IGHL) at its humeral attachment. No complete capsuloligamentous disruption is identified.

Acromioclavicular Joint and Bursa:

AC joint arthropathy is noted. Acromion is type II in morphology.

Mild-to-moderate fluid distension of the subacromial-subdeltoid bursa is seen.

Additional Findings:

Diffuse periarticular and surrounding soft-tissue edema is noted.

IMPRESSION:

Large acute Hill-Sachs impaction defect with surrounding marrow edema/ contusion, consistent with recent anterior shoulder dislocation.

Anterior labral tear/ soft-tissue Bankart lesion extending from anteroinferior to anterosuperior/superior labrum, with adjacent periosteal injury.

Partial tear of anterior IGHL at its humeral attachment with sprain/ partial tear of the anterior capsuloligamentous structures. No complete capsuloligamentous disruption.

Acute full-thickness tears of posterior supraspinatus and anterior infraspinatus tendons with associated rotator cuff strain/ partial tears as detailed.

Mild greater tuberosity fracture with associated marrow edema/ contusion.

Extensive periarticular and myofascial strain involving rotator cuff and deltoid musculature, extending into axilla/proximal arm.

Mild joint effusion and mild-to-moderate subacromial-subdeltoid bursitis.

Mild AC joint arthropathy.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Grade I anterolisthesis of L4 over L5 vertebra is seen. No spondylolysis is seen. Significant facet arthropathy is seen at this level.

Rest of the lumbosacral spine displays an exaggerated lordotic curvature.

The individual vertebrae are normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities.

Disc desiccation and facetal arthropathy is seen at all levels and ligamentum flavum thickening at multiple levels. The intervertebral discs are normal in heights. The vertebral end-plates are normal.

L1-2: Diffuse disc bulge with central disc protrusion and facetal arthropathy are seen causing mild anterior thecal sac indentation. No significant mass effect over nerve roots noted.

L2-3: Mild disc bulge with facetal arthropathy are seen. No significant mass effect over nerve roots noted.

L3-4: Diffuse disc bulge with right foraminal disc protrusion, ligamentum flavum thickening with facetal arthropathy are seen causing indentation of right exiting L3 nerve root.

L4-5: Uncovered disc with posterior disc bulge, ligamentum flavum thickening and facetal arthropathy are seen causing indentation of bilateral exiting L4 and traversing L5 nerve roots.

Simple cortical cyst measuring 6 x 4.8 cm is seen in the lower polar region of left kidney.

Diffuse degenerative changes of spine with L4-5 anterolisthesis as detailed.

Disc bulge, facetal arthropathy and flaval thickening causing mass effect over bilateral L4, L5 and S1 nerve roots at L4-5 and L5-S1 levels as detailed.

Disc bulge with protrusion and facetal arthropathy causing indentation of right L3 nerve root at L3-4 level as detailed.

Cervical spondylosis as mentioned.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Chronic complete full-thickness tear is seen involving the infraspinatus tendon from its insertion footprint with medial retraction measuring approximately 2.5 cm.

Grade III fatty atrophy of supraspinatus and infraspinatus muscles are noted.

Subscapularis tendinosis is seen with a chronic partial-thickness articular surface tear involving its cranial part (25%-50% thickness, measuring 0.9 mm in CC dimension). Few intramuscular cysts are noted within the subscapularis muscle.

Mild tendinosis of long head of biceps tendon (LHBT) is seen with intrasubstance longitudinal split tear and medial dislocation. Disruption of biceps pulley is noted.

The deltoid muscle appears normal.

Labroligamentous structures:

Degenerative changes are seen in labrum with chronic labral tears in superior, anterosuperior, posterosuperior and anteroinferior quadrants. Rest of the glenoid labrum is well demonstrated and is normal in signal intensity. No acute tear or displaced fragment is seen.

Mild synovial/ capsular thickening is seen in rotator interval and axillary recess regions. Thickening with increased signal intensity of biceps pulley and IGHL are seen.

AC joint:

Screening of rest of the spine: T2 sagittal

Postoperative changes:

Resolving postoperative changes with posterior element defects, bilateral pedicle screws, connecting rods and interbody spacers are seen at L2–L3 level. The orthopedic hardware appears grossly satisfactory in position.

Extensive postoperative edema and inflammatory changes are seen in the bilateral posterior paravertebral soft tissues. No significant postoperative fluid collection or hematoma is identified in the lumbar operative bed.

The lumbosacral spine displays a normal lordotic curvature. Rest of the individual vertebrae is normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities.

Disc desiccation and facetal arthropathy are seen at all levels. Severe facetal arthropathy is seen at L4-5 and L5-S1 levels with marrow edema at L4-5 level. Rest of the intervertebral discs is normal in heights. Rest of the vertebral end-plates is grossly normal.

Dr. Thamaraikkannan

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT KNEE JOINT

Clinical profile: H/o of recurring right knee locking over the past 1 year, more severe since yesterday with associated with knee swelling. No history of trauma or fever.

Technique: PDfs, IR, T1, T2 GRE in all planes, CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

The knee joint is normal with respect to alignment.

Mild to moderate right knee joint effusion is seen with adjacent synovial thickening.

A moderately defined lobulated intra-articular soft-tissue lesion measuring approximately 3.2 × 2.2 × 1.0 cm (TR × AP × CC) is seen in the anterior intercondylar region, along the posterior aspect of Hoffa's fat pad.

The lesion is slightly hyper intense to skeletal muscle on T1-weighted images and predominantly hyper intense on T2-weighted and STIR images, with patchy areas of T2/ STIR hypo intensity, areas of restricted diffusion and foci of susceptibility blooming on GRE images. No internal calcification or mineralisation is identified on CT.

The lesion causes mild indentation of the distal third of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) and partially surrounds the anterior horn and root of the lateral meniscus.

No adjacent cortical erosion, osseous involvement or marrow edema is seen. No aggressive imaging features are identified.

No significant articular cartilage loss or osteochondral loose body is seen.

The visualized distal femur, proximal tibia and patella demonstrate preserved cortical outlines and normal bone marrow signal intensity.

Meniscus:

The medial and lateral menisci are normal in configuration and signal intensities.

No acute tear or displaced fragment seen.

Ligaments:

The medial and lateral collateral ligaments and patellar retinaculum appear intact.

The anterior cruciate and posterior cruciate ligaments appear intact. The intermeniscal and meniscofemoral ligaments are also normal.

Posterolateral and posteromedial corner ligament complexes appear normal.

Rest of soft tissues:

The extensor mechanism appears normal. The surrounding muscles, tendons and neurovascular structures are normal.

IMPRESSION:

Moderately defined lobulated intra-articular lesion in anterior intercondylar region along posterior aspect of Hoffa's fat pad with characteristics as detailed.

Mild indentation of distal ACL and partial encasement of anterior horn/ root of the lateral meniscus by lesion, likely contributing to recurrent locking.

Mild to moderate knee joint effusion with synovitis.

No associated osseous erosion or marrow edema.

Imaging features are likely suggestive of localized tenosynovial giant cell tumor (localized TGCT/ nodular synovitis). Suggested clinical and HPE correlation / review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr Jayaprakash

MRI RIGHT UPPER LIMB NEUROGRAPHY (PLAIN AND CONTRAST)

Clinical history: History of dog bite over the distal right forearm 2 weeks back. Clinically suspected acute right median nerve injury with distal forearm muscle palsy.

Technique: Multiplanar, multisequence MRI of the right upper limb was performed, including the arm, forearm and hand. T1, T2, STIR/IR and DWI sequences were obtained. Pre- and post-contrast fat-suppressed T1-weighted images were acquired in all three planes through the forearm.

Findings:

Peripheral nerves:

Focal short-segment thickening and irregularity of the median nerve with increased IR signal intensity and abnormal post-contrast enhancement are noted in the distal forearm, at the level of the known dog bite injury. The nerve appears to be traversing the region of traumatic soft tissue injury, between the flexor digitorum superficialis and flexor carpi radialis tendons.

No definite complete discontinuity or retraction of the nerve ends is identified.

Mild smooth thickening, increased IR signal intensity and enhancement of the median nerve are also noted distal to this level, extending through the distal forearm into the carpal tunnel.

The median nerve in the proximal and mid forearm, traversing between the flexor digitorum superficialis and profundus muscles, appears grossly normal in caliber and fascicular architecture, apart from mildly increased signal intensity in its distal portion.

The right radial and ulnar nerves demonstrate preserved caliber, course and fascicular architecture, without significant abnormal signal intensity or enhancement.

Muscles:

Diffuse edema-like T2/ STIR hyper intense signal changes with contrast enhancement are noted involving the distal forearm flexor and extensor compartment muscles, predominantly along the radial aspect, in the region of the traumatic injury. No focal intramuscular collection.

No significant fatty infiltration or established muscle atrophy.

Rest of the visualised forearm and intrinsic muscles of the hand demonstrate preserved bulk and signal intensity.

Soft tissues:

An ill-defined collection measuring approximately 3.0 × 1.0 × 0.9 cm (CC × AP × TR) is noted deep to the flexor pollicis longus myotendinous junction. It demonstrates predominantly T2 hyper intense signal with relatively hypo intense internal contents, diffusion restriction and peripheral rim enhancement, suggestive of an infected collection.

Few additional small subcutaneous collections with similar imaging characteristics are noted along the dorsal aspect of the distal forearm, the largest measuring approximately 1.3 × 0.84 × 0.6 cm (CC × TR × AP).

Diffuse subcutaneous and intermuscular soft tissue edema and inflammatory changes are noted predominantly along the radial aspect of the distal forearm, corresponding to the site of the known dog bite injury.

Focal skin discontinuity is noted along the ventral and dorsal aspects of the distal forearm, consistent with the known traumatic wounds.

Bones and joints:

Visualized osseous structures demonstrate preserved marrow signal.

No focal marrow edema, cortical destruction or acute osseous abnormality.

No significant joint abnormality in the imaged field.

IMPRESSION:

Focal short-segment traumatic injury of right median nerve in distal forearm, at the site of known dog bite injury as detailed. No definite complete nerve discontinuity or retraction.

Mild diffuse thickening with  increased signal intensity and enhancement of median nerve distal to injury, extending into carpal tunnel, suggestive of associated distal neuritis/ neuropathy.

Diffuse signal changes involving distal forearm flexor and extensor compartment muscles, predominantly along radial aspect, likely representing traumatic/ inflammatory muscle changes.

Infected fluid collection deep to flexor pollicis longus, with additional smaller subcutaneous abscesses along dorsal aspect of distal forearm.

Extensive surrounding subcutaneous and intermuscular inflammatory changes at the site of the dog bite injury.

Suggested clinical correlation/ further evaluation and review as indicated.

Technique: PDfs, T1, T2, IR and GRE in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Acute to sub-acute subchondral trabecular insufficiency fracture with extensive edema is seen in medial femoral condyle. Additional trabecular injury with edema is also seen in non-articular parts of medial femoral condyle. No fracture line or displaced fragment seen. No significant features of osteonecrosis seen.

Osteoarthrosis of right knee joint is seen with partial thickness articular cartilage loss, chondral fissure and marginal osteophytes. No significant full thickness loss or osteochondral fragments seen in the present study.

Mild joint effusion is seen with reactive synovitis, lipoma arborescens and suprapatellar plica.

Rest of the articulating bones appears grossly normal for age.

Meniscus:

Mild degenerative changes are seen in medial and lateral menisci.

Small chronic oblique tear is seen in the anterior horn extending to anterior root of lateral meniscus. Small chronic tear is also seen in posterior root of medial meniscus.

Rest of medial and lateral menisci appears grossly normal. No significant acute tear or displaced fragments seen.

Ligaments:

Medial and lateral collateral ligaments appear grossly intact with mild degenerative changes. No significant tear or waviness is seen. The patellar retinaculum appears normal for age.

Degenerative changes are seen in ACL. No significant tear or waviness seen.

Posterior cruciate ligament appears normal for age.

Posterolateral and posteromedial corner ligament complexes appear intact.

Soft tissue edema is seen around the medial femoral condyle involving the adjacent soft tissue. Mild edema is also seen in the distal fibres of vastus medialis and lateralis muscles and adjacent fascia. No abnormal fluid collection is seen.

Extensor mechanism appears normal for age. Mild degenerative changes are seen in the proximal femoral attachment of medial and lateral gastrocnemius.

Rest of surrounding muscles, tendons and the neurovascular structures are grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Acute to sub-acute subchondral and trabecular insufficiency fractures in medial femoral condyle with extensive marrow edema as detailed.

Right knee osteoarthrosis with effusion as mentioned.

Mild degenerative changes of menisci with small chronic tears as detailed.

Degenerative changes of ACL and myotendinous changes as detailed.

Soft tissue edema around medial femoral condyle as mentioned.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI OF LUMBOSACRAL SPINE AND SCREENING OF REST OF THE SPINE

Clinical Profile: Complaints of stiffness of right upper limb fingers, neck muscles, pain in right upper limb, left lower limb, bilateral hip region.

Technique: Sagittal T1, T2, IR, Axial T2. T1 and IR Coronal for SI joints

Screening of rest of the spine: T2 sagittal, cervical spine T2 axial.

Incomplete sacralisation of L5 vertebra is seen with pseudo articulation on both sides (Castellvi type II b).

Grade I anterolisthesis of L3 over L4 and grade I retrolisthesis of L4 over L5 vertebra is seen. Severe facetal arthropathy is seen at these levels. No spondylolysis is seen.

Rest of the lumbar spine displays mild loss of lordotic curvature and normal vertebral column alignment.

The individual vertebrae are normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities. Vertebral body haemangioma is seen at L2 level.

Disc desiccation, facetal arthropathy and endplate changes are seen at almost all the levels. The intervertebral discs are grossly normal in heights.

L1-2 and L2-3: Diffuse disc bulge, facet arthropathy and flavum thickening are seen causing effacement of lateral recess. No significant mass effect or nerve roots seen.

L3-4: Uncovered disc with posterior bulge with facetal arthropathy and flavum thickening are seen causing effacement of lateral recess and mild indentation of bilateral traversing L4 nerve roots.

L4-5: Uncovered disc with posterior bulge, facetal arthropathy and flavum thickening (L>R) are seen causing effacement of lateral recess, compression of left exiting L4 and traversing L5 nerve roots and indentation of right traversing L5 nerve root.

L5-S1: No obvious abnormality detected.

The conus medullaris ends at D12-L1 level and the cauda equine is normal in appearance.

The prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues are grossly normal.

Both SI joints show mild degenerative changes with subarticular cysts/ edema (L>R).

Screening of cervical spine:

Loss of cervical lordosis is seen with disc desiccation at all levels and mild reduced disc height and endplate changes at few levels.

Disc bugle and uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy are seen at few levels. Mild indentation of cord and nerve roots is seen at few levels, more significant at C5-C6 level.

No spinal cord signal changes are seen. No other significant abnormality seen in the cervical spine.

Screening of dorsal spine:

Disc desiccation is seen at almost all levels and ligamentum flavum thickening at multiple levels. Small chronic Schmorl's nodes, endplate changes and disc bulge are seen at few levels. Spinal cord appears normal.

No other significant abnormality seen in dorsal spine.

IMPRESSION:

Incomplete sacralisation of L5 vertebra (Castellvi type II b).

Diffuse degenerative changes of spine with grade I listhesis at L3-L4 and L4-L5 levels as detailed.

Disc bulge with facetal arthropathy and flavum thickening mass effect over bilateral L4 and L5 nerve roots (L>R) at L3-4 and L4-5 levels as detailed.

Cervical spondylosis with mass effect over cord and nerve roots at few levels, more significant at C5-C6 level as mentioned.

Suggested clinical correlation / review as advised.

reports.fullText:
Dr Prakhyath

MRI SCAN OF BRACHIAL PLEXUS (PLAIN)

Clinical profile: H/o RTA with polytrauma? Left brachial plexus injury.

Technique: T1 coronals, 3D STIR coronal, 3D DWI neurography.

Screening of cervical spine: T2 sagittal and axial, DWI axial.

Screening of whole spine: T2 sagittal

Brachial plexus:

Left brachial plexus:

The preganglionic segments of the left C7, C8 and D1 nerve roots are not normally visualised, with lateral displacement of the corresponding dorsal root ganglia compared to the contralateral side. Findings are suspicious for preganglionic nerve root injury (root avulsion). No significant associated pseudomeningocele is identified.

The left C5 and C6 nerve roots appear grossly intact.

Evaluation of the left brachial plexus is significantly limited by extensive surrounding soft tissue and myofascial edema in the left supraclavicular and neck regions.

Mildly increased STIR signal intensity is noted involving the trunks, divisions and cords of the left brachial plexus, suggestive of associated postganglionic traction/ stretch injury.

Right brachial plexus:

The preganglionic and ganglionic segments of the right brachial plexus appear grossly intact.

Evaluation of the postganglionic segments is limited by extensive surrounding soft tissue edema in the right supraclavicular and anterior neck regions.

Screening of cervical spine:

Abnormal CSF-signal intensity epidural fluid collection is noted along the anterior epidural space, extending from C2–C3 to D3 vertebral levels, measuring up to 6.3 mm in maximum AP thickness at C7–D1 level. This results in effacement of the anterior thecal sac with mild smooth indentation of the cervicodorsal spinal cord.

The spinal cord appears normal in thickness and signal intensity, without evidence of significant cord edema or traumatic myelopathy signal changes.

Mild straightening of the cervical lordosis is noted.

Multilevel disc desiccation is seen.

Screening of dorsal spine:

Posterior epidural soft tissue edema/ fluid signal changes are noted, resulting in partial effacement of the thecal sac.

The dorsal spinal cord appears grossly normal in thickness and signal intensity.

Mild multilevel ligamentum flavum thickening is noted.

Screening of lumbar spine:

Conus medullaris terminates at L1 vertebral level. Cauda equina nerve roots appear grossly unremarkable.

Multilevel disc desiccation and facet arthropathy are noted, with mild disc bulges and posterior annular fissures at a few levels.

Visualized bones and soft tissues:

Displaced fracture involving the middle third of the left clavicle.

Comminuted displaced fracture of the left scapula.

Fractures involving the posterior aspects of the left upper ribs.

Extensive soft tissue injury with diffuse myofascial edema, strain and contusions involving the bilateral shoulder girdles, neck and upper thoracic regions, more pronounced on the left.

Abnormal increased STIR signal intensity involving bilateral supraspinatus (left more than right), infraspinatus, subscapularis and deltoid muscles, consistent with multifocal muscle strains/contusions.

Bilateral shoulder joint effusions are seen.

Postoperative changes with small fluid collections along the left anterior costochondral junctions of the first and second ribs.

Mild free fluid in the visualized pelvis, possibly representing haemoperitoneum in the setting of trauma.

IMPRESSION:

Findings suspicious for preganglionic injury/ root avulsion involving left C7, C8 and D1 nerve roots as detailed. No significant associated pseudomeningocele.

Mild increased signal involving rest of left brachial plexus, likely suggestive of associated postganglionic traction/ stretch injury. Evaluation is significantly limited by extensive surrounding soft tissue edema.

Right brachial plexus preganglionic and ganglionic segments appear grossly intact; postganglionic evaluation is limited.

Long-segment anterior epidural CSF-signal intensity fluid collection extending from C2–C3 to D3 causing thecal sac effacement and mild smooth indentation of cervicodorsal spinal cord, suggestive of traumatic spinal epidural CSF collection.

No significant cord signal abnormality.

Posterior epidural soft tissue edema/ fluid signal changes in dorsal spine with partial thecal sac effacement.

Multiple fractures and extensive soft tissue changes in neck, thorax and shoulder regions as detailed.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as clinically indicated.
