MRI SCAN OF RIGHT WRIST (PLAIN + CONTRAST)

Clinical profile: C/o acute onset of swelling and pain in right hand for 3 days.

Technique: T1, PDfs, IR, T2, DWI, GRE in all planes. CT correlation 

Bones and joints:

Mild wrist joint effusion is seen with synovial thickening and enhancement, suggestive of acute synovitis. No significant articular erosions or subarticular marrow edema.

No abnormal marrow signal intensity or enhancement to suggest acute osteomyelitis.

Carpal bones demonstrate normal alignment and articulation. No static subluxation, dislocation or intercarpal dissociation.

Radio carpal, ulnocarpal and visualized carpometacarpal joint spaces are grossly maintained.

Small fluid collection measuring approximately 0.9 × 0.7 cm is noted along the radio volar aspect of the wrist joint, appearing to communicate with the joint space, possibly representing a small loculated joint effusion/ synovial collection.

Soft tissues and tendons:

Extensive acute infective/ inflammatory tenosynovitis involving multiple extensor tendon compartments is seen, predominantly the second, third and fourth compartments, with mild fluid distension and surrounding inflammatory changes.

Acute radial and ulnar bursitis with fluid distension of the respective bursae, extending along the flexor tendon sheaths.

A small intramuscular fluid collection measuring approximately 1.7 × 0.7 × 0.8 cm is noted along the deep aspect of the thenar musculature, demonstrating diffusion restriction, suspicious for an intramuscular abscess.

Diffuse extensive inflammatory edema and enhancement involving the subcutaneous and deep fascial planes of the distal forearm, wrist and hand, along both palmar and dorsal aspects, significantly more pronounced along the dorsal aspect of the wrist and hand.

No definite tendon tear or tendinosis. No significant tendon retraction.

IMPRESSION:

Extensive infective/ inflammatory tenosynovitis involving multiple extensor tendon compartments, predominantly the 2nd, 3rd and 4th compartments.

Acute radial and ulnar bursitis with fluid distension and inflammatory changes extending along the flexor tendon sheaths.

Small diffusion-restricting intramuscular collection along deep aspect of thenar musculature, suspicious for an intramuscular abscess.

Extensive diffuse cellulitis and deep soft tissue inflammatory changes involving distal forearm, wrist and hand along both palmar and dorsal aspects as detailed.

Mild wrist joint effusion with synovitis and a small radio volar loculated fluid collection, possibly communicating with the joint.

No MRI evidence of acute osteomyelitis.

MRI SCAN OF BONY PELVIS (FOR RT PLANNING)

Clinical Profile: Known case of Carcinoma prostate; post radical prostatectomy in 2019, post RT in 2022, had increasing PSA levels, PET CT on 29.10.2026- soft tissue deposit in left gluteal region.

Technique: IR, T1, T2, PDfs, GRE, DWI, pre and post contrast T1 fs.

Soft tissues:

A well-defined nodular soft tissue lesion measuring approximately 6 × 4 mm is noted in the deep intermuscular plane between the left superior gemellus and gluteus maximus muscles, immediately posterolateral to the sciatic nerve, about 2-3 mm away.

The lesion appears mildly hyper intense on T2/IR sequences and isointense on T1-weighted images, with diffusion restriction and post-contrast enhancement.

Imaging features are suspicious for a metastatic soft tissue deposit, in view of the known primary malignancy and corresponding PET-CT findings.

No significant focal lesion is identified in the prostatectomy bed or elsewhere in the visualized pelvis.

Few discrete subcentimetric bilateral inguinal lymph nodes are noted, measuring up to 5 mm in short-axis diameter, likely reactive.

Visualized pelvic muscles and tendons otherwise appear unremarkable.

Bilateral inguinal hernias (left more than right) containing omental fat are noted.

Chronic tear of the left acetabular labrum with an associated paralabral cyst measuring approximately 2.2 × 0.5 × 0.5 cm along its lateral aspect.

Bilateral hip joint alignment and articular relationships are maintained.

Trace bilateral hip joint fluid without significant effusion or synovitis.

No imaging evidence of avascular necrosis of the femoral heads.

Bones and joints of pelvis:

Visualized pelvic bones and proximal femora demonstrate preserved marrow signal intensity.

No focal marrow-replacing lesion or suspicious osseous abnormality is identified.

Bilateral sacroiliac joints and pubic symphysis appear unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

Well-defined 6 × 4 mm enhancing, diffusion-restricting nodular soft tissue lesion in left deep gluteal region as detailed, suspicious for metastatic soft tissue deposit, correlating with recent PET-CT findings.

No significant focal lesion in prostatectomy bed or elsewhere in visualized pelvis.

No suspicious focal marrow-replacing lesion or osseous metastasis in visualized bony pelvis and proximal femora.

Chronic left acetabular labral tear with an associated paralabral cyst.

Bilateral fat-containing inguinal hernias (left more than right).

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr Christina

MRI OF BRACHIAL PLEXUS AND SCREENING OF CERVICAL SPINE

Clinical profile: RTA with traumatic brain injury (diffuse axonal injury), left parietal thin acute SDH, facial bone fractures. Left second rib fracture. Manubrium sterni displaced fracture. Complaints of weakness of right upper limb (involving all digits) and lower limb. Left upper limb weakness with difficulty in abduction (involving 1st 2 digits). Scan done to rule out brachial plexus injury.

Technique: 3DIR coronal, T2 SPACE, T2, T1, DWI coronal, T2 axial, T2 Dixon axial, T2 DRIVE coronal. Cervical spine – axial and Sagittal T2, CT screening.

Left brachial plexus:

Smooth indentation, mass effect and mild displacement of the preganglionic segments of left C5, C6 and C7 nerve roots are noted, secondary to thin anterior and left posterolateral epidural CSF-intensity fluid collections.

No definite discontinuity or complete disruption of the visualized preganglionic nerve root segments is seen.

No significant lateral displacement of the corresponding dorsal root ganglia. No significant pseudomeningocele formation.

Mild smooth thickening and increased signal intensity of the left C5, C6 and C7 nerve roots, without evidence of complete disruption or retracted nerve ends.

Mild diffuse smooth thickening and increased signal intensity of the left brachial plexus, involving the trunks, divisions and cords, predominantly in the upper plexus.

Left C8 and D1 nerve roots appear grossly normal in thickness and signal intensity.

Right brachial plexus:

The roots, trunks, divisions and cords of the right brachial plexus appear normal in thickness, course and signal intensity.

No evidence of pseudomeningocele, nerve root disruption or significant features of traumatic traction injury.

Cervical spine screening:

Mild levoscoliosis of the cervical spine with loss of normal cervical lordosis.

The individual vertebrae are normal in heights, morphology and bone marrow signal intensities. No significant acute fracture or dislocation seen in cervical vertebrae.

Mild loss of cervical lordosis is seen with multilevel disc desiccation. Disc bulge and uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy causing mild indentation of cord and nerve roots is seen at C3-4 and cord at C6-C7 levels.

Few thin epidural CSF intensity fluid collections are seen in the anterior, posterior and left posterolateral aspects of the cervical and upper dorsal regions and extending from C2 to D5 vertebral levels and with maximum thickness of 3.8 mm in left posterolateral aspect at C4 vertebral level.  Smooth mass effect over spinal cord and left exiting nerve roots is seen at few levels with effacement of thecal sac.

No abnormal signal changes are seen in the cervicodorsal spinal cord.

No other significant abnormalities are seen.

Bones and soft tissue:

Diffuse asymmetrical atrophy with IR hyper intensity is seen involving left shoulder, scapular and anterior chest wall muscles as compared to right side, suggestive of sub-acute denervation changes. No fatty infiltration is seen in the present study.

Rest of the visualised soft tissue appears grossly normal.

Resolving postoperative changes are seen in the sternum region.

IMPRESSION:

Mild smooth thickening and increased signal intensity of C5, C6 and C7 nerve roots, extending into trunks, divisions and cords, suggestive of post-traumatic stretch/ traction injury.

Thin multilevel epidural CSF-intensity fluid collections from C2 to D5 levels, causing smooth indentation and displacement of left C5–C7 preganglionic nerve root segments and mild mass effect over cervicodorsal spinal cord, likely traumatic epidural CSF collections related to occult dural injury.

No definite complete disruption/ avulsion of visualized left C5–C7 nerve roots. No significant pseudomeningocele formation.

MRI features of sub-acute denervation changes involving left shoulder girdle, periscapular and anterior chest wall muscles.

No significant abnormality of right brachial plexus.

Multilevel cervical spondylotic changes, as described. No abnormal signal changes in the cervicodorsal spinal cord.

Suggested clinical correlation / review as advised.

reports.fullText:
Dr Prakhyath

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT THIGH (PLAIN AND CONTRAST)

Clinical profile: H/o swelling and pain in anteromedial aspect of right thigh with history of hematoma evacuation 6 months back, now with recurrent increase in size and pain for past 2 months.

Technique: T1, T2, IR, DWI, GRE, pre and post-contrast T1fs in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Visualized right femur and right hip and knee joints appear unremarkable.

No evidence of cortical breach, bony erosion, periosteal reaction or abnormal marrow signal intensity.

Soft tissues:

Postoperative changes with residual scar tissue are noted along the anterior aspect of the right upper thigh.

A large, well-defined, mildly lobulated soft tissue mass lesion measuring about 7.9 × 6.5 × 7.5 cm (CC × TR × AP) is noted in the anteromedial aspect of the right upper thigh.

The lesion demonstrates a predominantly non-enhancing central component measuring approximately 5.8 × 5.1 × 5.8 cm (CC × TR × AP), showing heterogeneous T1 and T2 hyper intense signal characteristics, suggestive of sub-acute blood products/ haemorrhagic necrosis.

Along the posterosuperior, lateral and posterior aspects, there is an irregular, thick, rind-like nodular soft tissue component, measuring up to 3.2 cm in maximum thickness. This component appears predominantly T1 isointense and T2 hypo intense, with altered diffusion characteristics and heterogeneous post-contrast enhancement. Few small internal T2-hyperintense cystic/ necrotic foci are noted within the enhancing soft tissue component.

A small focal out pouching measuring approximately 0.9 × 0.8 cm is noted along the anterosuperior aspect of the lesion.

Minimal internal vascularity is noted within the solid component on USG Doppler correlation.

Mass effect and neurovascular relationships:

The lesion causes significant mass effect and displacement of adjacent muscular and neurovascular structures.

Anterolateral displacement of the Sartorius and rectus femoris muscles. Lateral displacement of the iliopsoas muscle. Posteromedial displacement of the pectineus and obturator externus muscles is seen.

Anteriorly, there is loss of intervening fat planes with the right femoral vessels, with focal compression of the right femoral vein. However, intraluminal flow is maintained on USG Doppler correlation.

The femoral neurovascular bundle is smoothly indented and displaced anterolaterally, without significant circumferential encasement.

Diffuse adjacent myofascial edema and increased IR signal intensity are noted involving the adductor compartment muscles, predominantly the adductor brevis and adductor longus, with associated intermuscular fascial edema.

Lymph nodes:

Few prominent right external iliac and femoral lymph nodes are noted, measuring up to 8.2 mm in short-axis diameter. Preserved nodal fatty hila are noted on USG correlation.

Rest of the visualized soft tissues appear unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

Large, well-defined, mildly lobulated haemorrhagic soft tissue mass in anteromedial aspect of right upper thigh demonstrating large non-enhancing central component containing sub-acute blood products/ haemorrhagic necrosis and an irregular, thick, nodular, enhancing peripheral soft tissue component with internal cystic/ necrotic foci.

Significant mass effect on adjacent muscles and femoral neurovascular structures, with focal compression of right femoral vein (maintained intraluminal flow on Doppler). No significant neurovascular encasement.

Adjacent myofascial edema involving adductor compartment muscles.

Few mildly prominent right external iliac and femoral lymph nodes.

In view of the history of previous hematoma evacuation and interval recurrence/ enlargement, the imaging appearance is suspicious for underlying haemorrhagic soft tissue neoplasm rather than a simple recurrent hematoma.

Suggested clinical and HPE correlation and review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr Prakhyath

MRI SCAN OF LEFT ANKLE AND FOOT (PLAIN AND CONTRAST)

Clinical profile: K/c/o rheumatoid arthritis on medication. Left ankle pain with tenderness? Chronic synovitis? Osteoarthritis.

Technique: T1, IR, T2, PDfs, DWI, GRE and PC T1 in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Diffuse reduction of articular cartilage thickness with associated joint space narrowing is noted involving the tibiotalar, subtalar (talocalcaneal), talonavicular and multiple midfoot articulations.

Features suggestive of partial fibrous ankylosis are noted across the talonavicular and medial and posterior subtalar articulations, with mild fixed subluxation of the talonavicular joint.

Diffuse hypertrophic synovial thickening with post-contrast enhancement is noted involving the ankle joint and multiple midfoot articulations, predominantly along the medial aspect. Mild synovitis is also noted in the remaining midfoot joints.

Few patchy subarticular marrow signal alterations with enhancement are noted involving the articulating bones across the aforementioned joints, likely representing inflammatory/ reactive osteitis.

Subarticular cystic changes are noted along the anterior aspect of the talus.

No significant cortical erosions are evident on CT correlation.

Rest of the visualized bones demonstrate preserved marrow signal intensity and cortical outlines.

Ligament complex:

Medial and lateral ligament complexes appear grossly intact.

Rest of the visualised ligaments appear intact.

Tendons and soft tissue:

Mild tenosynovial thickening and fluid with post-contrast enhancement are noted involving the flexor hallucis longus and flexor digitorum longus tendon sheaths, consistent with tenosynovitis.

Significant inflammatory changes within the sinus tarsi are noted, with effacement of normal sinus tarsi fat, enhancing synovial thickening and adjacent subarticular marrow signal alterations.

A tiny well-defined enhancing focus measuring approximately 3 × 3 × 2.5 mm (AP × TR × CC) is noted within the plantar subcutaneous fat beneath the head of the fourth metatarsal. It appears T1 hypo intense and T2/IR hyper intense, possibly representing a small rheumatoid/ inflammatory nodule.

Mild diffuse subcutaneous and soft tissue edema is noted around the ankle and along the dorsum of the foot.

No organized collection, abscess or sinus tract is identified.

Rest of the visualized tendons appear intact, without significant tear or retraction.

IMPRESSION:

Extensive inflammatory arthropathy with hypertrophic synovitis and diffuse cartilage loss involving left ankle and midfoot articulations as detailed.

Associated patchy subarticular marrow edema/ enhancement (inflammatory osteitis) and subarticular cystic changes. No cortical erosions on CT correlation.

Probable partial fibrous ankylosis across talonavicular and subtalar articulations, with mild fixed talonavicular subluxation.

Significant inflammatory synovitis involving sinus tarsi (sinus tarsi syndrome).

Mild flexor hallucis longus and flexor digitorum longus tenosynovitis.

Tiny enhancing plantar subcutaneous nodule beneath fourth metatarsal head, possibly representing a rheumatoid/ inflammatory nodule.

Mild diffuse periarticular and subcutaneous soft tissue edema.

Suggested clinical correlation / review as advised.

reports.fullText:
Dr Prakhyath

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: H/o pituitary macro adenoma s/p TSS (2023), now c/o right shoulder pain and weakness of right upper limb following RTA. To r/o rotator cuff tear and suprascapular nerve entrapment.

Technique: PDfs, IR, T1, T2 and GRE in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

The shoulder joint is normal with respect to joint space and alignment.

Minimal joint effusion is seen. No osteochondral fragment is seen.

Small subchondral cystic changes are seen at the insertion site of infraspinatus tendon along the posterior aspect of greater tuberosity.

No bony Bankart/ Hill-Sachs lesion is seen. Rest of the articulating bones is normal in outline and marrow signal intensities.

Rotator cuff and muscles:

Mild supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendinosis is seen. Small partial thickness articular surface tear (<25% thickness) is seen at insertion site of anterior part of supraspinatus tendon. Small intrasubstance tear is seen in infraspinatus tendon.

No full thickness tear or tendon retraction is seen.

Mild fatty atrophy of teres minor muscle is noted. The muscle demonstrates no significant edema or abnormal signal intensity. Its tendon is intact.

Mild diffuse PDfs/ IR hyper intensity involving the posterior part of the deltoid muscle with mild associated fatty atrophy is seen, suggestive of denervation changes (sub-acute to chronic). Subtle increased signal intensity is also noted in the anterior part of the deltoid muscle without significant volume loss or fatty replacement.

Rest of the rotator cuff muscles demonstrate preserved bulk and signal intensity without significant fatty atrophy or edema.

Long head of biceps tendon is intact within the bicipital groove.

Nerves:

The suprascapular and axillary nerves are grossly normal in their visualised course, caliber and signal intensity.

No focal compressive lesion is identified along the suprascapular nerve. No paralabral cyst or space-occupying lesion is seen in the suprascapular or spinoglenoid notch.

Labrum and capsuloligamentous structures:

Mild degenerative changes of labrum are seen with small chronic tear in anterosuperior quadrant. Rest of the glenoid labrum appears grossly normal for age. No acute tear or displaced fragment is seen.

Biceps pulley is intact. No definite capsular or ligamentous disruption noted.

AC joint:

Mild AC joint arthropathy is seen. The acromion is of type II morphology. The subacromial space is reduced and measures 4.3 mm. No subacromial bursitis is seen.

Rest of the soft tissue appears normal.

IMPRESSION:

Mild supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendinosis with small partial-thickness tears as detailed. No full-thickness tear or tendon retraction.

Denervation changes involving deltoid and teres minor muscles as detailed, suggestive of axillary nerve neuropathy.

Mild degenerative anterosuperior labral tear and minimal effusion.

Mild AC joint arthropathy with reduced subacromial space.

No definite structural abnormality or compressive lesion along visualised axillary and suprascapular nerves.

Suggested clinical and EMG/ NCS correlation and review as advised.

reports.fullText:
Dr Prakhyath

Brain:

Visualised brain parenchyma appears grossly unremarkable. No significant focal lesion or abnormal signal intensity is seen.

Mucosal thickening is noted in the right maxillary sinus.

Neck:

Diffuse oedematous signal changes are noted involving the superficial and deep fascial planes and intermuscular fascia of the neck.

Mild patchy oedematous signal changes are also seen in the visualised neck muscles.

No significant focal lesion or enlarged cervical lymph nodes are identified.

Thorax:

Diffuse oedematous signal changes are seen involving the superficial and deep fascial planes of the thoracic wall, extending along the intermuscular fascial planes bilaterally.

Mild patchy intramuscular oedematous signal changes are also noted involving the visualised thoracic musculature.

Visualised lung fields appear grossly unremarkable. Bilateral clavicles, ribs and acromioclavicular joints demonstrate normal marrow signal intensity.

No significant mediastinal abnormality is identified.

Abdomen and pelvis:

Visualised abdominal viscera appear grossly unremarkable.

Diffuse oedematous signal changes are noted involving the superficial and deep fascial planes of the abdominal wall and pelvic region, with associated diffuse subcutaneous oedema.

No focal collection or diffusion-restricting lesion is identified.

Visualised pelvic bones, bilateral iliac bones and sacroiliac joints appear unremarkable.

Bilateral hip joints are maintained without significant effusion or synovial hypertrophy.

Visualised upper limbs:

Bilateral humeri, radius, ulna and visualised bones of the hands demonstrate normal marrow signal intensity.

Diffuse oedematous signal changes are seen involving the superficial and deep fascia and intermuscular fascial planes of both upper limbs, extending across the visualised anterior and posterior compartments.

Mild patchy intramuscular oedematous signal changes are also noted involving multiple muscle groups bilaterally.

Diffuse subcutaneous oedema is seen.

Visualised lower limbs:

Bilateral femora, tibiae, fibulae and visualised bones of the feet demonstrate normal marrow signal intensity.

Diffuse oedematous signal changes are seen involving the superficial and deep fascia and intermuscular fascial planes of both lower limbs, involving the anterior and posterior compartments.

Mild patchy intramuscular oedematous signal changes are also noted involving multiple muscle groups bilaterally, more in the anterior compartments of thigh region.

Diffuse subcutaneous oedema is seen.

Muscles and fascial planes:

Overall, there is extensive, relatively symmetrical oedematous signal alteration involving the superficial and deep fascia, intermuscular fascial planes and subcutaneous tissues of the neck, thoracic wall, abdomen, pelvis and bilateral upper and lower limbs.

Associated mild patchy intramuscular oedematous signal changes are seen involving multiple muscle groups across the visualised body regions.

No significant diffusion restriction or focal fluid collection is identified.

No significant muscular volume loss, established fatty replacement or atrophy is evident.

No focal intramuscular abscess, organised haematoma or significant myonecrosis is seen.

Lymph nodes:

Few small, discrete, likely reactive lymph nodes are noted in bilateral axillary and inguinal regions.

IMPRESSION:

Bilateral extensive, diffuse and symmetrical signal changes involving superficial and deep fascia, intermuscular fascial planes and subcutaneous tissues of neck, thorax, abdomen, pelvis and bilateral upper and lower limbs as detailed. Imaging features are suggestive of extensive fasciitis, in the given clinical setting favouring eosinophilic fasciitis.

Mild patchy intramuscular oedematous signal changes involving multiple muscle groups bilaterally, suggestive of superadded inflammatory myositis.

No focal intramuscular or fascial collection/ abscess seen.

No significant established muscular atrophy or fatty replacement.

Few small reactive bilateral axillary and inguinal lymph nodes.

No focal marrow abnormality in visualised axial/ appendicular skeleton.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
MRI SCAN OF LUMBOSACRAL SPINE WITH SCREENING OF SI JOINTS AND WHOLE SPINE (PLAIN AND CONTRAST)

Clinical Profile: C/o back pain. Outside CT shows large lesion in right psoas muscle? Abscess.

Technique: Sagittal T1, T2, IR, Axial T2, DWI, Pre and post-contrast T1 FS sagittal and axial. Limited CT correlation. Screening of rest of the spine: T2/ IR sagittal.

Abnormal ill-defined marrow replacing lesion with restricted diffusion and contrast enhancement is seen involving L1, L2 and part of L3 vertebrae and towards right part of posterior elements. Mild cortical erosions of transverse process of L1 and L2 vertebrae are seen. No other significant destruction of bone is seen in present study.

Intervertebral disc spaces at L1-L2 and L2-L3 levels are relatively preserved, without significant disc signal alteration or endplate destruction, despite the adjacent vertebral marrow involvement.

The lesion extends to the right paravertebral region with a large extra osseous soft tissue component as described below.

A large, ill-defined lobulated complex soft tissue lesion with solid and cystic/ necrotic component is seen involving right psoas, quadratus lumborum and adjacent posterior paravertebral muscles. The complex lesion measures approximately 12.9 x 9.8 x 8.8 cm (CC x AP x TR).

A large non-enhancing necrotic area is seen within the lesion with haemorrhagic fluid components and patchy areas of blooming in the gradient images. CT correlation shows hyper dense content within the lesion, likely haemorrhagic component. No significant diffusion restriction is seen within this region. Few small calcific foci are seen within the lesion.

Ill-defined nodular and irregular thick rind of soft tissue component is seen along the posterior and medial aspect of the lesion showing significant diffusion restriction (0.8 to 1.0 × 10⁻³ mm²/s) and moderate post-contrast enhancement.

Multiple retroperitoneal lymph nodes are seen, largest measuring 1.4 cm in short axis.

Diffuse adjacent myofascial oedema is seen adjacent to the lesion.

Spinal canal:

Similar enhancing soft tissue component is seen within the lumbar spinal canal in epidural space, predominantly along anterior and anterolateral aspects from D12-L1 to L3 vertebral levels and with maximum thickness of 9 mm at L1 level. The soft tissue component is seen extending into the bilateral neural foramina as well (R>L).

Severe secondary spinal canal stenosis is seen at these levels causing compression of the conus medullaris and the cauda equina nerve roots. Compression of exiting and traversing nerve roots are also seen at these levels.

Minimal ascites is seen.

Diffuse subcutaneous oedema is seen in the abdomen anal wall and pelvic regions. Mildly diffuse oedema is also seen in the pelvic and gluteal muscles.

Rest of lumbar spine:

Complete sacralisation of L5 vertebra is seen.

Disc desiccation and facetal arthropathy are seen at almost all the levels. Reduced disc height with medic type II endplate changes are seen at L4-L5 level.

Grade I anterolisthesis of L4 over L5 vertebra is seen. Significant facetal arthropathy is seen at this level. No spondylolysis is seen.

L3-4: Diffuse disc bulge and facetal arthropathy are seen causing effacement of lateral recess and abutting bilateral traversing L4 nerve roots.

L4-5: Uncovered disc with posterior bulge and facetal arthropathy are seen abutting bilateral traversing L5 nerve roots.

The conus medullaris ends at L1 level.

Both SI joints show degenerative changes.

Screening of cervical Spine:

Straightening of cervical spine is seen with disc desiccation at all levels.

Mild disc bulge and uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy are seen at few levels and causing mild indentation of anterior thecal sac/ cord. No spinal cord signal changes are seen.

No other significant abnormalities are seen.

Screening of dorsal Spine:

Disc desiccation is seen at almost all the levels with mild flaval thickening at few levels. Small vertebral body haemangiomas are seen at D7 and D9 levels.

Spinal cord shows normal signal intensity.

Post-operative changes are seen in right hip joint region.

IMPRESSION:

Large aggressive infiltrative solid-cystic right paravertebral mass (12.9 × 9.8 × 8.8 cm), involving right psoas, quadratus lumborum and adjacent posterior paravertebral muscles, with extensive haemorrhagic/ necrotic components and irregular nodular enhancing solid tissue component as detailed.

Contiguous infiltrative marrow-replacing lesions involving L1, L2 and L3 vertebrae with right posterior element involvement and mild cortical erosions. Relatively preserved intervening disc spaces.

Extensive contiguous epidural and bilateral neural foraminal extension (R>L) from D12-L1 to L3, causing severe secondary spinal canal stenosis and compression of conus medullaris and cauda equina nerve roots.

Multiple enlarged retroperitoneal lymph nodes.

Sacralisation of L5 vertebra and degenerative changes of spine as detailed.

Overall imaging features are highly suspicious for a neoplastic process with vertebral and extensive paravertebral involvement. An infective etiology, particularly tuberculosis, is a less favoured differential.

Suggested clinical and HPE correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr Prakhyath

MRI SCAN OF LEFT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: Old h/o Left supraspinatus tendon repair, now with C/o recurrent pain, more on abduction above shoulder level ? Rotator cuff tear.

Technique: PDfs, T1, GRE, T2fs in all planes and CT correlation

Bones and joints:

Chronic postoperative changes are seen in the shoulder region with bio absorbable anchor in the humeral head region and subacromial decompression changes in the acromion.

Minimal joint effusion is noted.

No bony Bankart/ Hill-Sachs lesion is seen. Rest of the articulating bones is normal in outline and marrow signal intensities.

Rotator cuff:

Chronic postoperative changes are seen in rotator cuff tendon with and bio absorbable anchor tract in the greater tuberosity region.

Supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendinosis is seen with mild fraying of bursal fibres. Small chronic interstitial/ intrasubstance tears are seen in supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendons. No full thickness tears or retracted fibres seen.

Small chronic partial thickness articular surface/ intrasubstance tear are seen the subscapularis tendon.

Severe fatty replacement (Goutallier’s stage IV) of the subscapularis muscle is seen. Mild to moderate atrophy of infraspinatus muscle with grade II/ III fatty changes are seen in the infraspinatus muscle. Mild atrophy and grade II fatty changes are seen in teres minor muscle.

Atrophy with grade II/III fatty changes in teres major muscle and grade IV changes in posterior part of deltoid muscle are also seen.

Rest of the rotator cuff and shoulder girdle muscles appear grossly normal.

Long head of biceps appears intact.

Labroligamentous structures:

Mild degenerative changes are seen in the glenoid labrum with chronic tear in superior labrum extending from anterosuperior to postero-superior quadrant (SLAP tear). Small suspicious extension to the long head of biceps is also seen. Tear is also seen in the antero-inferior quadrant.

No displaced fragment is seen. Biceps pulley appears grossly intact.

No definite capsular or ligamentous disruption noted.

AC joint:

Significant AC joint arthropathy is seen. AC joint ganglion cyst measuring 9.3 x 6.3 x 5.1 mm is seen along the cranial aspect of the AC joint. Chronic post subacromial decompression changes are seen in the acromion.

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT KNEE JOINT

Clinical profile: C/o pain in anteromedial aspect of right knee joint region of past few months. No h/o recent injury.

Technique: PDfs, T1, T2, IR and GRE in all planes and cartilage sequence.

Bones and joints:

Advanced chondromalacia patellae is noted, predominantly involving the medial patellar facet and extending to the median patellar ridge, with areas of partial to full-thickness cartilage loss. A focal area of full-thickness cartilage loss measures approximately 16.6 × 11.9 mm. Mild underlying subchondral marrow oedema is noted. (Modified Outerbridge grade IV).

Mild chondral signal alterations and fissuring are also seen involving the opposing femoral trochlear cartilage, suggesting associated patellofemoral chondrosis (Grade II–III)

A prominent inferomedial patellar osteophyte is noted, causing mild impingement on the adjacent Hoffa's fat pad with focal oedematous changes.

Insall-Salvati ratio measures approximately 1.02 (within normal limits).

Medial and lateral tibiofemoral compartment articular cartilages are relatively preserved without significant focal cartilage loss.

Mild joint effusion with chronic reactive synovial thickening is noted. A small Baker's cyst measuring approximately 2.6 × 1.5 × 0.4 cm is seen. Additional small synovial cysts are noted along the posterior aspect of the joint.

Rest of the articulating bones demonstrate preserved alignment, contour and marrow signal intensity.

Meniscus:

Mild degenerative intrasubstance signal changes are noted in both menisci.

A small chronic tear involving the anterior horn/anterior root region of the medial meniscus is noted, with tiny adjacent parameniscal cysts.

Rest of the medial meniscus and lateral meniscus demonstrate preserved morphology and signal intensity.

No displaced meniscal fragment is seen.

Ligaments:

The medial and lateral collateral ligaments and patellar retinaculum appear intact.

The anterior cruciate and posterior cruciate ligaments appear intact. The intermeniscal and meniscofemoral ligaments are also normal.

Posterolateral and posteromedial corner ligament complexes appear normal.

Mild degenerative changes with small ganglion cysts are noted at the femoral attachment regions of the medial and lateral heads of gastrocnemius muscles.

Extensor mechanism, including quadriceps and patellar tendons, appears intact.

No focal soft tissue collection is identified. Rest of the visualised muscles, tendons and neurovascular structures appear unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

Advanced patellofemoral chondropathy (Modified Outerbridge grade IV) predominantly involving medial patellar facet with focal full-thickness cartilage loss, mild marrow oedema and associated trochlear chondral changes.

Prominent inferomedial patellar osteophyte causing mild impingement and reactive oedema of Hoffa's fat pad.

Small chronic tear of anterior horn/ anterior root region of medial meniscus with tiny adjacent parameniscal cysts.

Mild joint effusion with chronic reactive synovitis and small Baker's cyst.

reports.fullText:
MRI SCAN OF LEFT FOOT

Clinical profile: Non-healing wound in the plantar aspect of foot since 3 months; known diabetic, past h/o lepromatous leprosy.

Technique: T1, IR, T2, DWI, GRE, PDfs in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Ill-defined cortical erosions and destructive changes are noted along the plantar aspect of the calcaneum, with underlying abnormal marrow signal changes (T1 hypo intensity and T2/STIR hyper intensity) and altered diffusivity.

Few tiny intraosseous fluid-signal foci with diffusion restriction are noted within the involved calcaneum, suggestive of small intraosseous infective collections.

Associated mild comminuted pathological fracture is noted along the inferomedial aspect of the calcaneum, predominantly involving the plantar fascia attachment, with a small avulsed osseous fragment.

Overall features are suggestive of acute osteomyelitis of the calcaneum with small intraosseous abscesses and associated pathological fracture.

Minimal joint effusions are noted in the ankle, subtalar and few midfoot joints, without significant synovial thickening or other convincing imaging features of septic arthritis.

Rest of the visualized bones demonstrates preserved marrow signal intensity and cortical outlines. No other focal osseous destructive lesion is seen.

Soft tissue:

A focal soft tissue ulcer is noted along the plantar aspect of the heel pad, directly opposite the involved calcaneum. The ulcer tract extends up to the underlying calcaneal cortex, with loss of intervening normal soft tissue planes.

Thin rim of fluid collection with inflammatory changes is noted along the base of the ulcer, extending up to the plantar surface of the calcaneum, suggestive of an infected collection.

Significant surrounding soft tissue edema and inflammatory changes are noted in the plantar heel region, extending around the involved calcaneum.

Full-thickness tear/ avulsion of the plantar fascial attachment from the calcaneum is noted, with an associated small avulsed osseous fragment, as described above.

Diffuse fatty replacement and edema-like signal changes of the intrinsic muscles of the foot are noted, in keeping with diabetic myoneuropathy changes.

Diffuse inflammatory edema and subcutaneous fat stranding are noted involving the dorsum of the foot, ankle and visualized distal leg, suggestive of associated cellulitis changes.

No other significant loculated soft tissue collection or drainable abscess is identified.

Rest of the visualized tendons and soft tissue structures appear grossly unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

Plantar heel ulcer with underlying acute osteomyelitis of calcaneum, bone lysis and with few small intraosseous infective collections as detailed.

Comminuted pathological fracture of inferomedial calcaneum, with small avulsed fragment and full-thickness avulsion/ tear of plantar fascial attachment.

Small rim of infected fluid collection at base of plantar ulcer, extending up to the calcaneal cortex, with significant surrounding inflammatory changes.

Diffuse cellulitis changes involving the dorsum of the foot, ankle and visualized distal leg. No additional drainable soft tissue abscess.

Diffuse diabetic myoneuropathy changes involving intrinsic muscles of foot.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: H/o sports injury with Bankart and Hill Sach's lesion; s/p arthroscopic Bankart's repair and remplissage procedure. To look for foreign body.

Technique: PDfs, T1, T2, IR and GRE in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Immediate postoperative changes are seen in the right shoulder joint.

Postoperative suture anchor is noted along the posterolateral aspect of the humeral head, in keeping with the remplissage procedure.

Mild glenohumeral joint effusion is seen with few small air pockets within the joint cavity, consistent with immediate postoperative changes.

No significant residual glenohumeral dislocation or subluxation.

No significant osteochondral abnormality seen.

Labrum and capsuloligamentous structures:

Postoperative changes are noted along the anteroinferior glenoid capsulolabral region, in keeping with Bankart repair. No definite acute labral tear or displaced labral fragment is identified in the present study.

Mild waviness of the anterior band of the inferior glenohumeral ligament is noted; however, it remains continuous without definite disruption.

Rotator cuff:

Mild edema involving the supraspinatus and subscapularis tendons, suggestive of mild strain changes. No significant partial- or full-thickness tear is seen.

Rest of the rotator cuff muscles and tendons appear intact. 

Long head of biceps appears intact. The deltoid muscle appears grossly normal.

AC joint:

Mild acromioclavicular joint arthropathy with adjacent soft tissue edema, possibly representing associated sprain-related changes.

Soft tissues:

Diffuse postoperative soft tissue edema is seen along the anterior and posterior aspects of the shoulder, involving the periarticular muscles, fascial planes and subcutaneous fat planes. Minimal fluid tracking is seen along the fascial planes.

Multiple small air pockets are seen within the postoperative soft tissues, along the muscular and fascial planes, as well as within the glenohumeral joint cavity, consistent with immediate postoperative changes.

A small hyper dense focus measuring approximately 4 × 2 mm is noted in the soft tissues just inferomedial to the base of the coracoid process on CT correlation, suspicious for a small retained foreign body. Clinical and surgical correlation is advised.

No significant organized fluid collection or postoperative hematoma seen.

IMPRESSION:

Immediate postoperative changes following arthroscopic Bankart repair and remplissage procedure, with suture anchor along posterolateral humeral head and postoperative changes in the anteroinferior capsulolabral region.

Small hyper dense focus measuring 4 × 2 mm in the soft tissues just inferomedial to the base of the coracoid process, suspicious for a retained foreign body. Surgical correlation is recommended.

Diffuse postoperative soft tissue edema with multiple air pockets in periarticular soft tissues, muscular/ fascial planes and glenohumeral joint cavity, consistent with recent surgery.

Mild glenohumeral joint effusion. No significant organized collection/ hematoma.

Mild supraspinatus and subscapularis tendon strain. No significant cuff tear.

Mild waviness of anterior band of inferior glenohumeral ligament, which remains continuous. No definite acute labral tear or displaced labral fragment.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Dr Prakhyath

MRI SCAN OF LEFT FOOT & ANKLE (PLAIN + CONTRAST)

Clinical profile: H/o accidental injury to left leg 3 months back; now with c/o fever, chills and rigor for past 2 weeks, progressively increasing leg swelling. O/E- left leg - warm and tender - Cellulitis.

Technique: PDfs, IR, T1, T2, DWI, GRE and PC T1 in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Abnormal marrow edema (IR hyper intensity) with post-contrast enhancement is noted involving the head of the fourth metatarsal and base of the proximal phalanx of the fourth toe, across the fourth MTP joint. Minimal fourth MTP joint effusion with synovial thickening and enhancement is noted.

No significant cortical erosion, destruction or periosteal reaction is evident at present.

Patchy marrow edema-like signal changes are also noted involving the talus, calcaneum, cuboid and a few other tarsal bones, without significant cortical abnormality or associated soft tissue collection. These are likely stress-related trabecular changes. No convincing imaging features of osteomyelitis in these bones.

Minimal joint effusion is noted in the ankle and posterior subtalar joints.

Rest of the visualised bones and joints appear grossly unremarkable.

Soft tissue and collections:

A small soft tissue ulcer is noted along the plantar aspect of the fourth MTP joint. An underlying ill-defined fluid collection demonstrating restricted diffusion is noted along the plantar aspect of the fourth MTP joint, extending into the fourth interdigital space and minimally onto the dorsal aspect of the fifth toe region. It measures approximately 3.2 × 1.5 × 1.2 cm (CC × AP × TR), consistent with an infected collection/ abscess.

Extensive surrounding soft tissue edema, inflammatory changes and post-contrast enhancement are noted in the plantar forefoot, centered around the ulcer and underlying collection.

Diffuse subcutaneous edema with post-contrast enhancement is noted involving the skin and subcutaneous fat planes of the foot and ankle, predominantly along the dorsum, consistent with cellulitis changes.

No other significant drainable soft tissue collection is identified.

Mild edema is noted within the sinus tarsi.

Muscles, tendons and ligaments:

Diffuse edema-like signal changes are noted involving the intrinsic muscles of the foot, likely suggestive of diffuse myoneuropathy changes.

The anterior, medial, lateral (peroneal) and posterior tendon complexes appear intact. No evidence of tendon tear or significant tenosynovitis.

The visualised medial and lateral ligamentous complexes appear intact.

Plantar fascia is normal in thickness and signal intensity.

Rest of the visualised soft tissue appears grossly normal for age.

IMPRESSION:

Marrow edema and enhancement involving 4th metatarsal head and base of 4th  proximal phalanx, across MTP joint, with mild synovitis and joint effusion,  suspicious for early osteomyelitis with septic arthritis.

Small plantar soft tissue ulcer at fourth MTP joint with an underlying infected collection/ abscess and extensions as detailed.

Extensive surrounding cellulitis changes involving forefoot, with diffuse subcutaneous inflammatory edema extending along dorsum of foot and ankle.

Patchy stress-related trabecular marrow edema in talus, calcaneum, cuboid and other tarsal bones, without convincing features of osteomyelitis.

Suggested clinical correlation and review as indicated.

Dr Abhirami / Dr Prakhyath

MRI SCAN OF BILATERAL HIP JOINT& SCREENING OF LS SPINE

Clinical profile: C/o right leg pain. To evaluate for avascular necrosis / osteonecrosis.

Technique: T1, T2, IR, PD fs, GRE and DWI in all planes.

Lumbosacral spine screening: T2 sagittal and axial.

Right hip joint:

Geographic area of altered marrow signal with preserved central fatty signal intensity and a peripheral T1 hypo intense rim is noted in the anterosuperior aspect of the femoral head, involving less than 25% of the femoral head. Modified Kerboul combined necrotic angle measures approximately 156°. Features are consistent with Nishii type B, Ficat-Arlet stage II and Mitchell class A osteonecrosis.

No subchondral fracture, articular surface collapse, significant flattening or contour deformity of the femoral head.

No significant acetabular marrow abnormality or secondary degenerative changes.

Trace hip joint effusion is seen.

Left hip joint:

Femoral head demonstrates normal marrow signal intensity and preserved contour.

No evidence of osteonecrosis or subchondral fracture.

No significant acetabular or other periarticular osseous abnormality.

Trace hip joint effusion is seen.

Rest of the bony pelvis:

The visualized pelvic bones and remaining visualized osseous structures demonstrate normal marrow signal intensity.

Soft tissues:

Mild bilateral greater trochanteric peritendinous degenerative changes are seen. No significant trochanteric bursal distension is seen.

Visualized muscles and tendons are otherwise unremarkable.

Visualized femoral and sciatic neurovascular bundles appear normal.

Screening of lumbosacral spine:

Conus medullaris terminates at D12 level (considering the lowermost discrete vertebra as L5).

Asymmetric diffuse disc bulge with facetal arthropathy and ligamentum flavum thickening are seen at L4-L5, causing secondary spinal canal stenosis (residual AP thecal sac diameter approximately 9 mm) and compression of bilateral traversing L5 nerve roots (L>R).

No other significant disc abnormality or spinal canal stenosis in the visualized lumbar spine.

IMPRESSION:

Early osteonecrosis of right femoral head (Ficat-Arlet stage II) as detailed.

Mild bilateral greater trochanteric peritendinous degenerative changes.

Lumbar spondylosis with canal stenosis and mass effect over bilateral L5 nerve roots at L4-L5 level as detailed.

No other significant abnormality seen.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT KNEE JOINT

Clinical Profile: H/o trauma two days back; c/o pain and swelling over the right knee.

Technique: PDfs in all 3 planes, T1, T2 sagittal, GRE axial, STIR axial and coronal.

Bones and Cartilage:

Ill-defined marrow edema/ trabecular injury are noted involving the anterior to mid aspect of the lateral femoral condyle and the posterior part of lateral tibial plateau, consistent with impaction bone contusions secondary to a pivot-shift injury mechanism.

Small undisplaced osteochondral fragment is seen in lateral femoral condyle. A small focus of patchy marrow contusion is also noted in medial femoral condyle.

The knee joint is grossly normal with respect to alignment and joint space.

Moderate lipohemarthrosis is seen.  No full thickness cartilage loss or osteochondral loose body are seen.

Rest of the articulating bones appear grossly normal for age. No significant physeal injury is seen.

Meniscus:

Sprain/ partial tear is seen involving the posterior aspects of medial and lateral meniscocapsular attachment/ ligaments. Disruption of superior medial meniscocapsular ligament is seen in the posterior aspect (ramp-type injury).

Small inferior corner tear is seen involving the posterior horn of lateral meniscus. Small suspicious horizontal tear is seen in the outer third of body region of lateral meniscus.

Rest of the parts of the medial and lateral menisci are grossly normal in configuration and signal intensities. No other significant acute tear or displaced fragment seen.

Ligaments:

Acute full thickness tear of anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) is seen involving the proximal part with wavy contour of distally retracted fibres. The posterior cruciate ligaments appear grossly intact.

Grade II sprain/ partial tear are seen involving femoral attachment of MPFL/ medial patellar retinaculum with mild waviness of fibres.

Grade II sprain/ partial tear is seen involving femoral part of medial collateral ligament, predominantly involving the anterior fibres.

Grade I sprain changes of lateral patellar retinaculum and lateral collateral ligament are seen.

Grade II sprain/ partial tear changes are seen involving posteromedial and posterolateral corner ligament complex.

Rest of soft tissues:

Mild myofascial strain changes are seen around the knee joint and proximal leg region with oedema along the fascia under the subcutaneous fat plane. No significant sized haematoma or fluid collection seen in the present study.

Rest of the extensor mechanism appears normal. Rest of the surrounding muscles, tendons and neurovascular structures are grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Acute complete proximal ACL tear with distal retraction of torn fibres.

Pivot-shift pattern of osseous injuries with small undisplaced osteochondral fracture fragment of lateral femoral condyle.

Moderate lipohemarthrosis.

Posterior meniscocapsular injuries involving both medial and lateral menisci and small lateral meniscal tear as detailed.

Grade II sprain/ partial tears of femoral attachments of MCL and MPFL/medial patellar retinaculum.

Grade II sprain of posteromedial and posterolateral corner ligamentous complexes and other ligament changes as detailed.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
Dr Abhirami

MRI SCAN OF LEFT THIGH AND BONY PELVIS (PLAIN + CONTRAST)

Clinical Profile: C/o left hip pain radiating to loin for 2 days, nausea, vomiting. Incidentally detected lytic lesion in left femur.

Technique: IR, T1, T2, PDfs, GRE, DWI and PC T1 in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Multiple well-defined, slightly lobulated, predominantly longitudinally oriented intramedullary lesions are seen involving the left hemi pelvis, proximal femur and femoral shaft, with additional similar lesions in the visualized proximal left tibia.

The dominant lesion is seen along the anterior aspect of the left femoral neck, extending into the proximal metaphyseal region and measuring about 8.4 x 2.2 x 1.8 cm (CC x TRA x AP).  It demonstrates a geographic lytic appearance with a well-defined peripheral sclerotic rim (rind sign).

Mild osseous expansion/ remodeling with cortical thinning are noted in the region of the dominant proximal femoral lesion. No cortical breakthrough or extension to the subchondral articular surface.

Another similar, slightly lobulated, longitudinally oriented lesion is seen along the posterior aspect of the distal femoral metadiaphysis, demonstrating a thin peripheral sclerotic margin.

An additional similar lesion is seen within the medullary cavity of the mid femoral shaft. Few similar smaller lesions are noted in the visualized left pelvic bones and proximal left tibia. Few of the pelvic and femoral lesions demonstrate internal foci of macroscopic fat signal.

Mild internal trabecular thickening is noted within the proximal femoral lesion.

The lesions demonstrate predominantly T2/ IR hyper intense signal with heterogeneous post-contrast enhancement of the non-fatty components. No significant diffusion restriction. No cystic areas/ hemorrhage of fluid levels are seen.

CT correlation demonstrates variable internal matrix attenuation, with average values of approximately 109 HU in the midshaft femoral lesion and 259 HU in the distal femoral lesion.

No significant surrounding marrow edema, cortical destruction, aggressive periosteal reaction or extra osseous soft tissue component. No pathological fracture is identified.

Visualized left hip joint alignment and joint space are maintained. No significant hip joint effusion.

Visualized left sacroiliac joint and pubic symphysis is unremarkable.

Muscles and tendons:

Visualized gluteal, iliopsoas, adductor, hamstring and quadriceps muscle groups show normal bulk and signal intensity. No focal intramuscular lesion, muscle edema or collection.

Visualized iliopsoas, gluteal, adductor and hamstring tendon attachments are grossly intact.

No significant musculotendinous injury or tendinopathy.

Neurovascular structures:

Visualized sciatic and femoral nerves show normal course, caliber and signal intensity.

Visualized femoral and profunda femoris neurovascular bundles are unremarkable.

No focal neurovascular encasement or compression.

Soft tissues:

Visualized subcutaneous and intermuscular soft tissue planes are maintained.

No focal soft tissue mass, abnormal enhancement or fluid collection.

No significant regional soft tissue edema.

IMPRESSION:

Multiple well-defined, non-aggressive intramedullary fibro-osseous lesions involving left hemi pelvis, proximal femur, femoral shaft, distal femur and visualized proximal tibia, with left-sided (monomelic) distribution.

Dominant proximal femoral lesion demonstrates thin peripheral sclerotic rim with mild osseous expansion/ remodeling as detailed.

Variable internal matrix density with focal macroscopic fat-containing components in some pelvic and femoral lesions.

No aggressive imaging features, cortical breakthrough, extra osseous soft tissue extension or pathological fracture.

No other significant abnormality seen.

In view of imaging features, the possibility of polyostotic fibrous dysplasia with predominantly left-sided distribution is more likely. Suggested clinical correlation/ further evaluation and review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF LEFT LEG (PLAIN + CONTRAST)

Clinical profile: C/o left leg Non-healing ulcer for 20 years. S/p EVLA + foam sclerotherapy done in April 2026 - developed septic thrombophlebitis in June 2026 - wound debridement done. HPE dated 03.11.2026 - well differentiated squamous cell carcinoma of left leg.

Technique: T1, T2, IR, DWI, PDfs, GRE and pre and PC T1 in all planes. CT correlation.

Soft tissue:

Primary tumor:

An Ulceroproliferative enhancing soft tissue mass is noted along lateral aspect of the left leg, at the junction of the middle and distal thirds, measuring approximately 5.4 × 4.7 × 0.7 cm (CC × AP × thickness). The lesion demonstrates heterogeneous T2/STIR hyper intensity, significant diffusion restriction and avid post-contrast enhancement.

The lesion predominantly involves the skin and underlying subcutaneous fat, extending up to the deep fascia with suspected focal involvement of the underlying deep fascia.

At its inferior aspect, a small focal area of soft tissue extension beyond the deep fascial plane is suspected, abutting the lateral aspect of the peroneal muscle compartment.

However, no definite infiltration or abnormal signal alteration of the underlying peroneal muscles is identified.

No definite involvement of the adjacent tendons or neurovascular structures is evident.

No other discrete satellite soft tissue lesion is identified in the adjacent leg.

Regional soft tissue nodules / lymph nodes:

Few small nodular soft tissue lesions are noted along the posterolateral aspect of the Achilles tendon at the level of the lower part of the primary lesion, the largest measuring approximately 5.4 × 3.1 mm.

These demonstrate significant diffusion restriction and are suspicious for small satellite tumour deposits / regional nodal deposits.

No other significant regional soft tissue nodules are identified.

Bones and joints:

CT correlation demonstrates mild periosteal thickening along the distal third of the fibula.

No underlying aggressive cortical destruction, focal lytic lesion or definite direct osseous invasion by the adjacent tumour is evident.

Patchy areas of mildly altered marrow signal are noted in the proximal and middle thirds of the tibia, without significant diffusion restriction or convincing abnormal post-contrast enhancement. These are nonspecific and may represent reactive marrow changes / red marrow reconversion in the setting of chronic venous disease.

No focal aggressive marrow-replacing lesion is identified.

Visualised osseous alignment is maintained.

Other soft tissue and vascular structures:

Multiple dilated and tortuous superficial varicose veins are noted in the visualised left leg region.

Diffuse subcutaneous oedematous changes are seen throughout the left leg, with associated oedema along the deep and intermuscular fascial planes.

No significant organised fluid collection or drainable abscess is identified.

No definite intramuscular collection is seen.

The remaining visualised muscles and tendons demonstrate preserved morphology and signal characteristics.

IMPRESSION:

Ulceroproliferative enhancing soft tissue mass along lateral aspect of left leg at the middle–distal third junction, measuring 5.4 × 4.7 × 0.7 cm and corresponding to the biopsy-proven well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma.

Predominant involvement of skin and subcutaneous tissues with underlying deep fascial infiltration. Small focal extension beyond deep inferiorly, abutting peroneal muscle compartment, without definite underlying muscular invasion.

Few tiny diffusion-restricting nodular soft tissue lesions along posterolateral aspect of Achilles tendon (largest 5.4 × 3.1 mm), suspicious for satellite tumour deposits / regional metastatic nodules.

Mild periosteal thickening in fibula without cortical destruction/ direct invasion.

Diffuse subcutaneous and deep fascial oedema in left leg, likely related to chronic venous stasis and previous inflammatory / infective changes.

Multiple superficial varicose veins in the left leg.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

MRI SCAN OF RIGHT SHOULDER JOINT

Clinical profile: H/o trauma 15 days back. C/o shoulder pain and inability to move.

Technique: PDfs, T1, T2, IR and GRE in in all planes. CT correlation.

Bones and joints:

Mild to moderate joint effusion is seen with fluid extending to the anterior aspect of bony glenoid region and subacromial bursal region.

No significant acute fracture or displaced fragment is seen. Degenerative changes with marrow oedema are seen in the posterior aspect of humeral head region.

Rest of articulating bones are grossly normal in outline and marrow signal for age.

Diffuse intra-articular and periarticular calcifications are seen involving labrum, capsuloligamentous structures and tendons. Similar changes are also seen in the left shoulder joint and bilateral sternoclavicular joints in screening CT. Features are Calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease (CPPD/ chondrocalcinosis)

Rotator cuff:

Acute full thickness full width tear of subscapularis tendon is seen from its attachment to lesser tuberosity (CC dimension of 2.2 cm). Torn tendon is oedematous and wavy and is seen at the level of medial third of humeral head region with varying retraction. Maximum retraction is about 1.2 cm from insertion point.

Acute full thickness tear is seen involving the entire width of supraspinatus tendon and almost entire width of infraspinatus tendon (AP dimension of 3.5 cm). Torn tendon fibres are oedematous and wavy and with retraction of about 0.8 cm from insertion. Small extension of tears to the musculotendinous junctions of supraspinatus infraspinatus muscles is seen.

Residual part of infraspinatus tendon shows severe tendinosis with small intrasubstance tears. Mild teres minor tendon sprain changes are also seen.

Mild atrophy of supraspinatus, infraspinatus and subscapularis muscles are seen with grade II fatty infiltration in supraspinatus and subscapularis muscles and grade III in infraspinatus muscle.

LHBT tendinosis is seen. Partial thickness tears are also seen in the deltoid muscle.

Labroligamentous structures:

Degenerative changes are seen in the labrum with chronic tears in anterosuperior, superior and postero-superior quadrant (SLAP tear). Rest of the labrum appears grossly intact for age. No other significant acute tear or displaced fragment seen.

Sprain changes with partial tear of anterior IGHL and adjacent capsule is seen. Disruption of biceps pulley is seen.  Mild diffuse synovial/ capsular thickening is seen in the joint, likely suggestive of capsulitis.

AC joint:

AC joint arthropathy is seen. The acromion is of type II morphology and is laterally sloping. Subacromial space measures 6 mm. Mild sub acromial bursitis is seen with fluid collection.

Myofascial strain changes are seen around shoulder joint, predominantly involving subscapularis and supraspinatus muscles. Significant oedema is seen along the anterior aspect of the shoulder joint with minimal fluid collection anterior subscapularis muscle.

Few reactive discrete nodes are seen in the right axillary region.

Rest of the soft tissue appear grossly normal.

IMPRESSION:

Acute full thickness full width tears of subscapularis, supraspinatus and almost full width of infraspinatus tendons with retracted and edematous fibres and muscle changes as detailed.

Mild to moderate joint effusion, labral tears and capsuloligamentous injuries as detailed.

AC joint arthropathy with features of subacromial bursitis as detailed.

Myofascial strain changes around shoulder joint, predominantly involving subscapularis and supraspinatus muscles, partial tears in deltoid muscle and adjacent soft tissue edema and small fluid collection as detailed.

Diffuse intra-articular and periarticular calcifications involving labrum, capsuloligamentous structures and tendons as detailed, suggestive of calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease (CPPD/ chondrocalcinosis)

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Mild anterior wedge compression along superior endplate is seen involving D7 vertebra with about 10-20% height reduction. No posterior cortical fracture or retropulsion or spinal canal compromise seen.

reports.fullText:
MRI OF LUMBOSACRAL SPINE AND SCREENING OF REST OF THE SPINE AND BRAIN

Clinical Profile: Complaints of lower back pain for the past 2 weeks. Right lower limb numbness K/c/o Refractory primary mediastinal B cell lymphoma. Bilateral peroneal motor neuropathy, SPN sensory neuropathy, lower limb radiculopathy.

Technique: Sagittal T1, T2, IR, Axial T2. T1 and IR Coronal for SI joints

Screening of rest of the spine – T2 sagittal

Screening of brain: 3D FLAIR, DWI.

Grade I anterolisthesis of L5 over S1 vertebra is seen. No spondylolysis is seen.

Rest of the lumbosacral spine displays a normal lordotic curvature and vertebral column alignment.

Endplate irregularity with Chronic schmorl node are seen in superior endplate of S1 vertebra. Rest of the individual vertebrae are normal in heights and morphology.

Mild heterogenous marrow signal changes are seen without abnormal IR hyper intensity or aggressive features, likley treatment related changes.

Disc desiccation with facetal arthropathy are seen at few levels. Rest of the intervertebral discs are normal in heights. Rest of the vertebral end-plates are normal.

D12-L1, L1-2: Normal.

L2-3: Mild disc bulge is seen. No significant mass effect over nerve roots seen.

L3-4: Diffuse disc bulge with right extraforaminal disc protrusion and facetal arthropathy are seen causing indentation of right exiting L3 nerve root.

L4-5: Diffuse disc bulge with mild facetal arthropathy are seen. No significant mass effect over nerve roots.

L5-S1: Uncovered disc with diffuse disc bulge and facetal arthropathy are seen. No significant mass effect over nerve roots.

The conus medullaris ends at L1-2 level and the cauda equine is normal in appearance. No abnormal thickening of the nerves is seen.

The prevertebral and paravertebral soft tissues are grossly normal.

Both SI joints are grossly normal in joint space and signal intensities.

Screening of cervical spine:

Loss of cervical lordosis is seen.

Mild disc desiccation is seen at multiple levels. Mild disc bulge with early uncovertebral arthropathy causing anterior thecal sac indentation are seen at few levels. Spinal cord appears normal.

No other significant abnormalities in the cervical spine.

Screening of dorsal spine:

Chronic Post-radiotherapy changes with fatty infiltration of marrow are seen at multiple upper dorsal levels.

Mild chronic wedge compression with vertebral height reduction of 10-20% is seen at D7 vertebra.

Small disc protrusions causing indentation of anterior thecal sac/ cord is seen at few levels. Ligamentum flavum thickening are noted at few levels. No abnormal spinal cord signal changes seen.

No other significant abnormalities in the dorsal spine.

Screening of brain:

No abnormal DWI signal changes.

No significant neuroparenchymal abnormality seen.

Mild mucosal thickening are seen in the bilateral maxillary sinus.

IMPRESSION:

Mild diffuse degenerative changes in spine with grade I L5/S1 anterolisthesis.

Disc bulge with right extraforaminal disc protrusion causing indentation of right L3 nerve root at L3-4 level as detailed.

No other significant abnormalities in the spine.

No significant neuroparenchymal abnormality.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

reports.fullText:
MRI OF LEFT SHOULDER JOINT AND SCREENING OF CERVICAL SPINE

Clinical profile: C/o left shoulder pain for 4 months. K/c/o DM on medication for 15 years. No h/o trauma.

Technique: PDfs in all planes, T1 sag, T2/IR coronal, GRE axial.

Screening of cervical spine: T2 sagittal and axial.

Bones and joints:

Mild joint effusion is seen. No osteochondral loose body is seen.

Mild degenerative changes with small subarticular cysts are seen in humeral head region. No bony Bankart/ Hill-Sachs lesion is seen.

Rest of the articulating bones appear grossly normal in outline and marrow signal intensities for age.

Rotator cuff:

Supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendinosis is seen with significant fraying of articular surface fibres of supraspinatus tendon.

High grade partial thickness articular surface tear is seen in the anterior part of supraspinatus tendon about 1 cm from insertion foot print region (>50% thickness and 14.5 mm in AP dimension). Mild retraction of torn articular surface fibres is seen.

Chronic intrasubstance tear is seen also at the insertion footprint region of supraspinatus tendon with a small delamination component.

Subscapularis tendinosis is seen with small chronic partial thickness articular surface tear and small intramuscular cyst (13 x 3 x 2.5 mm)

No full thickness tears of rotator cuff tendon are seen in the present study.

Rest of the rotator cuff muscles and tendons appear grossly normal for age.

Mild tendinosis of the LHBT is seen. The deltoid muscle is also normal.

Labroligamentous structures:

Degenerative changes are seen in labrum with chronic labral tears in anterosuperior, superior and postero-superior quadrants (SLAP) tear. Tiny paralabral cyst is seen in the postero-superior quadrant. No acute tear or displaced fragment is seen.

Diffuse synovial/ capsular thickening is seen in rotator interval and axillary recess regions. Thickening with increased signal intensity of biceps pulley and IGHL are seen. No other definite capsular or ligamentous disruption seen.

AC joint:

AC joint arthropathy is seen. The acromion is of type II morphology and is laterally sloping.

The subacromial space is mildly reduced (5.5 mm). Minimal subacromial bursitis is seen with trace of fluid.  Rest of the soft tissue appears normal.

Screening of cervical spine:

Straightening of cervical spine is seen with disc desiccation at all levels and uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy at few levels.

C5-6: Disc bulge and uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy are seen causing indentation of the cord and bilateral exiting C6 nerve roots (L>R).

C6-7: Disc bulge and uncovertebral/ facetal arthropathy are seen causing indentation of the cord and bilateral exiting C7 nerve roots (L>R).

No spinal cord signal changes are seen. No other significant abnormality seen in screening cervical spine.

IMPRESSION:

Rotator cuff tendinosis with partial thickness tears, more significant in supraspinatus tendon as detailed.

Mild joint effusion with features of capsulitis as detailed.

Degenerative labral tears, tiny paralabral cyst and LHBT tendinosis as detailed.

AC joint arthropathy with reduced subacromial space and minimal subacromial bursitis, likely suggestive of sub acromial impingement.

Cervical spondylosis, more significant at C5-6 and C6-7 levels as mentioned.

Suggested clinical correlation/ review as indicated.

Multiple intensely hypermetabolic lytic lesion with soft tissue noted involving mandible on left side, left scapula, right humerus, D5 and L4 vertebra, sacrum, pelvic bones, bilateral distal shaft of femur, right proximal tibia, largest soft tissue noted in sacrum, measuring 4.7 x 4 cm, SUVmax 20.7. L4 vertebral the soft tissue causes cauda equina compression. Sacral soft tissue extending into sacral Neural foramen.
